title: GMDH-based comparative modeling and reliability assessment provide interpretable prediction of compressive strength in natural-zeolite concrete
abstract: Concrete production places increasing pressure on natural resources, motivating the use of natural zeolite in cementitious systems. This study developed an interpretable data-driven framework for predicting the compressive strength of zeolite-containing concrete using 324 laboratory specimens. The input variables were water-to-binder ratio (W/B), zeolite content (Z), superplasticizer dosage (SP), total aggregate content (TA), fine aggregate ratio (FA), and curing time (T). Three interpretable models, Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH), Response Surface Methodology (RSM), and Gene Expression Programming (GEP), were compared with Random Forest, Gradient-Boosted Regression Trees, and a Deep Neural Network. All models were evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Among the interpretable models, GMDH achieved the best performance, with R² = 0.8957, RMSE = 5.113 MPa, and MAE = 4.058 MPa. RSM ranked second (R² = 0.8828; RMSE = 5.422 MPa), while GEP showed the lowest accuracy (R² = 0.7060; RMSE = 8.585 MPa). Although some benchmark models achieved higher accuracy, GMDH provided an explicit formulation suitable for sensitivity and reliability analyses. SHAP analysis showed that curing time had the greatest influence (0.54), followed by W/B (0.32), while local sensitivity analysis identified SP as the strongest control variable around the reference mixture. At the maximum uncertainty level, the 65 MPa target had a failure probability of 0.0161 and a reliability index of 2.142. The proposed framework supports preliminary mixture design and risk-informed screening within the investigated data domain.

title: An intelligent internet of things-based artificial intelligence framework for adaptive mechanical process control and real-time performance optimization
abstract: Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) and Model Predictive Control (MPC) are the conventional methods used for Industrial Process Control (IPC). But these methods often fail to maintain optimal performance when the operating environment is nonlinear and changes dynamically. Internet of Things (IoT) models help with connectivity and monitoring in industry. These models lack predictive decision-making for real-time adaptation, energy efficiency, and early fault detection. This study aims to develop an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Control System (AI-ECS) that unifies real-time process management, predictive maintenance, and adaptive energy optimization for dynamic industrial environments. AI-ECS integrates IoT sensor networks with hybrid Random Forest (RF) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithms for predictive analytics. Further, real-time feedback control is achieved through dynamically tuned PID and MPC controllers running on an edge-computing platform. An experimental study was done on a continuous-flow industrial process testbed. The setup included multi-rate sensor sampling, Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) communication, and containerized edge services. AI-ECS was compared with traditional PID, Advanced Process Control (APC), and IoT-only systems. AI-ECS reduced control error by \(\:73.3\%\) , measured as the relative reduction in Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of the process variable relative to its setpoint. Energy Consumption (EC) decreased by \(\:9.1\%\) as well. Early Fault Detection (FD) also improved by a good margin. Anomalies were monitored over a \(\:48\) - hour pre-failure window, and the impending fault was detected up to \(\:36\) hours before failure. The system also presented faster disturbance rejection. Stability was verified across the \(\:24\) - hour and \(\:30\) - day operational windows of the testbed. The AI-ECS gives a reproducible, scalable, and energy-efficient model for intelligent industrial control. It provides a practical method for predictive, self-optimizing, and fault-tolerant manufacturing in accordance with the standards of Industry 4.0 by combining IoT-enabled sensing with adaptive decision-making driven by artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Deep learning-based quantum-secure framework for authentication and encryption of volumetric NIfTI neuroimaging data
abstract: As cloud-based healthcare systems, telemedicine platforms and the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) become more prevalent, the demand for secure authentication and protection of volumetric medical imaging data has grown significantly. Specifically, images provided by the Neuroimaging Informatics Technology Initiative (NIfTI) contain important information that needs to be safeguarded from unauthorized access, tampering, and new threats from quantum computing. In this paper, we propose a token-mediated authentication and encryption framework that establishes functional dependencies among deep feature authentication, chaotic encryption, and post-quantum token protection. To obtain strong feature representations from multi-modal MRI volumes, a 3D Siamese DenseNet architecture is used and authentication tokens are computed by applying a SHA-3 cryptographic hashing function. For the image encryption, a double pendulum chaotic system is used to generate highly sensitive keystreams to ensure confidentiality, and for protecting authentication tokens, ML-KEM lattice-based post-quantum cryptography is adopted against classical and quantum adversaries. This proposed framework was assessed with the multi-modal MRI dataset from BraTS2020, which consists of FLAIR, T1, T1CE and T2 modalities. Experimental results reveal high level of encryption security with a good NPCR, UACI, entropy and statistical analysis results. The results of the decryption process achieved PSNR values greater than 58 dB and SSIM values very close to 0.9999, which shows high-quality image reconstruction and preservation of diagnostic image quality. The results of authentication experiments demonstrated that the DenseNet model proposed in this work obtained better results than the CNN, ResNet and EfficientNet models. The robustness evaluation revealed that the proposed model was able to maintain its performance even in the presence of noise, cropping, compression, rotation and combined attacks. Moreover, experiments with adversarial tampering succeeded in finding all ROI and metadata alterations, and accurately identifying altered areas. The framework proposed in this study resulted in an average processing time of ~ 234.13 s/volume, exhibiting practical usability for secure storage and transmission of medical images. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides effective authentication, secure image protection, and high-fidelity reconstruction for volumetric NIfTI neuroimaging data. An additional independent evaluation on twenty volumetric COVID-19 CT cases further demonstrated the transferability of the encryption and reconstruction components beyond the BraTS2020 MRI dataset. The framework incorporates ML-KEM-based post-quantum protection for authentication-token exchange, while the security of the chaotic encryption component is supported by the experimental analyses presented in this study rather than by a formal post-quantum security proof.

title: ML-based performance prediction of CSRR-enhanced four-port fractal MIMO antenna for 6G communication systems
abstract: The rapid development of wireless communication systems and the growing demand for terahertz (THz) sensing have led to an increasing demand for compact antennas with high isolation, integrated with machine learning (ML), to meet the stringent requirements of the next-generation 6G networks. In this paper, a compact quad-port fractal MIMO antenna with Complementary Split-Ring Resonator (CSRR) for efficient mutual coupling suppression is proposed, along with an ML-based rapid performance prediction framework. A triangular fractal radiating structure of electrical size of 3.08λ 0 × 3.08 λ 0 on polyimide substrate along with a slotted-patch and CSRR-based isolation technique, efficiently suppresses the surface-current coupling and achieves an inter-port isolation better than −27 dB. The four port MIMO antenna operates at triple-band 6.35, 6.6, and 8.6 THz with wide bandwidths, with a maximum gain of 8.2 dB and the radiation efficiency of 89%. The MIMO performance is further validated with diversity metrics such as low Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) of 0.007 and high Diversity Gain (DG) of 9.965 dB indicating good port decoupling and reliable multi-stream transmission. In order to improve the design efficiency, five supervised ML regression models were trained on CST-generated data to predict the isolation performance. The Extra Trees regressor gave the best accuracy (R2 = 95.27%, MAE = 0.2095%, RMSE = 0.5731%) compared to the other models. The results show that ML-based prediction is an effective solution to reduce the dependence on computationally expensive simulations, making the proposed design a compact, wideband, and high-performance solution for THz MIMO systems in 6G THz wireless applications.

title: Evaluating typhoon cloud morphology as a candidate early satellite proxy for storm-surge risk under ERA5 physical benchmarking
abstract: Storm surge is driven by wind, pressure, tide, bathymetry, and coastal geometry; satellite cloud structure is therefore evaluated here as a candidate proxy for cyclone organization rather than a direct forcing. We matched Hong Kong Observatory residual-surge records for 72 tropical-cyclone events (2015–2025) with Himawari-8/9 B13 cloud metrics at 24, 12, and 6 h before the observed surge peak. Seventy-one events had complete sequences, including 19 events with peak residual surge \(\ge 0.70\) m. Under leakage-free event-grouped cross-validation, the seven-variable cloud Transformer showed no reliable stand-alone discrimination (ROC-AUC = 0.518, 95% CI 0.380–0.673; permutation \(p = 0.4209\) ) and yielded station RMSE = 0.420 m (95% CI 0.284–0.574). An untrained ERA5 wind-stress/pressure rank index achieved AUC = 0.853 and Spearman \(\rho = 0.741\) , while the ERA5 wind-pressure baseline achieved AUC = 0.860 and station RMSE = 0.313 m. Adding seven cloud variables changed ERA5 event AUC by \(-0.005\) (95% CI \(-0.023\) to 0.012). Cloud morphology provides reproducible observational descriptors, but in this sample it does not support a validated stand-alone early-warning model and is best treated as a contextual diagnostic alongside atmospheric and hydrodynamic guidance.

title: Influence of optimizing vibration-reducing measures on the post-earthquake running safety of trains in extradosed cable-stayed bridges
abstract: This study proposes a vibration mitigation scheme for seismic analysis of long-span bridges. Focusing on an extradosed cable-stayed bridge in high-speed railways, it investigates how damping-isolation devices affect both structural seismic responses and train operational safety. A coupled dynamics model of a high-speed train-ballastless track-bridge system incorporating friction pendulum bearings (FPBs) and viscous dampers (VDs) is established using the ABAQUS-SIMPACK co-simulation platform. Parametric analyses based on the uniform test method, multivariate regression, and random forest algorithm are used to optimize vibration isolation performance. Wheel-rail dynamic indicators, including lateral wheel-rail forces, derailment coefficients, wheel load reduction rates, and car-body accelerations are used to evaluate train operational performance on the optimized seismic-isolation bridge under earthquake excitation, along with the assessment of structural residual displacements. The findings provide a basis for assessing the effectiveness of optimized vibration-reducing measures in enhancing post-earthquake train running safety on extradosed cable-stayed bridges.

title: Effect of artificial intelligence assistance on skull radiograph diagnosis of craniosynostosis
abstract: Diagnosing craniosynostosis from skull radiographs is challenging, often leading to diagnostic delays or overreliance on computed tomography (CT). While ultrasound and MRI reduce radiation exposure, their need for specialized expertise and equipment limits routine triage adoption. In a multireader, multicase paired study, 23 clinicians interpreted 59 independent skull radiograph cases unassisted and subsequently with AI assistance. Using a DBM jackknife multireader multicase analysis that accounted for both reader and case variability, AI assistance significantly improved diagnostic accuracy from 75.0% to 84.7% (difference, 0.097; 95% CI, 0.053–0.141; p = 0.00015), bridging the performance gap between human readers and a standalone AI model (cross-validation mean AUROC 0.975). Improvements were most pronounced among neurosurgery residents, suggesting that AI may reduce diagnostic variability across experience levels. Furthermore, AI markedly improved the accuracy of high-confidence decisions. These findings indicate that AI assistance improves radiograph-based classification accuracy across experience levels. Whether this benefit translates into fewer misdiagnoses, more appropriate referral, or reduced CT utilization requires prospective evaluation.

title: Characterization of depressive symptoms in individuals with spinal cord injury through the Beck Depression Inventory, and their role in recovery
abstract: Depressive symptoms show an increased prevalence in individuals affected by spinal cord injury (SCI), yet their in-depth characterization and association with clinical outcomes remain underexplored. We investigated depressive symptoms, operationalized through the items in the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), in a longitudinal, observational study of 165 individuals with SCI, and explored their trajectories and association with neurological and functional recovery. 134 and 43 individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD) diagnosis from two reference cohorts were investigated to evaluate similarities and differences of the clinical manifestation of depression. At baseline (one month after injury), 25% of individuals with SCI showed a clinically relevant degree of overall depressive symptoms, and 21% at follow-up (six or twelve months after injury). Predominant depressive symptoms involved physical-somatic phenomena such as sleep disturbances, fatigue, changes in eating habits, and reduced libido. In contrast, individuals with MDD diagnosis exhibited a broader range of symptoms, particularly those related to self-rejection and self-blame. A development of a clinically relevant degree of overall depressive symptoms from the baseline to the follow-up stage in individuals with SCI was primarily reflected in increases in BDI scores for items related to self-hatred, anhedonia, emotional overload, or cognitive stress. A random forest (RF) model using psychiatric, SCI-specific, and demographic baseline features to predict the presence of a clinically relevant degree of overall depressive symptoms at follow-up demonstrated only mediocre predictive performance. In contrast, similar RF models exhibited good performances in predicting neurological and functional recovery following SCI, relying primarily on SCI-specific (rather than psychiatric) baseline features. Depressive symptoms in individuals with SCI appeared to be largely unrelated to neurological and functional recovery and were primarily related to physical-somatic phenomena. This distinguishes them from the broader range of symptoms observed in individuals with MDD diagnosis, which more commonly encompass self-blame, self-hatred, and other cognitive-emotional dimensions. To help reduce the risk of undetected development of a clinically relevant degree of overall depressive symptoms during SCI treatment, it may be useful to focus particularly on cognitive-emotional symptoms, alongside physical-somatic symptoms, which may be affected by the direct consequences of the injury itself.

title: An uncertainty-aware spatial overlay framework for prioritizing conservation planning
abstract: Spatially explicit and uncertainty-aware frameworks for habitat-based conservation planning remain methodologically limited, particularly in data-scarce landscapes. This study developed a novel uncertainty-aware dual-filter spatial overlay framework that operationalizes ensemble inter-model disagreement as an active spatial filter, rather than a residual diagnostic, to delineate priority conservation zones where high habitat suitability and strong model agreement converge. Rheum ribes L., an endangered montane plant species in northeastern Iran, served as a representative case study. Four machine learning algorithms (RF, GBM, ANN, DNN) were calibrated using 11 environmental predictors, including Landsat-derived remote sensing indices and topographic, climatic, and soil variables. Individual predictions were integrated via a TSS-weighted ensemble, which achieved the highest predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.94, TSS = 0.75). Spatial congruence analysis (Schoener’s D, Hellinger’s I) further revealed that tree-based algorithms showed closer spatial alignment with the ensemble (GBM: D = 0.81, I = 0.89; RF: D = 0.73, I = 0.84) than neural network models, indicating systematic differences in niche representation across algorithm families. Spatial uncertainty quantification revealed that ensemble variance carries ecologically meaningful information, with high-suitability habitats consistently associated with low inter-model disagreement. Applying the dual-filter framework delineated 19.2% of the study area as priority habitat zones. The framework provides a reproducible and transferable approach for biodiversity-informed conservation planning across ecosystems and taxa.

title: Terrain attributes and seasonal Sentinel-2 covariates for machine learning-based digital mapping of soil organic carbon fractions in a Himalayan watershed
abstract: Accurate spatial prediction of soil organic carbon (SOC) fractions is crucial for carbon accounting, mitigating climate change and sustainable land management of montane ecosystems. This study used four machine-learning (ML) models viz., Cubist, Random Forest (RF), boosted regression trees (BRT) and weighted k-nearest neighbours (wkNN) as part of a digital soil-mapping (DSM) system in the prediction of SOC, particulate organic carbon (POC), and dissolved organic carbon (DOC) across the Chattergul watershed, Ganderbal district, Kashmir. 157 surface soil samples at a depth of 0–15 cm with three covariate ensembles were studied, the terrain attributes based on SRTM DEM (DEM only), the terrain attributes based on DEM + summer Sentinel-2 spectral indices (DEM + SUM) and DEM + autumn Sentinel-2 indices (DEM + AUT). The values of the SOC were between 1.0% and 4.74% (mean 2.59%, SD 0.96%), and the mean values of POC and DOC were 1,421.21 mg kg − 1 and 20.49 mg kg − 1 respectively. Elevation, topographic position index (TPI), and valley depth were the dominant terrain predictors across all models. Cubist with DEM-only covariates achieved the best SOC prediction (RMSE = 0.73%; rRMSE = 28.2%; R² = 0.58). wkNN produced the most accurate POC predictions across all covariate sets (RMSE = 422 mg kg − 1 ; rRMSE = 29.7%; R 2 = 0.12) and DOC (RMSE = 1.29 mg kg − 1 ; rRMSE = 6.3%; R² = 0.58) across all covariate configurations. Moran’s I tests confirmed no significant spatial autocorrelation of model residuals ( p > 0.05; n = 157). These results demonstrate that terrain covariates alone suffice for SOC fraction mapping in this forest-dominated Himalayan catchment, while multi-temporal satellite imagery complements prediction of soil physico-chemical and biological properties, providing a reproducible and scalable multi-temporal framework for SOC monitoring and carbon-sequestration policy in humid Himalayan catchments.

title: A fairness-aware multi-objective integrated deep learning framework for intelligent tutoring systems
abstract: The advancements of modern artificial intelligence in education (AIEd) systems have greatly improved prediction accuracy and personal pacing. Traditional intelligent tutoring systems have the highest achievable aggregate predictive accuracy, a value that often is rooted in historical biases, mis-represents engagement signals from advantaged learner groups, and leaves vulnerable learner groups out of the picture. To address these challenges, we develop a mathematically robust framework of deep optimization with multiple objectives to ensure equity is maintained and carried forward across the tutoring lifecycle. We propose 5 main components: (i) demographic sensitivity gradient encoding (DSGE) for measures and limits direct demographic influence by computing gradient-level sensitivities of the learning loss with respect to latent demographic embeddings; (ii) counterfactual equity replay networks (CERN) which guided by the DSGE signal, CERN models the learning process through an explicit structural causal model and uses offline counterfactual simulation to quantify fairness-sensitive trajectory differences under stated identification assumptions. (iii) The engage-weighted fairness attention fusion dynamically balances student persistence and fairness risk, in order to not let high-level engagements mask concerns for fairness. (iv) Pareto-adaptive equity-accuracy-engagement optimizer adapts objective weights on the simplex space through a meta-gradient optimization which promotes stable convergence across the competing objectives under the adopted training procedure. In (v) equity-preserving policy distillation and validation, the high-capacity multi-objective model is compressed to a light-weight student model while ensuring that the student model preserves the equity of the multi-objective model when deployed. Our framework is validated using three real-world, publicly available educational datasets viz., EdNet, ASSISTments, and open university learning analytics dataset. Empirical results indicate that our framework achieves up to 67% lower learning gain disparity and 56% greater stability of dispersion in learning-gap distributions, while maintaining learning accuracy within 1.2% of the unconstrained, accuracy-only baselines.

title: On-demand instance-wise adaptation of large language models for radiology report generation
abstract: Radiology report generation (RRG) requires models to transform radiographs into structured and clinically precise findings, yet available radiograph-report datasets are limited and long-tailed. General-domain large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent text but may miss pathology-specific evidence, while conventional supervised fine-tuning requires substantial labeled data and prompt-based few-shot learning does not update parameters for the current case. We study ODAM, an instance-wise test-time adaptation method for RRG. ODAM selects a small training set for each test radiograph using training data selection (TDS), which combines visual feature comparing (VFC) with pathology matching (PM) so that visually similar but clinically different cases are less likely to dominate the selected set. It then updates the LLM on the selected radiograph-report pairs and applies contrastive instance discrimination (CID), where selected and unselected training instances provide positive and negative references. Experiments on two widely used RRG datasets show that ODAM improves natural language generation and clinical efficacy metrics over zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned baselines. We further clarify the boundary of the method, including visually similar but clinically different cases, rare or out-of-distribution findings, and deployment latency constraints.

title: The dynamics of beliefs in social decision-making: insights from intra- and inter-brain neural networks
abstract: Social beliefs are internalized expectations about others’ behaviors and intentions within social systems, shaping how individuals interpret, predict, and respond to interpersonal events. This study aims to examine how the dynamics of social beliefs influence neural activity and inter-brain synchrony within group interactions. To quantitatively assess relational changes, we implemented an iterated 3-player Prisoner’s Dilemma game paradigm, allowing for the observation of group-level behavioral patterns across repeated cooperation and defection scenarios. Participants were repeatedly exposed to cooperative and non-cooperative interactions, during which we observed neurophysiological responses associated with beliefs formation and change. Event-Related Potential analysis was used to assess individual cognitive responses to beliefs shifts, with P300 and N100 components reflecting sensitivity to social feedback. Additionally, intra-brain network analysis revealed changes centered around the parietal region, indicating altered social relationship representations at the individual level. At the group level, inter-brain synchrony significantly declined following beliefs changes, reflecting a disruption in shared intentionality and coordination. These findings suggest that violations of social expectations may induce cognitive instability and reduce neural synchrony in group decision-making contexts, offering new insights into the neural mechanisms underlying dynamic social cognition.

title: A hybrid framework based on quantum genetic algorithm and quantum support vector machine for noise-aware qubit mapping in NISQ systems
abstract: Quantum circuit compilation and qubit mapping represent critical challenges in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices due to limited qubit connectivity and the presence of hardware noise. Conventional heuristic mapping methods often generate suboptimal solutions under realistic noisy execution conditions. This paper proposes a hybrid learning-guided framework that integrates a quantum genetic algorithm (QGA) with a quantum support vector machine (QSVM) for noise-aware qubit mapping optimization in NISQ systems. In the proposed framework, QGA generates diverse candidate mappings, while QSVM-based supervised ranking identifies high-quality mappings using structural and execution-related features. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed mapping selection strategy, a QROC/Q-AUC-based evaluation mechanism is introduced to quantify the decision reliability and ranking capability of the mapping selection process under noisy quantum execution conditions. Extensive experiments on benchmark quantum circuits using noisy simulation environments derived from IBM Quantum hardware models demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces SWAP overhead and circuit depth while improving execution fidelity and the reliability of selecting high-quality mappings compared with conventional heuristic and evolutionary approaches. The results indicate that the integration of evolutionary optimization and quantum machine learning provides an effective solution for noise-aware qubit mapping in NISQ-era quantum compilation.

title: Brain tumor detection in MRI using HAMNET: a hybrid attention mechanism for improved accuracy and computational efficiency
abstract: Accurate and efficient detection of brain lesions from MRI images remains a major challenge in medical imaging, particularly due to the complexity of tissue patterns and the limited availability of labeled data. In this study, three distinct architectures are proposed: (1) HAMNET-based on a novel hybrid attention mechanism (HAM) combining channel, spatial, and self-attention; (2) a CNN-Transformer hybrid; and (3) a self-supervised learning framework based on SimCLR. Experimental results demonstrate that the CNN-Transformer and HAMNET achieve accuracies of 99.47% and 99.69%, and macro F1-scores of 99.43% and 99.68%, respectively, achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art Transformer-based models with substantially lower computational cost. Meanwhile, HAMNET, with only 5.03 million parameters, and the CNN-Transformer model, with 5.3 million parameters, are significantly more computationally efficient than pure Transformer-based models such as ViT (85.8 million parameters), while maintaining comparable classification performance. Furthermore, the SimCLR-based self-supervised framework leverages unlabeled data effectively: linear probing, partial fine-tuning, and full end-to-end fine-tuning achieve accuracies of 85.83%, 91.23%, and 98.93%, demonstrating strong representation transferability. All experiments were conducted on a dataset of 7023 four-class MRI images, split into two separate folders with an 80:20 ratio for training and testing. Overall, this study provides an effective and computationally efficient framework with potential applicability to future clinical MRI analysis.

title: AI-driven predictive modelling of residual stress of HVOF thermal sprayed carbon-based composite coatings using physics-informed neural networks
abstract: The residual stress is an important factor affecting the performance, durability and failure behaviour of High Velocity Oxy-Fuel (HVOF) sprayed based composite coating of carbon. Finite element analysis (FEA) and other conventional numerical methods are computationally demanding and constrained by assumptions, whereas machine learning (ML) models without physical interpretation can be trained entirely on less assumptions and purely using only data. This paper recommends a combined Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) model to predict HVOF thermal sprayed carbon-based composite coatings residual stress distributions. The model incorporates herein governing thermo-mechanical equations, such as heat transfer and elastic plastic deformation as a direct part of the neural network loss. Training and validation are done using experimental and simulated datasets. The suggested PINN model achieves a better accuracy (R 2 > 0.96) and much lower cost of computation than traditional ANN and FEA-driven surrogate models. The model gives a generalizable, scalable method of predictive modelling of coating integrity and optimization of the parameters of HVOF process.

title: Integrating planetary boundaries into energy system optimisation models for absolute environmental sustainability assessment: a methodological framework
abstract: Transforming energy systems to address climate change must avoid shifting burdens to other planetary boundaries. Yet most energy models still focus primarily on greenhouse gas reduction, often neglecting broader life-cycle impacts on critical Earth-system processes. This narrow scope can unintentionally shift environmental pressures from climate to land, materials, or ecosystems, even in scenarios deemed sustainable. To address this gap, we present a modeling framework that integrates prospective life cycle assessment and planetary boundary metrics into a national energy optimisation model. The framework first integrates life-cycle and planetary-boundary metrics into a multi-objective optimisation model, then uses goal programming to characterise the different trade-offs in environmental impacts, and finally applies interpretable machine learning to streamline the overwhelming set of trade-offs into system archetypes. Applied to a 2045 low-carbon scenario for Belgium as a case study, the approach reveals that all near-optimal pathways can meet the climate target but exceed boundaries for ecotoxicity and particulate matter under the most permissive downscaling principle, indicating that decarbonisation alone is insufficient for absolute sustainability. From the near-optimum space exploration and interpretable machine learning, four distinct system configurations emerge—dominated respectively by electrification, hydrogen, renewable power capacity, or mixed strategies—each achieving similar costs yet distinct environmental trade-offs. Future extensions of this work should incorporate dynamic demand changes, and behavioral adaptations to further align energy systems with absolute sustainability targets.

title: Machine learning-based inversion study on creep parameters of surrounding rock in fault rupture zones of super-large section tunnels
abstract: To determine the creep parameters of surrounding rock in the fault fracture zone of a super-large-section tunnel, the admissible ranges of the Burgers-model creep parameters were first established, after which a FLAC3D numerical model was developed to simulate the construction process of a super-large-section tunnel crossing the fault fracture zone. Fifty learning samples were generated through an orthogonal experimental design, and the corresponding surrounding-rock displacements at the monitoring section were obtained by numerical analysis. Sensitivity analysis was then performed to rank the sensitivities of the creep parameters. Comparative evaluation of Bald Eagle Search-Extreme Learning Machine (BES-ELM), Grey Wolf Optimizer-Extreme Learning Machine (GWO-ELM), and Sparrow Search Algorithm-Extreme Learning Machine (SSA-ELM) indicated that although GWO showed strong performance in fitness optimization, its generalization ability on the prediction set was relatively weak, whereas SSA was competitive in predicting certain parameters. Considering both the parameter-level evaluation indices and the forward-validation results of monitored-section displacements, BES-ELM showed the most favorable case-specific consistency among the three compared models under the present dataset, monitoring section, and 30-day validation period. The creep parameters inverted by BES-ELM can be used as a recommended parameter set for time-dependent stability evaluation at the investigated section and may provide an initial reference for adjacent sections within the same fault-fracture zone under comparable geological and construction conditions.

title: CLAIRE: a CNN–LSTM framework with adaptive and iterative refinement for multimodal emotion recognition
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in Deep Learning and bio signal processing have encouraged researchers to model human–computer interaction with greater accuracy. Emotion recognition is critical in facilitating the understanding and reaction of machines to the affective states of human beings. Many emotion recognition approaches have been suggested to identify emotions based on unimodal features. However, the use of unimodal features alone has resulted in more misclassification errors due to the presence of overlapping patterns among similar emotions. Although determining emotions in multimodal signal provides a higher recognition rate, it remains a challenging task. To address this challenge, this study proposes CLAIRE (CNN–LSTM with Adaptive and Iterative Refinement), a representation-level multimodal emotion recognition framework that independently learns modality-specific features from speech, EEG, and ECG using dedicated CNN–LSTM branches. Instead of performing direct sample-level fusion, the learned latent representations are projected into a shared embedding space and integrated through an adaptive fusion strategy for robust emotion classification. Furthermore, an Adaptive Grid Search Refinement (AGSR) algorithm is introduced to optimize the network hyperparameters efficiently while reducing computational overhead. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves an overall emotion recognition accuracy of 97.2%, outperforming the considered baseline methods while exhibiting improved robustness and computational efficiency. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of representation-level fusion for heterogeneous emotion datasets and highlight the potential of the proposed framework for affective computing applications.

title: Assessment of ChatGPT responses to nutrition queries of patients with inflammatory bowel disease
abstract: Considering the critical role of diet in the management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), patients with IBD often seek nutrition-related information from various sources. With the increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots across multiple fields, their use as a source of patient educational material has also expanded. However, the readability, accuracy, and comprehensibility of data provided by AI chatbots have not yet been fully established. Therefore, this study was conducted to evaluate the readability, scientific accuracy, and comprehensibility of AI-generated responses to the nutritional queries of patients with IBD. Twenty frequently asked questions about nutrition and IBD were retrieved from Google and were posed to Chat Generative Pretrained Transformer (ChatGPT), version 3.5. The readability of ChatGPT-generated responses was assessed using three validated measures: Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES), the Flesch Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), and the Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG). Scientific accuracy and comprehensibility were evaluated by nine nutritionists and dietitians specializing in IBD. Regarding readability, ChatGPT-generated responses were difficult to read, with FRES = 44.54, FKGL = 11.6, and SMOG = 13.8. Additionally, ChatGPT-generated responses to patient questions were generally scientifically accurate (mean score = 4.2 ± 0.5) and comprehensible (mean score 4.3 ± 0.6). However, both scientific accuracy and comprehensibility decreased when questions became more technical and complex. Overall, the assessment of AI-generated responses demonstrated low readability. However, in terms of scientific accuracy and comprehensibility, the AI chatbot provided relatively accurate and understandable information regarding the nutritional information needs of patients with IBD. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: A hybrid feature fusion framework integrating HSM-CNN and GLCM-SVM for real-time mango grading
abstract: Mango grading in post-harvest supply chains has traditionally relied on manual inspection, a process prone to subjectivity, inconsistency, and economic inefficiency. Automated quality assessment offers a compelling alternative, yet existing systems often lack the multi-dimensional feature integration necessary to replicate the nuanced judgements of experienced graders. This study presents a hybrid computational framework that fuses deep learning with handcrafted image analysis to achieve accurate, interpretable, and real-time mango grading aligned with established AGMARK quality standards. The framework simultaneously evaluates shape regularity, surface texture, and chromatic properties extracted from multiple colour spaces, combining a Hierarchical Shape Morphology Convolutional Neural Network model with a Grey-Level Co-occurrence Matrix Support Vector Machine classifier through a calibrated weighted fusion mechanism. Trained and evaluated on 1,800 mango images spanning four quality grades, the system achieved an overall classification accuracy of 96.8%, a macro F1-score of 0.967, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.991, surpassing standalone deep learning and traditional machine learning baselines by meaningful margins. Each image was processed in 42 ms on an embedded GPU platform, demonstrating suitability for deployment on industrial conveyor systems without sacrificing throughput. These results indicate that integrating morphological and textural handcrafted features with learned deep representations produces a more robust and generalisable grading system than either approach alone. Beyond mango assessment, the proposed fusion methodology offers a transferable blueprint for automated quality inspection across a broader range of horticultural produce, with the potential to reduce post-harvest losses, standardise grading practices, and support more efficient agricultural supply chains globally.

title: PSO-GA-BPNN optimization, physicochemical characterization, and molecular docking reveal the antioxidant potential of persimmon leaf polysaccharides
abstract: Persimmon leaves, as a functional food and traditional Chinese medicine, have long been used in China. However, few studies on the optimal extraction and antioxidant evaluation of polysaccharides from persimmon leaves have been reported. Thus, the optimization of the enzyme-assisted ultrasonic extraction (EAUE) of persimmon leaf polysaccharides (PLPs) was investigated using a hybrid back-propagation neural network combined with a particle swarm optimization and genetic algorithm (PSO-GA-BPNN) model, with the response surface methodology (RSM) as a comparison in this study. The results revealed that the optimal EAUE conditions for the PSO-GA-BPNN were as follows: an enzyme concentration of 50.0 mL/g, ultrasonication temperature of 67 °C, ultrasonication time of 60 min, a liquid-to-material ratio of 20 mL/g, and ultrasonication power of 350 W. Under these parameters, the polysaccharide extraction yield was 12.11%, which was better than the 10.23% yield optimized by RSM. The PLPs were characterized as homogeneous polysaccharides (Mw 126.5 kDa, Mw/Mn 1.23) with a random coil conformation, and were composed mainly of arabinose (31.79%), galactose (30.66%), and galacturonic acid (12.82%). Based on the structural features of the PLPs, five characteristic oligosaccharide fragments were constructed to represent local structural units for molecular docking. Network pharmacology revealed MAPK3, TNF, and IL6 as key oxidative stress targets. All five oligosaccharide fragments could dock into the active pockets of these targets, and their binding regions largely overlapped with those of quercetin. Fragment_A (GalAα1-2Rha) showed binding energies closest to those of quercetin, likely because of electrostatic interactions from its carboxyl group and spatial complementarity from its bent conformation. In the antioxidant activity assays, PLPs showed DPPH and hydroxyl radical scavenging activities. These findings suggest that the PSO-GA-BPNN is effective for optimizing PLP extraction, and that Fragment_A may be a key structural unit.

title: IbnSinaNet: a hybrid CSPDenseNet and squeeze attention under the supervision of group CNNs for automatic segmentation of MS lesions in MRI
abstract: Diagnosing Multiple Sclerosis (MS) relies on identifying brain plaques via Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and observing clinical symptoms. Given the morphological similarity between the MS lesions and normal brain tissue, as well as the limitations of the naked eye to detect subtle changes in plaque volume or number over time, the implementation of advanced, intelligent detection systems is essential. This study proposes IbnSinaNet, a deep learning framework for automatic MS lesion segmentation. The proposed network consists of three main blocks, including the Transition Down block, DenseNet, and Squeeze Attention under the supervision of the Group Convolutional Neural Network (G-CNNs). The Transition Down block is used for the augmentation of abstract features through the extraction of high-level features. The DenseNet Block is used with Cross Stage Partial Network (CSPNet) in the encoder and without CSPNet in the decoder. Incorporating CSPNet into the encoder significantly reduces the computational cost. Additionally, G-CNNs were employed to enhance the processing speed by considering the independence of input images. We designed the Squeeze Attention block to enhance pixel aggregation, thereby improving dense predictions and pixel-group attention. This led to the establishment of a novel architectural framework, termed IbnSinaNet. We used the widely recognized ISBI 2015 dataset acquired from MS patients to validate the proposed method. Our proposed method has achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of 86.93%, reflecting an improvement of 2.93% over the state-of-the-art MS diagnosis methods. These findings highlight the potential of IbnSinaNet as a robust and precise solution for automatic MS lesion segmentation in MRI, with promising implications for advancing clinical decision support and enhancing patient care. The code is available at https://github.com/MahshidDehghanpour/IbnSinaNet .

title: LSTM-RNN based PV sources integration with CC–CV charging for sustainable electric mobility
abstract: The growing adoption of Photo Voltaic (PV) powered Electric Vehicle (EV) charging systems are hindered by solar intermittency and the absence of coordinated forecasting-driven charging strategies. Existing methods often decouple PV generation from EV demand or rely on static scheduling, leading to suboptimal energy utilization and increased grid reliance. Additionally, thermal effects influencing PV output remain underexplored. This study proposes a data-driven framework that integrates Long Short Term Memory–Recurrent Neural Network (LSTM–RNN) based surplus solar forecasting with adaptive EV charging coordination for a 300 kW rooftop PV system in Kundrathur, Chennai, India. The model predicts surplus PV energy at 30-minute intervals using time-series inputs such as irradiance, temperature, load demand, and state of charge. These forecasts guide dynamic scheduling of slow and Direct Current (DC) fast charging under a Constant Current–Constant Voltage (CC–CV) protocol. Validated using real operational data, the model achieves a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 2.421%, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 24.65 kWh, and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 16.85 kWh, demonstrating short-term forecasting accuracy. The system delivers a daily surplus energy of 588.97 kWh, supporting approximately 18 EVs (32 kWh battery) or 14 EVs (40 kWh battery), eliminating grid dependency during peak solar periods. DC fast charging reduces charging time from 5 h to 2 h, while controlled constant voltage tapering and thermal management ensure safe battery operation. Furthermore, each EV charged solely using solar energy avoids approximately 28 kg of CO₂ emissions, aligning with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and 13 (Climate Action). Overall, the framework demonstrates that integrating solar forecasting with thermally aware adaptive charging enhances renewable energy utilization in EV charging systems, while highlighting the need for future improvements under variable conditions.

title: Interpretable rehabilitation-oriented motion anomaly detection using wearable sensor data
abstract: Accurate detection of motion anomalies during physical rehabilitation is important for patient safety and recovery monitoring. Traditional assessment methods rely on visual observation. This often leads to subjective and inconsistent evaluations. To address this limitation, we propose a Support Vector-Guided Decomposition (SVGD) framework for semi-supervised rehabilitation-oriented motion anomaly detection using wearable sensor data. The framework integrates low-rank and sparse matrix decomposition with margin-based discriminative learning. Multi-sensor motion signals are processed through sequential layers of preprocessing, feature extraction, decomposition, and anomaly scoring. This design enables separation of structured rehabilitation-like movements from irregular deviations and compensatory behaviors. The framework was evaluated using structured rehabilitation-like motion data with controlled perturbation-based anomaly generation under the Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) validation protocol. This provides a systematic proxy evaluation in the absence of clinically annotated rehabilitation datasets. The proposed approach achieves strong performance, with a Precision of 0.97, Recall of 0.96, F1-score of 0.965, and AUC of 0.98. These results outperform both classical and deep learning baselines. The findings demonstrate that SVGD is robust, interpretable, and computationally efficient. The framework performs well even with limited labeled data. These results highlight the potential of SVGD for rehabilitation-oriented motion anomaly detection using wearable sensor data. Validation on clinically annotated rehabilitation datasets will be considered in future work.

title: Integrating machine learning and artificial neural networks for dynamic analysis of a fractional order smoking-induced lungs cancer model
abstract: This study introduces a fractional-order framework for modeling the progression of smoking behavior and its relationship to cancer onset. The population is stratified into seven compartments: susceptible, exposed, chronic carriers, active smokers without intervention, smokers under treatment, cancer-diagnosed and recovered individuals. By employing the Caputo fractional derivative, the model inherently captures memory effects, reflecting cumulative smoking exposure and delayed cancer progression. A rigorous theoretical analysis establishes positivity, boundedness, existence and uniqueness of solutions, ensuring biological realism. The basic reproduction number \(\mathcal {R}_0\) is derived using the next-generation matrix and equilibrium and stability analyses identify thresholds for disease persistence or elimination. The system is solved numerically via the Adams–Bashforth–Moulton scheme. Additionally, a surrogate model based on a Levenberg-Marquardt backpropagation neural network is developed to estimate the behavior of each compartment. Machine learning tools, including Support Vector Machines and Random Forest classifiers, are applied to assess the surrogate’s performance. This combination of fractional calculus, dynamical systems theory and neural-network approximation illustrates the feasibility of using hybrid computational strategies for analyzing smoking-cancer interactions.

title: The impact of vibe coding on students’ programming self-efficacy and attitudes toward artificial intelligence
abstract: Vibe Coding is a generative AI–based programming approach that may support novice learners who lack confidence in their programming abilities, particularly given the cognitive demands of traditional coding. This study examined the impact of a Vibe Coding intervention on students’ programming self-efficacy and attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI). Employing a single-group pretest–posttest quasi-experimental design, 50 undergraduate students participated in a four-week intervention involving natural-language–mediated AI-assisted programming using GitHub Copilot. Data were collected using the Computer Programming Self-Efficacy Scale (CPSES) and the General Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence Scale (GAAIS). Results indicated a significant increase in programming self-efficacy following the intervention ( p < .001, d = 0.93). Subscale analyses showed significant improvements in both simple ( p < .001, d = 0.54) and complex programming tasks ( p < .001, d = 0.90). No significant change was observed in students’ attitudes toward AI; both positive ( d = 0.20) and negative ( d = 0.28) attitude subscales showed small effect sizes. These findings suggest that participation in a natural-language–based AI coding environment was associated with short-term improvements in programming self-efficacy within the four-week intervention period, while short-term changes in attitudes toward AI were limited. This study contributes to the growing field of generative AI–based learning by highlighting the potential pedagogical relevance of Vibe Coding for programming self-efficacy. The large effect size ( d = 0.93) indicates a substantial within-sample change in perceived competence.

title: Multi-label arrhythmia classification from Holter scatter plots using deep learning and clinically oriented thresholds
abstract: Automated analysis of long-term Holter recordings is important for efficient arrhythmia screening, but most deep learning approaches rely on raw electrocardiographic waveforms. Heart-rate scatter plots provide a compact visual representation of rhythm dynamics and may support image-based preliminary screening. In this retrospective single-centre study, we developed a deep learning framework for multi-label arrhythmia classification from Holter scatter plot images and evaluated clinically oriented label-specific thresholding. Six hundred de-identified patients, with one Holter record per patient, were included. Expert-reviewed rhythm conclusions were mapped to 15 rhythm labels for model development and evaluation. ResNet18-based models were trained using predefined scatter plot crops. The primary dual-branch model trained with weighted binary cross-entropy achieved macro-F1 = 0.738 (95% CI, 0.666–0.774), micro-F1 = 0.808 (0.777–0.838), macro-AUROC = 0.919 (0.895–0.941) and macro-AUPRC = 0.805 (0.758–0.858) using a fixed threshold of 0.5. Clinically oriented thresholds increased mean specificity from 0.844 (0.822–0.865) to 0.885 (0.860–0.909), but reduced macro-F1 to 0.693 (0.628–0.726). Strong discrimination was observed for atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, premature atrial contraction and premature ventricular contraction. These findings suggest that scatter plot-based deep learning may provide an efficient preliminary screening approach for Holter analysis, although multicentre external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Transfer learning approaches for fatigue life prediction of PVD-coated electro-conductive textiles with limited data
abstract: The reliability of flexible electro-conductive layers is a critical factor in the development of smart textiles (textronics). However, experimentally determining their fatigue life is a time-consuming and expensive process. This paper proposes the use of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent networks in a “many-to-one” configuration, utilizing Transfer Learning and Few-Shot adaptation techniques. The model was trained and tested on silver (Ag) and gold (Au) samples deposited via Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) onto composite textile substrates (Cordura and Membrane), utilizing experimental data from prior research. To address the challenge of limited experimental data availability, we applied a Deep Learning framework capable of extrapolating non-linear resistance trajectories based on short measurement histories and signal derivatives (degradation velocity and acceleration). The analysis revealed that the type of metal used is the decisive factor for model transferability, while the mechanical properties of the textile substrate are of secondary importance. The results indicate that transfer learning can provide accurate resistance-trajectory forecasts for selected source–target configurations, particularly when their degradation dynamics are sufficiently similar. However, the method performed poorly for Membrane-Au, demonstrating that severe degradation-timescale mismatch can prevent successful transfer. The proposed methodology can enable effective life-cycle estimation of textronic materials at the early stage of operation, significantly reducing the need for prolonged destructive testing.

title: Experimental and machine learning-guided optimization of tensile strength of concrete incorporating silica fume, waste foundry sand, and polypropylene fibers
abstract: Concrete has inherently low tensile strength, which restricts the performance and durability of a concrete structure. This study investigates the effect of Silica Fume (SF), Waste Foundry Sand (WFS), and Polypropylene Fiber (PPF) on Split Tensile Strength (TS) of M40 grade concrete. Experimental mixes were formulated by systematically replacing the SF with WFS (5–40%) and the WFS with PPF (0.5–2%) and cylindrical specimens were cast and cured under controlled conditions for 3–90 days. The results presented that the WFS (30%) and SF (15%) mixes had 90-day tensile strengths of 5.65 MPa and 6.11 MPa, respectively, with 10.6% and 8.0% increase compared with control, and the mix having ternary composition with PPF (1.0%) had the highest tensile strength of 6.11 MPa, which was 5.2% greater than the binary mix of SF and WFS. Machine learning Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) models were developed to predict tensile strength based on material proportions, curing period (CP), and temperature (TEMP). The optimized SVM model showed the highest accuracy (R 2 = 0.9871), root mean square error (RMSE) (0.1097 MPa), mean absolute error MAE (0.0724 MPa), and standard deviation ratio (RSR) (0.1135), The SHAP analysis showed that temperature (45%) and curing period (24%) were the most important factors, followed by WFS, Natural fine aggregate (NFA), PPF, SF, and cement (C). The study confirms the effectiveness of the application of SF, WFS and PPF to produce sustainable, high-performance concrete and offers a reliable basis for the design of mixes with improved tensile strength, crack resistance and durability.

title: Integration of principal component analysis and supervised classification for mineral alteration mapping using satellite imagery, Kafta Humera, Ethiopia
abstract: Remote sensing is an important technique for lithological mapping and hydrothermal alteration detection; yet, achieving high classification accuracy remains difficult in complex geological environments. This study addresses the difficulty of delineating lithological units and alteration zones in the Kafta Humera district of Ethiopia, a region within the East African Rift characterized by intricate volcanic and sedimentary formations. The primary objective was to evaluate the integration of Landsat-8 OLI and ASTER multispectral datasets for mapping basaltic rocks, Quaternary deposits, and mineralized zones while comparing the performance of supervised classification algorithms. The methodology involved atmospheric correction (FLAASH), Optimum Index Factor (OIF) analysis, and Selective Principal Component Analysis (SPCA) to reduce data redundancy and enhance spectral signatures. To classify these features, the study compared Maximum Likelihood Classification (MLC) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) methods. Results indicated that MLC outperformed SVM, achieving an overall accuracy of 80% compared to 73.5%. The MLC-derived maps accurately identified significant rock units—including granite, sandstone, and basalt—alongside diagnostic clay, iron oxide, and ferrous oxide minerals. ASTER’s shortwave infrared (SWIR) bands were particularly instrumental in distinguishing argillic, phyllic, and propylitic alteration halos. Furthermore, lineament analysis revealed critical structural conduits for hydrothermal fluids. In conclusion, the integration of PCA and MLC with multi-sensor datasets provides a robust, cost-effective framework for mineral exploration in rift-influenced terrains. To further enhance classification precision in geologically "noisy" environments, the study recommends the future adoption of hyperspectral imagery and advanced machine learning architectures.

title: HSegFormer: hybrid CNN–transformer with stage attention for brain tumor MRI segmentation
abstract: Brain tumor segmentation from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI remains challenging because of heterogeneous tumor appearance and complex boundaries. This study proposes HSegFormer, a hybrid CNN–Transformer architecture that combines convolutional feature extraction with transformer-based contextual modeling, attention-guided decoding, and deep supervision. The model is trained using a combination of binary cross-entropy and Dice losses and evaluated on the BRISC 2025 and Figshare datasets. Experimental results show that transformer-based and hybrid architectures achieve higher IoU and Dice scores than the evaluated CNN-based models. Among the evaluated methods, HSegFormer achieves the highest segmentation performance while maintaining competitive computational efficiency. Ablation studies indicate that stage-wise attention, deep supervision, and the proposed Combo Loss each contribute to the overall performance. These results suggest that integrating convolutional and transformer representations can improve brain tumor segmentation across the evaluated datasets.

title: A comprehensive study of facial expressions in ultra-trail racing
abstract: Numerous studies have linked participation in sporting activities to individual happiness. Advances in deep learning make it possible to analyze facial expressions in large volumes of images, thereby exploring this relationship through the language of the face in terms of observable facial expression patterns that may be associated with positive emotional state in a context-dependent manner. Facial Expression Recognition (FER) outputs can be considered as descriptive observations of facial behavior. It is interesting to notice that the acronym FER is also used in the Computer Vision community for Facial Emotion Recognition. This can cause a critical confusion. In fact, it is necessary to immediately underline that the emotional interpretation of observations of expression is necessarily limited, sometimes ambiguous, possibly culture-specific, and often related to specific situations. This conceptual distinction should be taken into account when attempting to use the FER descriptive outcomes of expression classification as possible clues to inner emotional state. In this paper, we use state-of-the-art FER methods to analyze images of an ultra-trail running event taken by professional photographers. Our results describe the distribution of facial expression categories detected by FER models, showing that the category happiness is among the most frequent across most race conditions, particularly at the finish line. As noted, these findings should be interpreted as observations of facial behavior patterns rather than direct measurements of internal emotional states. In addition, the longitudinal study across multiple editions of the competition allows the exploration of the differences in facial expression patterns observed under distinct contextual conditions.

title: A robust CurvLaneNet-YOLO framework for real-time lane curvature estimation and vehicle detection in intelligent transportation applications
abstract: Current road safety systems face challenges in detecting curved roads and vehicles under varying lighting and weather conditions, leading to lane departure and collision risks. To address this, we propose CurvLaneNet-YOLO, a deep learning framework based on YOLOv8 that simultaneously detects road curvature and vehicles in lanes. The system integrates a parallel polynomial lane detection head into the YOLOv8 architecture, enabling real-time curvature estimation alongside vehicle detection. This research develops an AI-enabled real-time monitoring system to substantially improve road safety. The system makes use of the enhanced capabilities and features of the YOLOv8 model, which involves data preparation, model training, extensive testing, and data augmentation to guarantee model precision. Main goals are estimation of road curvature in real-time, high-performance processing and better assist for the driver. To assess the research, the Cars sample from KITTI dataset on Kaggle, which includes 7,481 images of 640 × 640 resolution, were used. The research achieves an inference latency of 15.4 ± 0.3 ms/image on the test hardware, with mAP@0.5 = 0.9373 and mAP@0.5:0.95 = 0.9217, indicating significant improvements over existing work. This research demonstrates the feasibility of using deep learning techniques for vehicle detection and road curvature estimation in real-time. The results presented in this study show promising potential to integrate into a driver-assistance system, although the data used here is limited to a proof-of-concept validation on the KITTI dataset. The suggested solution is competitive in terms of accuracy and inference time on embedded hardware, providing a potential roadmap for its application in real-world scenarios within the context of intelligent transportation systems.

title: EIF4A1 and YBX3 as stress granule-related screenability biomarkers in osteoarthritis synovial tissue: an integrated transcriptomic and scRNA-seq study
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most prevalent degenerative joint disease, yet its molecular pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Stress granules (SGs) are membraneless organelles that regulate mRNA translation and cell fate under cellular stress. However, the role of stress granule-related genes (SGRGs) in OA has not been systematically investigated. OA synovial-tissue transcriptomic datasets (GSE55235, GSE55457, GSE82107) from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were integrated as the training cohort. GSE12021, an independent OA synovial-tissue dataset, served as the external validation cohort. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using limma, and while weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was used to detect modules correlated with OA-related traits. Candidate genes were defined by overlapping DEGs, WGCNA hub genes, and 464 SGRGs, followed by functional enrichment and protein–protein interaction (PPI) analyses. Four machine learning approaches—random forest (RF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and support vector machine–recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE)—together with maximal clique centrality (MCC) analysis was employed to construct composite models. Single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE216651) were further analyzed to determine cell-type-specific expression patterns. In addition, immune infiltration assessment, competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network construction, transcription factor (TF) prediction, and molecular docking analyses were carried out. Finally, quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) validation was performed using synovial tissue samples from 10 patients with OA and 10 healthy controls. We identified 1165 DEGs and 2857 WGCNA hub genes, yielding 15 candidate SGRGs enriched in Salmonella infection, pentose phosphate, and metabolic pathways. Multi-machine learning composite model identified Eukaryotic Translation Initiation Factor 4A1 (EIF4A1) and Y-box binding protein 3 (YBX3) as key genes with acceptable screening performance (Training set: EIF4A1 = AUC: 0.848, YBX3 = AUC: 0.731; independent validation set: EIF4A1 = AUC: 0.822, YBX3 = AUC: 0.778). Single-cell analysis revealed EIF4A1 downregulation in fibroblasts and YBX3 upregulation in endothelial cells (ECs) during OA. A ceRNA network was constructed, with Forkhead box C1 (FOXC1) and cAMP response element-binding protein 1 (CREB1) identified as shared TFs. Molecular docking confirmed favorable predicted binding interactions for vincristine-EIF4A1 and danazol-YBX3. RT-qPCR validated significant differential expression of both genes in OA tissues. This integrated transcriptomic and single-cell analysis nominates EIF4A1 and YBX3 as SG-related screening biomarker candidates and structurally engageable targets in OA synovial tissue, providing hypotheses for future mechanistic and translational investigation.

title: MSTDualNet: multi-scale state-space dual-branch network for electroencephalography-based motor imagery decoding
abstract: Deep learning has substantially advanced electroencephalography (EEG)-based motor imagery (MI) decoding. However, existing MI-EEG decoding models insufficiently capture temporal dynamics at multiple resolutions, which are important for EEG signals containing transient event-related desynchronization/synchronization (ERD/ERS) changes and sustained rhythmic modulations. To address this issue, we propose MSTDualNet, a dual-branch spatiotemporal framework for within-subject binary MI-EEG decoding. MSTDualNet uses a pyramid multi-scale state-space temporal encoder to model temporal dependencies at different resolutions. A channel-wise spatial Transformer branch captures inter-channel relationships, while a compact multi-level decision module combines prototype-guided classification with an auxiliary temporal convolution branch to enhance feature discriminability. Experiments were conducted on BNCI2014001, BNCI2014002, and BNCI2015001 under the chronological order (CO) and five-fold cross-validation (CV) protocols. MSTDualNet achieved accuracies of 83.81%, 82.07%, and 84.82% under the CO protocol and 87.39%, 83.16%, and 86.12% under the CV protocol, respectively, yielding the highest mean accuracy in all evaluated settings. Compared with DBConformer, a strong structurally related baseline, MSTDualNet improved the average accuracy by 3.02 and 1.80 percentage points under the CO and CV protocols, respectively, while maintaining moderate model complexity. These results highlight the effectiveness of MSTDualNet for within-subject binary MI-EEG decoding and its potential as a multi-scale state-space framework for MI-EEG decoding.

title: Machine learning survival models for colorectal cancer: advantages of random survival forests over classification algorithms
abstract: Colorectal cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, motivating the development of accurate prognostic models. Despite advances in machine learning for survival prediction, a common practice in the literature reformulates time-to-event outcomes as binary variables and applies standard classification algorithms, disregarding censoring and the temporal nature of survival data. In this study, we critically evaluate this practice and argue that it is unnecessary and methodologically concerning, given the availability of machine learning methods specifically designed for survival analysis that properly account for censoring while offering comparable interpretability. Using population-based data from colorectal cancer patients in the state of São Paulo - Brazil , we revisit a recent classification-based study that employed a classification XGBoost model and refit the same data using Random Survival Forests (RSF) under multiple splitting rules. Predictive performance was evaluated using Harrell’s concordance index and the Integrated Brier Score, and interpretability was assessed using SHAP values derived from a scalar risk quantity. RSF achieved stable performance and identified clinically meaningful predictors of mortality, while classification models systematically underestimated survival probabilities, particularly as censoring increased, a pattern confirmed through simulation studies. These findings reinforce the importance of using survival-specific machine learning methods for censored time-to-event data.

title: Self-organizing map–derived regimes as a basis for basin-integrated diagnostics of Baltic Sea hydrographic change (1993–2023)
abstract: The Baltic Sea has experienced substantial hydrographic changes over the past three decades, including warming, increasing deep-water salinity, and intensified vertical stratification. While these changes are well established, their temporal evolution and transitions between distinct hydrographic states remain less well understood. In this study, we use a Self-Organizing Map (SOM), a neural network–based unsupervised classification approach, to assess monthly temperature and salinity profiles from a 1993–2023 physical ocean reanalysis. This approach identifies six distinct hydrographic regimes, representing a progression from colder and fresher to warmer and saltier states, interspersed with transitional phases. The timing of these regimes is consistent with known episodes of major inflow from the North Sea and associated variability in basin-scale exchange. We further quantify changes in internal heat and salt content, vertical stratification strength, and the relative roles of temperature and salinity in shaping density gradients. Results show that, alongside strengthened stratification during the study period, salinity remains the primary control on density structure. However, recent regimes exhibit an increasing thermal contribution to the density gradient relative to earlier years. This pattern indicates a system that remains largely haline-controlled but is becoming increasingly influenced by temperature, with implications for future stratification, vertical mixing, deep-water renewal, and ecosystem functioning in the Baltic Sea.

title: Moisture damage analysis of asphalt mixtures using surface free energy and mix design parameters with ANN modeling
abstract: Moisture exposure reduces the durability of asphalt concrete (AC). While the role of thermodynamic and mix design parameters in AC moisture sensitivity is well known, their complex interactions and influence due to material diversity require further discussion. This study introduces a dual-phase analysis that integrates surface free energy (SFE) parameters with mix design variables and employs artificial neural network (ANN) to capture their nonlinear interactions affecting the initiation and progression of the moisture damage. SFE parameters were measured via universal sorption device and Wilhelmy plate methods. Moisture susceptibility was evaluated using the Hamburg wheel tracking device, extracting stripping inflection point (SIP) and stripping slope. Both developed models achieved acceptable performance criteria, including an R² of approximately 99% and an RMSE of around 0.0006. Results of the sensitivity analysis of the developed models showed that cohesion free energy (CFE), adhesion free energy (AFE), aggregate index, bitumen film thickness, and aggregate specific surface area are directly associated with an increase in the SIP and a decrease in the stripping slope. The opposite relationship was observed for debonding energy. The CFE ranged from 63.5 to 104.0 ergs/cm² and had the most significant positive influence on SIP (sensitivity: 0.468), indicating that using bitumens with higher cohesion resistance can be the most effective approach to delaying the onset of the stripping process. AFE (122.4–162.8 ergs/cm²) had the greatest positive influence on stripping slope (sensitivity: 0.266), indicating that high-adhesion bitumen-aggregate combinations, such as limestone-based mixtures, are most effective at reducing the rate of moisture deterioration.

title: Application of artificial neural networks for prediction modeling and analysis of the thermophysical properties of Fe₃O₄/water ferrofluid using experimental measurement
abstract: The use of nanofluids has attracted significant attention due to their improved thermal performance compared with conventional heat transfer fluids. Because nanoparticles are on the nanometer scale, problems such as channel blockage and severe abrasion can be reduced. Among these, Ferrofluid containing Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles is of particular interest to researchers due to its unique properties, including favorable magnetic properties and environmental friendliness. In this study, an artificial neural network model is developed to predict the thermal behavior of Fe 3 O 4 /Water Ferro-nanofluid, and the effective factors, such as volume fraction (φ = 0.05% to 4.0%) and temperature (T = 24 °C to 50 °C), on thermal conductivity and dynamic viscosity are investigated. The performance of the ANN is validated by comparing the obtained results. The results show that when the \(\:\varphi\:\) changes from \(\:\varphi\:\) = 0.05% to 4.0%, the dynamic viscosity increases from 0 cP to 0.77 cP. The results showed that thermal conductivity increased with increasing nanoparticle concentration, while dynamic viscosity decreased with increasing temperature. In contrast, viscosity increased at higher nanoparticle volume fractions due to stronger particle interactions within the base fluid. The ANN models showed reasonable overall performance in estimating thermal conductivity, with correlation coefficients of 0.98 and errors of 1.56 × 10 − 5 .

title: Electric vehicle charging planning in complex systems considering HARL dynamic pricing
abstract: To address the challenges of spatio-temporal coordination and economic optimization for electric vehicles(EVs) charging infrastructure planning in energy-transportation coupled networks, this paper proposes an integrated planning framework combining Heuristic Accelerated Reinforcement Learning (HARL) dynamic time-of-use (TOU) regulation, a small-world network model and the NSGA-III multi-objective optimization algorithm. First, a closed-loop coupling model of charging demand response and electricity price regulation is established with the electricity price elasticity matrix, which quantifies how peak, flat and valley TOU prices shift EVs charging demand in both time and space. On this basis, a real-time dynamic TOU adjustment mechanism driven by HARL is developed. Second, we leverage the local clustering and long-distance connection properties of small-world networks to optimize the spatial layout of charging stations, balancing charging accessibility and the robustness of the traffic-grid coupled network. Third, the NSGA-III algorithm is adopted to carry out multi-objective collaborative optimization. Numerical comparisons with traditional fixed TOU schemes verify the advantages of the proposed method. The framework cuts peak load at key grid nodes by 14.6%, reduces the total investment of roads, charging stations and distribution network retrofitting by more than 200,000 RMB, and declines the average charging expense of EVs users by around 15%. These numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness and practical superiority of the proposed framework for integrated energy-transportation coupled systems.

title: Earthquake magnitude estimation using an optimized CNN-DNN-GRU model with binary differential evolution and firefly algorithm
abstract: Accurate earthquake magnitude estimation is critical for mitigating seismic hazards; however, the inherently nonlinear and dynamic characteristics of geophysical data present persistent modeling challenges. To address this complexity, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework, CNN-DNN-GRU. This architecture synergizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction, Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) for hierarchical data representation, and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) for capturing long-term temporal dependencies. The framework’s efficacy is further enhanced by integrating Binary Differential Evolution (BDE) for robust feature selection and the Firefly Algorithm (FA) for rigorous hyperparameter tuning. The model was trained and evaluated on a comprehensive tabular dataset comprising 3,500,000 seismic event instances—detailing parameters such as magnitude, depth, and geospatial coordinates—spanning from 1990 to 2023, utilizing a chronological 70%–15%–15% split for training, validation, and independent testing, respectively. Empirical evaluation demonstrates the proposed model’s high predictive accuracy, yielding a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0109, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.1048, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0837, Median Absolute Error (MedAE) of 0.0709, Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 0.0230, and a Coefficient of Determination ( \(R^2\) ) of 0.9918. These findings validate the architecture’s superior generalization capabilities, establishing it as a highly reliable computational tool for a magnitude-estimation component that may support future early-warning-oriented systems when integrated with real-time waveform and station-level data.
