title: Dynamic interplay between cognitive load and teaching presence among university English teachers in generative AI-augmented instruction: a longitudinal mixed-methods study
abstract: University teachers who bring generative AI into the classroom face a double demand: they must manage the mental cost of working with the tool while sustaining the pedagogical presence their students rely on. This study asks how the two are related. Survey data were collected from 186 English teachers at 24 Chinese universities across three waves of a single semester (Weeks 2, 8 and 15), and 28 of these teachers were interviewed once the final wave had closed. Structural equation modeling indicated that extraneous cognitive load was negatively associated with all three teaching presence dimensions, most strongly with facilitating discourse, whereas germane load was positively associated with presence, most clearly with direct instruction. AI proficiency moderated the extraneous-load pathway, flattening it for more proficient teachers, and AI attitude carried a small share of that association. Across the three waves extraneous load fell while germane load and teaching presence rose. The interviews corroborated these patterns for most participants and identified teachers for whom they did not hold, including some who experienced intrinsic demand as productive. Because the design is observational, spans one semester, and relies throughout on self-report, the results describe covariation rather than developmental or causal effect. The study nonetheless extends the Community of Inquiry framework by specifying cognitive antecedents of teaching presence, and offers situated guidance on tool procurement, tiered training and graduated support in Chinese higher education. Full instruments, the coding framework, the analysis code and the de-identified data set are provided at Related files.

title: Clogging risk mapping of cemented paste pipeline transport using a knowledge guided transfer learning framework
abstract: Pipeline blockage is a critical reliability constraint in cemented paste backfill (CPB) transport. Existing machine learning studies mainly predict rheology, pressure drop, deposition velocity, or blockage diagnosis from relatively consistent input sets, but CPB clogging risk mapping often has to use sparse records, heterogeneous labels, and missing operating variables. This study proposes a knowledge guided transfer learning framework for screening transport failure related to clogging. The framework converts available slump and yield stress measurements into a unified flowability index (UFI), combines UFI with solids mass concentration to build an interpretable chart prior, and represents unreported inlet velocity and pipe diameter through latent process priors and Monte Carlo marginalization. Bootstrap samples with jitter provide a pseudo source dataset for pretraining, followed by fine tuning and evaluation on a compiled dataset of 52 records with six positives under the main label definition. The evidence is evaluated through repeated splits containing both classes, LOPO case level analysis, label sensitivity definitions, prior learning ablations, paired baseline comparisons, UFI uncertainty propagation, and process prior sensitivity tests. The resulting risk map integrates sparse field records with explicit prior information and shows plausible increases in screening score at higher solids concentration and poorer flowability, which provides a transparent tool for design screening, diagnostic scenario comparison, and selection of cases requiring closer hydraulic assessment.

title: Learning precise segmentation of neurofibrillary tangles from rapid manual point annotations
abstract: Accumulation of abnormal tau protein into neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) is a pathologic hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD). Accurate detection of NFTs in tissue samples can reveal relationships with clinical, demographic, and genetic features through deep phenotyping. However, expert manual analysis is time-consuming, subject to observer variability, and cannot handle the data amounts generated by modern imaging. We present a scalable, open-source, deep-learning approach to quantify NFT burden in digital whole slide images (WSIs) of post-mortem human brain tissue. To achieve this, we developed a method to generate detailed NFT boundaries directly from single-point-per-NFT annotations. We then trained a semantic segmentation model on 45 annotated 2400 μm by 1200 μm regions of interest (ROIs) selected from 15 unique temporal cortex WSIs of AD cases from three institutions (University of California (UC)-Davis, UC-San Diego, and Columbia University). Segmenting NFTs at the single-pixel level, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic of 0.832 and an F1 of 0.527 (196-fold over random) on a held-out test set of 664 NFTs from 20 ROIs (7 WSIs). We compared this to deep object detection, which achieved comparable but coarser-grained performance that was 60% faster. The segmentation and object detection models correlated well with expert semi-quantitative scores at the whole-slide level (Spearman’s rho ρ = 0.654 ( p = 6.50e-5) and ρ = 0.513 ( p = 3.18e-3), respectively). We openly release this multi-institution deep-learning pipeline to provide detailed NFT spatial distribution and morphology analysis capability at a scale otherwise infeasible by manual assessment.

title: AI-driven circular plastic recycling model based on q-Fractional fuzzy Z-information
abstract: This study focuses on creating an AI-based circular plastic recycling decision-making framework to enhance the sustainability and operational efficiency of plastic waste management systems in a decision-making environment with unknown decision conditions. The proposed recycling facility utilizes artificial intelligence to improve plastic sorting, processing, and resource recovery; and minimize environmental impacts. In order to select the optimal recycling strategies, a multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) framework is presented that is based on the recently developed q-Fractional Fuzzy Z-Numbers (q-FFZNs). To achieve more realistically realistic decision analysis, the proposed model introduces Sugeno-Weber aggregation operators to take into account uncertainty and the reliability of expert evaluations simultaneously. The potential applicability of the proposed framework is illustrated by a case study on an AI based circular plastics recycling plant, where recycling alternatives are assessed based on economic, environmental, energy consumption and process efficiency. For further comparison, the ranking performance of the proposed approach is validated by comparing it with WASPAS method. The outcomes show that the proposed approach based on the q-FFZN framework offers stable and stable rankings and is suitable for dealing with uncertain information and information based on reliability, which helps to find the best recycling strategy. The detailed framework proposed in this work is an efficient decision support tool for sustainable plastic recycling and can be extended to other complex industrial decision-making problems with uncertain information.

title: Baseline-aware monthly PM10 prediction in Istanbul and Ankara: a city-level panel study comparing persistence, AR(1), and random forest models
abstract: Monthly PM 10 prediction was evaluated for Istanbul and Ankara with a 2020 − 2023 city-month panel combining air-quality, meteorological, and traffic-intensity variables. The calendar index comprised 96 city-months, of which 92 had observed PM 10 . Missing PM 10 targets were excluded from scoring. The primary analysis required an observed one-month PM 10 lag; a sensitivity analysis permitted linearly interpolated values only for lag construction. Persistence, city-specific AR(1), and Random Forest models were assessed in five expanding-window rolling-origin folds and a ten-month chronological holdout. Predictive R 2 was calculated as 1 − SSE/SST. In pooled cross-validation, Random Forest achieved RMSE = 6.89 µg/m 3 , MAE = 5.53 µg/m 3 , and R 2 = 0.50; corresponding values were 7.40, 5.68, and 0.43 for AR(1), and 8.65, 6.65, and 0.22 for persistence. In the final holdout, persistence achieved the lowest error (RMSE = 4.57 µg/m 3 ; MAE = 3.71 µg/m 3 ; R 2 = 0.55), followed by Random Forest (5.87, 4.71, and 0.26) and AR(1) (6.20, 5.14, and 0.17). Block-bootstrap intervals supported an AR(1) RMSE reduction in pooled cross-validation; holdout differences from persistence included zero. Model ranking therefore varied between development and final holdout periods, with persistence providing the strongest holdout performance.

title: A novel methodology for predictive modeling of patient outcomes using multi-modal transformer networks and SHAP models
abstract: Precision medicine requires predictive models that can exploit genomic, clinical, imaging and continuously monitored physiological data at the same time, yet most existing models operate on a single modality and behave as black boxes. This paper proposes the Integrated Multi-Modal Contextual Network (IMCN), a predictive modelling framework that combines multi-modal transformer networks for cross-modal fusion, recurrent neural networks with attention for real-time sequential signals, pre-trained autoencoder networks for dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional genomic data, and a context-aware multi-task learning network for personalised risk and treatment predictions. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are integrated to provide global and local feature attributions, so that clinicians can see which genomic markers, clinical variables and contextual factors drive each prediction. Across breast, lung, colorectal, cardiovascular, diabetic and chronic kidney disease cohorts derived from The Cancer Genome Atlas, the framework reports higher AUC, precision, sensitivity, recall and F1-score than the literature-reported benchmarks used for comparison, together with a reduction in false positives. Limitations, including the use of simulated physiological monitoring signals and the absence of independently re-implemented baselines, are stated explicitly.

title: Physics-informed inverse identification and dynamic reconstruction of high-speed gear systems with asymmetric mesh stiffness
abstract: Gear transmission systems are critical components in engineering applications, yet their dynamic modeling under high-speed conditions remains challenging. This study develops a physics-informed learning framework for inverse identification and model diagnosis in nonlinear gear dynamics. Rather than using PINNs only as a parameter-estimation tool, the proposed framework is employed to examine the structural validity of the classical symmetric mesh-stiffness assumption. Benchmark tests first confirm that the PINN can accurately recover effective stiffness and damping parameters. When applied to ADAMS-generated transmission-error data, the identified symmetric stiffness successfully reconstructs the low-speed heavy-load response but exhibits a clear mismatch under the high-speed light-load condition, showing that parameter adjustment within the classical symmetric formulation is insufficient. Additional contact-state information extracted from ADAMS reveals that the low-speed response remains predominantly on a single contact branch, whereas the high-speed light-load response repeatedly switches between the drive-side and coast-side contact branches. This independent contact-state evidence, together with the mechanical nonequivalence of the two tooth flanks, motivates the manual formulation of a bilaterally asymmetric mesh-stiffness model. The proposed model provides a more consistent reconstruction of the high-speed light-load response and demonstrates that direction-dependent stiffness switching can provide an independent source of non-smoothness, including grazing-type transitions in the zero-backlash limit.

title: Drought and flood risk assessment under the IPCC risk framework in an agriculturally dominated tropical river basin, India
abstract: Climate change increases the severity and frequency of water-related hazards in tropical areas, posing significant risks to agriculture as well as the livelihoods of rural communities. The present work advocates an integrated approach to climate-induced risk assessment of agricultural systems in the tropical river basin, specifically the Shilabati River, India. In this work, risk maps were developed using the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) framework by integrating hazard, exposure, and vulnerability indices derived from 34 physiographic, climatic, hydrological, edaphic, and socio-economic indicators. The Random Forest (RF) model was employed to predict flood and drought risk across the study area, while RF-based Mean Decrease Gini analysis identified maximum temperature, relative humidity, drought intensity, soil moisture, elevation, population density, land use, Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), proximity to rivers, and lithology as the most influential factors. The results indicate that 17.64% (407 km²) of the agricultural land is flood-prone, affecting approximately 3.63 lakh people, while 27.02% (623 km²) is drought-prone, impacting about 4.56 lakh people. Overall, 45% of the basin falls within the high agricultural risk category, highlighting the acute vulnerability of small and marginal farmers to climate-induced flood and drought hazards. By integrating multiple hazards (i.e., floods and drought) within a unified framework, this research advances beyond previous approaches on single-hazard studies and provides actionable insights for climate-resilient agricultural planning. The findings directly support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 1 : No Poverty, SDG 2 : Zero Hunger, SDG 13 : Climate Action) by informing targeted adaptation strategies, strengthening food security, and promoting sustainable rural development in hazard-prone areas of the basin.

title: Socioeconomic, treatment, and sociodemographic predictors of health related quality of life among cancer patients in Bangladesh
abstract: Cancer patients in low- and middle-income countries face substantial physical, psychological, and financial challenges that compromise quality of life (QoL). This study assessed socioeconomic barriers, clinical treatment, and sociodemographic predictors of Health-related Quality of Life (HRQoL) among cancer patients in Bangladesh. It was a cross-sectional study that randomly enrolled 278 cancer inpatients from three tertiary hospitals in Dhaka and Chattogram (July–September 2025). Data on sociodemographic status, clinical profiles, and socioeconomic barriers were collected via interviews and medical records. HRQoL was assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and analyzed with a median split of the Global health status score of QoL. Following Boruta feature selection, ten machine learning classifiers were developed using stratified 10-fold cross-validation, with model interpretability achieved via SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Mean QoL global health score was severely compromised (23.73 ± 13.59), with high symptom burden for fatigue (79.94 ± 26.01), pain (71.35 ± 27.86), and financial difficulties (89.41 ± 19.76). Bivariate analyses showed significant QoL associations with income, education, marital status, family type, mode of diagnosis, caregiver support, and treatment financing. In the primary median-split analysis, Boruta confirmed 27 predictors, and Gradient Boosting Machine and CatBoost performed best (accuracy 0.914, 95% CI 0.874–0.944; ROC-AUC 0.939; PR-AUC 0.954), well above the no-information rate of 0.622. SHAP analysis of CatBoost model identified mode of cancer diagnosis, family type, monthly family income, primary caregiver identity, and treatment-cost financing as the most influential predictors. Machine learning found key sociodemographic and socioeconomic determinants of HRQoL, highlighting the need for targeted financial protection, caregiver-centered interventions, patient education, and enhanced palliative care access to reduce inequities in inpatient oncology services.

title: Machine learning-guided discovery of natural anti-inflammatory agents targeting NF-κB p65
abstract: Natural products with anti-inflammatory properties have broad applications in biotechnology and healthcare, including nutraceuticals and therapeutics. Here, we present a machine learning-guided experimental framework to identify natural anti-inflammatory agents targeting NF-κB p65. A large-scale dataset of 179,771 protein-compound IC 50 values was compiled from the Anti-Inflammatory Compounds Database and BindingDB entries associated with inflammation-related pathways. Concatenated features of natural products and protein sequences were used to train multilayer perceptron, random forest, and XGBoost regression models. Among these, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.893, and was applied to predict inhibitory activity of 101 natural products against NF-κB p65, a central transcription factor in inflammatory signaling. Luteolin was predicted to show the strongest inhibitory effect after JSH-23, which served as a positive control. Experimental validation confirmed that luteolin suppressed poly(I:C)-induced p65 activation and reduced expression of NF-κB target genes IL6 , TNF , IL1B , and CXCL8 in human keratinocytes and three-dimensional human epidermal models. Structural analysis using AlphaFold 3 supported luteolin binding to p65 and interference with DNA interaction. Together, these results demonstrate the utility of integrating machine learning with biological assays to accelerate discovery of natural anti-inflammatory agents for biotechnological applications.

title: Identification of equivalent GBM meso-parameters using GA-BP and crack fractal dimension
abstract: Aiming at the low efficiency of traditional trial-and-error parameter assignment in discrete element modeling and the lack of quantitative constraints on crack morphology, this paper proposes a GA-BP-based equivalent meso-parameter identification method that incorporates crack fractal dimension within a Grain-Based Model (GBM) framework. Within the GBM framework, the parallel bond (PB) and smooth joint (SJ) models were integrated to construct a particle system with intra- and inter-granular characteristics. Sensitivity analysis was employed to screen key mesoscopic parameters, and fractal dimension was introduced to quantitatively characterize crack morphology. Furthermore, a GA-BP neural network was developed to map selected macroscopic response indicators and crack fractal dimension to equivalent mesoscopic parameter sets within prescribed parameter ranges. Genetic algorithm was used to optimize initial weights, while ReLU activation function and dynamic strategies were adopted to enhance prediction performance. The results showed that, across five repeated randomized evaluations with 60 independent test records per run, the mean parameter-wise R² values ranged from 0.9563 to 0.9989 and the mean MAPE values ranged from 0.6809% to 9.1012%. Compared with conventional BP, GA-BP increased the aggregate mean R² from 0.9834 to 0.9899 and reduced RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by 35.07%, 41.02%, and 16.44%, respectively. Cross-lithology validation further showed good agreement between simulated and experimental mechanical responses and crack morphology. Equifinality analysis confirmed that similar response vectors may correspond to different mesoscopic parameter combinations; therefore, the identified parameters should be interpreted as model-dependent equivalent solutions within the adopted GBM framework rather than unique physical constants.

title: Feature extraction of new-type urbanization from remote sensing images based on convolutional neural network
abstract: This study uses the Forest, Urban, and Suburban Land Use Dataset (FUSU) to improve the extraction accuracy of urbanization features from ultra-high-resolution remote sensing images. This study also intends to quantify the spatial correlation between these urbanization features and regional economic growth. Under standardized data preprocessing and unified training settings, this study compares four Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models. The models include vanilla CNN, ResNet-18, DenseNet-121 and EfficientNet. Several urbanization indicators are extracted from remote sensing identification outputs. These indicators cover building density, road density, green space ratio and urban expansion rate. Combined with regional economic statistics, three spatial econometric models are adopted for subsequent analysis. The selected models are the spatial lag model, spatial error model and geographically weighted regression model. They are used to explore economic correlations and spatial heterogeneity. Experimental results verify that EfficientNet achieves optimal overall performance across all four data subsets. For the urban subset: accuracy = 0.92, precision = 0.89, recall = 0.91, F1-score = 0.90. For the forest subset: accuracy = 0.93, precision = 0.90, recall = 0.95, F1-score = 0.92. For the suburban subset: accuracy = 0.90, precision = 0.86, recall = 0.89, F1-score = 0.87. For the mixed subset: accuracy = 0.93, precision = 0.90, recall = 0.93, F1-score = 0.91. In regression evaluation, the mean square error (MSE) values of EfficientNet equal 0.030, 0.028, 0.040 and 0.033 for urban, forest, suburban and mixed subsets separately. Their corresponding coefficient of determination (R 2 ) values are 0.93, 0.95, 0.89 and 0.92 in sequence. Spatial econometric analysis shows that building density, road density, green space ratio, urban expansion rate and population density exert significant positive effects on regional gross domestic product (GDP). In conclusion, EfficientNet strikes a favorable trade-off between high classification accuracy and low computational overhead. Integrating this network with spatial econometric models can clarify intricate interactions between spatial urbanization signatures and regional economic development. The proposed framework supplies methodological references for urban layout design and coordinated regional development.

title: Machine learning–guided design of shape memory composite: balancing piezoelectricity and mechanical recovery in PVDF/SMPU/BTO
abstract: PVDF-based multifunctional composites capable of simultaneously delivering piezoelectric energy harvesting and shape memory behavior are highly desirable for next generation flexible electronics, soft robotics and wearable system. In this study a data – driven design approach combining Taguchi L27 design of experiments and machine learning (ML) was employed to optimize Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) /Shape memory polyurethane (SMPU)/ Barium Titanate (BTO) nanocomposite. Structural characterization confirmed that BTO promotes β-phase nucleation and enhance crystallinity, while SMPU improves flexibility and elastic recover. SMPU-rich composites exhibited excellent shape recovery (> 90%), whereas PVDF/BTO-rich formulation delivered high piezoelectric output voltage (up to 12 V), revealing a trade-off between actuation and energy harvesting. An optimized composition (85 wt% PVDF, 5 wt% SMPU, 10 wt% BTO) achieved a balance tensile strength of 21 MPa with multifunctional functional performance. ML models were developed to establish structure-property relationships yielding R 2 = 0.81 for shape recovery and R 2 = 0.75 for output voltage using leave-one-out-cross-validation (LOOCV). Gradient boosting showed higher apparent accuracy for shape recovery (R 2 = 0.96), while ridge regression provided more stable voltage predictions. Feature importance analysis identified SMPU as dominant factor for shape recovery, whereas PVDF and β-phase content governed piezoelectric response. This study demonstrates an integrated experimental –ML framework for optimizing multifunctional polymer composites for advanced flexible device application.

title: Machine learning-based optimization, characterization and CI engine assessment of biodiesel synthesised from waste soybean cooking oil
abstract: Waste cooking oil as a feedstock for biodiesel production is a sustainable choice which resolves the environmental concerns related to its disposal. The present paper focusses on biodiesel production from waste soyabean oil via transesterification using ethanol and potassium hydroxide (KOH) as catalyst. To estimate the yield of biodiesel, Central Composite Design (CCD) technique used adjustments of reaction temperature, catalyst concentration, alcohol-oil ratio, and reaction time. The created response surface model was further optimized by machine learning-inspired metaheuristic algorithms like Dragonfly Algorithm (DA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA). Of these techniques, GOA showed best results, achieving a maximum predicted yield of 80.057%, whereas DA and GA provided 76.384%, and 76.593% respectively. Experimental validation at best conditions (100 °C, 1.3% KOH, 50 min reaction time, and 8:1 alcohol-oil ratio) showed yields between 78.95% and 81.68%, thereby supporting the optimization results. Fatty acid Ethyl esters production was confirmed via FTIR, GC-MS, and NMR techniques and, also. Biodiesel characteristic ester, carbonyl, and hydrocarbon functional groups presence were confirmed. The produced biodiesel was mixed with diesel (B10D90 – B50D50) and were tested in a single-cylinder Kirloskar TV1 compression-ignition (CI) engine. With reference to neat diesel, B20D80 and B30D70 resulted in lower levels of CO emissions, by upto an average of 42–48%, HC emissions by 41–45%, and also higher brake thermal efficiency by 6–11%. At medium to high loads, the specific fuel consumption was further reduced by 8–18% without any need for engine modifications. The findings visibly indicate that a combination of machine learning-assisted optimization and waste cooking oil utilization offers a promising and reliable route for biodiesel production and use in CI engines.

title: Cognitive UAV-driven agro-surveillance framework for predicting crop stress–induced yield loss using spatio-temporal learning and adaptive irrigation control
abstract: Precision agriculture is becoming more and more of a challenge that requires the use of intelligent systems that are able to predict stress and prevent yield loss before it is too late. Traditional methods of agricultural surveillance are predominantly reactive with irrigation demands being based on thresholds or individual yield forecasts models that do not represent the intricate spatio-temporal interactions that exist between crop physiology, soil status, and environmental stresses. Besides, the majority of the current practices do not have an autonomous decision-making approach to preventive intervention which leads to inefficient use of water and slows down the response to stress. This paper suggests a cognitive UAV-assisted agro-surveillance system to predict yield vulnerability caused by crop stress and optimize adaptive irrigation with the help of spatio-temporal deep and reinforcement learning. The framework combines UAV-obtained RGB and multispectral and thermal imagery with measurements of soil sensors and meteorological data obtained with the Crop Health and Environmental Stress Dataset. A new GeoSpatio-TRiNet model is used to acquire long-range spatial relationship, time stress development, and diffusion of stresses across agricultural regions. The model predicts the vulnerability trajectories of the stress instead of the direct yield regression, and this allows early detection of yield risk. Such predictions serve to generate a cognitive environmental state of a Soft ActorCritic (SAC) reinforcement learning agent that autonomously computes zone-based irrigation behaviors to reduce the recurrence of stress at the minimum water usage cost. As shown by the results of the experiment, the proposed framework has a stress forecasting accuracy of 96.3% and performs much better than the traditional machine learning, CNN-based, and transformer-based baselines. The system also decreases the predicted yield vulnerability by 46.6 and enhances water-use efficiency by 41.1 as compared to irrigation strategies based on rules. The results confirm the usefulness of spatio-temporal intelligence with predictive control in terms of effectiveness, and the proposed framework is a scalable and sustainable solution to precision agriculture of the next generation.

title: Triple band Yagi antenna design and performance prediction for next generation (6G) wireless applications using supervised regression models
abstract: This study presents a high-performance Yagi antenna designed for sub-terahertz (sub-THz) and terahertz (THz) wireless communication applications, addressing the growing demands of emerging technologies such as high-resolution imaging, short-range secure communication, sensing, spectroscopy, and next generation 6G systems. Developed on a polyimide substrate with compact dimensions of 53 μm × 47 μm, the proposed antenna achieves exceptional directional radiation characteristics across the targeted frequency bands. Simulation results reveal a maximum gain of 14.9 dB and an outstanding efficiency of 99.65%, highlighting its suitability for advanced high-frequency applications. To ensure reliable performance evaluation, the antenna is analyzed and validated using multiple approaches, including full-wave simulations through CST, HFSS, and Altair FEKO, as well as curve-fitting techniques and an RLC equivalent circuit model. In addition, machine learning techniques are employed to predict antenna efficiency based on extensive simulation datasets, incorporating both neural network models and supervised regression algorithms. Among the evaluated models, Random Forest Regression exhibits superior prediction accuracy compared to other neural network and regression methods. The integration of high gain, near-perfect efficiency, and robust predictive modelling establishes the proposed Yagi antenna as a promising candidate for future sub-THz and THz wireless systems, particularly for 6G communication infrastructure.

title: AI competency, attitudes, and experience as predictors of overall learning interaction via AI integration and creative tasks in GenAI-supported EFL classrooms
abstract: Although generative AI is increasingly integrated into higher education, its impact on student’s learning experience remains unclear. This study examined factors predicting learning interactions in EFL (English as a Foreign Language) contexts, focusing on student’s AI competency, attitudes, and experience. Grounded in constructivist theory and the WEST model (Will, Experience, Skill, and Tools), a questionnaire was administered to 884 students at a Chinese higher vocational college. Structural equation modeling shows that AI integration and involvement in creative tasks directly predict learning interaction, while competency, attitudes, and experience exert indirect effects via these variables. Theoretically, this study provides quantitative evidence that student’s AI-related characteristics may contribute to learning interaction through AI-supported learning practices and creative task involvement. In practice, students can be more active in classroom interactions by adopting AI tools and participating in appropriate creative tasks designed by their teachers. Consequently, teachers play an important role in determining how AI tools are integrated and what types of tasks are assigned to students in the English classroom to support a better interactive learning environment.

title: Climate change based yield production using hybrid deep learning with optimal feature selection
abstract: Accurate agricultural yield prediction under changing climate conditions has become the challenge task due to the increasing variability in environmental factors like temperature fluctuations, irregular rainfall patterns and soil degradation. Traditional statistical and machine learning approaches have issues in capturing the complex nonlinear relationships and temporal dependencies among the climate-driven agricultural data. To address the limitations, this research proposed the novel Climate Change based Yield Production using Hybrid Deep Learning (CY-HDLNet) model with data normalization, optimal feature selection and deep learning based yield prediction. Initially, log transformation is employed to standardize skewed climate data distributions and feature selection is employed using the proposed Chaotic Basketball Team Optimization (CBtO) algorithm that integrates Chebyshev chaotic mapping to enhance global search and avoid local optima. The acquired optimal best feature is then processed using the proposed Recurrent Dual Attention Transformer (RDAT) model with dual attention mechanism to capture both feature-level and temporal dependencies and recurrent unit for improving the sequential learning capability. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly enhances prediction accuracy and convergence speed for climate-resilient agricultural planning and decision-making.

title: A quantum-inspired framework for real-time trust estimation in human–AI interaction: a pilot study
abstract: Trust is a determinant of effective human–AI collaboration, shaping whether users appropriately accept or reject system recommendations. In safety-critical domains, miscalibrated trust can lead to unsafe overrides or uncritical acceptance of erroneous outputs. However, existing trust measurement approaches are often static, rely on subjective self-reports, and struggle to capture dynamic fluctuations during interactions. This study introduces a quantum-inspired computational framework for real-time trust estimation in human–AI teamwork. The model represents trust as a probabilistic state that evolves in response to multiple interaction variables (e.g., sentiment, task progress, response clarity, and accuracy proxies), enabling context-sensitive assessment without assuming fixed linear relationships. We instantiated the framework in a text-based interaction setting and compared model-estimated trust with 349 self-reported trust ratings from 15 participants. The quantum-based estimates closely tracked human trust ratings, with a mean bias of − 0.78 (on a 0–100 scale) and a strong correspondence with self-reported trust ratings. This work demonstrates the feasibility of applying quantum-inspired modeling to real-time trust assessment for human–AI interaction. The framework provides a proof of concept for AI systems that monitor and adapt to evolving user trust in domains such as autonomous driving, clinical decision support, and other high-stakes environments.

title: Microstructure-aware deep learning bridges atomistics to macroscale for shock-to-detonation prediction
abstract: The shock-to-detonation transition in energetic materials is governed by coupled processes at extreme temperatures, pressures, and strain rates spanning Ångstroms to millimeters and femtoseconds to microseconds. Traditional multiscale models fail due to the lack of equilibrium and scale separation across the phenomena involved. We address this grand challenge by directly bridging large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with continuum finite-element (FE) models using MISTnetX, a convolutional deep neural network. Trained on MD simulations of shock propagation through complex microstructures, MISTnetX captures shock–microstructure interactions, hotspot formation, and the transition to deflagration, supplying critical sub-grid information to FE simulations of mechanics, shocks, thermal transport, and chemistry. Applied to a synthetic but realistic nanostructured plastic-bonded RDX composite, MISTnetX enables parameter-free prediction of the full run-to-detonation transition.

title: Sports tourism as a pathway to older adults’ psychological well-being: a dual-pathway model integrating broaden-and-build and social identity perspectives
abstract: This study explores how sports tourism is associated with older adults’ eudaimonic well-being through dual psychological mechanisms. Drawing on Broaden-and-Build Theory and Social Identity Theory, the research examines an emotion pathway in which positive emotions and sense of physical challenge achievement are linked to psychological resources, and an identity pathway in which sports group identification is linked to positive age identity. Survey data from 467 older Chinese sports tourism participants were analyzed using PLS-SEM and artificial neural network analysis. PLS-SEM results provide support for both pathways, while neural network sensitivity analysis further reveals that sense of physical challenge achievement is the most important predictor of psychological resource accumulation, and psychological resources showed greater importance in predicting well-being than positive age identity. Peer social support showed significant moderating effects on the achievement-to-resources and identification-to-age-identity relationships.

title: An explainable Deep Q-learning and convolutional neural network framework for rice leaf disease detection
authors: K. V. S. S. Rama Krishna
abstract: Rice leaf diseases pose a significant threat to global food security by reducing crop productivity and causing substantial economic losses. The traditional diagnosis method is manual method, which is low in efficiency, subjective and not suitable for large-scale agricultural monitoring. Despite the advances in automated disease detection using deep learning methods like CNNs, GANs, and transfer learning models, these techniques remain highly computational, not very flexible, and struggle to perform well in different imaging scenarios. Considering these drawbacks, this paper introduces an Explainable Deep Q-Learning based CNN framework which employs CNN-based feature extraction and Deep Q-learning-based adaptive policy optimization for rice leaf disease classification. The proposed model continuously refines the classification actions through reward-based learning, which makes the model more robust in various agricultural imaging environments, in contrast to traditional supervised CNN models that have static classification decisions. The proposed model achieved 98.5% accuracy, 98.52% precision, 98.50% recall, and a 98.51% F1-score, outperforming existing CNN, GAN, reinforcement learning, and transformer-based methods. It also offers a high computational efficiency of 14.2 GFLOPs, 248 MB memory consumption, ~ 48 min of training time, and 6.8 ms inference time per image suitable for resource constrained applications in agriculture. The results demonstrate the effectiveness, scalability, and practical applicability of the proposed framework. The proposed framework performs well on benchmark datasets but more research in the deployment of the edge-devices under different real-world agricultural settings will be investigated in future work.

title: Volumetric reference data of the orbit: a deep learning MRI analysis in the German national cohort
abstract: Manual segmentation of orbital magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is labor-intensive, hindering large-scale morphometric studies. To overcome this, we developed a fully automated deep learning pipeline to segment orbital MRIs and establish age- and sex-stratified normative reference data. We analyzed T1-weighted brain MRIs from 30,868 participants in the population-based German National Cohort (NAKO). After quality control, 28,779 participants (mean age 48.1 years; 44.1% female) were included. The model, validated against expert manual segmentations, accurately extracted 34 volumetric and geometric parameters across 15 orbital structures (Dice Similarity Coefficients: vitreous 0.97, lens 0.89, optic nerve 0.85). Mean [SD] axial length was 23.5 [1.2] mm. Mean [SD] volumes were 34.4 [3.9] cm³ for total orbital contents, 6.3 [0.8] cm³ for the vitreous, and 0.17 [0.03] cm³ for the lens. Males exhibited significantly larger dimensions across all parameters ( p < 0.001). Age-stratified percentile curves revealed continuous age-dependent lens growth (Spearman’s ρ = 0.57 in men, 0.51 in women) alongside modest volume increases in the orbit, optic nerve, and extraocular muscles. This deep learning tool effectively resolved the bottleneck of manual segmentation, providing comprehensive orbital reference data for the German population. This foundation enables future high-throughput epidemiological research into the associations between orbital anatomy, systemic health, and disease.

title: Multidimensional trust perceptions of AI medical conversational agents: framework development and scale validation
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming embedded in everyday life through an expanding range of applications, services, and products. As its potential to improve diagnosis, personalize treatment, and enhance operational efficiency becomes increasingly evident, healthcare is undergoing profound transformation. However, trust and distrust operate as dual mechanisms shaping technology diffusion: trust facilitates adoption, whereas distrust constrains large-scale deployment. Trust therefore remains a persistent barrier to the widespread use of artificial intelligence in healthcare services. At present, empirical evidence on the pathways linking trust and acceptance of AI medical conversational agents (AIMCAs) remains limited. Grounded in trust theory, this study aimed to develop and validate a multidimensional trust-perception scale for AIMCAs, establish its dimensional structure and psychometric quality, and examine its associations with an external acceptance-related behavioral criterion. Methodologically, the study first used grounded-theory-informed abductive qualitative analysis to identify the structure of public trust perceptions of AIMCAs and generated and screened measurement items through expert Q-sorting; independent samples were then used for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, followed by assessments of internal consistency, test-retest reliability and absolute agreement, within-construct indicator convergence, discriminant validity, and criterion-related validity. Parallel analysis and the scree plot jointly supported a five-factor solution. Principal axis factoring with Direct Oblimin oblique rotation yielded a 15-item, five-dimensional structure, with the five common factors explaining 76.07% of the total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis further supported a five-dimensional structure comprising cognitive trust, affective trust, functional trust, human-like trust, and interactional trust; model-fit indices, standardized factor loadings, latent-variable correlations, and residual diagnostics collectively provided evidence for its internal structure. The Fornell-Larcker criterion and bootstrap confidence intervals for HTMT jointly provided evidence for internal discriminant validity among the five AIMCA trust dimensions. An ordinal logit model using actual use frequency as an external behavioral criterion was statistically significant overall, likelihood-ratio χ²(5) = 71.963, p < 0.001, McFadden pseudo-R² = 0.125. Interactional trust showed the strongest association with higher use frequency (OR = 3.096, 95% CI [2.257, 4.246]). The resulting scale captures multidimensional public trust perceptions of AIMCAs and provides a structured measurement basis for research on acceptance-related behavior. The findings support a 15-item, five-dimensional structure comprising cognitive trust, affective trust, functional trust, human-like trust, and interactional trust. An ordinal logit model using self-reported AIMCA use frequency as an external behavioral criterion provided additional criterion-related evidence. The scale can be used to characterize multidimensional public trust perceptions of AIMCAs and provides a structured measurement foundation for subsequent research on acceptance, use intention, continuance intention, and actual use.

title: Condition-based washing decision of high-voltage insulators using leakage current harmonic–phase analysis
abstract: High-voltage insulators operating in contaminated environments are subject to progressive degradation due to the combined effects of pollution and moisture, resulting in increased leakage current and an elevated flashover risk. This paper proposes a physics-informed hybrid harmonic–phase framework for condition-based washing decision-making of polymeric insulators. Unlike conventional approaches that analyze harmonic distortion and voltage–current phase displacement independently, the proposed method integrates these characteristics into unified diagnostic indices that capture the coupled electrodynamic behavior of contaminated insulation surfaces. Experimental investigations were conducted on both new and aged insulators under controlled contamination and humidity conditions. Four hybrid indices were developed by combining harmonic amplitudes with phase information to represent nonlinear discharge activity, surface conductivity variation, and wetting dynamics. These features were evaluated using multiple machine learning models, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, XGBoost, and ensemble learning strategies. The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid indices provide superior discriminative capability compared to conventional features such as total harmonic distortion and individual harmonic components. Ensemble models further improve classification robustness and generalization performance across varying environmental conditions. The proposed framework is computationally efficient, interpretable, and suitable for real-time implementation using low-cost sensing systems. It offers a practical and reliable solution for condition-based maintenance, enabling optimized washing scheduling and improved operational reliability of power systems.

title: Cross-modal consistency gated fusion network for selfie-based body satisfaction prediction
abstract: Accurately predicting users’ satisfaction with their body image in selfies is of significant importance for understanding body perception, preventing psychological issues, and developing personalized health services. To this end, this study proposes an innovative selfie-based body satisfaction prediction model that integrates Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers-Convolutional Neural Network (BERT-CNN). The model aims to achieve more precise inference of psychological states by deeply integrating multimodal information. It employs a dual-branch architecture: the text branch leverages a pre-trained BERT model to extract deep semantic features, capturing sentiment tendencies and self-evaluation in descriptions, while the image branch uses Residual Network-50 (ResNet-50) combined with a channel attention mechanism to focus on key visual cues such as facial expressions and body posture in selfies. A core innovation lies in the cross-modal attention fusion module, which enables fine-grained interaction between text and image features through a bidirectional attention mechanism. An adaptive gating unit dynamically integrates information from both modalities, producing a more discriminative joint representation. Experiments conducted on the Selfit dataset show that the model achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.310 and a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.211 on the test set. When converting predicted values into discrete satisfaction levels for classification tasks, the model attains an accuracy of 83.0% and a weighted F1 score of 0.828, significantly outperforming single-modality approaches and existing state-of-the-art multimodal fusion baselines. This study validates the effectiveness of deep text-image integration for predicting body satisfaction and also offers a methodological reference for multimodal psychological computing. The approach has potential applications in digital mental health assessment and intelligent content understanding.

title: A high-performance deep feature encoding network using GeoFusion-ChangeNet for land cover mapping and change detection in remote sensing imagery
abstract: Remote sensing-based land cover classification and change detection are essential for ensuring environment, planning cities, and managing resources. Accurately extracting spatial and temporal information from high-resolution multi-temporal images remains challenging due to feature inconsistency, class imbalance, and limited integration of spatial–temporal representations in existing methods. Traditional deep learning approaches often fail to capture subtle variations, struggle to generalize across complex and heterogeneous landscapes, leading to reduced accuracy in change detection. To overcome these constraints, this research introduces an advanced deep learning framework, GeoFusion-ChangeNet, for high-resolution land cover mapping and automatic change detection. The proposed model integrates hierarchical convolutional feature encoder with a residual deep feature backbone to effectively capture rich multi-scale spatial features. An attention-based mechanism is included to improve feature representation by concentrating on informative regions while suppressing irrelevant information. Furthermore, a multi-temporal feature fusion method that combines feature concatenation and feature differencing is used to effectively capture temporal variations between input images. The proposed system is also deployed through an interactive interface to enable real-time visualization of classification and change detection results. The experimental results on the SECOND benchmark dataset achieved Accuracy of 95.00%, IoU of 86.00%, F1-Score of 93.00%, and Kappa Coefficient of 84.00%. In addition, cross-dataset evaluation on the LEVIR-CD benchmark achieved Accuracy of 93.12%, F1-Score of 90.61%, IoU of 82.83%, and Kappa Coefficient of 81.47%, indicating that GeoFusion-ChangeNet maintains stable performance under an additional remote sensing change-detection setting.

title: MHA-FusionNet: a pretrained convolutional autoencoder framework for four-class Alzheimer’s disease severity classification from structural MRI
authors: Anto Lourdu Xavier Raj Arockia Selvarathinam
abstract: Accurate and early detection of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) remains a critical challenge due to the heterogeneous nature of structural and clinical disease manifestations. Existing unimodal deep learning methods often fail to capture this heterogeneity, while traditional multimodal fusion strategies rely on static feature concatenation that limits discriminative power. To address these challenges, this study proposes MHA-FusionNet, a multimodal hybrid attention network that integrates structural MRI slices with structured clinical variables for robust AD classification. The framework employs modality-specific encoders, embedding harmonisation layers, and a cross-modal attention mechanism to dynamically weight MRI and clinical contributions. Extensive experiments were conducted using CNN, VGG16, and ResNet50 baselines with and without PCA serving as comparative models against the MRI-based configuration of the proposed architecture. While PCA improved unimodal performance, all baseline architectures plateaued at 80–83% accuracy and AUC values between 0.86 and 0.91. The MRI-based classifier achieved a patient-level accuracy of 91% and an AUC of 0.92, with McNemar’s test confirming the statistical significance of this improvement over every baseline ( p < 0.001 in all cases, Bonferroni-corrected). Ablation analysis confirmed that autoencoder pretraining and data augmentation each contribute significantly to this performance. A parallel clinical-data classifier, evaluated separately since the two datasets could not be patient-paired, achieved 94.4% binary accuracy. These findings demonstrate that a rigorously validated, pretrained MRI classifier can substantially outperform standard transfer-learning baselines on this task; clinical deployment would require external validation on an independent cohort, prospective testing, and comparison against clinician-level diagnostic accuracy, none of which are performed in this study.

title: Hybrid MobileNetV2–vision transformer approach for multi-label classification of chest X-rays
abstract: The precise identification of thoracic disorders using chest X-rays (CXRs) is essential for favorable clinical diagnosis. However, it continues to be difficult because of inter-class similarities and overlapping symptoms. This study introduces a hybrid MobileNetV2–Vision Transformer (ViT) framework for multi-label classification of CXR images into 14 disease categories on NIH CXR14 dataset. MobileNetV2 serves as a lightweight feature extractor to obtain distinctive spatial representations that are tokenized and enhanced with positional encodings. The encoded features were processed via transformer layers, wherein self-attention mechanisms captured long-range interdependence and global contextual relationships. An output layer based on the sigmoid function facilitated the concurrent prediction of various illness labels. The novelty of the proposed work lies in the PSO-tuned hybrid architecture, which adaptively optimizes key hyperparameters of the MobileNetV2–ViT framework to achieve improved accuracy, faster convergence, and enhanced computational efficiency compared to conventional approaches. This implementation uses an economical, GPU-accelerated instance tailored for inference workloads. It is equipped with a single NVIDIA A10G GPU with 24 GB of dedicated GPU memory, and the proposed work is carried out on AWS SageMaker. The experimental assessment employing five-fold cross-validation showed strong performance, with an average accuracy of 94.6%, precision of 88.1%, recall of 85.9%, specificity of 94.17%, and F1-score of 91.1%. Grad-CAM representations increased interpretability by identifying disease-relevant areas. The results underscore the efficacy of the proposed hybrid technique as a dependable instrument for computer-aided diagnosis of thoracic illnesses.

title: Engineering proactive risk fields in mixed-autonomy traffic via anticipatory swarm intelligence: a digital twin perspective
abstract: Ensuring safety and resilience in mixed-autonomy traffic systems presents a critical engineering challenge due to the stochastic nature of human-driven vehicles (HDVs) and complex interactions with connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs). Traditional safety models predominantly rely on reactive post-conflict assessment, lacking the capability for proactive intervention. To address this gap, this study proposes an Anticipatory Risk Field Dynamics (ARFD) framework and develops an Anticipatory Swarm Intelligence (ASI) algorithm for proactive risk engineering. Methodologically, the ARFD framework establishes a novel closed-loop formulation of risk evolution governed by partial differential equations, distinguishing it from static potential models.The ASI algorithm integrates Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) for multi-step trajectory prediction and Distributed Particle Swarm Optimization (DPSO) for decentralized collaborative decision-making, enabling CAVs to actively reshape the spatiotemporal distribution of traffic risk fields. A high-fidelity digital twin platform, calibrated with empirical drone trajectory data and real-world road network topologies, was constructed to validate this methodology. Extensive simulation experiments demonstrate that the ASI strategy reduces high-risk events by 42.8% and improves system resilience by 28% under extreme perturbations, with a marginal efficiency trade-off of only 3.5%. Furthermore, the algorithm exhibits robust performance under realistic communication imperfections. This research provides a robust, empirically validated technical toolkit that transitions traffic safety management from passive prediction to active field engineering, offering actionable insights for sustainable urban mobility infrastructure.

title: The impact of artificial intelligence attention on urban carbon peaking pressure
abstract: Alleviating urban carbon peaking pressure is a central imperative for achieving “dual carbon” goals. Using panel data for 272 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2011 to 2024, this paper examines the association between artificial intelligence (AI) attention and carbon peaking pressure. AI attention is constructed based on the Baidu Index, and carbon peaking pressure is proxied by the fixed-base growth rate of carbon emissions relative to 2010. This study finds a significant negative association between AI attention and urban carbon peaking pressure, and this relationship remains robust across a series of robustness checks. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the estimated negative association is larger in magnitude in central and western cities, high-emission cities, and population-outflow cities. Mechanism analysis provides evidence consistent with the view that entrepreneurial activity, industrial structure upgrading, and energy utilization patterns may serve as important channels linking AI attention to lower carbon peaking pressure. Furthermore, the estimated association is nonlinear: its negative magnitude diminishes as AI attention increases and is strongest at lower levels of attention. Meanwhile, higher local AI attention is associated with a slower growth rate of local carbon emissions and may also be linked to reduced carbon peaking pressure in neighboring cities. These findings contribute to the literature on AI attention and urban carbon governance. Policymakers may therefore consider measures to strengthen the social foundation for intelligent green transition, accelerate the realization of AI’s technological dividends, and establish interregional coordination mechanisms to achieve continuous improvements in carbon peaking performance.

title: Explainable schizophrenia detection using fusion of convolutional neural network and vision transformer from electroencephalogram
abstract: Schizophrenia (SZ) is associated with subtle alterations in neural dynamics that are difficult to capture using conventional electroencephalogram (EEG) features. This study introduces a unified deep learning framework that integrates recurrence plots (RP) with wavelet synchrosqueezed transform (WSST) representations into a single fused image modality and leverages attention-enhanced hybrid convolutional–transformer architectures for subject-level classification. Specifically, we propose RP+WSST image fusion combined with convolutional neural network (CNN)–vision transformer (ViT) hybrids (ResNet-18–ViT and EfficientNet-B0–ViT) to jointly model local spatial patterns and global contextual dependencies. Subject-wise 10-fold cross-validation and a strictly isolated hold-out protocol (70/15/15 split) are employed to prevent subject leakage and provide unbiased performance estimates. Compared with single-backbone CNN and ViT models, the proposed hybrid architecture demonstrates competitive generalization. Interpretability is enhanced using appropriate XAI. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) for the CNN branch and Attention Rollout for the ViT branch. The proposed framework is applied to automated SZ detection from resting-state scalp EEG using two independent databases (Warsaw and Atieh schizophrenia EEG (ASEEG)). On the Warsaw dataset, the ResNet-18–ViT hybrid achieved 82.14% accuracy (AUC 83.58%) using Amor-based WSST features. On the ASEEG dataset, performance reached 95.04% accuracy with AUC values above 95%. Channel-wise analysis identified frontal, temporal, and central electrodes as the most discriminative regions, consistent with known SZ-related electrophysiological abnormalities. These findings demonstrate the practical feasibility of deploying the proposed explainable AI (XAI) framework for reliable EEG-based clinical decision support in psychiatric engineering applications.

title: Machine learning-based prediction of bead geometry in AZ31 magnesium alloy using robotic cold metal transfer WAAM
abstract: This research proposes a machine learning (ML)-assisted framework for bead geometry analysis and optimization in cold metal transfer (CMT)-processed AZ31 magnesium parts. This work aims to predict and validate the bead geometry of single beads using ML techniques. This approach can be used to fabricate thin-walled AZ31 magnesium alloy components via robotic wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM). In this article, the impact of current, voltage, wire-feed rate, and travel speed on bead height, bead width, and contact angle was evaluated through experimental runs. Microstructural analysis revealed a preference for equiaxed grains as the dominant microstructural entities. The increased heat input initiated grain coarsening, while the bead edges exhibited a finer equiaxed structure due to rapid cooling, indicating that the local thermal history is the most significant controlling element. The experimental data were used to develop predictive models using polynomial regression (PR), decision trees (DT), random forests (RF), and gradient boosting regression (GBR). These models predict principal bead characteristics, such as width, height, and contact angle, to determine optimal process conditions that minimize defects and ensure uniformity. From the results, it is observed that the gradient boosting regressor consistently outperformed the other models, achieving coefficient of determination (R²) values of 95.16%, 91.11%, and 89.47% for bead height, width, and contact angle, respectively, along with the lowest mean squared error (MSE) values of 0.0788, 0.1146, and 28.92, respectively. The results demonstrated the effectiveness of the ML methodology in enhancing process stability, improving bead quality, and enabling reproducible manufacturing of AZ31 parts, with far-reaching implications for aerospace, automotive, and biomedical applications.

title: Hyperspectral handwriting analysis for writer verification and ink mismatch detection using a hybrid CNN–LSTM model
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging captures detailed spectral reflectance information over a broad wavelength range, providing capabilities beyond those of conventional RGB imaging. This rich spectral information can be used in forensic document analysis to identify subtle variations in ink composition and handwriting characteristics that cannot be detected using conventional imaging methods. Nevertheless, current research tends to focus on writer analysis and ink discrimination as two distinct tasks, and in many cases, ignores the potential of their combination.This paper proposes a unified spectral–spatial metric-learning framework for hyperspectral handwriting analysis that jointly addresses writer verification and ink mismatch detection through a shared sentence-level embedding space. Each sample is modeled as a three-dimensional hyperspectral cube containing 149 spectral bands, with spatial dimensions standardized during preprocessing. To minimize variability introduced by image acquisition conditions, band-wise normalization is applied. The framework employs a hybrid CNN–LSTM architecture as the feature learning backbone, where convolutional neural networks extract discriminative spatial handwriting characteristics and the LSTM models spectral dependencies across hyperspectral bands. A contrastive learning strategy optimizes the shared embedding space, enabling similarity-based verification through Euclidean distance between learned representations. Comprehensive experiments conducted on a large-scale hyperspectral handwriting dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for both tasks. The results demonstrate that learning a unified spectral–spatial representation within a verification-oriented framework improves representation consistency, enhances generalization to previously unseen writers and ink samples, and highlights the practical applicability of hyperspectral imaging for forensic document analysis.

title: MDFNet: a lightweight multi-stream network tailored for real-time GIS and disaster monitoring applications
abstract: Very high-resolution remote sensing image scene classification (RSSC) is a key enabling technology for geographic information systems (GIS) in disaster prevention, emergency response, and recovery. Current methods often suffer from excessive complexity, restricting their capability to meet the stringent computational efficiency requirements of time-sensitive edge deployment. To address these structural bottlenecks, this paper presents MDFNet, a lightweight multi-stream dual-stage fusion network based on transfer learning. The model uses parallel low-, middle-, and high-level streams to extract hierarchical features, adopts a dual attention mechanism to enhance discriminative regions, and employs multi-source feature aggregation to reduce redundancy. Extensive experiments on AID, UC Merced, and NWPU-RESISC45 datasets demonstrate that MDFNet achieves competitive or superior accuracy with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational costs. This parameter-efficient design provides a foundational accelerated architecture highly tailored for prospective real-time GIS inference and emergency mapping.
