title: Pricing autonomy under global shocks: a parsimonious and empirically validated SVAR-transformer framework for Shanghai crude oil futures market maturity
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic response of Shanghai crude oil futures (INE) to international benchmark price shocks and evaluates the evolution of market maturity from its inception to early 2025. Using weekly data from March 30, 2018, to April 30, 2025, we propose a hybrid modeling framework that integrates a Structural Vector Autoregression (SVAR) with a Transformer architecture. The SVAR component captures linear structural relationships and enables economic interpretation through impulse response and variance decomposition, while the Transformer—specifically its linear attention mechanism—models nonlinear dynamics and extreme event patterns that elude purely linear models. Rather than assuming that the neural component is superior by construction, the framework is evaluated against a conventional VAR/SVAR, a multilayer perceptron (MLP), and a linear-attention-only specification using chronological holdout evaluation, expanding-window validation, ablation tests, and alternative structural identification schemes. The full hybrid specification reduces the out-of-sample RMSE for INE returns by approximately 7.7% relative to VAR(2), while the improvement over the linear-attention-only specification is concentrated in high-volatility weeks. The mean nonlinear contribution ratio is approximately 0.184 in crisis weeks compared with 0.051 in normal weeks. Empirical results reveal a three-stage maturation process: an initial cultivation period (2018–2019) characterized by external-dependent mild fluctuations; an extreme shock period (2020–2022) marked by resonance-driven volatility; and a mature transition period (2023–2025) where internal and external shocks achieve more balanced contributions. The findings indicate that INE has moved toward greater market maturity, with improved but still incomplete pricing autonomy. The unconditional variance decomposition remains close to the conventional SVAR result, whereas the principal incremental contribution of the hybrid model lies in identifying state-dependent nonlinear adjustments during crisis periods. Results remain qualitatively robust under sign restrictions, a long-run restriction, and reverse recursive ordering.

title: Optimized deep learning for cardiovascular disease diagnosis
abstract: The heart plays a key role in the human body, where it helps to deliver oxygen and nutrients by circulating blood all over the body. Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) is the leading cause of increasing mortality rates globally, specifically among the elderly and adults. In recent years, different approaches have been utilized to accurately and timely diagnose CVD to provide timely medical interventions and safeguard patients’ lives. However, these methods encounter difficulties in handling noisy data and extracting meaningful patterns from high-dimensional data. This paper presents an optimization-enabled deep learning model, Exponential weighted Serval Optimization Algorithm Shuffle-Attention Network (Ex-SOA_SA-Net) for the diagnosis of CVD. Initially, median normalization is used to normalize the accumulated input data. Then, the selection of relevant features is performed using Pearson’s Correlation Coefficient (PCC), Relief, and information gain from the normalized data. In addition, the efficacy of Ex-SOA_SA-Net is validated by utilizing different performance indicators. The experimental outcomes show that the Ex-SOA_SA-Net attained high results with an accuracy of 93.469%, True Positive Rate (TPR) of 95.237%, True Negative Rate (TNR) of 91.543%, precision of 97.098%, and an F1-score of 97.960%, respectively.

title: A hybrid metaheuristic optimization and machine learning framework for smart healthcare based cardiovascular disease prediction
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), particularly heart attacks, remain among the most serious global public health challenges, causing millions of deaths annually and imposing substantial pressure on healthcare systems worldwide. Early identification of at-risk individuals is therefore essential for timely intervention and improved clinical outcomes. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for supporting medical decision-making through the analysis of complex clinical and lifestyle data. However, the predictive effectiveness of ML models is often limited by the presence of redundant, irrelevant, or noisy features, which can reduce model accuracy, increase computational complexity, and hinder interpretability. To address these challenges, this study proposed an optimization-driven feature-selection framework to enhance the predictive performance of ML-based heart disease diagnosis systems. The proposed approach systematically integrated metaheuristic optimization algorithms with classical ML classifiers to identify the most informative feature subsets from cardiovascular datasets. Two widely used benchmark datasets, namely the CVD dataset and the Heart Attack dataset, were employed to evaluate the effectiveness of the framework. Six state-of-the-art metaheuristic optimization algorithms were investigated for feature selection, including the Bat Algorithm (BA), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), Jaya Algorithm (JA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Firefly Algorithm (FA), and Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA). The optimized feature subsets were subsequently evaluated using three well-established ML classifiers: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naïve Bayes (NB), and Decision Tree (DT). The experimental results demonstrated that integrating metaheuristic feature selection significantly improved classification performance compared with baseline models trained using the full feature space. Among the evaluated optimization methods, the Jaya Algorithm consistently produced the most effective feature subsets across both datasets and achieved the highest predictive performance. In particular, the JA-based models achieved classification accuracies of up to 98.0% on the CVD dataset and 93.4% on the Heart Attack dataset, outperforming other optimization strategies as well as conventional ML models. To demonstrate practical applicability, the developed predictive model was integrated into a prototype mobile application that enabled preliminary heart risk assessment based on user-provided health information. By combining optimized feature selection, ML-based prediction, and a mobile-enabled healthcare interface, the proposed system provided a scalable and accessible solution for early cardiovascular risk screening. Overall, the study demonstrated that metaheuristic-driven feature optimization can significantly enhance the reliability and accuracy of ML-based cardiovascular disease prediction systems, thereby contributing to the advancement of intelligent diagnostic solutions within the emerging Healthcare 4.0 ecosystem.

title: From aesthetics to authenticity: a stimulus–organism–response model of audience responses to AI-generated intangible cultural heritage design
abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used in heritage visualization, yet its outputs often raise concerns about cultural authenticity. Prior studies have focused more on technical fidelity and symbolic preservation than on how audiences evaluate the authenticity of AI-generated heritage imagery. To address this gap, this study develops and tests a Stimulus-Organism-Response model using AI-generated Wuxi clay figurine images. A randomized between-subjects online experiment with 330 participants examined the associations of visual information quality, AI technical novelty, and symbol salience with perceived aesthetics, perceived authenticity, cultural identity, and acceptance intention. The theory-specified model showed that visual information quality, technical novelty, and symbol salience were positively associated with perceived aesthetics, while perceived aesthetics and symbol salience were positively associated with perceived authenticity. Perceived aesthetics and perceived authenticity were also associated with cultural identity and acceptance intention. However, the HTMT analysis indicated limited discriminant validity, particularly among visual information quality, technical novelty, symbol salience, and perceived aesthetics. A supplementary second-order model representing these four perceptions as facets of an overall perceived design quality factor showed acceptable fit and comparable downstream associations. In this alternative specification, perceived authenticity was no longer independently associated with acceptance intention. Accordingly, the construct-specific path estimates should be interpreted cautiously. Overall, the findings are consistent with the presence of a substantial holistic evaluative component in audience responses to AI-generated heritage imagery.

title: Adaptive federated edge intelligence with semantic communication and trust-aware optimization for heterogeneous IoT networks
abstract: The rapid growth of heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) networks introduces significant challenges in communication efficiency, energy consumption, and reliable distributed intelligence due to diverse device capabilities, dynamic channel conditions, and limited computational resources. Existing bit-level communication and conventional federated learning approaches often suffer from excessive communication overhead, inefficient resource utilization, and unstable model convergence under non-IID data and unreliable device participation. To address these limitations, this paper proposes FEI-SemCom, an adaptive federated edge intelligence framework that integrates semantic communication, federated learning, and joint resource optimization for heterogeneous IoT systems. The proposed framework introduces a heterogeneity-aware semantic encoder, adaptive semantic compression mechanism, semantic contribution-based client selection strategy, and trust-aware aggregation scheme to improve communication efficiency and learning robustness. Unlike existing approaches that optimize communication, learning, and resource allocation independently, FEI-SemCom jointly adapts semantic representation, client participation, transmission parameters, and aggregation weights according to device capability, channel quality, and energy availability. Furthermore, the proposed framework improves resilience under intermittent connectivity conditions by enabling adaptive client participation, reliability-aware aggregation, and resource-aware communication decisions, allowing federated edge intelligence to operate effectively despite temporary link failures and unstable device availability. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves 91.2% accuracy at 5 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), converges within approximately 120 training rounds, and reduces communication overhead, energy consumption, and latency to 45 MB, 48 J, and 110 ms, respectively. Compared with conventional approaches, FEI-SemCom reduces communication overhead by up to 38% while maintaining stable convergence and robust learning performance. These results demonstrate the potential of adaptive semantic communication combined with federated edge intelligence for scalable and resource-efficient IoT applications.

title: Generative AI interaction styles and mental health among college students: a latent profile analysis
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is now widely used by college students, but the mental health implications of different interaction patterns remain unclear. Because GenAI can support task-focused, cognitive, and emotionally salient forms of engagement, engagement quality may be more informative than use intensity alone. We used latent profile analysis to identify human–AI interaction styles among 7,029 Chinese college students from six universities. Five indicators captured use intensity, perceived interaction quality, trust, psychological closeness, and emotional attachment; depressive and anxiety symptoms were assessed as mental health outcomes. Five profiles emerged: Efficient-Instrumental (27.00%), Exploratory-Casual (31.97%), Deep-Emotional (12.18%), Ambivalent-Attached (9.23%), and Detached-Avoidant (19.62%). Profiles differed significantly in depressive and anxiety symptoms. The Ambivalent-Attached profile, characterized by high emotional attachment but low perceived quality and trust, showed the highest symptom levels, with mean depressive symptoms in the moderate range. Symptom differences aligned more closely with relational quality indicators than with use intensity. Random forest and SHAP analyses identified smartphone addiction, neuroticism, conscientiousness, and cognitive reappraisal as the most informative features for classifying profile membership. These findings suggest that university mental health services should consider how students relate to GenAI, not only how often they use it.

title: Comparative predictive modelling of machine learning techniques for network traffic analysis
abstract: Network traffic analysis plays a critical role in intelligent network management by providing insights into communication patterns, resource utilization, and network performance. The increasing complexity and volume of modern network traffic necessitate predictive modelling techniques capable of capturing nonlinear relationships among diverse traffic characteristics. This study presents a comparative predictive modelling framework for network traffic analysis by reformulating the prediction task as a supervised regression problem using the benchmark UNSW-NB15 dataset. Unlike its conventional use for intrusion detection, the dataset is transformed into a model of continuous network traffic metric derived from quantitative flow characteristics, enabling the prediction of traffic behaviour rather than attack classification. Five state-of-the-art machine learning regression algorithms, namely Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest Regression (RFR), XGBoost Regression, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) Regression, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) Regression, are developed and evaluated to investigate their predictive capability for network traffic analysis. The comparative evaluation is performed using multiple regression performance metrics, including Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Relative Accuracy, Tolerance Accuracy, and the coefficient of determination ( \(\:{R}^{2}\) ). The numerical analysis shows that XGBoost demonstrates a higher performance with \(\:{R}^{2}\) of 0.9969, accuracy of 0.9921, closely followed by LightGBM with \(\:{R}^{2}\) of 0.9957 and accuracy of 0.9906. The ensemble model split its weight almost evenly between these two models (47.5% each), achieving R² of 0.9965 and tercile accuracy of 99.12%, competitive with the best single model, indicating high precision and generalization ability and pointing to the stability and applicability of the model in real-world settings.

title: Interpretable spatio-temporal graph neural networks for air quality prediction under real-world multi-station monitoring data
abstract: Air quality forecasting has a crucial place in environmental management, public health safety, and sustainability of urban areas. The dynamic nature of air pollution leads to both spatial relationships between monitoring Stations as well as nonlinear relationships between meteorological and air pollutant Factors at specific times, which complicates accurate prediction. In this research, we present an interpretable Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network (CIST-GNN), which utilizes Graph Attention Networks (GATs) to capture spatial dependencies from the air pollution monitoring stations, Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) to learn temporal patterns in the features of the Time Series Data, and a feature attention mechanism that improves the interpretation of feature contributions. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is evaluated using the actual dataset (i.e., the UCI multi-site air quality measurements from Beijing), consisting of 420,768 observations collected from 12 separate monitoring sites for the years 2013 through 2017. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the CIST-GNN achieves an R 2 score of 93.23%, RMSE of 21.66 μg/m 3 , and MAE of 12.08 μg/m 3 on the test set. The model uses pollutant concentrations and meteorological variables, including PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, SO2, O3, temperature, humidity and wind speed information. In addition, the feature attention mechanism highlights which environmental variables provide interpretable feature importance to the model’s predictions. The proposed framework has additional advantages over GRU (which uses only temporal information), such as dealing with spatial dependence, providing feature attribution, and being robust to different types of spatial monitoring networks. These results demonstrate that the proposed CIST-GNN provides an effective and interpretable framework for air quality forecasting.

title: Driver activity detection and classification using deep learning-based YOLO models for intelligent transportation systems
abstract: Driver distraction is one of the major causes of road traffic accidents worldwide, resulting in significant economic losses, injuries, and fatalities. Intelligent driver monitoring systems have emerged as effective solutions for improving road safety through real-time detection of unsafe driving behaviors. This study proposes a deep learning-based framework for driver activity detection and classification using YOLO object detection architectures. A real-world driver activity dataset containing 5,422 annotated images was collected from drivers under natural driving conditions. The dataset consists of eight driver activity classes, including safe driving, drinking, eating, phoning, operating vehicle components, makeup/hair adjustment, object management, and talking to passengers. Four YOLO models, including YOLOv5s, YOLOv5m, YOLOv5l, and YOLOv8n, were trained using transfer learning and evaluated based on precision, recall, AP, mAP@0.5. The results showed a consistent improvement in detection performance as model complexity increased. YOLOv5s achieved 90.1% precision, 88.7% recall, and 90.0% mAP@0.5, while YOLOv5m improved these values to 91.9%, 90.5%, and 92.5%, respectively. YOLOv5l further increased performance with 93.3% precision, 92.1% recall, and 95.0% mAP@0.5. YOLOv8n achieved the highest accuracy with 96.0% precision, 95.2% recall, and 96.3% mAP@0.5, demonstrating superior detection capability and computational efficiency. The findings indicate that advanced YOLO architectures provide accurate and efficient solutions for real-time driver activity recognition and can significantly contribute to intelligent transportation systems and road safety enhancement.

title: Integrating sentinel-1 SAR and sentinel-2 optical data for crop mapping and flood inundation assessment in agricultural systems
abstract: Precise and timely evaluation of the impacts of flooding on agricultural systems is essential for planning food security strategies and responding to disasters, especially in key crop-producing areas. In this study, an integrated remote sensing approach that uses Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery is proposed to identify crop types and assess the extent of flooding and its impacts on agricultural systems in the prominent agricultural area of the Jianghan Plain, China, specifically in the Jingzhou study area, from 2018 to 2022. Flood inundation mapping during a significant flood event in July 2020 was conducted using dual-polarization (VV and VH) Sentinel-1 C-band SAR data. Flooded regions were extracted using a change-detection approach coupled with histogram-based thresholding (Otsu’s method) of the VV/VH ratio, enabling a clear distinction between floodwater and non-flooded regions, as well as between permanent water bodies and non-flooded regions. The random forest classifier for Sentinel-2 time-series imagery in 2020 achieved an overall accuracy of 92.7% and a Kappa of 0.892. It classified the total agricultural area as 11,442 km², of which rice, wheat, and cotton were grown on areas of 888 km², 384 km², and 43 km², respectively. The study demonstrates the potential of combining optical and SAR data for effective, crop-specific flood monitoring in near real time.

title: Artificial intelligence and environmental sustainability: a nonlinear analysis of the load capacity factor in OECD countries
abstract: Amid the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) and growing concerns over ecological constraints, understanding the environmental consequences of emerging technologies has become increasingly important. This study investigates the nonlinear relationship between AI and environmental sustainability, which is proxied by the Load Capacity Factor (LCF), while considering the moderating effect of trade openness. Based on panel data from OECD countries between 1993 and 2023, the empirical results indicate a significant U-shaped relationship between AI and LCF. Specifically, AI initially reduces LCF but enhances environmental sustainability after exceeding a certain threshold. Moreover, trade openness is shown to flatten the U-shaped curve and shift its turning point. These findings provide meaningful policy insights for integrating digital transformation with sustainable development objectives.

title: CrystalGRW: generative modeling of crystal structures with targeted crystallographic properties via geodesic random walks
abstract: Determining whether a candidate crystalline material is thermodynamically stable depends on identifying its true ground-state structure, a central challenge in computational materials science. We introduce CrystalGRW, a diffusion-based generative model on Riemannian manifolds that proposes candidate crystal configurations in stable phases, validated through density functional theory calculations. Our model is designed for de novo generation , which creates crystal structures together with their compositions. The crystal properties, such as fractional coordinates, atomic types, and lattice matrices, are represented on suitable Riemannian manifolds, ensuring that new predictions generated through the diffusion process preserve the periodicity of crystal structures. We also incorporate an equivariant graph neural network to account for rotational and translational symmetries within the model. CrystalGRW generates crystal structures that are stable and closely resemble their density-functional-theory ground states. The model also supports conditional control, such as enforcing a specified crystallographic point group, thereby accelerating materials discovery and inverse design by providing symmetry-consistent, energetically stable candidate crystals for experimental validation.

title: A battery health state index-driven digital twin framework for battery condition assessment and predictive maintenance in electric vehicle charging environments
abstract: The increasing deployment of electric vehicles (EVs) has intensified the need for intelligent battery monitoring and predictive maintenance solutions capable of ensuring battery reliability, safety, and operational efficiency. Although battery State of Health (SOH) estimation has received considerable research attention, existing approaches primarily focus on degradation assessment while providing limited integration of charging behavior characteristics and maintenance-oriented decision support. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Battery Health State Index (BHSI)-driven digital twin framework for battery condition assessment and risk-aware maintenance prioritization. Laboratory battery cycling data obtained from an Arbin battery testing system were utilized to estimate battery health conditions and develop a normalized BHSI representation. Subsequently, a Digital Twin Score (DTS) was formulated by integrating battery health, energy consumption, and charging power characteristics into a unified assessment metric. Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models were employed to estimate the normalized Battery Health State Index (BHSI) and evaluate the machine learning component of the proposed framework. Experimental results demonstrated that the Random Forest model achieved superior performance, with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.998, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.079, and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.310, outperforming XGBoost. The predicted BHSI values were subsequently integrated with charging behavior characteristics to compute the proposed Digital Twin Score (DTS). Correlation analysis revealed a strong inverse relationship between BHSI and DTS ( r = − 0.788), demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed score in representing battery health and operational characteristics. The analysis of the feature importance of analysis further indicated that battery capacity and energy-related variables were the dominant contributors to BHSI prediction. The developed framework successfully classified charging sessions into low-, medium-, and high-risk categories, enabling maintenance prioritization and operational decision support. Overall, the proposed BHSI–DTS digital twin framework provides an interpretable and effective solution for battery condition assessment and intelligent maintenance support within EV charging environments.

title: DemoGCL: Demographic-augmented graph contrastive learning for cold-start recommendation
abstract: One of the most persistent problems in e-commerce recommendation is what happens when a new user signs up or a new product goes live the system knows almost nothing about them, and graph-based collaborative filtering, which depends entirely on interaction history, produces embeddings that are essentially random. Existing approaches tend to address cold users and cold items as two separate problems, often at the cost of serving-time language model inference that is far too slow for production systems. In this work, we present DemoGCL, a unified Demographic-Augmented Graph Contrastive Learning framework that resolves both cold-start scenarios within a single lightweight model. At its core, DemoGCL builds on a three-layer LightGCN backbone for warm collaborative signal and augments it with two dedicated branches: a two-layer MLP that projects a five-dimensional behavioral proxy vector derived from publicly observable demographic signals into the shared embedding space for cold users who have no purchase history, and a LoRA-adapted DistilBERT encoder (rank 8, 332K trainable out of 66.7M parameters, or 0.50%) that generates cold-item embeddings from product text alone. A sigmoid-gated fusion layer harmonizes the warm and cold representations, and a cross-view InfoNCE objective aligns them during training so that cold embeddings land in the same semantic neighborhood as their warm counterparts. We evaluate on Amazon Beauty, Amazon Clothing, and Epinions under a sampled ranking protocol and find that DemoGCL achieves warm-split NDCG@10 of 0.0612, 0.0487, and 0.0831, cold-user NDCG@10 of 0.0543, 0.0411, and 0.0762 (retaining 88.7%, 84.4%, and 91.7% of warm performance), and cold-item NDCG@10 of 0.0388, 0.0319, and 0.0594. On Amazon Beauty, based on LLMDiRec’s published numbers under its own evaluation setup, DemoGCL improves over LLMDiRec by 0.18% on cold users and 77.2% on cold items, although the evaluation protocols differ. Ablation studies confirm that the demographic branch is the single most critical component, with its removal causing up to a 41.4% drop in cold-user NDCG@10, while dropping LoRA fine-tuning reduces cold-item performance by up to 37.9%. Because warm embeddings are precomputed and cached as lookup tables, the serving path avoids online large-language-model generation and keeps cold-user inference limited to a small projection module, which supports a lightweight deployment structure for e-commerce pipelines.

title: AI-assisted scaffold-based nanobody design identifies Nb01 as a promising pan-variant candidate targeting SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro
abstract: Despite the transition to a post-pandemic phase, SARS-CoV-2 continues to generate genetically diverse variants that challenge existing therapeutic strategies. The 3-chymotrypsin-like protease (3CLpro) is a highly conserved viral enzyme essential for replication, making it an attractive target for variant-agnostic antiviral intervention. Nanobodies offer distinct advantages over conventional antibodies, including small size, high stability, and strong antigen-binding potential, but their rational design remains technically challenging. We developed a scaffold-based, AI-assisted pipeline for nanobody design that integrates large language model-driven generation of complementarity-determining region (CDR) sequences with structure-guided grafting onto a conserved humanized nanobody scaffold. Nanobody structures were predicted using AlphaFold2, and binding performance was evaluated through molecular docking against 3CLpro from multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants. Physicochemical properties and structural stability were assessed using established computational tools. Among the candidates generated, Nb01 consistently showed favorable predicted binding to 3CLpro across major SARS-CoV-2 variants. Compared with benchmark nanobodies (S43, bn03, R14, and 3-2A2-4), Nb01 showed stronger predicted binding performance for Alpha, Gamma, Omicron BA.2, BA.4/5, BF.7, and XBB variants, while maintaining competitive predicted performance across other lineages. Nb01 also exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including low predicted toxicity, acceptable stability, and a profile consistent with potential biophysical suitability. Nb01 represents a promising computationally identified nanobody candidate targeting the conserved SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro. This scaffold-based, AI-assisted design strategy provides a systematic and generalizable computational pipeline for the development of antiviral nanobody candidates with potential broad variant coverage. Further experimental validation will be required to confirm the binding properties and therapeutic relevance of Nb01.

title: Explainable machine learning characterizes temporally structured EEG differences in pragmatic processing between children with autism and typically developing peers
abstract: Pragmatic impairment is a core feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet its neural mechanisms remain poorly understood within a systematic explanatory framework. Traditional research focusing on isolated ERP components has been limited in capturing the temporal organization of pragmatic comprehension. Guided by a multi-stage framework of pragmatic processing, this study combined theory-driven feature construction with explainable machine learning to examine within-dataset group-discriminative EEG patterns during a context-sentence matching task. EEG data were collected from 103 children with ASD and 107 typically developing children (aged 4–10 years). Neural features were constructed from overlapping time-window × ROI measures, and classification analysis was performed using L2-regularized logistic regression within a nested cross-validation framework, followed by Haufe-transformed feature interpretation, bootstrap stability assessment, and complementary temporal and analytical-specification controls. The classifier achieved modest but statistically above-chance group discrimination (AUC = 0.652, empirical p = 0.001), indicating limited group-level separability within the current sample. Haufe-transformed pattern analysis showed a non-uniform descriptive distribution of model-associated EEG information across temporal ranges and scalp ROIs, with the largest mean absolute Haufe-pattern magnitude in the early range (0–300 ms) and over the temporal scalp ROI, middle-range concentration over the frontocentral scalp ROI, and predominantly temporal-scalp contributions in the late range. Exploratory brain-behavior analyses within the ASD group indicated opposite-direction associations of early- and late-temporal features with receptive vocabulary ability. Repeated cross-validated evaluation showed only limited improvement in within-dataset out-of-fold performance when the EEG features were added beyond age, and these findings should not be interpreted as direct behavioral evidence of pragmatic competence. These findings provide a within-sample description of how modest group-discriminative EEG information was distributed across time and scalp ROIs during the task and motivate independent replication and models that explicitly estimate temporal dependencies.

title: A medical image classification algorithm based on a hierarchical and complementary attention-enhanced Swin Transformer model
abstract: With the rapid development of precision medicine and intelligent diagnostic technologies, automatic medical image classification has become an important tool for assisting clinical decision-making. However, substantial variations in lesion scale, complex long-range dependencies of tissue structures, and the need to capture subtle anatomical features present significant challenges to existing deep learning models. To address the limitations of the Swin Transformer in modeling multi-scale lesions and multi-level feature interactions, this study proposes a hierarchical complementary feature enhancement framework based on the Swin Transformer for medical image classification. The proposed architecture performs collaborative feature learning at three representation levels, including macro-scale lesion perception, global contextual interaction, and local detail refinement. Specifically, a Multi-scale Depthwise SE Block (MSD-SE Block) is introduced at the input of each stage of the Swin Transformer to enhance the model’s multi-scale feature representation capability. Subsequently, a Residual Convolutional Attention (RCA) module is integrated following the self-attention mechanism and the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to strengthen global contextual modeling, while a Local Detail Enhanced Residual Channel-Spatial Attention (LDERCSA) module is employed to refine subtle anatomical structures and discriminative local features. Through the coordinated interaction of these components, the proposed framework establishes a hierarchical feature enhancement mechanism that effectively improves medical image representation across multiple scales and feature levels. Comprehensive experiments were conducted on eight core subsets of MedMNIST v2, including BloodMNIST, BreastMNIST, DermaMNIST, OCTMNIST, OrganSMNIST, PathMNIST, PneumoniaMNIST, and RetinaMNIST, using an input resolution of 224 \(\times\) 224. Single-module comparison and ablation studies demonstrate that each proposed component contributes positively to the overall performance. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves significant performance improvements on BreastMNIST, OCTMNIST, OrganSMNIST, and PneumoniaMNIST. Furthermore, comparative evaluations across all datasets confirm that the proposed framework exhibits strong robustness and generalization capability when processing multiple medical imaging modalities, including ultrasound, CT, X-ray, endoscopic, and microscopic images, thereby providing reliable technical support for computer-aided medical diagnosis systems.

title: Exploring electrophysiological signal features for drought stress assessment in plants
abstract: Climate change is increasing environmental stress, particularly rising temperatures and water scarcity, in both natural and human-managed systems such as agroecosystems and urban environments. Traditional methods for monitoring plant health in human-managed systems remain limited, underscoring the need for novel approaches. This study explored the potential of plant electrophysiological signals (EPS) and derived statistical features for the early detection of drought stress. The two main objectives of this research were: i) to identify EPS features that are both ecologically relevant and statistically robust for detecting drought stress, and ii) to develop statistical models that integrate these features. EPS data was collected from two drought-stress experiments, one on tomato plants and one on apricot trees. Seventeen features from both time and frequency domains were selected and evaluated. Two models, a logistic and a machine learning classifier, were developed and compared using accuracy, precision, and recall metrics. In apricots, ten time-domain features (Frequency Centre, Generalized Hurst Exponent, Hjorth Complexity, Hjorth Mobility, Kurtosis, Root Mean Squared Frequency, Root Variance Frequency, Shape Factor, Skewness and Standard Deviation) showed significant differences between stressed and control groups. In tomatoes, four frequency-domain features (Frequency Centre, Root Variance Frequency, Root Mean Squared Frequency, and Power Law Distribution Exponent) were significantly different. Model accuracy was approximately 50% for apricots and 66% for tomatoes, insufficient for practical deployment but indicative of potential. This study illustrates the potential value of plant EPS data, its derived statistical features, and models for developing early drought stress detection indicators in both agroecosystems and urban forestry management contexts.

title: Explainable AI–enhanced pavement deterioration modeling using hybrid classification–regression deep learning architecture
abstract: Effective Pavement Management System (PMS) planning depends on the ability to anticipate both the severity and physical extent of multiple distress types under real-world data constraints. This work introduces an interpretable dual-stage Deep Learning (DL) framework that sequentially classifies distress severity and then predicts the corresponding crack lengths, alligator cracking areas, and pothole quantities. The first stage uses an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) optimized with Focal loss to overcome severe class imbalance, while the second employs an ANN with Huber loss and targeted non-zero weighting to counteract outlier dominance and the zero-inflation inherent in sparse distress records. Data scarcity is addressed through the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and Gaussian noise augmentation. To assess whether the learned predictive relationships are consistent with established Mechanistic-Empirical (M-E) pavement knowledge, an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework combining Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), Partial Dependence Plots (PDP), and Individual Conditional Expectation (ICE) curves is integrated. These post hoc analyses do not establish causality; rather, they show that high-severity alligator cracking is the most influential predictive indicator associated with pothole area, a pattern consistent with established pavement deterioration mechanisms. Beyond prediction quality, the design is substantiated through systematic ablation experiments: a shared-backbone Multi-Task Learning (MTL) variant is shown to degrade regression accuracy due to gradient interference between conflicting loss objectives, while network capacity is empirically scaled, using a bottleneck regularization strategy for data-scarce targets such as pothole area and count, to prevent overfitting without compromising expressiveness. The framework achieved F1-scores of 0.843, 0.930, and 0.982 for linear crack, alligator crack, and pothole severity, respectively. In addition, R 2 values of 0.941, 0.954, 0.823, and 0.885 were obtained for linear crack length, alligator crack area, pothole area, and pothole count, respectively. However, the pothole-severity result should be interpreted as a high point estimate obtained from a small and highly sparse sample rather than as evidence of near-perfect population-level classification performance. Paired statistical tests indicate no detectable systematic bias in the evaluated predictions. The proposed framework provides strong and stable performance for the linear and alligator cracking targets, whereas the pothole area and count results should be regarded as preliminary because of the extremely limited number of available pothole observations. Accordingly, the framework offers a promising and interpretable basis for pavement maintenance planning within the Long-Term Pavement Performance (LTPP) context, while further external validation is required before operational deployment for sparse pothole-related targets.

title: Predictive modeling of mechanical properties in CO₂ laser welding of hastelloy X using supervised machine learning
abstract: A supervised machine learning (ML) regression study was performed to predict the tensile strength of CO₂ laser-welded Hastelloy X joints using data from 27 experimental trials involving variations in laser power, welding speed, and focal length. Five regression algorithms — Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), CatBoost (CB), and AdaBoost — were evaluated, initially using an 80:20 train-test split, under which Random Forest produced the strongest apparent performance (R² = 0.9483, MAE = 9.28, MSE = 132.937). Given the limited size of the experimental dataset, 5-fold and leave-one-out cross-validation were additionally performed to obtain a more robust assessment of model generalization; under both schemes, Random Forest and CatBoost consistently outperformed the remaining models, with cross-validated R² values of 0.61–0.65, indicating more modest but reliable predictive performance relative to the initial split evaluation. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) performed on the experimental dataset independently confirmed laser power as the dominant and only statistically significant process parameter influencing tensile strength, corroborating the feature importance rankings obtained from the machine learning models. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of ensemble-based machine learning approaches, particularly Random Forest and CatBoost, in predicting tensile strength from laser welding process parameters, while highlighting the importance of cross-validation for reliable model assessment on small experimental datasets, with implications for reducing experimental effort and improving process optimization in the fabrication of high-temperature alloy joints.

title: Boundary aware dual encoder learning for accurate cell segmentation
abstract: Accurate cell segmentation is a fundamental task in computational pathology and biomedical image analysis, directly impacting applications such as disease diagnosis, cancer grading, and drug discovery. Despite recent advances in deep learning, existing methods often struggle with precise boundary delineation in densely packed and morphologically complex cellular structures. In this paper, we propose a novel boundary-guided dual encoder architecture that explicitly separates semantic region representation from structural boundary modeling. The proposed framework integrates a ResNet-50 based region encoder with a lightweight ResNet-18 boundary encoder, enabling effective multi-scale feature fusion through a boundary guided attention mechanism. This design enhances segmentation accuracy, particularly along ambiguous and low contrast boundaries. Experimental results on the BCCD dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a Dice score of 95.85% and pixel accuracy of 97.47%, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods while maintaining significantly lower computational complexity. Specifically, the model requires only 12.70 M parameters and 36.86 GFLOPs, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained medical environments.

title: Leveraging temporal patterns in forecasting
abstract: Recurring temporal patterns emerge naturally from underlying processes and interactions in a variety of disciplines, ranging from epidemiology and ecology to social sciences and physics. These patterns hold considerable promise for enhancing time series forecasting. This study introduces a method that identifies these repeating patterns and incorporates them as dynamic covariates in traditional time series forecasting models. Using subsequence time series clustering, we obtain cluster solutions for various window lengths and k combinations, and only retain the ones with the lowest standard deviation at \(t+1\) , indicative of the level of signal entailed in the clusters. Our methodology is evaluated with three widely used forecasting models: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Random Forest (RF), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Each model is implemented in its standard form and subsequently augmented with dynamic covariates. The empirical evaluation draws on a data set comprising 1000 time series spanning a broad array of domains. The results show that the introduction of dynamic covariates significantly improves the prediction accuracy. Through combining static and dynamic variants in a compound model, our algorithm effectively filters out conditions under which time series clusters pick up meaningful signal and discards noise.

title: Mine water inflow (inrush) source identification model based on the RFE-GA-LightGBM model
abstract: Accurate identification of mine water inflow sources is essential for water hazard prevention and emergency decision-making in underground coal mining. However, source discrimination is often difficult because different aquifers may exhibit similar hydrochemical characteristics, and mining-induced fractures can enhance hydraulic connection and water–rock interaction. In this study, the 5110 working face of Yushupo Coal Mine was selected as the engineering case, and a mine water source identification model based on recursive feature elimination and genetic algorithm-optimized Light Gradient Boosting Machine, namely RFE-GA-LightGBM, was developed. Piper trilinear diagrams were first used to analyze the hydrochemical types and ion composition characteristics of different aquifers. Field observations showed that the maximum measured height of the water-conducting fractured zone reached 178 m, indicating that roof sandstone aquifers may be hydraulically connected during mining. Recursive feature elimination was then employed to screen key hydrochemical indicators, and Ca 2+ , Na + , SO₄² – , HCO₃ – , and Cl – were selected as input variables for model training. The GA-LightGBM model was compared with default LightGBM, PSO-LightGBM, and Bayesian-LightGBM models to verify the effectiveness of feature selection and hyperparameter optimization. The results show that Cl⁻ is an auxiliary indicator for identifying Lower Shihezi Formation water, whereas SO₄² – is sensitive to coal-measure sandstone aquifers affected by pyrite oxidation and water–rock interaction. Compared with the other models, GA-LightGBM achieved the best overall classification performance, with an accuracy of 96.1%, precision of 89.2%, recall of 89.5%, F1 score of 90.2%, specificity of 98.42%, and AUC of 0.96. The prediction results indicate that the water inflow at the 5110 working face is mainly related to the Taiyuan Formation sandstone aquifer and the K2 aquifer of the Shanxi Formation. This study provides a data-driven and hydrogeochemically interpretable method for rapid mine water source identification under complex mining conditions.

title: Land subsidence hazard mapping using a federated learning architecture with satellite and local environmental data
abstract: Land subsidence has become one of the most critical environmental and geomorphological hazards in recent years, threatening groundwater resources, urban infrastructure, and ecosystem stability. This study presents a novel Federated Learning (FL)-based framework for land subsidence hazard mapping in Poldokhtar County, Iran, without requiring direct access to centralized raw data. The proposed framework integrates Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR)-derived subsidence rate maps from Sentinel-1 time-series data (2015–2025) with 13 environmental conditioning factors across multiple spatial clients. Five machine learning and deep learning algorithms Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Deep Neural Network (DNN), and Logistic Regression (LR) were employed as local base models within the FL framework, using FedAvg and FedProx aggregation strategies. The results revealed generally weak to moderate correlations between subsidence and individual environmental factors, highlighting the complex and multi-factorial nature of the subsidence process. Client-based data distribution analysis confirmed a non-IID (Non-Independent and Identically Distributed) condition, with Client 1 representing severe subsidence areas (wider range of negative values) and Client 3 representing areas with weak or negligible subsidence (narrower range near zero). Among the global federated models, RF achieved the highest accuracy (R 2 = 0.963), followed closely by LSTM (R 2 = 0.956) , demonstrating their strong capability in capturing complex spatiotemporal patterns. In contrast, LR exhibited the poorest performance (R 2 = 0.375) with the highest error rates, confirming its limitation to linear relationships. Feature importance analysis identified Digital Elevation Model (DEM), groundwater level, and soil type as the most influential predictor variables associated with subsidence risk in the study area. The findings demonstrate that the proposed FL-based framework not only enhances prediction accuracy through collaborative learning across distributed clients but also preserves data privacy by avoiding raw data sharing. This approach offers a scalable and effective decision-support tool for sustainable groundwater management and land-use planning in subsidence-prone regions.

title: Enhancing Arabica and Robusta coffee prices forecasting through machine learning approaches
abstract: Machine learning was applied to predict Arabica and Robusta coffee prices 2–6 months ahead using climatic, production, and economic data from 2009 to 2025. SHAP analysis revealed that global and Brazilian stock levels, Vietnamese drought, Colombian rainfall, and U.S. dollar exchange rate were the most influential drivers of price variation, showing that even features with weak simple correlations can have high predictive power. We compared Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and two stacking configurations (RF/XGBoost/ELM) and (RF/XGBoost), both combined through a meta-learner. For Robusta, the three-model stacking configuration (RF/XGBoost/ELM) achieved the best overall accuracy with Pearson’s correlation coefficient (PA) of 0.9264, Hit Rate (HR) of 92.8000%, Root-Mean-Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0793, and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 9.3051%. Arabica proved more difficult to forecast, and the ELM delivered the highest independent test performance with PA of 0.9064 and HR of 94.1167%. To assess model robustness under future warming, we also tested two extreme climate scenarios derived from historical data and literature for major Arabica and Robusta producing regions (Brazil, Colombia, and Vietnam). These scenarios combined higher temperatures, reduced production, lower stocks, expanded production area, increased global consumption, and concurrent logistic and climatic shocks. Despite these stringent assumptions, the models did not project strong price surges and showed greater difficulty when extrapolating Arabica prices, while Robusta forecasts remained more consistent with realistic market values. These results underscore the ability of machine-learning models and SHAP interpretation to reveal the complex economic, climatic and productive factors governing global coffee price dynamics and highlight their conservative extrapolation when confronted with unprecedented climatic conditions.
