title: AC flashover voltage prediction of silicone rubber insulators under mechanical defects and non-uniform pollution using experimental, machine learning, and numerical approaches
abstract: This study investigates the combined effects of ring non-uniform (RNU) and ring–longitudinal non-uniform (RLNU) pollution, together with mechanical defects, on the AC flashover voltage of silicone rubber insulators under varying humidity conditions. Moving beyond previous studies focused on isolated pollution or defect factors, this work experimentally evaluates their combined influence under realistic environmental conditions. Non-uniform pollution significantly affects flashover performance. Increasing the longitudinal non-uniformity index (P) increases the flashover voltage, whereas increasing the polluted radius under RNU conditions (R) reduces it, indicating that more uniform contamination weakens insulation performance. Mechanical defects further degrade dielectric characteristics by intensifying local electric fields and promoting earlier arc initiation, reducing flashover voltage by up to 31.9% compared with intact insulators. A novel empirical model is proposed to estimate flashover voltage as a function of salt deposit density (SDD), relative humidity (H), and the pollution non-uniformity index (P). Artificial intelligence-based prediction models, including Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), were developed to improve prediction accuracy. The MLP model outperformed the conventional ANN model, while a comparative evaluation of several machine learning regression algorithms identified the CatBoost regressor as the most accurate model. Furthermore, finite element method (FEM) simulations were performed to corroborate the experimental findings and provide a deeper insight into the influence of pollution distribution on electric-field characteristics. Uniform pollution increased the electric-field intensity by 25.7% compared with non-uniform pollution, whereas RLNU pollution produced 11% lower electric-field intensity than RNU, indicating a more stable field distribution. Mechanical defects also increased the maximum electric-field intensity by approximately 63.81% compared with intact insulators. The integrated framework, combining experimental investigation, artificial intelligence-based prediction, machine learning, and finite element simulations, provides a comprehensive understanding of flashover behavior and significantly improves the predictive capability of silicone rubber insulators operating under harsh environmental conditions.

title: Data-driven modeling and optimization of nano-belite cementitious composites incorporating internal NaCl and Na2SO4 additives
abstract: This study evaluates the interactive effects of nano-belite cement replacement ( \(\:0\text{\--}20\%\text{\:wt.}\) ) and internal salt additions ( \(\:5\%\text{\:wt.}\) of either \(\:\text{NaCl}\) or \(\:{\text{Na}}_{2}{\text{SO}}_{4}\) ) on the compressive strength and bulk electrical resistivity of concrete composites up to 180 days of curing. A dataset of 225 experimental records was used to train a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network, which was subsequently coupled with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) to optimize the mixture design. Experimental results indicate that under salt-free conditions, a \(\:10\%\) nano-belite replacement optimizes microstructural development, yielding a compressive strength of \(\:50.26\text{\:MPa}\) and an electrical resistivity of \(\:174.40\text{}{\Omega\:}\cdot\:\text{m}\) at 180 days. The internal addition of \(\:{\text{Na}}_{2}{\text{SO}}_{4}\) acts synergistically with nano-belite by promoting pore refinement through secondary hydration products, elevating the 180-day compressive strength to \(\:52.49\text{\:MPa}\) . In contrast, internal \(\:\text{NaCl}\) incorporation exhibits an antagonistic relationship at nano-belite dosages exceeding \(\:5\%\) , causing a drop in electrical resistivity due to enhanced ionic mobility in the pore network. The developed MLP model predicted the experimental outcomes with high accuracy ( \(\:{R}^{2}>0.98\) for both properties). Multi-objective optimization via NSGA-II identified a balanced optimum replacement level at \(\:9.82\%\) nano-belite. Independent validation testing of ten physical specimens fabricated at this optimal dosage demonstrated close agreement with model predictions, yielding relative errors of \(\:2.94\%\) for bulk electrical resistivity and \(\:13.13\%\) for compressive strength. Additionally, explicit algebraic equations derived from the network weights provide a direct mapping tool for mix design without the need for active machine learning execution.

title: Mindfulness, creative self-efficacy, and communal-agentic orientation in human–AI decision-making with implications for adaptive AI design
abstract: Human decision-making is increasingly augmented by artificial intelligence (AI), yet individuals vary in whether they revise their judgments after receiving AI-generated input. We examined how trait mindfulness and creative self-efficacy (CSE), together with communal-agentic personality orientations, relate to decision revision following AI input. Data from 549 UK-based professionals were analysed using binary logistic regression, with revision of the initial budget allocation (change versus no change) as the outcome. The mindfulness × CSE interaction was significant, indicating that the association between mindfulness and decision revision varied by CSE. The pattern was positive at lower CSE and negative at higher CSE, although neither median-split simple slope reached conventional significance. CSE showed no independent main effect. Communal-femininity moderated the association between mindfulness and revision, whereas the hypothesised mindfulness × CSE × communal-femininity interaction was trend-level and is treated as suggestive. Because the outcome captured any revision rather than movement toward the AI recommendation, the findings concern the likelihood of reconsidering an initial decision after AI input, not acceptance of AI advice or improvement in decision quality. These results refine understanding of individual differences in human–AI decision revision and identify testable considerations for adaptive AI design.

title: High-fidelity 3D reconstruction of navel oranges using 3D Gaussian splatting
abstract: Reliable 3D visual reconstruction is important for documenting the external quality of navel oranges and supporting future phenotypic analysis. Conventional Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines struggle with the weakly textured characteristics and highly specular surfaces of navel oranges, resulting in incomplete reconstructions, sparse point clouds, and severe visual artifacts. To address these challenges, this study develops a high-fidelity 3D reconstruction framework that integrates deep-learning-based feature matching with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). For the sparse reconstruction phase, the SuperPoint detector and SuperGlue matcher are employed, leveraging deep feature extraction and graph neural networks to enhance matching robustness on complex surfaces. To address the initialization challenges of 3DGS, a spatial-colorimetric cascade purification strategy—combining pass-through filtering, HSV masking, and statistical filtering—is developed to effectively eliminate noise and provide a high-confidence initialization prior. Subsequently, 3DGS is utilized for dense reconstruction and high-fidelity neural rendering. Experimental results demonstrate that the developed framework significantly outperforms the conventional SfM pipeline in terms of registered image count, point cloud density, and trajectory length. The 3DGS-optimized model achieved improved PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS values on held-out views, indicating enhanced novel-view rendering quality and visual fidelity. This approach offers an efficient photorealistic digitization solution for weakly textured and highly specular fruits, thereby establishing a reliable visual foundation for future non-destructive phenotypic analysis in smart agriculture.

title: Multimodal collaborative modeling of teacher verbal and non-verbal classroom behaviors for teaching effectiveness prediction
abstract: Teacher classroom behavior sits at the centre of any serious attempt to understand and improve instructional quality, yet the verbal and the non-verbal channel are still typically examined apart, which leaves their pedagogically meaningful interdependence unmodelled. This paper proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that models the two channels collaboratively and predicts teaching effectiveness from their joint representation. Four modules compose the framework: temporal synchronization of the audio and video streams, parallel unimodal encoding through BERT-based language representation and SlowFast spatiotemporal networks, bidirectional cross-modal attention fusion regulated by a gated modality weighting mechanism, and a dual-head prediction network optimized jointly for effectiveness classification and continuous score regression. On a corpus of 186 classroom sessions recorded in 12 schools, the framework attains 82.3% classification accuracy, 80.1% macro-F1, an RMSE of 6.58 and a Pearson correlation of 0.879, ahead of ten comparison systems spanning unimodal, traditional machine learning and state-of-the-art multimodal fusion approaches. Ablation identifies bidirectional cross-modal attention as the component that matters most, and an attention analysis conducted across all test sessions indicates that verbal-gestural temporal synchrony accompanies higher observer-rated teaching effectiveness. The framework thus offers a scalable, automated route from multimodal teacher behavior to instructional outcomes, with potential applications in teacher professional development and intelligent classroom observation systems.

title: Relation-aware multimodal knowledge graph learning for drug–drug interaction prediction
abstract: Drug–drug interactions (DDIs) can alter therapeutic efficacy and lead to adverse events, making accurate DDI prediction important for drug safety assessment. Existing computational methods often rely on limited drug features or do not sufficiently capture heterogeneous biomedical relations surrounding drugs. We present RA-DDI, a relation-aware knowledge graph framework for DDI prediction. RA-DDI constructs a drug-centered knowledge graph (KG) from DrugBank and initializes drug representations by integrating molecular structures, textual descriptions, and graph-derived relational features. These multimodal representations are then refined through relation-aware graph learning to capture multi-hop dependencies among drugs and related biomedical entities. A prediction module combines the learned drug embeddings with pairwise interaction features to classify DDI types. We evaluated RA-DDI on three public benchmark datasets, DrugBank, DDInter, and PDD-Graph. The proposed framework achieved competitive performance and showed consistent improvements over representative baselines on several key classification and ranking metrics. These findings demonstrate that combining multimodal drug representation learning with relation-aware knowledge graph modeling is effective for DDI prediction.

title: Prevalence of comorbidity symptoms of anxiety and depression and importance of influencing factors among adolescents in Shaanxi Province: a large-scale school-based survey
abstract: Abstract Comorbidity symptoms of anxiety and depression disorders (CAD) is common among adolescents and threaten the health and safety of adolescents. This study estimated the prevalence of CAD and examined its relative important influencing factors for formulating targeted intervention programs. Data were from the National Student Common Disease and Risk Factors Surveillance program in Shaanxi province, Northwestern China in 2023. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) respectively. An Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithm (XGBoost) model combined with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) was applied to explore the relative predictive contribution of behavioral factors by school grade. A total of 94 472 students were included, in whom 15 113 (16.00%) had CAD, and the prevalence of CAD in senior high school students (22.08%) was higher than junior high students (12.01%). There was a gender specific difference in the prevalence of CAD, the proportion of CAD in boys was lower than in girl in junior high school (10.22% vs. 13.87%) and senior high school (20.45% vs. 23.64%). The all health-risk behaviors included in this study can influence the CAD among students, but there importance varied with gender and academic stage. The top three contributing factors were unhealthy diet, internet addiction and bully in junior high school boys. The top three contributing factors were unhealthy diet, internet addiction and sleep deprivation in junior high school girls. The top three contributing factors were sleep deprivation, internet addiction and unhealthy diet in both senior high school boys and girls. CAD is common among adolescents in Shaanxi Province, the prevalence of CAD increased with academic stage, while the junior high school students also screen-positive for CAD risk. The prevalence of CAD both in junior high school and senior high school students was mainly related to unhealthy life behaviors, such as unhealthy diet, internet addiction and sleep deprivation, and bully. Integrating behavioral risk surveillance with adolescent mental health services may help improve early identification and targeted intervention.

title: Identification of RAB36 and NINL as potential diagnostic biomarkers for gestational diabetes mellitus and polycystic ovary syndrome
abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) are common endocrine and metabolic disorders in women, with PCOS increasing the risk of GDM. However, shared molecular markers that could support early diagnosis and the mechanisms underlying them remain insufficiently defined. This study integrated public transcriptome datasets for GDM and PCOS to identify shared differentially expressed genes, which were then analyzed via machine learning, diagnostic model construction, pathway analysis, regulatory network analysis, drug prediction, molecular docking, and reverse transcription (RT)-qPCR-based validation in clinical blood samples. Among the 15 shared candidate genes identified, RAB36 and ninein-like (NINL) were selected as potential diagnostic biomarkers. Nomogram and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses indicated that the two-gene models have diagnostic value for both GDM and PCOS, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.71 and 0.98, respectively. Functional analyses suggested that RAB36 and NINL may be associated with pathways related to immune regulation, cell cycle-related processes, metabolic signaling, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation. Drug prediction and molecular docking further identified cinnamaldehyde and valproic acid as potential compounds targeting both biomarkers. RT-qPCR revealed increased RAB36 expression and decreased NINL expression in clinical blood samples. This study identifies potential biomarkers shared between GDM and PCOS and mechanistic clues for early diagnosis and personalized disease management.

title: Generalizable lower-limb muscle MRI segmentation and quantification on heterogeneous multisite datasets
abstract: Neuromuscular diseases are a heterogeneous group of disorders affecting muscles and peripheral nerves, leading to progressive muscle weakness and functional impairment. Muscle MRI facilitates the assessment of muscle pathology, but current analysis relies on time-consuming manual segmentation or subjective visual scoring. Validation across diverse patient populations and imaging protocols is lacking in existing automated methods. Deep learning segmentation methods were developed to quantify intramuscular fat infiltration and muscle volume across all lower limb muscles using heterogeneous multi-site data. Three convolutional neural network architectures (U-Net, U-Net + + , and Attention U-Net + +) were evaluated on a multi-site dataset comprising 27,858 slices from 797 muscle MRI scans across 376 patients, spanning 12 neuromuscular diseases and 12 international sites. Thirty-two individual muscles across pelvis, thigh, and lower leg regions were segmented. High accuracy was achieved by all architectures (DSC = 0.97). Leave-One-Site-Out experiments revealed strong generalisability across sites (average DSC = 0.96). Automated fat quantification placed 90.9% of muscles within one point of ground truth on standard visual scales and correlated strongly with quantitative fat fraction measurements (r = 0.995, p < 0.001). High correlation with ground truth was demonstrated by cross-sectional area predictions (r = 0.94, p < 0.001). Diverse imaging protocols were handled with minimal preprocessing. Accuracy equivalent to observer variability was achieved by automated segmentation, potentially eliminating the need for manual correction in large-scale applications.

title: Enhanced seam segmentation for automated welding robot in construction through transfer learning: addressing limitations of bilateral segmentation network
abstract: Reliable weld seam segmentation is essential for autonomous robotic welding in construction, where severe illumination changes, specular reflections, and thin weld geometries frequently degrade segmentation performance. This paper proposes a lightweight post-training optimization framework that systematically improves existing real-time semantic segmentation networks without modifying their architectures. Starting from an Online Hard Example Mining (OHEM)-pretrained checkpoint, the proposed framework combines controlled fine-tuning with a hybrid Cross-Entropy–Lovász objective to enhance pixel-level classification, region-level seam continuity, and recovery from reflection-induced segmentation failures while preserving real-time inference efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework substantially improves segmentation performance. Using BiSeNetV2, Joint IoU increases from 59.40% to 81.76% (+22.36 percentage points), while mIoU reaches 90.73% without increasing parameter count, FLOPs, inference latency, or memory consumption. Furthermore, the proposed framework successfully recovers 96.33% of severe zero-IoU failure cases caused by strong reflections, substantially improving the operational reliability of downstream robotic perception. To evaluate the generality of the proposed optimization framework, additional experiments were conducted using U-Net, DeepLabV3+, SegFormer-B0, and PIDNet-S under multiple fine-tuning configurations. The results reveal that the effectiveness of post-training optimization is strongly architecture-dependent: lightweight real-time segmentation networks, particularly BiSeNetV2 and PIDNet-S, consistently benefit from the proposed framework, whereas larger semantic-oriented architectures exhibit comparatively smaller and less stable improvements. In robotic welding experiments, the proposed BiSeNetV2 model was the only evaluated approach capable of consistently generating a valid weld seam trajectory, achieving an average joint-center offset of \(2.47 \pm 0.78\) mm during robotic path planning, corresponding to an approximately 9.8 \(\times\) reduction compared with the previous BiSeNetV2-based robotic welding system. Overall, the results demonstrate that carefully designed post-training optimization provides a practical and computationally efficient alternative to architectural redesign, substantially improving failure recovery, seam continuity, and robotic trajectory generation for autonomous welding in reflective construction environments.

title: A unified benchmark of supervised and retrieval-based methods for viral genomic sequence classification
abstract: The rapid growth of genomic sequencing demands fast, accurate, and scalable analysis methods. In viral genomic classification, expanding labeled reference collections can make supervised models costly to update and dependent on fixed label sets, motivating retrieval-based genomic classification as a simpler, more flexible alternative. We present a unified benchmark of supervised and retrieval-based methods for viral genomic sequence classification across three viral classification tasks: hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotyping, COVID-19 discrimination, and human papillomavirus (HPV) genotyping. We compare standard sequence encodings (one-hot, k -mers, FCGR) with dense embeddings (dna2vec, DNABERT). For each representation, we evaluate supervised classifiers (Random Forest, Decision Tree, XGBoost) and retrieval-based classification, where sequence vectors are indexed with FAISS and labels are assigned via similarity-weighted k-NN. Furthermore, we benchmark multiple FAISS index types (Flat, IVF, HNSW, IVFPQ, OPQ) to characterize accuracy-speed–memory trade-offs at scale. The results show that XGBoost and retrieval using Flat or IVF indexes achieve strong classification performance under different computational profiles. Compressed indexes such as IVFPQ and OPQ substantially reduce memory usage, although their accuracy loss depends on the dataset and representation. Overall, supervised XGBoost provides a favorable accuracy–size trade-off, while retrieval-based classification remains competitive and allows labeled reference sequences to be incorporated without retraining a global classifier. This benchmark provides practical guidance for selecting sequence representations, classifiers, and vector-search indexes under different accuracy, memory, and update requirements.

title: Hybrid encoder-decoder to preserve long-range context in brain tumor segmentation with EfficientNetB7 and a convolutional vision transformer mechanism
abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain tumors in MRI is critically important for clinical diagnosis, particularly challenging for Low-Grade Gliomas (LGGs) in FLAIR sequences where precise delineation directly impacts treatment planning and patient monitoring. Conventional U-Net architectures face limitations in this domain, exhibiting structural degradation from repetitive down-sampling and inefficient feature propagation between encoder and decoder components. Furthermore, most existing approaches rely on manual hyperparameter optimization, which is both computationally intensive and prone to suboptimal convergence. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel hybrid encoder-decoder framework that integrates an EfficientNetB7 backbone with a single-stage Convolutional Vision Transformer (CvT) and a TransUNet style decoder, systematically optimized through Bayesian hyperparameter tuning. The architecture leverages EfficientNetB7 for multi-scale feature extraction while the CvT module implements convolutional token embedding and multi-head self-attention to model long-range dependencies without patch-based transformations, maintaining structural coherence for optimized feature fusion. The decoding pathway employs bilinear upsampling enhanced with residual convolutional blocks for precise boundary refinement. Extensive evaluation on the Kaggle Low-Grade Glioma (LGG) and Brain Tumor Segmentation datasets demonstrates superior performance, achieving Dice coefficients of 0.9290 and 0.9262 respectively. These results confirm that our architecture effectively preserves fine structural details while capturing global context, yielding robust and accurate tumor segmentation, demonstrating strong potential for future integration into clinical decision support systems, pending prospective clinical validation. The integration of Bayesian optimization further ensures reproducible and optimal model configuration, enhancing the framework’s reliability for medical imaging applications.

title: Explainable machine learning predicts adolescent cognitive development from sport engagement in a national longitudinal survey
abstract: Globally, over 80% of adolescents fail to meet recommended physical activity levels, raising concerns about cognitive development during a critical neurodevelopmental period. Physical activity is associated with cognitive benefits in young people, yet large-scale predictive evidence on how extracurricular sport engagement and PE-related school resources relate to adolescent cognitive development remains limited. This study applied explainable machine learning to the China Education Panel Survey, a nationally representative longitudinal dataset, to predict follow-up cognitive ability from baseline extracurricular sport engagement, PE-related school resources, and contextual variables among 9366 seventh-grade students. Five models were compared: Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Support Vector Regression, and a Stacking ensemble. The Stacking model achieved the best performance (R² = 0.593, RMSE = 0.523, Pearson r = 0.770). SHAP analysis revealed that baseline cognitive ability and academic achievement were the strongest predictors, while sport-engagement and PE-related school-resource variables collectively accounted for 5.5% of total SHAP contribution, with individual behavioral engagement (3.7%) exceeding PE-related school resources (1.8%). Among PE predictors, running-track length, weekend sport duration, and frequency of exercising with parents ranked highest. SHAP dependence analysis indicated a negative association between excessive weekday sport time and cognitive outcomes, alongside a positive moderating role of family economic status on weekend sport engagement. Propensity score matching identified a significant association between sport interest and cognitive development (ATT = 0.071, p = 0.004), though sensitivity analysis indicated limited robustness to unobserved confounding. These findings suggest that extracurricular sport engagement, particularly intrinsic sport interest, shows a modest but meaningful association with adolescent cognitive development over one year.

title: An explainable ensemble machine learning approach for coefficient of compressibility prediction of Chengdu clay
abstract: Accurate prediction of the coefficient of compressibility (a v ) for regional clays remains a fundamental challenge in geotechnical engineering. Focusing on Chengdu clays, this study proposes a machine learning framework that integrates physically constrained data augmentation, differentiated hyperparameter optimization, and interpretability analysis. Based on 338 experimental datasets, a hybrid optimization strategy (Grid Search + Bayesian Optimization) is employed to ensure fair model comparison. The statistical significance of performance differences is rigorously validated using 30 iterations of Monte Carlo cross-validation combined with paired t-tests. Generalization capability is assessed via spatial grouping cross-validation, accompanied by Bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification. Results demonstrate that LightGBM achieves the highest predictive accuracy (test R 2 = 0.8817), significantly outperforming comparison models (p < 0.05). XGBoost exhibits comparable accuracy (R 2 = 0.8805), while Random Forest demonstrates superior robustness in spatial cross-validation (R 2 = 0.7273). Multi-model analysis consistently identifies water content and liquidity index as the dominant factors governing a v , with cumulative contribution exceeding 95%. SHAP analysis confirms both factors exhibit monotonically positive effects with approximate additivity. Tree-based models yield Bootstrap confidence intervals with mean widths ranging from 0.0526 to 0.0653 MPa -1 , providing essential risk references for engineering practice. This study not only delivers a reliable predictive tool for a v of Chengdu clays but also establishes a reproducible, physically guided, and statistically rigorous paradigm for regional geotechnical machine learning research.

title: Learning aligned EEG representations with subject-specific encoders
abstract: Cross-subject EEG decoding promises more training data, but it also exposes neural networks to strong inter-subject distribution shifts. We study whether task supervision and architecture alone can learn subject-aligned representations. We replace a shared EEG encoder with subject-specific encoders followed by a common classifier, and compare this hybrid model with standard EEGNet, AttentionBaseNet, and CTNet baselines with Euclidean Alignment (EA) on three motor-imagery datasets and one motor-execution dataset. EA improves shared encoders by recentering subject covariances, whereas the hybrid encoder reduces reliance on EA: removing EA has little effect on validation-loss dynamics or latent-space organization, and both hybrid variants consistently outperform non-aligned shared baselines. Subject-specific heads increase class distinctiveness and place each subject close to its own latent manifold while improving within-subject class separation. However, on cross-subject classification, subject-specific heads hinder direct parameter transfer to unseen subjects, motivating quantitative head selection and a brief calibration session. Although decoding gains depend on the dataset and backbone, our main findings concern the solely use of architecture pressure promotes representation learning and alignment in a direction complementary to domain adaptation methods such as Euclidean Alignment. A per-subject low-rank adapter of only \(2\,C\,r\) parameters recovers the full encoder’s accuracy across five backbones and ranks \(r=1\) to 16, so the per-subject module can be compressed by two to three orders of magnitude.

title: CLAUNet-LFB0-CBAM a deep learning framework for explainable liver fibrosis stage classification from ultrasound images
abstract: Automated liver fibrosis staging through ultrasound images is still difficult owing to low contrast, speckle artifacts, and minor differences between successive stages. We propose a hybrid deep learning architecture named CLAUNet-LFB0-CBAM for multi-class liver fibrosis classification from ultrasound images. The method uses a preprocessing pipeline step followed by an augmented EfficientNet-B0 network with CBAM. Moreover, to deal with class imbalance issue, the method employs weighted cross-entropy loss and weighted random sampling, combined with augmentation techniques. The proposed network is compared with baseline architectures like VGG-16, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, and EfficientNet-B0 within identical experimental conditions. Experimental results show that the proposed method provides superior results in terms of 99.05% accuracy, 0.980 F1-score, and 0.9987 AUC, surpassing all evaluated baseline architectures under identical experimental conditions. Importantly, the performance improvement is achieved mainly in intermediate liver fibrosis stages which are crucial for clinical evaluation. Grad-CAM analysis supports that the network learns the appropriate features from anatomical liver regions. Moreover, the network achieves lightweight implementation with only around 4.8 million parameters.

title: Multidimensional contemporaneous prediction of harmonized consumer price index levels across countries using reproducible machine learning and deep learning models
abstract: Accurate modeling of the consumer price index (CPI) is important for inflation monitoring and policy analysis. This study develops a multidimensional cross-country framework for CPI prediction and, in response to reproducibility concerns, replaces the principal neural-architecture ranking with a fully re-estimated and documented benchmark. The reproducible benchmark uses the supplied 545-observation, 39-country common-feature panel for 1995–2020, partitioned chronologically into 337 training observations (through 2014), 102 validation observations (2015–2017), and 106 holdout observations (2018–2020). For each country-year, CNN, RNN, and LSTM models receive up to the four most recent observed predictor vectors ending in year t; CPI itself is excluded from the input. Scaling is fitted on the training period only. Final architectures, selected hyperparameters, trainable-parameter counts, software versions, five fixed random seeds (101, 202, 303, 404, 505), per-seed holdout predictions, selected checkpoints, learning curves, and three expanding-window fold forecasts are reported and archived. The CNN contains 2,433 trainable parameters, the RNN 641, and the LSTM 7,073. Across five seeds, CNN has the lowest mean RMSE (0.1943, SD = 0.0094) and ranks first by RMSE in all five runs; LSTM has the lowest mean MAE (0.1128) and MAPE (0.0803). CNN also has the lowest RMSE in each of the three 2018–2020 expanding-window folds. Because the original TFT, GNN, and hybrid implementations cannot be reconstructed from the archived materials, they are removed from the principal comparative conclusions rather than assigned reconstructed architectures. The full-feature CatBoost/SHAP analysis and the lagged ex-ante benchmark branch remain separate analyses with their original information-set qualifications. The resulting conclusions emphasize reproducible performance, metric-specific trade-offs, and model-ranking stability rather than unsupported architecture superiority. Any legacy TFT, GNN, or hybrid point estimates that remain solely for traceability are explicitly treated as archived exploratory results and are not used for reproducibility claims, model rankings, inferential comparisons, or substantive conclusions. The chronological split is instantiated before every sample-dependent fitting operation, and the fitted StandardScaler objects, target-normalization parameters, split-membership files, and sequence-construction audits are preserved for the main split and for each expanding-window fold. No sample-dependent variable screening, PCA, graph construction, wavelet transformation, or imputation is used in this confirmatory principal benchmark; historical analyses requiring unavailable preprocessing objects remain outside the confirmatory conclusions. Because the exact row-level inclusion key and complete variable matrix for the historical 396-observation full-feature branch are not available in the current archive, that branch is retained only as archived exploratory/descriptive evidence and is excluded from the principal confirmatory conclusions; any interpretation of its SHAP, ablation, expanded-education, or subgroup results is limited to the data-observable country-years represented in that selected complete-case sample. Dependence-aware resampling further narrows the inferential claim: country-block and two-way crossed-cluster bootstrap intervals do not separate the reproduced neural architectures from one another under the loss functions associated with their reported rankings, whereas the CNN-CatBoost squared-loss difference remains below zero under both resampling schemes. The central empirical claims are restricted to the fully reproducible 545-observation benchmark: the final analysis dataset, executable estimation code, split-specific fitted preprocessing objects, fixed random seeds, observation-level predictions, learning curves, expanding-window fold forecasts, and dependence-aware comparison inputs are supplied as a single replication package. Analyses for which the complete row-level design matrix or implementation-defining objects are unavailable are excluded from confirmatory conclusions.

title: How cultural values influence green consumption intentions among Chinese consumers: a PLS-SEM-ANN approach
abstract: Green consumption is a key pathway to achieving sustainability. The primary goal of this study was to investigate the factors influencing Chinese consumers’ green consumption intentions. This study integrates the extended theory of planned behavior and norm activation theory to develop a comprehensive framework of direct and indirect green consumption intention antecedents. Survey data were collected from 420 consumers and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation Modelling-Artificial neural network (PLS-SEM-ANN). The findings indicate that both environmental attitudes and personal norms significantly enhance consumers’ green consumption intentions. Furthermore, collectivism, face consciousness subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and green self-identity were significantly related to environmental attitudes. Awareness of consequences, ascription of responsibility, subjective norms, and perceived consumer effectiveness positively influenced personal norms. Our findings suggest ways to influence green consumption intentions and have practical implications for policymakers and marketers.

title: Generative AI emotion recognition from bodily gestures and vocal tone reveals modality-specific performance and positivity bias
abstract: Advances in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) have prompted interest in its application in sensitive fields, including mental health. Yet the validity of its nonverbal social-cognitive abilities remains unclear. This study addresses two issues that probe GenAI’s social intelligence: its capacity to interpret nonverbal channels (bodily gestures and vocal tone) with accuracy comparable to humans, and whether accuracy of emotion recognition is different by emotional valence. Emotion recognition accuracy of three Gemini GenAI models (Pro 1.5, Pro 2 (Experimental) and Flash 2) were evaluated using the EU-Emotion Stimulus Set of bodily gestures and vocal tone depicting basic emotions. Model accuracy was compared to validated human benchmarks. Advanced GenAI models achieved near-human accuracy in recognizing emotions from vocal tone. However, their performance was significantly lower than that of humans in interpreting bodily gestures. GenAI models recognized positive emotions more accurately than negative ones. This bias was significant across all models for bodily gestures and in the advanced models for vocal tone. GenAI models exhibit a non-humanlike social-cognitive profile, excelling with positive emotions but struggling with the negative content. This finding carries profound clinical and theoretical relevance, highlighting the risks of integrating GenAI into sensitive fields and underscoring the need for continued validation.

title: A novel prediction method for slope deformation based on adaptive mode decomposition and interpretable deep learning
abstract: To address the issues of non‑stationary signal processing and the black‑box nature of models in slope deformation prediction, this study proposes a prediction framework based on the Dung Beetle Optimizer (DBO), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), and Long Short‑Term Memory (LSTM), and introduces SHAP for interpretability analysis. DBO simultaneously optimizes the VMD decomposition parameters (number of modes and penalty factor) and LSTM hyperparameters (number of hidden layer neurons, learning rate, and number of iterations), achieving end-to-end adaptive optimization. A case study on a red clay high slope in Jiangxi Province showed that the proposed DBO‑VMD‑LSTM model achieved an RMSE of 0.155 mm and an R² of 0.993, significantly outperforming comparison models such as SSA‑VMD‑LSTM ( p < 0.001). SHAP interaction analysis revealed an alternating coupling pattern between displacement rate and multi‑scale rainfall—positive for short‑term, negative for medium‑term, and positive for long‑term—and the magnitude of interactions differed markedly between periodic and trend components (the maximum for the trend component was only 15% of that for the periodic component), validating the physical effectiveness of the VMD decomposition. This study provides a high-precision and interpretable method for predicting high-slope deformation.

title: River water temperature prediction using REMD, RLMD, and SVMD coupled with deep learning models
abstract: River water temperature (T w ) is a critical parameter for the freshwater ecosystems and the aquatic life. Daily water temperature time series can be used for many applications and included as input variable for various modelling tools. In this study, four deep learning (DL) models (i.e., LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, and BiGRU) were used for modelling daily water T w measured at four rivers stations in Poland. Furthermore, a new method is adopted in the present study based on signal decomposition (SD) for improving the performances of the single DL models. Three different SD algorithms were used in the present study namely: robust empirical mode decomposition (REMD), robust local mean decomposition (RLMD), and successive variational mode decomposition (SVMD). For each DL we have adopted four scenarios: ( i ) using only air temperature (T a ) as input variables, and ( ii ) by using the product functions (PFs) obtained using the RLMD and the intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) obtained using the REMD and SVMD. All models were first calibrated using 70% of the dataset and validated using 30% of the dataset, and their performances were evaluated using the root mean squared error (RMSE), the mean absolute error (MAE), the coefficient of correlation (R), and the Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE). In general, the smallest RMSE and MAE are obtained for the models using the signal decomposition, whereas the largest errors metrics are achieved by the single DL models. Among all stations, the best performances were achieved using the REMD-BiGRU with R, NSE, RMSE, and MAE of 0.986, 0.973, 0.966, and 0.752, respectively, while the poorest performances were obtained by the GRU with R, NSE, RMSE, and MAE of 0.815, 0.659, 3.456, and 2.613, respectively.

title: Social media influencers drive healthy food intentions through perceived value and electronic word-of-mouth
abstract: This study aims to investigate the mechanisms through which social media influencers shape consumers’ intention to consume healthy food in Iran. The research specifically focuses on the roles of perceived consumption values (epistemic and social), electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM), and influencer–follower congruence. Data were collected via an online questionnaire from 452 followers of health and nutrition influencers on Instagram in Iran. A hybrid analytical approach combining partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and artificial neural networks (ANN) was employed to test the research hypotheses. PLS-SEM results indicated that eWOM, perceived social value, and perceived epistemic value all exert significant positive effects on consumers’ intention to consume healthy food. Furthermore, both perceived social and epistemic values significantly influenced followers’ willingness to share eWOM. However, the moderating role of influencer-follower congruence was not supported. Sensitivity analysis through ANN revealed that eWOM holds the highest relative importance in predicting healthy food consumption intention, followed by perceived social value, perceived epistemic value, and congruence, respectively. The findings suggest that perceived epistemic value enhances both healthy food consumption intention and eWOM sharing behavior. Although congruence did not function as a moderator, it emerged as a significant independent predictor. The integrated SEM-ANN analysis confirmed the model’s high predictive power and identified eWOM as the most critical driver of healthy food consumption intention.

title: A metabolomics and machine learning-based predictive model for AKI-to-CKD progression risk
abstract: Progression from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases mortality risk, yet reliable tools for early risk stratification remain limited. We performed untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC–MS)-based plasma metabolomics in 74 participants, including 44 AKI-nonCKD patients with renal function recovery, 19 AKI-to-CKD progressors, and 11 healthy controls. A two-step differential analysis identified 104 consensus metabolites showing concordant directional changes between AKI-nonCKD and AKI-to-CKD groups. These metabolites were subsequently used as a predefined candidate metabolite pool for predictive modeling, with downstream Boruta screening and LASSO modeling performed within a nested cross-validation framework. A candidate 5-metabolite signature consisting of 2-Furoate, 1H-Pyrrole-2-carboxaldehyde, LPE(18:0), Cyclopentylamine, and Glycerophosphocholine was selected based on repeated LASSO retention frequency and model parsimony analysis. The 5-metabolite model showed comparable discrimination with a numerically higher AUC than the 4-metabolite model (0.981 vs. 0.957), whereas adding a sixth metabolite did not further improve discrimination. In nested cross-validation, the clinical-only model showed limited discrimination, while the metabolite-only and integrated LASSO models achieved substantially higher pooled AUCs in repeated nested cross-validation, with pooled AUCs of 0.999 and 0.999, respectively. Label-permutation negative control analysis reduced model performance to near-chance level, supporting that the observed discrimination was not generated by the resampling procedure alone. These findings suggest that plasma metabolomic signatures may provide candidate metabolomic predictors for early AKI-to-CKD risk stratification, although external validation in multi-center cohorts is required before clinical application.

title: Persona-prompted LLM agents achieve modest but genuine prediction of human social media reactions
abstract: Social media platforms mediate how billions form opinions and engage with public discourse. As autonomous AI agents increasingly participate in these spaces, understanding their behavioral fidelity becomes critical for platform governance and democratic resilience. Previous work demonstrates that LLM-powered agents can replicate aggregate survey responses, yet few studies test whether agents can predict specific individuals’ reactions to specific content. This study benchmarks LLM-based agents’ accuracy in predicting human social media reactions (like, dislike, comment, share, no reaction) across 120,000 + unique agent-persona combinations derived from 1,511 Serbian participants and 27 large language models. In Study 1, agents achieved 70.7% overall accuracy, with LLM choice producing a 13%-point performance spread. Study 2 employed binary forced-choice (like/dislike) evaluation with chance-corrected metrics. Agents achieved Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.29, indicating genuine predictive signal beyond chance. However, conventional text-based supervised classifiers using TF-IDF representations outperformed LLM agents (MCC of 0.36), indicating that the predictive signal derives from semantic text content rather than from any capacity for individualized behavioral simulation. The genuine but modest predictive validity of zero-shot persona-prompted agents suggests that, while current accuracy is insufficient for precise individual targeting, the capacity to predict reactions at rates above chance warrants attention in discussions of AI-driven influence and social simulation methodology. The advantage of zero‑shot agents is that they require no task‑specific training, which makes large‑scale deployment easy across diverse contexts, including election campaigns and mass‑scale manipulation. Limitations include single-country sampling. Future research should explore multilingual testing and fine-tuning approaches.

title: Automated cervical vertebral maturation staging using deep learning: an anatomically guided framework for orthodontic skeletal maturity assessment
abstract: Accurate assessment of skeletal maturity is essential for orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning, particularly when growth-modifying interventions depend on the timing of the pubertal growth spurt. Cervical vertebral maturation (CVM) analysis provides a practical method for skeletal maturity assessment using routine lateral cephalometric radiographs without additional radiation exposure. However, conventional CVM staging remains susceptible to examiner variability, particularly during transitional maturation stages. Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown potential in improving diagnostic consistency in medical imaging, although many previously reported automated CVM systems have relied on relatively small datasets or limited annotation protocols. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an anatomically guided artificial intelligence framework for automated CVM staging. A retrospective dataset of 1,047 anonymised lateral cephalometric radiographs from patients aged 6–17 years was used for model development. CVM stages were determined using the modified Baccetti classification system by calibrated orthodontic examiners following structured consensus procedures. Chronological age and sex were not used as input variables during model development. The dataset was partitioned into training (80%) and internal testing (20%) subsets at the patient level. A two-stage framework consisting of YOLOv8 vertebral localisation followed by Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM)-based morphological classification was implemented. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic analysis, and Cohen’s kappa statistics. Independent testing was performed using 30 previously unseen radiographs. Inter- and intra-examiner reliability demonstrated excellent agreement, with ICC values ranging from 0.946 to 0.967 and Cohen’s kappa values ranging from 0.852 to 0.891. The proposed framework achieved an adjacent-stage accuracy of 96.67% and an exact-stage accuracy of 80.00% on the independent testing dataset. Most misclassifications occurred between adjacent maturation stages, particularly between Stages III and IV. Cohen’s kappa analysis demonstrated substantial to near-perfect agreement between automated predictions and expert consensus. The proposed framework demonstrated promising performance for automated CVM staging using an anatomically guided two-stage architecture trained on calibrated expert annotations. While substantial agreement with expert consensus was observed within the study dataset, the findings should be interpreted as preliminary due to the retrospective design and limited independent testing sample. Further multicentre validation and prospective evaluation are required before routine clinical implementation.

title: Neural responses to AIGC based on the associative propositional evaluation model
abstract: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content (AIGC) can improve production efficiency and reduce creation costs, but consumer evaluations of AIGC applications remain mixed. Based on the Associative-Propositional Evaluation (APE) model, we used event-related potentials (ERPs) to examine consumers’ automatic neural responses and behavioral judgments of AIGC applications across different levels of emotional engagement.Pairing positive adjectives with AIGC content elicited more negative N2 amplitudes, which reflects early cognitive conflict or mismatch during associative-dominant processing. In high-emotional-engagement scenarios, negative adjectives triggered more negative N2 amplitudes than in low-emotional conditions, showing that early evaluative processing is modulated by the application context.Behaviorally, acceptance rates for negative adjectives were higher than for positive adjectives in low-emotional scenarios, meaning implicit responses differ across emotional contexts.These findings offer preliminary neurophysiological evidence for AIGC evaluation, but the results should be interpreted with caution. The N2 component primarily indexes early cognitive conflict, and is not a process-specific marker of definitive attitude valence. The study uses a small, non-probability volunteer sample, which limits the generalizability of the findings. Future research needs to replicate these effects with larger, more representative populations to validate the results.

title: A trustworthy anatomically-guided region-aware deep learning framework for automated Alzheimer’s disease classification from brain MRI
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative condition that gradually deteriorates the function of cognitive abilities accompanied by irreversible degeneration of brain tissues. Accurate AD diagnoses based on brain MRI are still complicated by the small-scale anatomical changes of the brain, subtocol variability, structural complexity, and overlapped features between the various stages of the disease. In consequence, it makes difficulties in discriminative identification of neurodegenerative biomarkers, reliable classification, weak generalizability, and low confidence for automated diagnostic algorithms. To cope with these problems, this study proposes a novel framework of Trustworthy Anatomically-guided Intelligent Region-aware Alzheimer’s Disease (TAIRA), which is based on region-aware feature representation, adaptive learning, and explainable intelligence in an end-to-end manner. Proposed Attention-guided Region-Aware Residual Dense Network (ARA-RDNet) automatically focuses on sensitive brain regions and extracts discriminative neurodegenerative features with multi-scales by utilizing the methods of spatial attention, channel attention, residual dense connection, and context feature fusion. Moreover, an Adaptive Flatness Guided Convergence Optimizer (AFGCO) is devised for increasing convergence stability, minimizing overfitting problems, and enhancing generalization capabilities. In order to increase the transparency of the model, a Grad-CAM + + explainability approach is utilized, which is validated by conducting perturbation stability testing, faithfulness testing, and localization consistency testing. Classification accuracy on the AA MRI and OASIS datasets was reported as 98.52% and 98.79%, respectively. These results reveal that the proposed approach is capable of recognizing disease-related anatomical patterns, providing reliable Alzheimer’s disease classification.

title: Hybrid intensity normalization and translation network for structure-preserving intensity normalization in medical imaging
abstract: Intensity generalization among the training and test images of one modality from different vendors is the key for better performance of deep learning models. During inference, deep learning classifiers trained on chest X-rays from one scanner often fail when applied to images from a different scanner due to contrast variations. With Shenzhen–Montgomery tuberculosis benchmark, the drop can be as large as 0.95 to 0.73 in AUC. We present HINT-Net, a single-generator framework for unpaired, multi-domain intensity normalization of medical images. The architecture builds on a U-Net backbone and introduces two mechanisms: (i) Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) layers that conditions every encoder and decoder stage on a target-domain vector so that one model can serve any number of domains without retraining and (ii) an Additive Spatial Gate (ASG) at the bottleneck that learns a pixel-level intensity correction map to suppress scanner-specific artifacts while leaving anatomy intact. Training combines a hybrid loss of adversarial, Patch-based Noise Contrastive Estimation (PatchNCE), Structural similarity Index (SSIM), Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), and gradient terms. On paired synthetic intensity domains from NIH ChestX-ray14, HINT-Net reaches SSIM above 0.98, LPIPS below 0.008, and Peak Signal-to-noise Ratio (PSNR) above 34 dB-outperforming CycleGAN by 3.3% in SSIM with 86% lower LPIPS. On the unpaired Shenzhen–Montgomery benchmark it achieves SSIM of 0.78 (versus 0.74 for CycleGAN) and raises area under the curve of tuberculosis detection from 0.64 to 0.91 with AlexNet and from 0.78 to 0.97 with ResNet-18.

title: Non-standard proteins in the lens of AlphaFold 3: a case study of amyloids
abstract: While three-dimensional structures of globular and transmembrane forms are available for many amyloid proteins, structures of their amyloid forms are scarce in the PDB. Amyloids pose major challenges for both experimental structure determination and computational modelling. We evaluated how AlphaFold 3 (AF3) performs for amyloid proteins using three datasets: Positive-control dataset ( n = 153, amyloid sequences without experimentally determined 3D amyloid structure), Negative-control ( n = 56, non-amyloid peptides). ResolvedAmyloidStructure ( n = 7, 3D amyloid structure is known). Amyloid structures were predicted for 34% of the Positive-control dataset, but unfortunately also for 54% of Negative-control. Amyloid structures were successfully predicted for five out of seven proteins from ResolvedAmyloidStructure . We discuss reasons for the poor performance of AF3 on amyloid proteins and factors that may influence the prediction quality. A correct amyloid structure prediction is more likely to be obtained for shorter fragments. AF3 performance in prediction of amyloid structures seems hindered by low abundance of amyloid structures in the PDB and high prevalence of structure data for their non-amyloid forms. This seems to lead to AF3 tendency to assign a higher quality score to globular oligomeric models than to the amyloid ones. Our work also suggests the steps needed to achieve a better performance in the near future.

title: Evaluating walkability and vitality in cold-region historic districts of China via street view semantics and SHAP
abstract: As historic districts undergo sustainable urban regeneration, enhancing walkability is important for supporting local vitality. However, conventional walkability evaluation frameworks often emphasize openness and may not fully account for the climate-adaptive characteristics of compact spatial configurations in severe cold regions. Moreover, traditional linear models may overlook nonlinear and threshold-like relationships between micro-scale built environments and population vitality. To address these gaps, this study developed an integrated framework combining Street View Imagery, points of interest (POIs), and Location-Based Services (LBS) thermal data to evaluate two typical historic districts, Buzili and Dajingmen, in Zhangjiakou, China. DeepLabV3 + semantic segmentation and K-Means clustering were used to characterize street-view environments and identify spatial patterns, while Random Forest regression coupled with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was employed to examine nonlinear associations between built-environment characteristics and population vitality. The prediction model achieved an \(\:{R}^{2}\) of 0.736, with an RMSE of 4.22 and an MAE of 2.94. Global SHAP analysis identified POI Density (mean absolute SHAP = 3.0496) and Functional Mix (2.1150) as the dominant predictors, followed by Walkable Space Ratio (0.9645) and Green View Index (0.6504). The POI-density relationship exhibited a reproducible nonlinear transition around the standardized range of approximately 0.067–0.083, whereas GVI showed a robust J-shaped response pattern across bootstrap models, but with substantial uncertainty in the exact turning-point location. Walkable Space Ratio showed a predominantly negative nonlinear association with population vitality within the observed study area. These findings suggest that openness-oriented walkability criteria may require climate- and context-specific reconsideration in cold-region historic districts, where compact spatial configurations may be compatible with pedestrian vitality. However, because the LBS observations were collected during the National Day period and no direct winter microclimatic measurements were conducted, the proposed mechanisms should be interpreted as associations rather than direct evidence of thermal adaptation. The findings provide context-specific empirical evidence for differentiated historic-district renewal and highlight the need for multi-season and multi-site validation before these transition ranges can be generalized as planning standards.

title: Quantum computing-enhanced deep learning for real-time detection and mitigation of cyberattack patterns
abstract: Cyberattacks are increasing in sophistication. As a result, traditional cybersecurity systems based on classical computing and conventional deep-learning techniques are increasingly exhibiting limitations and vulnerabilities. Although deep-learning models offer substantial advantages over traditional methods for automated intrusion detection through large-scale security data analysis and pattern recognition, they suffer from notable constraints related to high-dimensional feature spaces, scalability, and stringent real-time inference requirements. This work proposes a quantum-enhanced deep learning (QEDL) framework for detecting and mitigating real-time cyberattack patterns. Quantum computing technologies—specifically quantum feature selection and quantum data encoding—are integrated into a classical–hybrid quantum deep-learning architecture. The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is employed for quantum feature selection to enable efficient identification of discriminative features from high-dimensional cybersecurity datasets. In addition, quantum data encoding exploits superposition and entanglement to process multiple complex inputs simultaneously. The resulting quantum feature representations are processed using parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs), followed by classical deep-learning layers for accurate threat classification. The proposed QEDL framework is evaluated using the CIC–IDS2017 dataset, and its performance is compared against classical deep-learning models and pure quantum neural networks. Experimental results demonstrate that, within the proposed hybrid quantum–classical framework, the QAOA-based feature selection strategy achieved higher classification performance than the evaluated classical feature selection methods under the reported experimental settings. In addition, the proposed framework exhibited improved generalization to previously unseen attacks. These findings suggest that the proposed hybrid quantum–classical framework is a promising approach for cyberattack detection under the experimental conditions considered in this study. The experiments in this study were simulated using IBM Aer backend, without physical quantum hardware. The results obtained in this study serve as a simulation-based proof of concept.

title: A context-aware dynamic model selection framework based on proximal policy optimization for day-ahead PV power forecasting
abstract: To enhance the accuracy of day-ahead photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting and overcome the limited adaptability of individual models under varying weather conditions, this paper proposes a scenario-aware dynamic model selection method based on an actor-critic contextual policy learning approach. The approach first performs cluster analysis on temporal features extracted from meteorological variables that influence PV output, classifying historical weather patterns into four typical scenarios: clear, partly cloudy, overcast, and rainy. A forecasting model library comprising multiple deep learning architectures is then constructed. A reinforcement learning agent based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is trained to learn an optimal policy that dynamically selects the most suitable model from the library according to the day-ahead meteorological features of the target day. By adaptively matching the optimal model to the specific characteristics of each target day, the proposed method substantially improves prediction accuracy. Experimental results on real-world PV data show that the proposed method effectively leverages the complementary strengths of multiple models. Compared with the static optimal strategy, it reduces RMSE by 13.97% overall. These results demonstrate its strong effectiveness and adaptability to complex and variable weather scenarios.
