title: Physically constrained Mamba forecasting supports multiobjective reservoir water quality decisions
abstract: Reservoir water-quality management requires forecasts that remain dynamically plausible and scenario choices that balance water-quality objectives against the magnitude of requested trajectory change. Historical monitoring archives, however, rarely contain labelled control actions. We develop a physics-informed inverse-decision framework that combines a decomposition–interaction Mamba forecaster, observation-space oxygen-balance diagnostics, a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and preference-conditioned multi-objective search. The forecaster separates multiscale dynamics before channel-specific state-space encoding and gated cross-variable exchange. A lumped Streeter–Phelps residual regularises dissolved-oxygen forecasts, while the CVAE represents DO–CODMn recovery changes observed after natural events. Evaluation on Miyun Reservoir observations from June 2021 to January 2025 gives 24-step RMSE values of 0.305 for dissolved oxygen and 0.318 for CODMn. The physical-violation rate, defined as disagreement between predicted and Streeter–Phelps model-implied DO-increment signs, decreases from 8.4% without the two output-space terms to 0.3% with the full model. Fixed-horizon latent search yields a hypervolume of 0.824, compared with 0.706 for NSGA-III and 0.487 for weighted-sum latent search, with no diagnostic-margin crossings in 55 evaluated decisions. Because the archive contains no device-action records, the method returns candidate target trajectories and dimensionless concentration-equivalent demand-and-roughness values, not executable commands or calibrated costs. Prospective use requires independent validation of the physical diagnostic, event generalisation, recursive forecasting and measured actuator response.

title: Identification and validation of T cell proliferation-associated transcriptomic biomarkers in ischemic stroke
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a major global cause of mortality and chronic disability and is associated with complex immune dysfunction. This study aimed to identify T cell proliferation-related genes (TRGs) associated with IS pathogenesis and to identify T cell proliferation-related transcriptomic biomarkers associated with IS and evaluate their ability to distinguish IS from controls. Gene expression profiles from patients with IS were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus. Candidate genes were identified through differential expression analysis by determining differentially expressed genes that overlapped with AmiGO2-derived TRGs. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression and Support Vector Machine-Recursive Feature Elimination selected biomarkers (with validation). The diagnostic performance of these biomarkers was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and nomogram development. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and immune infiltration analyses were performed to characterize the identified biomarkers. Biomarker expression levels were confirmed in clinical samples by Reverse Transcription quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-qPCR). ARG1 and TNFSF13B were consistently upregulated in patients with IS across cohorts and demonstrated strong diagnostic performance (area under the curve [AUC] > 0.7). The AUC for the nomogram model reached 0.92, suggesting favorable predictive performance that warrants further validation. GSEA revealed that ARG1 was positively enriched in CD4 + T cell activation-related sets, while TNFSF13B was negatively enriched in stemness-related sets. The immune profiling revealed that ARG1 was negatively correlated with activated B cells (cor = − 0.63, p < 0.001) and TNFSF13B was inversely associated with activated CD8 + T cells (cor = − 0.34, p < 0.01). RT-qPCR confirmed their higher expression in IS vs controls ( p < 0.05). These findings support ARG1 and TNFSF13B as candidate TRG-related transcriptomic biomarkers for distinguishing IS from controls and provide hypothesis-generating insights into their immune-related biological functions. Given the small RT-qPCR cohort, the experimental validation should be considered preliminary, and larger clinically stratified cohorts are required to further confirm their diagnostic value and biological relevance.

title: Investigating the effect of natural aggregate on asphalt mixture performance by integrating experimental evaluation and explainable machine learning
abstract: Natural aggregate (NA) is commonly incorporated into asphalt mixtures as part of the aggregate skeleton; however, excessive NA content may adversely affect mechanical strength and deformation resistance. This study investigates the influence of NA content on asphalt mixture performance using an integrated experimental, statistical, and explainable machine learning (XML) framework. Asphalt mixtures were prepared using crushed coarse aggregate with varying NA contents of 0%, 4%, 8%, 12%, 16%, 20%, and 24% by weight. The experimental program included Marshall stability and flow, indirect tensile strength (ITS), and wheel tracking tests to evaluate strength and deformation responses. Pearson correlation, ANOVA, and stepwise regression examined relationships between mixture variables and performance indicators. Random Forest (RF) models were then developed to predict mixture performance, achieving strong predictive capability, with testing R 2 values exceeding 0.95 and corresponding MAPE values below 2.5% for all targets. Feature importance identified NA content as the most influential variable governing mixture performance. SHAP and response surface analyses further quantified the contribution of mixture variables and illustrated their combined interaction effects. The obtained results indicated that increasing NA content reduced stability and ITS while increasing flow and rut depth. The findings also revealed that the most pronounced incremental deterioration occurred between 12% and 16% NA, where tensile strength and deformation responses exhibited high sensitivity to increasing NA replacement. This integrated framework supports reliable prediction, engineering interpretation, and informed design decisions for NA-containing asphalt mixtures.

title: A global–local momentum contrastive framework with critical feature calibration for field plant disease identification in precision agriculture
abstract: Plant diseases can substantially affect crop production and food supply stability, making accurate disease identification important for effective crop management. Although deep learning has been widely applied to plant disease recognition, model performance may degrade in complex field environments because of large intra-class variations, subtle inter-class differences, and background interference. To address these challenges, we propose GLC-Net, which integrates global–local momentum contrastive learning with critical feature calibration (CFC) for field plant disease identification. Specifically, a label-guided momentum contrastive learning mechanism is introduced to dynamically construct multiple positive pairs through a labeled queue, thereby promoting intra-class compactness and inter-class separability in the feature space. In addition, a global–local contrastive strategy based on cropped local views is designed to enhance multi-scale representation learning, enabling the model to capture both global contextual information and fine-grained pathological details. Furthermore, the proposed CFC module calibrates global representations using complementary local features, allowing the network to preserve more disease-relevant information under complex background conditions. Experiments on the Paddy and Soybean disease datasets demonstrate that GLC-Net consistently improves recognition performance across different backbone networks and compares favorably with representative existing methods. Ablation and visualization analyses further verify the contributions of the proposed components to feature discrimination and disease-region representation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of GLC-Net for field plant disease identification, while further evaluation across additional crop species and more diverse field conditions remains necessary to establish its broader generalization capability.

title: Exploring artificial intelligence usage preferences among medical students in Iran: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical education, offering opportunities to enhance learning, research, and clinical preparation. Although previous studies have explored medical students’ attitudes and acceptance of AI, evidence regarding their AI usage preferences remains limited, particularly in developing countries where AI integration into medical education is still evolving. Understanding these preferences is essential for designing context-appropriate educational strategies and responsible AI integration. This study aimed to examine the preferences and patterns of AI usage among students at Shiraz University of Medical Sciences (SUMS), Iran. This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among undergraduate and postgraduate students at SUMS. Using stratified random sampling, 384 students were recruited. Data were collected between July and October 2025 using a validated self-administered questionnaire (AI-UPSS; Cronbach’s α = 0.935), assessing AI usage across eight domains. Responses were rated on a 4-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed using one-sample t-tests, independent t-tests, and one-way ANOVA in SPSS version 24, with a cutoff mean score of 2.5. The highest mean preference scores were observed in Research & Writing (Mean = 2.66 ± 0.79, p < 0.001) and Self-learning/Education (Mean = 2.61 ± 0.81, p = 0.010). Moderate preferences were found for Curiosity & Entertainment (Mean = 2.36 ± 0.81, p = 0.001) and Health Counseling (Mean = 2.40 ± 0.96, p = 0.044). The lowest scores were reported in Design & Programming (Mean = 1.54 ± 0.79, p < 0.001) and Art (Mean = 1.68 ± 0.77, p < 0.001). Significant gender differences were observed in Art ( p = 0.010), Self-learning ( p = 0.027), and Health Counseling ( p < 0.001). GPA was significantly associated with Content Development ( p = 0.004), Design & Programming ( p = 0.031), and Art ( p = 0.032), with higher usage among students with lower GPAs. Undergraduate students showed significantly higher preferences across several domains, including curiosity and health counseling ( p < 0.01). Medical students primarily use AI for academic, research, and self-directed learning purposes, while engagement with technical and creative applications remains limited. AI usage preferences are influenced by academic level, gender, and GPA rather than age or field of study. These findings underscore the need for structured, level-specific AI education to promote effective and ethical AI integration in medical curricula.

title: Assessment of AI development level in construction cost management using AHP- cloud model: a case study of China’s Yangtze River Delta Region
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration is crucial for solving traditional inefficiencies and data fragmentation in construction cost management, driven by the demands of Industry 4.0. However, a significant gap exists in holistically evaluating AI development levels, lacking a framework and empirical analysis that systematically bridges macro-environmental factors and micro-organizational readiness. This study aims to assess the AI development level in construction cost management across China’s Yangtze River Delta (YRD) region. A novel PEST-O (political, economic, social and technological-organizational) framework was established, and an integrated Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and cloud model approach was used to analyze expert data. Findings indicate the YRD’s overall AI development is “average” (Ex = 52.71), revealing a critical imbalance. Although the Political dimension shows strong support, the organizational, technological, and social dimensions remain “worse,” confirming organizational incapacity as the primary bottleneck. Regionally, Shanghai and Zhejiang significantly outperform Jiangsu and Anhui. This research theoretically validates the PEST-O model and provides quantitative diagnosis. Practically, the findings of this research provide policymakers and other stakeholders with a diagnostic tool tailored to specific regions. They also help facilitate the implementation of differentiated measures for leading and lagging regions.

title: Explainable machine learning for shear capacity prediction of reinforced concrete deep beams
abstract: The shear capacity prediction of reinforced concrete (RC) deep beams remains a challenging issue in design of concrete structures. Although the code-based strut-and-tie method is widely accepted, it is often time-consuming for routine design applications, while existing empirical equations are unable to fully capture the highly nonlinear interactions among material properties, geometric characteristics, and reinforcement variables. To address this limitation, this study proposes an explainable machine learning framework for predicting the shear capacity of RC deep beams. A comprehensive database of 419 experimentally tested specimens was compiled from the literature, and eight supervised machine learning models were developed with hyperparameters optimized using the Optuna framework. Comparative analysis showed that the optimized Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) model achieved the best predictive performance, with a test coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.93. A synthetic Gaussian input-perturbation study was conducted to assess the numerical sensitivity of the models under progressively disturbed inputs. To interpret the black-box behavior of the model, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and three-dimensional Partial Dependence Plots (3D-PDPs) were employed. The resulting feature-response patterns were broadly consistent with established deep-beam behavior, particularly the positive effect of concrete compressive strength and the negative influence of the shear-span-to-depth ratio, along with important nonlinear interactions among key variables. Finally, a user-friendly graphical user interface integrating the optimized GBDT model was developed to provide rapid and interpretable shear-capacity estimation for practical engineering applications.

title: A QMIX-driven routing protocol for dynamic Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks
abstract: Reliable and energy-efficient data collection remains a fundamental challenge in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks (UASNs) owing to limited battery capacity, high propagation delay, dynamic network topology and unreliable communication links. To address these challenges, we propose a Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CMARL)-based data routing framework for dynamic UASNs. The routing problem is modeled as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP), where each relay node acts as an autonomous routing agent using locally available information. The framework adopts a Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm, in which cooperative routing policies are learned using the QMIX algorithm and executed through trained local Q -networks. Each agent constructs its local observation from residual energy, relative forwarding progress towards the sink, estimated link quality and neighboring node availability, while the action space consists of cooperative next-hop selection. A UASN-oriented reward function that jointly optimizes packet delivery reliability, energy efficiency and network lifetime by encouraging reliable packet forwarding and discouraging inefficient routing decisions. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms representative routing protocols across key metrics - packet delivery rate, end-to-end delay, and network lifetime, providing an effective, scalable and intelligent routing solution for next-generation UASNs.

title: Bearing capacity and safety factors of ring foundations in spatially variable soils: a hybrid FELA-machine learning approach
abstract: Ring foundations efficiently support axisymmetric structures like silos, storage tanks, chimneys, and cooling towers with reduced concrete volume compared to solid circular foundations. Their ultimate bearing capacity is strongly affected by asymmetric loading and spatial variability in soil properties. This study presents a hybrid machine learning framework to predict normalized bearing capacity factors and safety factors for ring foundations in spatially variable cohesive-frictional (c-φ) soils. Datasets were generated via finite element limit analysis (FELA) in OptumG2, incorporating random field modeling of effective cohesion (c’) (lognormal, depth-linear mean: µ c’ = 10 kPa, k = 1 kPa/m, COV = 0.3) and friction angle (φ’ up to 40°). Four loading configurations (complete, internal half, middle half, external half), inner-to-outer radius ratios of 0–0.9, rough/smooth interfaces, and nine anisotropic scale-of-fluctuation cases (horizontal: 10–60 m; vertical: 2–8 m) were analyzed. A Convolutional Neural Network processed random field images and parameters, achieving R² > 0.95 and relative errors < 3%. External half and complete loading gave highest capacities; internal half reduced them by up to 40%. Spatial variability in c’ and φ’ contracted failure envelopes by 10–25%, emphasizing reliability-based design. The framework dramatically reduces computational cost versus traditional FELA/Monte Carlo while retaining accuracy, supporting preliminary design, optimization, and risk assessment.

title: Enhancing network science with large language models and federated artificial intelligence
abstract: Sixth generation (6G) networks require intelligent and privacy-preserving solutions to handle traffic complexity, resource allocation, and security challenges. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer advanced reasoning and Federated Artificial Intelligence (FAI) enables distributed learning without directly sharing raw data, their combined application in large-scale network science remains limited. Key issues include non-IID data, decision latency, and limited robustness of centralized models. To address these challenges, this work introduces FALCON-6G (Federated AI and LLM-Oriented Cognitive Optimization in 6G Networks), a novel framework for distributed anomaly detection, traffic prediction, and adaptive resource management. Experiments conducted under federated learning settings with 50 participating clients and 200 global communication rounds on two Open RAN and four intrusion detection datasets show a 22.7% average relative improvement in throughput prediction accuracy and a 17.6% reduction in decision latency compared with FedAvg, along with up to a 23.9% relative improvement in intrusion detection F1-score over FedAvg and a 34.0% reduction in communication overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of FALCON-6G for privacy-aware 6G network optimization. The current evaluation is primarily based on benchmark datasets, and validation in live large-scale 6G/O-RAN environments remains an important direction for future work.

title: Person-independent and cross-dataset evaluation of convolutional and recurrent architectures for eye movement classification
abstract: Classifying eye movements into fixations, saccades, and smooth pursuits is a basic step in the analysis of gaze recordings. Deep models are now common for this task, but they are often evaluated on windows that share participants between training and test sets, which leaves open how well they work for people the model has not seen. This paper reports a person-independent comparison of three architectures—a one-dimensional CNN, an LSTM, and a CNN–LSTM hybrid—for four-class eye movement classification on the GazeCom dataset (54 participants, 250 Hz, expert frame-level annotations). Each model is trained and tested under leave-one-person-out cross-validation, so every participant is held out in turn, and each architecture is run with two input representations: raw gaze position and a derived set that adds velocity, acceleration, and angular change. Model differences are assessed at the participant level (paired tests over 54 folds, Holm-corrected) rather than on overlapping windows. Two findings are consistent across the study. First, recurrent modeling is what separates the strong models from the weak one: the LSTM and the hybrid reach a macro-F1 of about 0.82 with the derived input, while the CNN reaches 0.71, and the gap holds for every participant. Second, adding the convolutional front end to the LSTM does not help: the hybrid and the plain LSTM are statistically indistinguishable with the raw input and separated by less than 0.01 macro-F1 with the derived input, so the extra component is not warranted by the data; the hybrid carries about 70% more parameters than the LSTM for no measurable gain. The derived input improves every architecture, most for the CNN and for the smooth-pursuit class. Three non-learned or lightweight baselines (velocity threshold, velocity–dispersion, and a Random Forest on kinematic features), tuned per fold and evaluated under the same protocol, stay near 0.53–0.54 macro-F1 on the fixation/saccade/pursuit task, well below all three deep models. When the GazeCom-trained models are tested without retraining on the Lund2013 recordings and scored against both expert raters, accuracy falls as expected, but the ordering of the architectures is preserved. The plain LSTM is therefore an adequate model for this task; the smooth-pursuit class remains the main source of error and is the most useful target for future work.

title: Lymphocyte-predominant inflammation refines lung histopathology scoring in preclinical respiratory viral infection: support from deep learning analysis
abstract: Respiratory viral infections such as influenza and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) remain major causes of morbidity and mortality. Although lung histopathology is a major endpoint in preclinical studies, conventional H&E-based grading primarily evaluates the extent of inflammatory-cell infiltration and may not distinguish progressive from resolving disease. Here, we investigated whether inflammatory-cell composition could refine lung histopathology assessment using convolutional neural network (CNN)-based analysis. In SARS-CoV-2 mouse cohorts, systemic disease severity was classified according to body-weight loss and splenic white-pulp atrophy. H&E-based inflammatory-cell infiltration scores and CNN-derived inflammatory-cell-rich areas did not fully correspond to systemic disease status in several infection and vaccine-challenge settings. In contrast, lesions associated with lower disease-severity or recovery-phase states were enriched in lymphocytes and CD8⁺ T cells, whereas higher disease-severity or lethal-phase lesions showed macrophage- and neutrophil-rich patterns. A two-step CNN workflow that detected inflammatory-cell-rich regions and subsequently classified them as recovery-like or lethal-like supported this composition-based distinction across independent SARS-CoV-2 cohorts. Similar lymphocyte- and CD8⁺ T-cell–enriched inflammatory patterns were also observed during recovery in influenza A infection. These findings support lymphocyte predominance as a practical histopathologic parameter that complements conventional inflammatory-cell infiltration scoring in murine respiratory viral infection models.

title: Impulsivity, cognitive inflexibility, and brain network dysregulation in etomidate use disorder: A clinical and EEG microstate study
abstract: Etomidate, a short-acting GABA_A receptor modulator and emerging novel psychoactive substance, is increasingly abused non-medically. Despite rising clinical concern, the neuropsychological profiles of etomidate use disorder (EUD) remain poorly characterized, prompting this systematic investigation of its clinical and neurophysiological features. 152 individuals with EUD and 67 age-matched healthy controls (HC) were recruited. Participants completed a series of standardized assessments measuring craving, impulsivity, inhibitory control, and habitual behavior. Resting-state EEG data were analyzed using microstate analysis to characterize the temporal organization of large-scale brain activity, and a multidimensional feature-based support vector machine (SVM) model was built to distinguish EUD from HC. The EUD group exhibited significantly higher craving and impulsivity, and poorer performance on stop-signal and reversal learning tasks. Microstate analysis revealed significantly longer durations of microstates B, C, and D and reduced occurrence of microstate A in the EUD group. SVM classification achieved an AUC of 0.777. This is the first comprehensive characterization of EUD, demonstrating distinct clinical features and alterations in the temporal organization of large-scale brain activity. These findings characterize cross-sectional clinical and neurophysiological features associated with EUD and highlight the potential value of EEG microstate analysis to probe such brain network temporal changes.

title: Reservoir eutrophication prediction with explainable framework integrating temporal convolutional networks and bidirectional sequence modeling
abstract: Accurate prediction of total nitrogen (TN) concentration in dam reservoirs is recognized as one of the significant challenges in water resources management. In this regard, the present study, to develop an intelligent and robust modeling framework, introduced the integrated model, which consists of the combination of the improved variational mode decomposition algorithm (IVMD), the attention mechanism-based temporal convolutional neural network (AttTCN), the bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU), and the grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA), which is used to predict the total nitrogen of Mahabad Dam. The results of this study suggest that the proposed framework has a significant advantage over conventional models, as the analysis of the indices indicated that, with each layer of complexity added to the model, prediction accuracy improved significantly. The 80% reduction in the mean absolute error value from the basic BiGRU model to the final IVMD-GOA-AttTCN-BiGRU model, along with the improvement of Willmott’s index of agreement from 0.75 to 0.99, confirms the superiority of the proposed integrated approach. This significant improvement in accuracy demonstrated that the intelligent combination of data preprocessing, an attention mechanism, and hyperparameter optimization can yield models with greater reliability in water quality prediction. The use of interaction terms such as turbidity × pH corrected the systematic bias of the model, which is hydrologically justified. In summary, the proposed framework shows promise as an accurate prediction tool and provides a useful analytical basis for better understanding water quality dynamics in the Mahabad reservoir, subject to further validation with larger datasets.

title: Operationalizing biological interpretability in health-related visual stimuli using multimodal artificial intelligence as standardized non-human raters
abstract: Evaluation and assessment research in health communication requires structured, construct-based approaches for interpreting visual materials. This study introduces the Asclepius Biological Interpretability Scale, developed through a two-stage modified Delphi process (a joint image-and-item panel followed by an independent item-only panel) grounded in the Biopsychosocial Model and Visual Literacy Theory, and examines whether multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) systems can reproducibly apply this framework relative to internally generated human reference scores. Six artworks (four health-themed and two controls) were evaluated by three multimodal AI models and four researchers (internal human reference) using a standardized protocol with independent researcher-operated accounts, memory-isolation procedures, repeated assessments over two days, and the final 20-item scale. Because Image Type varied across only six stimuli, health-themed versus control differences were summarized at the image level (Cohen’s d), human–AI differences were summarized descriptively at the rater level, and reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Spearman correlations. Within this development image set, AI-generated scores were descriptively higher for health-themed than for control images on the three biomedical subscales (image-level Cohen’s d = 0.91–1.38) but not on Non-Medical Interpretability (d = 0.49); with four health-themed and two control images, these differences were not statistically significant ( p = 0.19–0.60). Reproducibility across researcher-operated accounts was excellent for the three biomedical subscales (ICC = 0.90–0.97) and moderate for Non-Medical Interpretability (ICC = 0.57), whereas agreement across assessment days was poor (ICC = 0.04–0.46). The four researchers’ internal reference scores were higher than the AI-generated scores on the biomedical subscales for health-themed images (mean differences 1.41–1.96 points) and lower on Non-Medical Interpretability (− 2.02 to − 2.19 points). These findings provide preliminary methodological evidence that multimodal AI can reproducibly apply a structured interpretability framework to controlled visual stimuli. Although day-to-day stability and the Non-Medical Interpretability subscale, which showed substantial internal-consistency problems, require further refinement, the results support the feasibility of using AI as standardized non-human raters within controlled methodological settings. Broader validation using authentic health communication materials and independent external human raters remains necessary.

title: A MATLAB-based AI-IoT simulation framework for LSTM-driven smart solar irrigation and renewable energy management
abstract: Smart irrigation offers a great avenue for better water use efficiency, and farming sustainability. However, most of the studies conducted so far tend to concentrate on the monitoring systems and platforms of the Internet of Things (IoT) or on the prediction models based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) (but not on both). To address this gap, this research study proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Internet of Things (IoT) system to predict the water consumption requirements and control the energy produced by a PV system along with a battery State of Charge (SOC) management system, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm, adaptive pump-speed control, and conceptual IoT communication architecture. A dataset of real environmental data from the NASA POWER database was used to test the framework for Egypt’s New Delta region. The LSTM model was able to classify the irrigation pump operating states with an accuracy of 96.11%, a recall of 0.9820, a precision of 0.9100, and an F1-score of 0.9446. It had a better performance than the two models, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) when compared and robustness testing with various independent training runs showed a stable performance in predicting. An estimated annual water-saving rate of 28.57% was obtained relative to the assumed conventional fixed-schedule baseline, while motor energy use was reduced by 74.74% through adaptive pump-speed control. A sensitivity analysis was also performed, showing that the model was stable to moderate variations in environmental and operating conditions. Combined, these findings suggest that the use of AI-based modelling for renewable energy management in the context of an irrigation simulation model built in MATLAB could be a valuable asset in improving irrigation efficiency and lowering water and energy use, which is a promising start for future implementation of hardware versions of intelligent, solar-powered irrigation devices.

title: Uncertainty-aware adaptive fusion with graceful degradation for trustworthy cervical cytology
abstract: Trustworthy cervical cancer screening requires not only accurate classification but also reliable estimation of predictive uncertainty to identify cases that should be referred to clinical experts. This study presents an uncertainty-aware deep learning framework that integrates an ensemble image encoder comprising ResNet50, DenseNet121, and EfficientNet-B0 with dedicated clinical and genomic encoders through an adaptive fusion mechanism. Modality-specific predictions are subsequently combined using a convex weighting scheme driven by predictive entropy estimated via Monte Carlo Dropout. As paired patient-level multimodal data were unavailable, clinical features were derived from an independent risk-factor cohort and genomic features were synthetically generated. The proposed framework serves as a proof-of-concept for uncertainty-guided multimodal fusion. When auxiliary modalities are uninformative, the framework automatically suppresses their influence, maintaining identical test-set predictions across all image-containing configurations, while a static equal-weight baseline reduced the AUC from 0.993 to 0.982. Evaluated on a combined SIPaKMeD and Herlev benchmark of 6,849 cervical-cell images, the framework attains an AUC-ROC of 0.993 (95% CI 0.988–0.997), 97.08% accuracy, 98.07% sensitivity, and 96.08% specificity, with well-calibrated probabilities (Brier 0.025; ECE 0.014). Cross-dataset transfer experiments revealed a notable generalisation gap, highlighting the need for external validation, while confidence-based selective prediction demonstrated the framework’s potential for human-in-the-loop triage.

title: An interpretable ANFIS-NSGA-II framework for evidence-stratified modular wearable risk fusion in elder-health monitoring
abstract: Wearable health monitoring spans fall, cardiac, oxygenation, sleep, mobility, behavioural and long-horizon neurodegenerative indicators that arise from different sensors, labels and time scales. This study presents an evidence-stratified Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System optimized with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (ANFIS-NSGA-II) that fuses module-specific actionability scores into an interpretable monitoring-priority index (MPI) without treating heterogeneous risks as equivalent disease probabilities. Because no synchronized seven-modality older-adult cohort was available, the complete fusion mechanism is evaluated in a controlled subject-indexed synthetic benchmark of 240 subjects and 2,880 observation windows, while real datasets provide module-level evidence and prospective validation targets. The full 3 7 antecedent grid is reduced to a training-derived 64-rule library by an explicitly specified ranking criterion, and the Pareto-selected policy retains 20 active rules. On 48 held-out subjects the frozen policy achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.914 (95% participant-cluster bootstrap CI 0.871–0.948), area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) 0.888 (0.824–0.935), sensitivity 0.868 (0.779–0.935) and specificity 0.751 (0.639–0.832). Paired participant-cluster comparisons show that logistic regression, a generalized additive model, a random forest and a quality-weighted mean all reach discrimination that is statistically indistinguishable from the proposed model after correction for multiple comparisons; the proposed model is significantly better only than a max-risk rule. Ablations show that the 17 mandatory anchor rules alone are significantly worse than the selected policy (AUROC 0.861), that relaxing the anchor requirement lets the optimizer reach significantly higher discrimination with only 8 rules, and that quality-weighted marginalization is preferable to zero-filling but significantly inferior to simple imputation when signal quality is uniformly high, the alternatives converging only when quality is genuinely variable. A scenario analysis that varies interaction strength, interaction identity, label noise, target functional family and the share of escalation propensity driven by unobserved latent state quantifies how much of the reported performance reflects recovery of the authors' own generating mechanism: without label noise the target is deterministic conditional on the seven scores and the generator's subject-level offset, the model attains 72–98% of the oracle discrimination computed from the true propensity, and it exceeds logistic regression in only 1 of 14 scenarios. The contribution is therefore an auditable, reproducible fusion and policy-selection architecture rather than a gain in predictive accuracy, and every quantitative result is a proof-of-concept methodological finding on synthetic data. Prospective synchronized multimodal validation with clinician evaluation remains necessary before any clinical use.

title: Hybrid transformer and CNN for hyperspectral image classification with spectral band selection
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSI) play a vital role in remote sensing applications such as surveillance and precision agriculture, yet they face challenges including limited labeled samples and class imbalance. This paper presents a new method for HSI classification by integrating spectral band selection with advanced deep learning techniques. First, we propose an optimized band selection method alongside data augmentation using crop-and-resize transformations to enhance feature diversity. Second, we introduce a hybrid convolution-transformer framework that combines Vision Transformer (ViT) and 2D-CNN architectures, supplemented with a sequence aggregation layer to mitigate overfitting on small datasets. This hybrid model effectively captures both spatial and spectral features while preserving critical spectral details. Finally, we employ a support vector machine for robust classification. Extensive experiments on three widely used HSI datasets demonstrate that our proposed ViT-CNN-BS framework achieves superior classification accuracy compared to state-of-the-art few-shot learning methods and traditional approaches. Beyond achieving higher accuracy, our approach also reduces computational complexity, making it suitable for resource-constrained applications. The findings highlight the potential of hybrid deep learning frameworks for advancing remote sensing analytics, with possible extensions to environmental monitoring, disaster management, and precision agriculture.
