title: Peripheral serum biomarkers and MRI-derived accelerated brain aging: a cross-sectional study using deep learning-based brain age estimation
abstract: Brain age gap is an emerging neuroimaging marker that captures interindividual variation in brain structural aging. Identifying accessible peripheral biomarkers associated with accelerated brain aging may improve early risk recognition and provide insight into systemic biological processes linked to brain health. This study investigated the associations between routine serum laboratory biomarkers and MRI-derived brain age gap in a health examination cohort. We included 852 participants with available structural MRI and routine laboratory data. Brain age was estimated from structural MRI using a deep learning model, and corrected brain age gap (CorrectedBAG) was derived to reduce age-related prediction bias. We evaluated 25 serum laboratory biomarkers spanning metabolic, immune-inflammatory, hepatic, renal, and bone/nutrition-related domains. Multivariable linear regression was used to examine associations with CorrectedBAG, and restricted cubic spline models were applied to assess potential nonlinear dose-response relationships. Binary logistic regression was further used to evaluate accelerated brain aging defined by brain age gap thresholds. Among the 25 biomarkers examined, serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) showed independent positive associations with CorrectedBAG. Higher ALP was associated with greater CorrectedBAG (β = 0.4073, 95% CI 0.1534–0.6613; P = 0.0017), as was higher NLR (β = 0.2558, 95% CI 0.0164–0.4952; P = 0.0365). In logistic regression analyses, ALP was consistently associated with greater odds of accelerated brain aging defined as BAG > 0 years (OR = 1.011, 95% CI 1.003–1.019; P = 0.010) and BAG > 3 years (OR = 1.013, 95% CI 1.004–1.023; P = 0.006). NLR was also associated with BAG > 3 years (OR = 1.333; P = 0.005). Restricted cubic spline analyses supported approximately linear associations of ALP and NLR with CorrectedBAG. In this Asian health examination cohort, higher serum ALP and NLR were associated with greater MRI-derived brain age gap. These findings suggest that routinely available serum biomarkers may capture peripheral biological processes related to accelerated brain structural aging. Further studies are warranted to clarify the temporal relationships and biological pathways underlying these associations.

title: Interpretable inverse design of optical multilayer thin films based on global neural adjoint
abstract: Existing artificial intelligence methods for the inverse design of optical multilayer thin films (OMTs) often function as “black boxes,” offering limited insight into parameter–performance relationships. We propose the global neural adjoint (GNA) framework, which achieves a strong balance across six criteria: accuracy, efficiency, diversity, scalability, flexibility, and interpretability. At its core is the OMT-mixer, a forward architecture that accurately and efficiently predicts optical properties across diverse material configurations, a predefined set of layer numbers, and thicknesses. By incorporating material and constraint loss functions into the neural adjoint loss, the GNA enables scalable and flexible inverse design, while gradient-based sensitivity profiles quantify the accumulated sensitivity of the design loss to the thickness and material index of each layer during optimization. The OMT-mixer achieves accuracy comparable to transformer-based surrogates while reducing the training time per epoch by approximately 37–42%, and by approximately 61% relative to OptoGPT. Evaluated against a genetic algorithm, GNA without material loss, and OptoGPT across six test spectra and six band-pass-filter targets, the GNA achieves mean accuracy comparable to the strongest reference methods while providing significantly better peak accuracy and substantially greater diversity. Under a fabrication constraint fixing the first layer to 100-nm-thick \(\hbox {SiO}_2\) , the GNA retains significantly better peak accuracy and greater diversity than OptoGPT with top-k sampling, albeit at a higher computational cost. Gradients in the relaxed material space and the effects of rounding and filtering are quantitatively analyzed, while the reliability of the sensitivity profiles is further validated through gradient-aggregation, perturbation, and ablation analyses. These results establish the GNA as a robust, interpretable, and versatile framework for advanced OMT inverse design.

title: A scalable process aware routing architecture for resilient wireless communication in industrial and control networks
abstract: Industrial carbon-capture plants depend on timely and reliable communication among distributed sensors, controllers, and process models. Existing studies commonly examine fault recovery, energy-aware routing, reinforcement learning, or digital-twin monitoring as separate problems, leaving limited evidence on their coordinated use in one reproducible industrial communication framework. This study presents a process-aware MeshStar wireless sensor network (WSN) that combines low-overhead star clusters with redundant mesh links among cluster routers. A tabular Q-learning controller selects recovery and traffic-management actions from network reliability, latency, congestion, residual energy, link availability, and thermal-process criticality. The framework is evaluated through OMNeT++/INET network simulation coupled with a MATLAB/Simulink carbon-capture process model. Thirty independent seeds are used for each method and operating scenario, with comparisons against static Dijkstra, RPL-MRHOF, energy-aware RPL, conventional Q-routing, and deep Q-network routing. Under the revised evaluation protocol, the proposed method achieved a 95th-percentile latency of 84.6 ms, a packet delivery ratio (PDR) of 98.32%, and a route-recovery time of 3.74 s, corresponding to improvements of 12.6%, 0.78 percentage points, and 16.1%, respectively, over the strongest baseline. Scalability, security stress, process stability, and scenario-based economic results are reported separately. Because the validation is software-dominant, the findings demonstrate comparative feasibility rather than field-deployment readiness.

title: An enhanced model-based EEG source imaging method captures dynamic changes during motor skill learning
abstract: Understanding brain reorganization during motor learning requires methods with both high temporal and spatial resolution. We developed an enhanced model-based approach to solve the EEG inverse problem that combines a multi-layer perceptron neural network with finite element modeling for subject-specific head conductivity estimation. The framework resolves up to six simultaneously active sources across 116 cortical and subcortical regions and achieves 85.98% source localization accuracy, outperforming existing methods (67.1% accuracy, 1 even under varying noise conditions. A dedicated leakage analysis using single- and multi-region simulations confirmed minimal cross-talk between cortical motor and deep subcortical/cerebellar sources, supporting reliable separation of activity across brain depths. As a proof-of-concept application, we used this framework to analyze EEG data from five healthy adults performing a novel foot-drawing motor learning task across multiple sessions, with behavioral performance improving after the fourth session. Model-based source estimates revealed a broad reorganization of cortical and subcortical activity across sessions, consistent with functional refinement of motor networks with practice; given the small cohort ( n = 5), these findings are preliminary and offered as suggestive of learning-related dynamics rather than definitive evidence. This enhanced model-based EEG source localization approach offers a practical, non-invasive method for combining computational modeling with neuroimaging of motor behavior.

title: Physics-informed learning detects islanding and discriminates power-quality disturbances in grid-forming inverter-dominated distribution networks
abstract: The proliferation of grid-forming (GFM) inverters in modern distribution networks has fundamentally altered the islanding-detection problem. Unlike grid-following converters, droop- and virtual-synchronous-generator (VSG)-controlled GFM units actively regulate voltage and frequency, suppressing the very deviations that conventional passive schemes rely upon and thereby enlarging the non-detection zone (NDZ) under near-balanced power conditions. This paper proposes a Physics-Informed Lightning-Search-Optimised Temporal Attention Network (PI-LSO-TAN) that jointly detects unintentional islanding and discriminates it from power-quality disturbances (PQDs) and non-islanding faults in GFM-dominated feeders. The framework fuses a physics-informed feature set rate-of-change-of-frequency (ROCOF) estimated from the analytic signal, total harmonic distortion, phase-jump and current-imbalance descriptors with a raw-window convolutional embedding processed by a self-attention pooling layer. A Lightning Search Algorithm (LSA) simultaneously optimises the network hyperparameters and a physics-informed decision threshold, removing manual tuning. Across 10 independent dataset realisations of a documented, fully reproducible synthetic GFM feeder operated in the near-balanced NDZ regime, PI-LSO-TAN attains a four-class test accuracy of 96.34% (SD 0.96 percentage points), a macro-F1 of 0.9636 and an islanding recall of 93.49% at an islanding false-positive rate of 0.70%, misdeclaring 2.40 of 175 power-quality windows as islanding. Two findings define what the method does and does not contribute. First, when ten baselines spanning kernel, ensemble, convolutional, recurrent, attention-based and graph architectures are given the identical physics-informed side-channel, all 11 models fall within 1.20 percentage points of one another; none of the 6 deep sequence architectures differs significantly from the proposed model under Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests, and of the ten baselines only 1 differ significantly at all MLP-SVM hybrid, ahead by up to 0.73 percentage points these being among the simplest feature-space classifiers in the comparison. On this task the discriminative power resides in the physics-informed representation rather than in the temporal-modelling mechanism. Substituting an alternative fourteen-dimensional representation confirms this directly principal components of the raw window reach 52.37%, wavelet band energies 73.60%, generic statistics 62.94%, and a purely learned embedding 30.17%, against 96.20% for the physics-informed set. Second, noise resilience is a property of the training distribution, not of the architecture: training at a single SNR leaves accuracy at 52.18% when the measurement noise floor moves to 30dB, whereas sampling the training SNR across 15 dB to 50 dB restores 88.79% at 30dB and 84.54% at 20dB for a cost of − 6.14 percentage points at the nominal operating point. The practical contribution is protective rather than architectural. A security-calibrated passive over/under-frequency, ROCOF and over/under-voltage relay detects none of the 3872 scanned near-balanced islanding events, leaving a 100.0% non-detection area, whereas the proposed detector reduces it to 0.00%, with no cell of the power-mismatch plane falling below 87.5% detection. Measured sliding-window detection latency is 80 ms on average and 130 ms at the 95th percentile, inside the 2 s envelope of IEEE 1547-2018 and IEC 62116, at 337 μsof computation per window and 28.7 kB of parameters. The results indicate that reliable anti-islanding protection in inverter-dominated grids is obtained by pairing a physics-informed representation with noise-augmented training, and that the resulting detector covers a region of the operating plane in which conventional passive protection is blind by construction.

title: Data-driven optimization and multiscale characterization of sustainable epoxy-benzoxazine hybrid composites for high-performance structural applications
abstract: The polymer composites with enhanced mechanical, thermal, and tribological properties are increasingly important for advanced structural applications. In this study, hybrid composites based on an epoxy-benzoxazine matrix reinforced with basalt fibers (BF), waste cotton textile fibers (WCTF), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) were developed. Optimization of BF content, WCTF content, GNP loading, and curing temperature for tensile strength, flexural strength, impact strength, and Shore D was performed using a Taguchi L9 experimental design. The optimized composite (30% BF, 10% WCTF, 1% GNPs, and a curing temperature of 160 °C) achieved a tensile strength of 138 MPa, flexural strength of 208 MPa, impact strength of 42 kJ m⁻², and Shore D hardness of 87. In addition, the optimized composite exhibited a storage modulus of 5.2 GPa and a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 132 °C. FTIR, AFM, FESEM with EDS, DMA, DSC, TGA, and wear analyses supported enhanced matrix-reinforcement interactions, improved interfacial adhesion, and favorable thermomechanical and tribological performance. Random Forest and XGBoost machine learning models were created for predicting the composite properties, and XGBoost yielded the highest prediction accuracy (R² = 0.9870–0.993). The proposed experimental, statistical, and machine learning strategy is effective for the design of high-performance epoxy–benzoxazine hybrid composites for applications in structural engineering.

title: Two-stage classification of glioma subtypes using a hybrid CNN-ViT model
abstract: Gliomas are among the most serious brain tumor types due to their aggressive behavior. Recent advances in automated methods for early brain tumor detection that analyze whole-slide images of brain tissue enable rapid and precise diagnosis. Therefore, we propose a hybrid approach combining a convolutional neural network and a vision transformer for deep analysis of whole-slide patches. This hybrid model employs a two-stage classification strategy to address highly imbalanced class distributions. The first stage uses a binary-label classifier to label patches as either normal or abnormal. The second stage employs a multi-label classifier to classify abnormal patches into their corresponding glioma subtypes. We evaluated the two-stage hybrid model on an imbalanced test set, achieving the highest balanced accuracy (95.31%), macro-averaged precision (96.08%), and macro-averaged F1-score (95.51%). The two-stage classification approach addressed class imbalance. Furthermore, the hybrid model, which combines a convolutional neural network and a vision transformer, captured deeper features, achieving superior performance and outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

title: An integrated explainable machine learning framework for prediction explanation and audit in high stakes binary classification
abstract: Machine learning classifiers are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision systems, yet their opacity creates governance risks that undermine accountability and trust. This study proposes an integrated framework unifying predictive modelling, explainability, and model auditing, evaluated on a primary public tabular dataset (Lending Club) and an independent benchmark dataset (Give Me Some Credit) drawn from the consumer-credit domain. The framework enforces a strict decision-time feature-availability policy under which all post-origination repayment variables are excluded, defines default over a fixed 24-month outcome horizon, and combines class-imbalance handling, seven benchmark classifiers (including a traditional scorecard), probability-calibration assessment, global and local explainability analysis with quantified SHAP–LIME agreement, and a six-dimension audit covering performance stability, feature reasonableness, error structure, subgroup fairness screening, threshold policy, and robustness to missing inputs. On the temporally held-out Lending Club test set, LightGBM achieved the strongest discrimination, with an AUC-ROC of 0.8451 (95% CI 0.8421–0.8481), AUC-PR of 0.6118, F1-score of 0.6097, and KS statistic of 0.5127; its advantage over CatBoost was not statistically significant, whereas both exceeded the non-boosting baselines. A similar ordering was observed on the independent benchmark, where severe class imbalance made AUC-PR more informative than accuracy. SHAP explanations identified interest rate, loan grade, revolving utilization, debt-to-income ratio, credit-history length, and income as the dominant predictors, and SHAP–LIME attributions agreed strongly across a systematic evaluation sample (mean Spearman correlation 0.84). The audit revealed stable cross-validation performance, mild temporal drift, adequate post-calibration reliability, and elevated false-positive rates for low-income and short-credit-history subgroups; because the datasets contain no directly observed protected attributes, these results constitute socioeconomic subgroup screening rather than a demonstration of demographic fairness. The study shows that predictive performance, interpretability, calibration, and auditability can be jointly evaluated in a single reproducible workflow, providing an operational technical-audit template that complements, but does not replace, legal and institutional review.

title: An explainable machine learning model based on ultrasound and clinical features for impacted gallstone
abstract: Impacted gallstones present a severe form of gallstones. Although positional adjustment during ultrasound examination has well-established clinical utility for evaluating stone impaction, there are still differences between the preoperative diagnosis results and the intraoperative findings. Machine-learning model may help accurate diagnosis prior to surgery. This retrospective cohort study included 1119 patients with gallbladder neck or duct stone. They underwent cholecystectomy to verify the stones were impacted or not. Fifteen candidate variables were evaluated, encompassing ultrasound features and clinical indicators. Six supervised algorithms were constructed with tenfold cross validation. Model performance was evaluated by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis, and interpretability was assessed with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Nine variables were retained, including C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, Alkaline phosphatase, γ-glutamyltranspeptidase, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, gallbladder’s length and Length/Width, wall thickness, stone Length/Width. The GBM model exhibited the best performance with an AUC of 0.951 (95% CI: 0.930–0.973), and the lowest Brier score (0.1561) in the internal validation set. A proof-of-concept web calculator was developed to explore individualized risk assessment. The GBM model shows promise in identifying impacted gallstones preoperatively. Pending external validation, this tool may assist clinicians in making more precise decisions.

title: TriAlign UDA for hybrid domain adaptation of frozen histopathology foundation model representations
abstract: Foundation models produce strong patch-level representations in histopathological image analysis; however, domain shifts across different centers, staining protocols, and scanner conditions can limit the direct generalizability of these representations. In this study, a hybrid feature-level unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework called TriAlign-UDA, which operates on frozen histopathology foundation model representations, is proposed. TriAlign-UDA aims to reduce the mismatch between the labeled source domain and the completely unlabeled target domain without requiring encoder fine-tuning. The method combines statistical alignment, prototype-based semantic preservation, and adversarial adaptation components within a common learning framework based on a bottleneck residual adapter. In the experiments, NCT-CRC-HE-100K was used as the labeled source domain, TCGA-COAD/READ as the unlabeled target domain, and CRC-VAL-HE-7K as the independent external evaluation dataset. In the results obtained over five different seeds, TriAlign-UDA reached the highest mean accuracy of 0.9669 ± 0.0050, balanced accuracy of 0.9560 ± 0.0063, and Macro-F1 of 0.9515 ± 0.0067 on CRC-VAL-HE-7K among the evaluated methods, including the recent EUDA and PLADA-f baselines. DANN and EUDA produced closely competitive results; however, the differences between TriAlign-UDA and DANN, EUDA, or PLADA-f did not reach statistical significance. These findings indicate that frozen-feature UDA should be evaluated not only through individual alignment objectives but also through independent external generalization performance.

title: Uncertainty-aware estimation of compressive strength for fly ash concrete with enhanced probabilistic prediction performance by incorporating the associated mortar strength
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has been widely utilized to estimate the compressive strength ( f c ) of fly ash (FA) concrete due to its high efficiency and accuracy. However, the inherent variability in concrete materials introduces significant uncertainty in f c value, which traditional deterministic ML models cannot quantify. To address this engineering problem, this study proposes to adopt natural gradient boosting (NGBoost), a renowned probabilistic ML model, to estimate f c for FA concrete. Normal distribution-based prediction interval is determined to quantify model uncertainty. Furthermore, the associated mortar strength of the FA concrete is incorporated into NGBoost as an additional feature to evaluate its impact on prediction performance and to explore underlying mechanisms. Results demonstrate that including mortar strength (Model 2) improves the generalization performance of NGBoost compared to excluding it (Model 1). Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) reveal that for the deterministic interpretation, adding mortar strength does not significantly alter the variation trends between original features and their corresponding SHAP values. Mortar strength itself exhibits a strong positive correlation with its SHAP value, allowing Model 2 to capture variations in f c more accurately with an improved coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.921 on the testing dataset. For the probabilistic interpretation, incorporating mortar strength inevitably introduces some uncertainty, with its mean absolute SHAP value of 0.12 MPa in Model 2, but it significantly reduces uncertainties for other features, decreasing their corresponding values by 0.17–0.33 MPa. Consequently, Model 2 attains better probabilistic prediction performance, with a negative log-likelihood of 3.802 on the testing dataset. This study offers a new perspective for observing the reduction and redistribution of uncertainty in ML models and provides a new method for the probabilistic prediction of the strength of FA concrete.

title: Machine learning-based association analysis and cross-sectional classification of physical exercise behaviors and mental health among vocational medical students
abstract: Psychological distress is common among vocational medical students, yet how multidimensional exercise behavior relates to their mental health remains coarsely described. This cross-sectional study surveyed 1,127 students at three vocational medical colleges in China between September and November 2024, applying machine learning to two analytically separate tasks: describing association patterns between exercise profiles and psychological status, and classifying concurrent psychological risk. Exercise behavior was measured with the IPAQ Short Form plus purpose-written items on modality, motivation, social context and temporal regularity; psychological status with the GAD-7, PHQ-9, PSS-10 and SWLS, combined into three ordered categories that are operational rather than diagnostic. Random forest ranking, Apriori rule mining and K-Means profiling agreed on three points: weekly frequency carried the most information among behavioral variables; frequent moderate-intensity aerobic activity co-occurred most often with low anxiety and depression; and four partially overlapping profiles emerged. XGBoost classified best on an internal hold-out test set of 226 students, one fifth of the full sample (accuracy 0.889, 95% CI 0.842 to 0.924; macro-averaged AUC 0.943), yet reached only 0.769 sensitivity for severe distress, and accuracy fell to 0.858 under leave-one-college-out validation. Because the design is cross-sectional and validation internal, these findings describe associations rather than supply a screening tool.

title: Long-term multi-section traffic flow forecasting using the CNN–RNLSTM–MLR neural network
abstract: Nowadays, traffic congestion significantly contributes to severe economic and environmental problems in cities. Anticipating traffic flow is a highly effective strategy for mitigating congestion, and accurate predictions are vital for practical traffic guidance, management, and control. However, many existing approaches either treat spatial correlations and temporal dependencies separately or rely on single-architecture models, which limits their ability to capture complex spatiotemporal patterns in real-world networks. Even in cases where these factors have been considered in a combined manner, our proposed model is showed lower error rates compared to them. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network enhanced by Multiple Linear Regression (MLR). The proposed model utilizes CNN to extract meaningful latent features from input data while also taking advantage of LSTM-MLR's ability to capture temporal context. In the first stage, a CNN–RNLSTM model is employed to forecast traffic conditions on four highways in the United Kingdom that are closely associated with a target road, jointly modeling spatial interactions and nonlinear temporal dynamics. In the second stage, the CNN–RNLSTM–MLR model leverages these intermediate forecasts, together with explanatory variables, to estimate traffic conditions on the target roadway through a regression-based fusion layer. This two-stage design allows the model to combine the representation power of deep learning with the interpretability and correction capability of linear regression. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach consistently outperforms conventional baselines, including standalone MLR, LSTM, and MLR–LSTM models, as measured by Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). Notably, the RMSE exhibits a 22.96% improvement compared to the RNLSTM–MLR model. Overall, the proposed framework achieves the lowest error rate among state-of-the-art methods, indicating its superior ability to capture complex spatiotemporal dependencies in traffic flow forecasting.

title: A Graphormer approach for predicting peptide half-life, secondary structure, solvent accessibility, and post-translational modifications
abstract: Peptides represent a promising class of therapeutic agents due to their high target specificity, favorable safety profiles, and efficient tissue penetration. However, their clinical development remains limited by poor in vivo stability, rapid enzymatic degradation, and short plasma half-lives. The structural flexibility of peptides and their high solvent accessibility further increase their susceptibility to proteolysis, resulting in rapid clearance and reduced therapeutic efficacy. Although strategies such as cyclization and incorporation of non-natural amino acids can improve stability, it remains challenging at early stages to identify which peptides would benefit from such modifications based on their pharmacokinetic and physicochemical properties. Here, we present a Graphormer-based machine learning framework for predicting four key peptide properties: half-life, relative solvent accessibility, secondary structure, and post-translational modifications. The framework supports both cyclic peptides and non-natural amino acids, extending beyond the scope of many currently available tools. To evaluate performance, we benchmarked our predictive models against existing methods for each property. Rather than focusing on surpassing current approaches, this study emphasizes the practical applicability of the proposed framework for peptide property prediction. Additionally, the half-life prediction model was validated using an experimental dataset generated by a pharmaceutical company, demonstrating the flexibility of the approach for training on user-generated experimental data.

title: Neuromorphic control of a simulated shape-memory-alloy-driven multi-legged robot using a spiking neural network
abstract: We present spiking-neural-network (SNN) reinforcement learning for autonomous locomotion control of a starfish-inspired multi-legged soft robot driven by shape memory alloy (SMA) actuators. Such robots are usually driven open loop by pre-designed periodic signals, because coordinated motion is hard to hand-design at high degrees of freedom. We replace the actor of Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) with an SNN: a Spiking Actor Network. The membrane potential, an internal SNN state, is reconstructed at update time from a short observation history through the current actor, rather than stored at collection time. To reduce the controller’s inference cost, we add a regularization term on the squared membrane potentials, encouraging actions from fewer spikes. In simulation the agent acquired the leg coordination needed to approach a target, and its firing patterns developed a periodicity matched to the SMA response. The resulting gait gives continuous propulsion without excessive firing. Goal error matched an ANN-actor TD3 baseline with smaller spread across seeds, and reconstruction gave the lowest goal error of the membrane-state treatments. The regularization lowered the firing rate until the estimated inference energy fell below the ANN’s.

title: Biomechanics-driven deep reinforcement learning improves Wushu skill acquisition in physical-education students over an eight-week controlled intervention
abstract: Wushu instruction still rests on the coach’s eye and on repeated demonstration, an approach that resists quantification, delivers feedback only after a routine ends, and cannot retune difficulty for each learner. We therefore asked a deliberately narrow question: does a training paradigm in which biomechanically grounded features drive a reinforcement learning policy improve skill acquisition more than conventional coaching? Four directional hypotheses, stated before analysis, framed the test. Open-source inertial sensing was fused with markerless pose estimation to recover joint kinematics and inverse-dynamic torques, and a joint-angle-torque coupling scheme encoded those descriptors as a structured state tensor. A proximal-policy-optimization agent, driven by a composite reward and a dynamic difficulty-adjusting function, selected the training difficulty and the feedback shown to each learner. Sixty physical-education students completed an eight-week controlled intervention that compared the adaptive system with conventional coaching, with assessments at weeks 0, 4 and 8. Across sessions the instrumented measures proved reliable, with intraclass correlation coefficients from 0.82 to 0.91, and expert scoring showed good-to-excellent agreement both between raters, 0.91, and within raters, 0.93. Linear mixed-effects models with a random intercept for participant returned significant group-by-time interactions on all four skill dimensions: movement accuracy, \(F\) (2, 116) = 18.42, \(p\) < 0.001, partial \({\eta }^{2}\) = 0.24; movement fluency, \(F\) (2, 116) = 14.68, \(p\) < 0.001, partial \({\eta }^{2}\) = 0.20; force-control rationality, \(F\) (2, 116) = 21.17, \(p\) < 0.001, partial \({\eta }^{2}\) = 0.27; and rhythmic stability, \(F\) (2, 116) = 11.31, \(p\) < 0.001, partial \({\eta }^{2}\) = 0.16. The first three sit clearly above the conventional large-effect benchmark, whereas rhythmic stability only just clears it, and we read it accordingly. At the post-test the adaptive group exceeded the control group by 10.50 points on accuracy (95% CI 4.14 to 16.86, \(d\) = 0.85) and by 11.60 points on force control (95% CI 5.06 to 18.14, \(d\) = 0.92). Joint-angle variability also settled at a reduced plateau in the adaptive arm, and every within-participant change in an instrumented parameter exceeded the minimal detectable change of its own instrument. The convergence and transfer results point to the quality of the state encoding as a decisive design factor, although network depth itself was never varied, and the prediction that lower-baseline learners would gain most was not borne out. Because feedback modality and difficulty control were manipulated together, their separate contributions cannot be isolated in this design; the findings therefore support the packaged paradigm rather than either component on its own, and transfer to other coordination-intensive sports or to rehabilitation remains an untested conjecture. Trial registration : The trial was registered retrospectively rather than prospectively. Registration with a public clinical trial registry was applied for once data collection had ended, and the registration identifier will be supplied to the editorial office as soon as the registry record is issued; the absence of prospective registration is stated as a limitation in Section “Discussion”.

title: Deep learning-based analysis reveals patient-level cancer therapy trajectories using single-cell PBMC chromatin images
abstract: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) profiled in different data modalities have emerged as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for cancer. Here we demonstrate that PBMC chromatin images contain sufficient information to track patients’ trajectories during and after radiation therapy. We collected images from 150 patients across a variety of cancer types including Central Nervous System (CNS) cancer, Head & Neck cancer, Chordoma and Chondrosarcoma, Sarcoma, and Lymphoma, and adapted a multiple instance learning-based framework, which effectively enhanced the patient-level classification and interpretation of images from diverse samples compared to simpler cell-level neural network-based classifiers. We found that patients whose PBMCs returned to a state more similar to healthy after the therapy had more favorable outcomes. Moreover, our framework could indicate whether Head & Neck cancer patients’ PBMCs would likely return to a state similar to healthy after radiation therapy using solely chromatin images from before the treatment. These findings motivate further study of PBMC chromatin images to be used as a non-invasive, easily obtained, and inexpensive biomarker for cancer detection, treatment monitoring, and treatment response prediction.

title: The effect of appearance features of sidewalk autonomous delivery robot on perception of pedestrian
abstract: Sidewalk autonomous delivery robots (SADRs) are increasingly appearing on urban sidewalks and sharing public space with pedestrians. This study aims to investigate how different appearance features of SADRs influence four dimensions of human perception: Likeability, Competence, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. In Study 1, an affinity diagram method was used to classify the appearance features of existing SADRs into four categories—contour, proportion, facial features, and color scheme—which were then used as the design variables in Study 2. In Study 2, 100 participants completed an online questionnaire after viewing AI-generated videos of SADRs and evaluated the robots on the four perceptual dimensions. The statistical results showed that rounded contours and the presence of facial features significantly increased Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. White–black and yellow color schemes generally received higher ratings for Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance than black–gray and red color schemes. In addition, a tall proportion significantly reduced Likeability. Study 3 used online semi-structured interviews to further examine the reasons underlying these evaluations and to explore participants’ subjective perceptions of SADRs. The findings provide practical guidance for designing SADR appearances that can foster more positive pedestrian perceptions and acceptance.

title: Development of machine learning and integrated design for prediction of pharmaceutical solubility in dense solvent at different temperature levels
abstract: This research explores the solubility behavior of Nystatin in a ternary system of supercritical carbon dioxide (SCCO 2 ) and ethanol, focusing on the effects of temperature and pressure. The study employs three distinct machine learning models, Gradient Boosting (GB), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Polynomial Regression (PR), to predict the ternary solubility of Nystatin in SCCO 2 and ethanol. The hyper-parameter tuning for these models is accomplished using the Dragonfly Algorithm (DA), enhancing their predictive accuracy. The dataset, comprising temperature, pressure, and corresponding ternary solubility values, is analyzed using these models, and their performance is assessed through key evaluation metrics. The GB model achieves a score of 0.863 in R 2 metric. The RMSE and MAE both exhibit values below 0.1, thereby indicating the model’s high level of precision. The K-nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm demonstrated a high level of accuracy, as evidenced by its impressive coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.978. This result suggests that the KNN model exhibited a strong alignment with the underlying data. The performance of the PR model is outstanding, by its high R 2 score of 0.991, indicating its precise representation of solubility trends. The low RMSE and MAE values further confirm its precision.

title: Tracing working capital pressure in concentrated supply chains with temporal graph transformers
abstract: Concentrated trading relationships can improve coordination, yet they can also amplify operational stress when inventories, delivery commitments, and short-term obligations become misaligned. Conventional concentration ratios summarize dependence at the firm level but reveal little about how this pressure develops over time or travels through multi-tier supplier–buyer relations. This study presents SC-GraphTransformer-Press, a temporal graph framework that combines upstream and downstream concentration, product-specific transaction structure, recurrent firm states, and attention-based propagation to forecast working capital pressure. Pressure is operationalized as an inventory-backed stress proxy derived from unmet inventory-related obligations and available inventory, with firm-scale and network controls used to distinguish firms that have similar relative pressure but different operating capacities. The forecasting experiments use three SupplySim-derived benchmarks in which the required inventory and backlog states are observable. Under chronological multi-horizon evaluation, the proposed model achieves the strongest predictive performance among econometric, machine-learning, static graph, and temporal graph baselines, with its advantage increasing at longer horizons and under supply disruption. Network diagnostics further associate concentrated dependencies with persistent downstream pressure, while model-based scenarios indicate that supplier exits and supply shocks produce larger predicted responses than customer concentration and that product substitution can moderate these responses. Chronological audits and robustness tests across concentration assignments, shock locations, and simulator settings support the stability of these findings. The framework therefore offers a practical route from static concentration measurement to forward-looking diagnosis of working capital stress in dynamic supply-chain networks.

title: Proof carrying agent actions enable verifiable licensing of language model tool use
abstract: LLM agents increasingly call tools and take irreversible actions, yet the reasoning that licenses an action is rarely checked before execution. We present Proof-Carrying Agent Actions (PCAA) : each governed action carries a typed Action Certificate that a planner-independent checker must accept before execution. A trusted execution shim derives the obligation set and the irreversibility classification from an authoritative tool contract and binds the certificate to the exact invocation with a canonical SHA-256 commitment. The checker compares that context with the certificate, re-derives typed support (proof, belief, hypothesis, contingency, conflict, or no-progress), and validates formula-level inference rules. Irreversible actions require Proof for every declared licensing obligation. The checker accepts the two valid certificates and rejects all fifteen unsafe certificates in a semantic battery; four additional structural cases confirm rejection of argument substitution, precondition omission, and risk-flag downgrade. A microbenchmark of a three-obligation payment certificate measures 53.7 μs median and 65.7 μs p95 for construction, checking, serialization, and buffered local persistence. A stateful guardrail with the same certified-state predicate matches PCAA on safety; PCAA’s distinct contribution is a typed, replayable decision artifact. Guarantees are relative to trusted tool contracts: PCAA checks their use, not their real-world semantic correctness.

title: Hantavirus species detection from viral genome sequences using explainable artificial intelligence techniques
abstract: Hantaviruses are important zoonotic pathogens associated with severe human diseases, including hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome. The World Health Organization (WHO) has recognized the importance of strengthening hantavirus surveillance and early detection because of their public health impact. Nevertheless, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based approaches for hantavirus species identification from viral genome sequences remain largely unexplored. This study developed and evaluated an explainable AI-based approach for hantavirus species identification using viral genome sequence fragments representing six hantavirus species. A transformer-based genomic representation approach (DNABERT-2) was used to generate representations for various Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models. Sequence redundancy was quantified before model development, and performance was assessed using a 99%-sequence-identity group-aware partitioning strategy with five-fold group-aware cross-validation and an independent internal test set. Direct sequence-similarity auditing confirmed that no sequence pair with ≥ 99% global nucleotide identity crossed the development and test boundary. LightGBM achieved the highest mean group-aware cross-validation performance, with an Accuracy and weighted F1-Score of 99.51%, Cohen’s Kappa coefficient of 99.41%, and Brier Score of 0.19%. On the independent internal test set, LightGBM achieved an Accuracy and weighted F1-Score of 99.25%. SHAP analysis identified influential nucleotide sequence tokens contributing to LightGBM predictions, while a separate DNABERT-2 attention-based analysis identified highly attended nucleotide sequence patterns within the genomic encoder. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed approach as an auxiliary method for post-sequencing hantavirus species identification, genomic surveillance, and sequence-based research.

title: Cognitively robust model using a deep learning framework for target recognition under suboptimal illumination in intelligent video surveillance system
abstract: This paper presents a cognitively robust deep learning framework for target recognition under suboptimal illumination, which is developed to enhance the recognition performance and stability of intelligent video surveillance systems. The proposed framework integrates three complementary modules: an Illumination-Adaptive Enhancement Module (IAEM) that performs LIME-based illumination estimation and correction followed by linear contrast adjustment; a Deep Recognition Backbone (DRB) based on transfer-learned CNNs for robust feature extraction; and a Cognitive Robustness Evaluator (CRE) that quantitatively assesses recognition stability across optimization and illumination conditions. Importantly, CRE operates exclusively as a post-training evaluation module and does not participate in model training, parameter optimization, loss computation, or inference. The framework was evaluated on the Extended Yale Face Database B and NIR Dataset for closed-set face recognition and on the BDD100K Night Subset for multi-class object detection. The proposed IAEM–DRB pipeline achieved classification accuracies of 99.81% and 99.62% on the two face-recognition datasets, respectively, while BDD100K performance was evaluated using detection-specific metrics. Under illumination levels ranging from 20 to 400 lx, recognition accuracy varied from 98.16% to 99.87%, with a Cognitive Robustness Index (R c ) of 0.981. Component-wise ablation experiments further examined the effects of input enhancement, backbone selection, and alternative enhancement methods. The results demonstrate high recognition accuracy and limited performance variation under the evaluated illumination conditions. The results demonstrate high recognition accuracy and limited performance variation under the evaluated illumination conditions, therefore, the framework showing its potential for illumination-robust video surveillance systems.

title: Hybrid stacked bidirectional deep learning with attention based air pollution prediction for environmental sustainability
abstract: Environmental sustainability for air pollution monitoring necessitates utilization of advanced technologies like internet of things (IoT) devices and Artificial Intelligence (AI) AI to track air quality in real-time, controlling policy and measures to reduce to mitigate pollution for ensuring long-term environmental health. This mechanism aids sustainable development by safeguarding general public, combating climate change and establishing more flexible communities. Hence pollutant level monitoring is of paramount significance to maintain the pollutant concentrations under control. Nevertheless, pollutant concentration monitoring is not easy as it necessitates installing monitoring stations to obtain pertinent pollutant data that comes with high installation and maintenance costs. In this research, an attempt has been made to simulate the concentrations at three districts in Dhaka, Bangladesh using Deep Learning (DL) methods by applying Hybrid Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention Mechanism (HSBi-LSTMA) method for environmental sustainability. An efficient model specifically tailored for encoding and generating multi-class imbalance results using Label Encoded Synthetic Edited Nearest Neighbor-based pre-processing for different air pollution concentration features provided as input is introduced. Next, Hybrid Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention Mechanism first used attention mechanism to select the most influential features of the original air pollution concentration features and then used Hybrid Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory to generate the classified results for air pollution prediction. Extensive experiments were conducted on Air Pollution Monitoring Generated Using IoT dataset, comparing the HSBi-LSTMA method with two existing methods. The results demonstrate that the HSBi-LSTMA method significantly improves the air pollution prediction accuracy by 25% and reduces the mean absolute error by 46% as compared to the existing methods. With this the HSBi-LSTMA method represents a notable evolution in advancing environmental sustainability.

title: HAAF-RT-DETR: hybrid attention and high-resolution feature fusion based RT-DETR for kidney stone detection
abstract: Accurate localization and detection of kidney stones in computed tomography (CT) images are important for computer-aided medical image analysis. However, accurate detection remains challenging due to the small size of stones, weak boundaries, and complex renal anatomical backgrounds. To address these issues, this work proposes HAAF-RT-DETR (Hybrid Attention and High-Resolution Feature Fusion Based RT-DETR) for kidney stone detection. HAAF-RT-DETR integrates hybrid attention mechanisms and high-resolution feature fusion strategies into the RT-DETR framework to enhance feature representation and improve small-object detection performance. Within this framework, the HGBlock-AssemFormer module is introduced to jointly model local convolutional feature aggregation and Transformer-based global dependencies, thereby strengthening high-level semantic representations. In addition, a Convolution–Attention Fusion Module (CAFM) is employed to further refine high-level feature representations and reduce background interference. Furthermore, a high-resolution P2 feature level is incorporated, extending the original three-scale pyramid (P3–P5) to a four-scale representation (P2–P5), enabling fine-grained spatial details to participate in the DETR-style unified decoding process. Experiments on stone-positive CT slices from TEZ_ROI_AUG and the Kidney Stone Dataset demonstrate improvements in mAP, Recall, and F1-score over the evaluated YOLO-based detectors and RT-DETR baseline.

title: Effects of within-season temporal aggregation of weather variables on performance and interpretability in rice yield machine learning models
abstract: While crop responses are inherently stage-dependent, machine learning yield models often rely on weather variables aggregated over the entire growing season. This study evaluates how within-season temporal aggregation of weather variables affects both predictive performance and interpretability in machine learning-based rice yield modeling. Using CYGMA (Crop Yield Growth Model with Assumptions on Climate and Socioeconomics)-simulated potential yield as a synthetic response variable, we minimized confounding effects from observational noise and management variability, enabling a clearer evaluation of the role of within-season weather aggregation. Daily weather variables were averaged over the rice growing period after dividing each season into multiple equal-length segments, and several machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated using temporally independent validation. Increasing within-season temporal resolution improved model performance up to a moderate level, after which gains diminished. Interpretation using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and response diagnostics consistently indicated that yield sensitivity concentrates in specific windows of the season, with temperature-related effects emerging most strongly early in the season and humidity-related effects later. Finer temporal aggregation sharpened the identification of window-specific nonlinear and threshold-like responses that were obscured under coarse seasonal averages. Overall, moderate within-season aggregation provides a practical balance between predictive skill and mechanistic interpretability, supporting more reliable identification of phenology-relevant meteorological risks for climate-impact assessment and decision support.

title: Secure signal encoding and temporal feature extraction for multi class intrusion detection in smart grid environments
abstract: To ensure the reliability, security and operational stability of smart grid environments, real-time monitoring of electrical data is necessary. It is especially crucial that proper anomaly detection becomes the key to detecting malicious events, preventing disruption of the service, and supporting secure energy transmission. Nonetheless, traditional intrusion detection systems are typically not able to represent long-range temporal relationships, signal variations arising behind secured communication links, and attack-specific relationships, which can result in slow or inaccurate detection. To overcome these weaknesses, this paper suggests a hybrid intrusion detection system called Dilation-Gated Multi-Scale Fusion Encoding-Hierarchical Shifted Window Attention Network-Quadratic Discriminative Capsule Network (DG-MFE + H-SWANet + QDC-Net). In the proposed setting, meter readings are protected in transit by a lightweight chaotic Advanced Encryption Standard-Recursive Diffusion Embedding (AES-RDE) scheme and are decrypted by the authorized grid gateway, so detection is carried out on the recovered measurement stream and not on ciphertext. Then, DG-MFE extracts multi-scale time features, H-SWANet captures local and cross-window contextual dependencies, and QDC-Net performs classification of multi-class intrusion based on confidence. The proposed model was tested on the Smart Grid Real-Time Load Monitoring dataset, with intrusions injected into the measurements before encryption or into the ciphertext during transmission, covering false data injection, replay attack, stealth drift, binary tampering, and protocol corruption. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieved 98.32% accuracy, 98.72% precision, 98.93% recall, 98.82% F1-score, 97.67% Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), 99.08% specificity, 0.91% false acceptance rate (FAR), and 12.8 ms inference time, outperforming Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), ConvNeXt-1D, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Residual Attention Network-1D (RAN-1D), and Depthwise Separable Convolutional Neural Network (DSCNN) baselines. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective task-specific solution for multi-class intrusion detection under the configured secure-transmission smart-grid signal modeling and synthetic attack evaluation setup.

title: Deep learning-assisted graphene-based THz metasurface for label-free and high-performance MCF-7 breast cancer cell sensing
abstract: A triple-band graphene-based terahertz metasurface, integrated with a DL framework, is proposed for high-efficiency polarization conversion and label-free MCF-7 breast cancer cell detection. The unit cell, comprising concentric graphene elements and silver strips on an \(\mathrm {Al_2O_3}\) substrate with a silver ground plane, facilitates reflective-mode operation with polarization conversion ratios (PCR) exceeding 90% across three distinct operational bands. The finite-element method (FEM), finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique, and multiple-interference theory rigorously validate the physical mechanisms and electromagnetic responses, showing strong agreement. For biosensing applications, the metasurface leverages the distinct dielectric signatures of MCF-7 cells, inducing measurable resonance shifts at 1.48, 2.85, and 4.12 THz. The platform achieves a peak sensitivity of 0.866 THz/RIU and a figure of merit of 4.04 RIU \(^{-1}\) . To improve spectral analysis, we develop a one-dimensional convolutional neural network to predict PCR responses directly from THz spectral data. This model shows exceptional robustness, achieving an \(R^2\) of 0.972 even under 5% additive white Gaussian noise. By accurately resolving minute refractive-index variations associated with early-stage cellular-level oncogenic alterations, the proposed deep-learning-assisted biosensor offers a highly sensitive, non-contact, and non-destructive platform with significant potential for early-stage breast cancer screening.

title: TPACK and digital literacy among foreign language teachers in higher education institutions: a cross-sectional serial mediation analysis
abstract: Preparing foreign language teachers for AI-assisted teaching requires instructional knowledge and critical, responsible technology use. However, the roles of technology acceptance and psychological resilience in the association between teachers’ integration knowledge and digital literacy remain insufficiently explored. Informed by the theory of planned behavior, this study examined these relationships using cross-sectional survey data from a convenience sample of 721 foreign language teachers in Chinese higher education institutions. Structural equation modeling examined a theoretically specified serial mediation model, with gender, age, academic rank, and educational attainment included as control variables for digital literacy. The literacy measure covered self-reported AI understanding, use, social impact awareness, and ethical behavior. Technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) was positively associated with digital literacy. The model yielded positive indirect associations through technology acceptance and psychological resilience separately, as well as along the theoretically proposed sequence from technology acceptance to psychological resilience. These findings highlight the relevance of teachers’ technology evaluations and psychological resources alongside instructional knowledge, while distinguishing classroom integration knowledge from broader digital capabilities. The study offers a rationale for developing and evaluating professional learning that combines pedagogical knowledge, critical appraisal of AI tools, and support for managing technology-related demands.

title: Structured information extraction from geoscientific literature with GeoExtractor
abstract: Earth science research increasingly depends on the integration of large volumes of heterogeneous data distributed across publications. A substantial amount of quantitative information remains embedded in unstructured literature, making large-scale data compilation labor-intensive and difficult to maintain. Here, we introduce GeoExtractor, a large language model (LLM)-powered multi-agent framework designed to automatically extract structured information from geoscience literature. GeoExtractor employs a hierarchical extraction strategy that combines an iterative decision–retrieval–generation workflow with a two-stage retrieval mechanism, enabling the recovery of complex multi-instance scientific records from heterogeneous document sources. We evaluate the framework on four benchmark datasets spanning diverse geoscience sub-disciplines, using three LLMs and repeated runs to quantify variability. GeoExtractor generally performs better than the comparison methods on multi-record and multi-field tasks, while its limitations on single-record datasets are also characterized. To demonstrate its practical utility, we compiled a literature-derived database containing 2,259 zircon analyses from 179 publications of the Central Asian Orogenic Belt (CAOB), and the resulting dataset reproduces previously recognized tectonic patterns in the region. These results demonstrate that LLM-based multi-agent systems can facilitate the transformation of unstructured geoscientific literature into structured knowledge resources, substantially reducing the effort required for database construction and accelerating data-driven research across Earth science disciplines.

title: TMS timed to interictal epileptiform discharges
abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) are pathological hypersynchronous bursts of electrical brain activity that occur between seizures in patients with epilepsy. IEDs are caused by transient brain states that are difficult to predict, making them a challenging neurophysiological and technological case for brain-state-dependent stimulation. Administering stimulation at IED onset may provide insight into the epileptic network and optimize neurostimulation therapies. Here, we assessed the feasibility of IED-triggered transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in two children with self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), a common pediatric epilepsy in which IEDs emerge from the motor cortex. A convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained on the participants’ pre-recorded electroencephalography (EEG) data with IEDs annotated by an epileptologist. The CNN was integrated into an EEG-processing pipeline that classified EEG segments as “IED” or “non-IED” in real time. With this pipeline, TMS pulses were administered during IED or non-IED periods in an interleaved, randomized design. We stimulated both the motor cortex generating the IEDs and the contralateral motor cortex and tested the impact of IEDs on TMS-evoked potentials (TEPs). Our study demonstrated that TMS can be timed to IEDs and that there is a site-specific increase in TEP amplitude when stimulating during IEDs. Out of the TMS pulses aimed at an IED, 19% and 39% were successfully delivered during an IED for the two participants, respectively. For future research, we propose ways to address the methodological challenges of IED-timed TMS, enabling brain-state-dependent TMS for epilepsy research and treatment.

title: Intelligent MPPT in PV Systems using metaheuristic-optimised deep neural networks
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems face problems with multiple local maxima, poor tracking efficiencies and unstable maximum power point tracking (MPPT) when the irradiance changes rapidly or when there is partial shading on the panels. Traditional MPPT methods including Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductance display slow convergence and oscillation around the steady state in the changing environment. This paper proposes a Digital Twin-based Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO-Deep Neural Network) intelligent MPPT system for solar PV systems to overcome these two issues.This paper proposes a hybrid Grey wolf optimization –Deep neural Network (GWO_DNN) based MPPT technique for photovoltaic systems. The comparison between hybrid deep neural network (DNN)-based controllers for maximally tracking MPPs through Grey Wolf Optimisation (GWO), Golden Eagle Optimisation (GO) and Moth-Flame Algorithm (MFA) are evaluated by comparing relative effectiveness based upon converging performance, prediction accuracy, computational efficiency and stability. The proposed method improves tracking efficiency, reduces steady-state oscillations and achieves faster convergence under varying irradiance conditions. Computational models show GWO-DNN controllers achieving lower test mean absolute distance from the true MPP compared to the other controllers with mean absolute mean square errors (MAE) reported as 0.6138 V (GWO-DNN), 0.3506 V (MFA-DNN) and 0.4978 V (GO-DNN). The GWO-DNN controllers also have a lower degree of oscillation in steady-state conditions, showing faster convergence than all other controllers as well as significantly lower prediction errors. In contrast, Moses-DNN performs more reliably with respect to optimal positioning, but its predictive capabilities will limit its effectiveness for practical real-time implementation. Although GO-DNN provides lower inference time than both the GWO app and MFA model as is a whole, the standard deviation of how far down the MPP would be estimated will increase for the time taken to make the prediction. A traditional CNN-LSTM model has demonstrated to consistently underperform under dynamic operating conditions. Thus, the results demonstrate that GWO-DNN represents a superior balance of MPPT controller characteristics across dynamic operating ranges, as such, GWO-DNN will provide the most robust and predictable MPP capability for use in smart solar energy applications. This initiative helps meet the UN Sustainable Development Goals through the past improvements made in renewable energy extraction efficiency, the creation of more intelligent energy infrastructure and ultimately the contribution to greater levels of solar energy production, while also reducing wasted energy through better designs. Specifically, it contributes to SDG7 - Affordable and Clean Energy; SDG9 - Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure; and SDG13 - Climate Action by facilitating the creation of sustainable, resilient and low-carbon energy systems.

title: Citrus leaf pathology multi-class image dataset and a hybrid multi-branch attention fusion network for lemon leaf disease classification
abstract: The productivity of lemon (Citrus lemon) crops is severely undermined by foliar diseases, which constitute the leading cause of global harvest degradation. The conventional reliance on manual identification by experienced specialists poses a significant bottleneck, as these methods are both time-consuming and prone to human error under field conditions. Recently, deep learning techniques have been employed to identify and diagnose citrus foliar diseases from digital images, automating the classification process and providing non-experts with accessible diagnostic tools. While several deep learning applications have been used to classify lemon diseases with the aim of improving classification accuracy, most of these studies fail to achieve high accuracy and rely on datasets with an insufficient number of disease classes. In this paper, we introduced a dataset named “Citrus Leaf Pathology Multi-Class Image Dataset” with 14 different classes, and we proposed a Hybrid Multi-Branch Attention Fusion Network (HMAF-Net). The architecture consists of four parallel feature extraction branches, each incorporating branch attention and channel attention, followed by classification using a Neural Network (NN). A DenseNet121 backbone is combined with lightweight convolutional branches, refined through squeeze-and-excitation channel attention and a learnable branch-weighting fusion mechanism to adaptively integrate complementary feature representations. The model attains 96.63% precision and 95.59% accuracy on the proposed dataset. The model further demonstrates strong generalization, achieving 97.48%, 95.89%, and 98.23% accuracy on three independent external lemon and citrus leaf datasets, with statistical significance confirmed through paired t-tests across five independent runs. Explainable AI visualizations further confirm that the model’s predictions are grounded in disease-relevant leaf regions, supporting its potential for reliable deployment in real-world agricultural diagnostic systems.

title: A single-phase high step-up common-ground direct AC–AC converter with reduced switches stress
abstract: This paper introduces a single-stage boost AC–AC converter based on a switching-cell configuration. The suggested topology is designed to achieve high voltage gain while reducing the size and weight of magnetic components, and also, minimizing overall conduction losses. By providing continuous input and output current waveforms, the converter reduces current ripple, while the experimentally measured THD values confirm the limited distortion of the input current and output voltage waveforms. The proposed design provides a duty-cycle-controlled voltage gain while preserving the phase and frequency of the input voltage at the output. This operating principle enables direct high step-up AC voltage conversion without requiring a bulky line-frequency transformer. Additionally, the simplified circuit, fewer bidirectional switches, and reduced voltage stress on semiconductor devices enhance efficiency, and implementation feasibility. A detailed theoretical analysis is presented, including operating principles, mode analysis, component design considerations, and performance evaluation. The effectiveness of the introduced converter is validated experimentally. The laboratory test is conducted at an input voltage of 20 V, a duty cycle of D = 0.7, a switching frequency of 50 kHz, an output voltage of 110 V, and an output power of 250 W. The obtained results confirm the capability of the converter to provide high voltage gain and enhanced performance, making it suitable for inductive power transfer systems, AC power conditioning applications, and low voltage AC energy interfaces.

title: Land suitability analysis for taro (Colocasia esculenta) cultivation based on topo-edaphic variables in a smallholder farming system
abstract: Taro ( Colocasia esculenta ), one of the neglected and underutilized crop species (NUCS), is regarded as a climate-smart crop due to its ability to tolerate harsh environmental conditions associated with climate change. The crop plays a critical role in enhancing food and nutritional security while promoting resilience through crop diversification, particularly in smallholder farming systems in developing countries. Despite its recognized potential, a substantial knowledge gap exists regarding the identification of optimal areas for maximizing yield in local contexts. Hence, this study employed the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) machine learning algorithm to conduct a Land Suitability Analysis (LSA) for taro within rural landscapes dominated by smallholder farmers. To quantify the area suitable for cultivation, we evaluated topographic and edaphic influences at 0-20 and 20-50 cm using five models: (1) topographic- variables, (2) edaphic variables at 0-20 cm, (3) a combined model using topographic + edaphic variables at 0-20 cm, (4) edaphic variables at 20-50 cm, (5) a combined model using topographic + edaphic variables at 20-50 cm. Model 5 achieved the highest mean AUC (0.821 ± 0.083 SD) based on 10 replicated validations, although paired t-tests revealed that this improvement was statistically significant only when compared to the lowest-performing Model 1 (p = 0.005), while comparisons with Models 2, 3, and 4 were not significant (all p > 0.05). The results from Model 5 indicated that 7.92%, 11.04%, 16.80%, and 26.64% of the study area were classified as highly suitable, suitable, moderately suitable, and marginally suitable for taro cultivation, respectively. Based on the MaxEnt Jackknife test, slope, Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), and the soil’s calcium, iron, and phosphorus were the most important variables for taro growth. These findings provide practical information to support improved land-use planning, promote the integration of NUCS into local farming systems, and contribute to food and nutritional security, particularly within smallholder farming communities in rural areas.
