title: ANN-GA-based optimization of a hybrid battery thermal regulation system with helical liquid cooling, PCM, and copper foam
abstract: Effective thermal management is essential for ensuring the safety, performance, and longevity of Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). In this study, an optimized hybrid Battery Thermal Regulation System (BTRS) is proposed, integrating helical liquid cooling mini-channels and phase change material (PCM) embedded in a copper foam matrix (CPCM) to enhance heat dissipation. To efficiently explore the complex design space, a coupled framework integrating numerical simulations, a Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) was developed. The approach successfully identified an ideal configuration (OCD1) characterized by a 10 mm PCM thickness, a 0.08 m/s inlet velocity, and a \(65^\circ \) helical angle. Under a severe 3C discharge condition, this optimal design achieved a maximum temperature reduction of 21.27 K, representing an 82.25% improvement over a standalone cell. Furthermore, the optimized hybrid system demonstrated superior cooling efficacy compared to individual strategies, outperforming case A (liquid cooling) by 33.67%, case B (pure PCM) by 69.35%, and case C (CPCM) by 45%. The developed ANN model exhibited high predictive accuracy, with R 2 values exceeding 0.99 for both thermal responses. These findings provide a high fidelity and scalable framework for advanced thermal management of next-generation electric vehicle battery systems.

title: Automated detection of focal cortical dysplasia in epilepsy using machine learning on structural MRI
abstract: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) represents a structural brain anomaly of developmental origin that significantly contributes to epilepsy. This proof-of-concept study evaluates the feasibility of machine learning (ML) algorithms to distinguish patients with FCD type II-associated epilepsy from healthy controls (HCs) using high-resolution structural MRI. Structural MRI data from a publicly available dataset comprising 167 subjects (both FCD-associated epilepsy patients and HCs) were analyzed. Neuroanatomical features were extracted with FreeSurfer software. Preprocessing steps included dataset reconstruction, feature scaling, dimensionality reduction, and encoding of demographic variables. Multiple supervised ML models—including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest—were trained and evaluated using nested cross-validation with 10 outer folds and 5 inner folds. Among the evaluated classifiers, Random Forest achieved the highest AUC (0.791). This model demonstrated balanced classification ability, as reflected by its ROC and Precision-Recall curves. While promising, these results reflect the model’s performance on the current dataset and require further validation. This study demonstrates the preliminary potential of ML techniques to distinguish FCD-associated epilepsy from HCs using structural MRI, providing supportive information for clinical review. However, further studies with larger, independent clinical cohorts are necessary to validate these results before considering any clinical implementation.

title: Physics informed distributionally robust learning for urban distribution network resilience under extreme events
abstract: Extreme events expose urban distribution networks to correlated branch outages, uncertain hazard evolution, and rapidly changing operating conditions. Static indices and repeated Monte Carlo studies remain useful, but they either compress recovery behavior into a fixed score or impose substantial computational cost when many hazard realizations must be screened. This study develops a physics-informed, distributionally robust graph-learning framework for estimating node- and system-level resilience from scenario-dependent topology, measured post-event operating states, and hazard information. The contribution lies in the joint implementation of masked graph propagation, auxiliary electrical-state reconstruction, Wasserstein-robust training, and a common recovery-prioritization interface; none of these ingredients is claimed as new in isolation.The network encoder uses branch-availability masks and physical edge attributes to update graph messages. An auxiliary decoder reconstructs voltage, active and reactive injection, and branch-flow quantities, allowing AC-balance, voltage, and thermal residuals to regularize the latent representation. These penalties promote physical consistency but do not constitute hard feasibility guarantees. Distributional uncertainty is represented by a Wasserstein ball over normalized continuous operating and hazard features, while discrete topology masks remain fixed during each inner maximization. The learned resilience score is supervised by a transparent trajectory-based target constructed from restored service, unmet demand, time to 50% recovery, and voltage-violation exposure. The principal quantitative evaluation uses 20,000 operating states generated from 500 hazard scenarios on a modified IEEE 123-bus feeder. Across five random seeds, the full model attains an MAE of \(0.031\pm 0.002\) , an RMSE of \(0.042\pm 0.003\) , and an \(R^2\) of \(0.935\pm 0.008\) . Removing Wasserstein training increases RMSE to \(0.058\pm 0.004\) , while removing the operator block increases it to \(0.052\pm 0.004\) . When every assessment method is coupled to the same restoration simulator, the proposed ranking signal is associated with \(25.1\%\pm 1.5\%\) load shedding at hazard intensity \(\xi =0.8\) and a \(2.48\pm 0.16\) h time to 50% restoration. These recovery quantities measure the effect of assessment-informed prioritization under fixed restoration assumptions; the learning model does not directly issue switching, dispatch, or repair actions.

title: AI-ready design of realistic 2D materials and interfaces with Mat3ra-2D
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models in materials science are predominantly trained on ideal bulk crystals, limiting their transferability to real-world applications where surfaces, interfaces, and defects dominate. We present Mat3ra-2D, an open-source framework for the rapid design of realistic two-dimensional materials and related structures, including slabs and heterogeneous interfaces, with support for disorder and defect-driven complexity. The approach combines: (1) well-defined standards for storing and exchanging materials data with a modular implementation of core concepts and (2) transformation workflows expressed as configuration-builder pipelines that preserve provenance and metadata. We implement typical structure generation tasks, such as constructing orientation-specific slabs or strain-matching interfaces, in reusable Jupyter notebooks that serve as both interactive documentation and templates for reproducible runs. To lower the barrier to adoption, we design the examples to run in any web browser and demonstrate how to incorporate these developments into a web application. Mat3ra-2D enables systematic creation, provenance tracking, inspection, and reuse of realistic 2D- and interface-aware structures, providing the structure-generation layer needed for future AI/ML dataset construction for training.

title: Energy management optimization algorithm for data center microgrids based on solid-state transformers
abstract: The proliferation of hyperscale data centers, together with tightening carbon-neutrality targets, exposes the limits of the line-frequency transformer (LFT) that still dominates data-center power distribution and motivates a fresh look at the conversion and dispatch layer. This paper develops an energy management framework for a data-center microgrid whose grid interface is a three-stage solid-state transformer (SST), so that renewable, storage, and IT loads sit on independently regulated AC and DC ports rather than behind a passive iron core. A multi-objective mixed-integer nonlinear program (MOMINLP) is formulated to jointly minimise operating cost, carbon emission, a composite power-quality index, and average PUE, subject to bus power balance, SST port transfer, battery SOC, ramp, and demand-response constraints. Uncertainty in PV, wind, and IT workload is condensed through Latin hypercube sampling with Kantorovich-based scenario reduction, and tail risk is capped by a CVaR constraint at the 95% confidence level. Dispatch is decomposed across day-ahead, intra-day, and real-time MPC layers, and the nonconvex problem is solved by an improved whale optimization algorithm (IWOA) that combines Tent chaotic initialization, an adaptive convergence coefficient, differential-evolution mutation, and Lagrangian relaxation of the diesel and battery integer commitments. On a 10 MW-class pilot the proposed scheme raises renewable accommodation by 17.2% points, cuts annual operating cost by 11.7%, reduces \(\:{CO}_{2}\) emissions by 12.9%, and lowers average PUE from 1.52 to 1.40 relative to a line-frequency-transformer baseline, while keeping bus voltage deviation below 1.7% on the DC bus and 2.4% on the AC bus. Against PSO, GA, standard WOA, and NSGA-II, IWOA halves the iterations needed to reach 1% of the final fitness (78 versus 134–187), tightens the relative gap to the best-known solution to 0.62% (versus 2.4–5.1%), and drops the coefficient of variation to 0.018 (versus 0.061–0.094), showing that the observed gains come from the coupling of hardware-aware modelling and algorithmic tailoring rather than from either alone.

title: Course-embedded AI-augmented teaching is associated with engagement and performance in software education
abstract: AI-augmented teaching may reduce feedback delays in software courses, but semester-long classroom evidence remains limited. This course-level quasi-experimental study evaluated a course-embedded AI-augmented teaching (AIT) model in an undergraduate Python course. Two intact classes participated: 60 students in the AIT class used a large language model teaching assistant restricted to course-specific materials and instructional rules for question answering, code diagnosis, personalized recommendations, and teacher monitoring, whereas 60 students in the conventional-instruction class received the same course instruction without access to the AIT platform. Student-level analyses, interpreted cautiously because of the class-level design, showed higher posttest, programming assignment and final composite scores in the AIT class after baseline adjustment. Learning engagement also showed clearer gains, especially overall and behavioral engagement. AI usage intensity was moderately associated with engagement but weakly associated with academic performance. Mediation analysis provided clearer evidence for an indirect engagement pathway for project practice performance than for final composite performance. Open-ended feedback indicated that students valued immediate feedback and debugging support but remained concerned about accuracy, dependency and ethical boundaries.

title: Attention-based and contrastive deep learning models for real-time anomaly detection in Edge-IIoT networks
abstract: The rapid expansion of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems has increased the cyber-attack surface of critical infrastructure, requiring intrusion detection systems (IDS) that are accurate, robust, and efficient under resource-constrained edge environments. Traditional approaches suffer from limited generalization, poor handling of class imbalance, and lack of statistical reliability and interpretability. This paper proposes a modular deep learning framework integrating TabTransformer, Variational Autoencoder, and contrastive learning, combined through multi-trial training (N = 10), statistical aggregation, and F1-weighted ensemble fusion. Experiments on the Edge-IIoTset dataset ( \(\approx \) 1.9M samples, 15 classes) achieve 97.60% accuracy and 83.42% F1-score, with multi-trial aggregation reducing the uncertainty associated with single-run reporting. From a computational perspective, training is performed using large-batch optimization (batch size = 16,384) with early stopping (patience = 50), while inference requires a single forward pass per model followed by constant-time fusion. The framework operates on compact tabular inputs ( \(\approx \) 96 features), resulting in a lightweight memory footprint (on the order of a few megabytes per model) and enabling efficient deployment. The inference pipeline processes batches in a few milliseconds on GPU-class hardware, ensuring real-time responsiveness for high-throughput IIoT traffic streams while maintaining low computational overhead and energy demand. Ablation analysis shows that removing ensemble fusion reduces F1-score by approximately 1%:2%, while eliminating multi-trial aggregation significantly increases variance, highlighting the importance of statistical robustness. Furthermore, SHAP-based explainable AI (XAI) provides insight into feature-level contributions, enhancing transparency and supporting human-in-the-loop security operations. Overall, the proposed framework achieves a balanced trade-off between predictive performance and computational efficiency, delivering a reproducible, interpretable, and deployment-oriented IDS solution for real-time IIoT environments. Practical deployment considerations, including model export to ONNX format and quantization for edge hardware, are outlined as immediate next steps.

title: A lightweight privacy-aware federated vision transformer for tomato leaf disease classification
abstract: Smart farming increasingly depends on intelligent disease diagnosis systems to improve crop productivity while protecting the privacy of agricultural data distributed across farms, research institutions, and edge devices. Conventional centralized deep learning approaches require collecting large volumes of data at a central location, raising concerns about data privacy, ownership, and communication overhead. To address these challenges, this study proposes FedVRT, a lightweight privacy-aware federated learning framework for tomato leaf disease classification. The proposed framework combines a Vision Transformer (ViT) with a lightweight ResNet26 architecture within the Federated Averaging (FedAvg) framework, enabling collaborative model training without exchanging raw agricultural images. The Vision Transformer captures global contextual relationships among disease symptoms, while the ResNet26 branch extracts fine-grained local lesion and texture features. Their complementary feature representations are fused to improve disease classification under heterogeneous non-IID data distributions commonly encountered in real-world agricultural environments. The proposed framework was evaluated on a dataset of 11,108 tomato leaf images across six disease categories in federated settings with 3, 12, 24, and 36 distributed clients. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), confusion matrix analysis, confidence intervals, and statistical significance tests. FedVRT achieved a classification accuracy of 98.50%, with precision 98.42%, recall 98.35%, F1-score 98.38%, and an AUC of 0.997 across 36 participating clients. Comparative experiments further demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms established federated optimization methods, including FedSGD, FedProx, FedNova, SCAFFOLD, FedOpt, and FedDyn, while maintaining lower communication overhead and faster convergence. Unlike existing federated Vision Transformer-based approaches that primarily focus on classification accuracy, FedVRT integrates lightweight hybrid feature extraction, comprehensive statistical validation, scalability analysis, and communication efficiency evaluation within a unified framework. These characteristics demonstrate the effectiveness of FedVRT as a scalable, privacy-aware, and practically deployable solution for intelligent tomato leaf disease diagnosis in next-generation smart farming environments.

title: Grey wolf optimization-driven convolutional neural network for robust cardiac MRI-based heart disease classification under class imbalance
abstract: Heart disease diagnosis through Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a vital clinical diagnostic technique that enables the non-invasive evaluation of cardiac structure and identification of cardiovascular diseases. Nevertheless, the automation of such a task using deep learning faces some critical problems in terms of limited data size, class imbalance, and manual tuning of hyperparameters, which might hinder the accuracy and reliability of the process. Therefore, this paper introduces a novel algorithm called GWO-CNN for heart disease classification based on cardiac MRI. In this algorithm, structured pre-processing, contrast enhancement, augmenting-based class balancing, CNN-based spatial features extraction, and GWO-based hyperparameters selection will be used for the classification process. Cardiac MRIs are preprocessed through normalization, Gaussian filtering, contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization, cropping, and resizing improve anatomical clarity and generate standardized image inputs. Moreover, the classifier model consists of a CNN model to identify between normal and abnormal heart MRIs and Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm to find optimal values of hyperparameters (learning rate, dropout rate, batch size, configuration of convolutional filters, and dense layer size). Experimental results, obtained via patient-level five-fold cross-validation repeated across five random seeds (25 runs in total), demonstrated that the GWO-CNN framework attained a mean accuracy of 98.30% ± 0.42% (95% CI: 98.13–98.47%), a mean F1-score of 97.50% ± 0.46%, and a mean AUC of 98.60% ± 0.39%, with a representative single-fold configuration reaching 98.42% accuracy, 97.86% precision, 97.31% recall, a 97.58% F1-score, a specificity of 98.91%, a Dice score of 97.52%, a Jaccard similarity index of 95.23%, a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 96.41%, and an area under the curve (AUC) of 98.74%. Paired statistical testing (t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank, p < 0.001) confirmed that the improvements attributable to preprocessing, GAN-based augmentation, and GWO-based tuning, as well as the improvement over baseline CNN, ResNet-based, and transfer-learning-based comparators, are each statistically significant. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed GAN-assisted GWO-CNN framework for cardiac MRI classification under limited and class-imbalanced data conditions. A preliminary external evaluation on the independent ACDC dataset, performed without any retraining, yielded 92.00% accuracy, a moderate decrease from the internal cross-validated mean consistent with real but non-catastrophic distributional shift. However, because the primary evaluation is based on a relatively small single public dataset and external validation was limited to one additional cohort assessed once, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary proof-of-concept evidence rather than confirmation of clinical applicability. Further validation using larger and independent multi-center cardiac MRI cohorts is required before the proposed framework can be considered for clinical deployment.

title: G2T: Gate guided transformer for medical image segmentation
abstract: Inspired by the human cognitive process and memory capabilities, we present a novel vision transformer (ViT) in this paper, called G ate G uided T ransformer (G2T) for medical image segmentation. G2T addresses a key limitation of cascaded decoder blocks in vision transformers; that is their difficulty in retaining and propagating important information from earlier stages, which often leads to suboptimal feature decoding in later blocks. Our proposed G2T has (i) a novel feature-aware decoder (FAD) consisting of three convolutional gates named Refine, Expand, and Produce (REP), which deal with forgetting irrelevant features, remembering relevant features, and generating the output features, respectively; (ii) a novel attention mixing module called LH-RAAM (Low to High-Resolution Attention Accumulation Module) that accumulates attentions computed in the encoder blocks from low-level features to high-level features, and aggregates them with the attentions computed in the decoder blocks to emphasize similar features during both the encoding and decoding stages. Evaluated on six medical imaging datasets, G2T consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art models by 1-3%, achieving a 94.67% mean Dice score ±0.01 standard deviation on the ACDC dataset and 92.90% ±0.02 on the Synapse dataset. Ablation studies additionally justify the utility of each component of G2T along with strong generalizability outside the medical domain.

title: Multidimensional spatiotemporal differentiation and driving mechanisms of soil erosion in a mountainous small watershed: an ST-TransUNet-R framework
abstract: Soil erosion threatens ecological security and water conservation in mountainous small watersheds. To improve pixel-level assessment under complex terrain and incomplete multi-source raster inputs, we developed ST-TransUNet-R, a deep-learning framework that integrates a ResNet-50 encoder, a Transformer module, a joint-validity mask, and masked mean squared error loss. The framework was applied to the Xikouwai Small Watershed upstream of the Miyun Reservoir for five assessment years between 2005 and 2020 and achieved R² = 0.87, RMSE = 2.08, MAE = 1.15, and PBIAS = − 3.13%. Multidimensional analysis showed that the 600–900 m elevation band contained 48.0% of the eroded area, whereas zones above 1100 m produced disproportionately high soil loss per unit area. Slopes > 35°, vegetation cover < 30%, unused land, and skeletal soils were consistently erosion-sensitive. SHAP analysis identified slope as the dominant predictor, followed by slope length and vegetation cover, indicating that terrain-controlled runoff concentration and surface protection jointly shaped spatial erosion heterogeneity. These findings provide a high-resolution basis for prioritizing erosion-control measures in mountainous water-source protection areas.

title: Multimodal deep learning with particle swarm guided feature refinement for automated pain detection
authors: Fatma Al Zahraa Hamed Abdel Hameed
abstract: Pain assessment remains a significant challenge in clinical practice because conventional self-reporting methods are subjective and unreliable for non-verbal, cognitively impaired, and critically ill patients. Existing automated pain detection approaches primarily rely on single-modality data or limited multimodal integration, resulting in inadequate feature representation, feature redundancy, and reduced classification performance. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates physiological signals, facial images, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and clinical text for objective pain detection. The physiological branch employs a hybrid architecture comprising a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and Deep Neural Network (DNN) to learn hierarchical spatial-temporal representations. The facial branch combines EfficientNet and Residual Network (ResNet) to extract discriminative facial features, while a CNN-based architecture processes MRI images. Clinical narratives are encoded using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and BioBERT to capture contextual semantic information. An Adaptive Feature Refinement Layer (AFRL) enhances modality-specific feature learning, followed by Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) for feature selection and a novel PSO-Guided Feature Refinement Layer (PFRL) for adaptive feature weighting prior to multimodal fusion. We implement the framework in TensorFlow and PyTorch and evaluate it on the BioVid, UNBC-McMaster, and Trigeminal Neuralgia MRI datasets. Experimental results achieve 96.2% accuracy, outperforming Support Vector Machine (82.4%), K-Nearest Neighbors (79.6%), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (88.9%), and AdaBoost (90.7%). The proposed framework provides a robust, scalable, and clinically applicable solution for automated multimodal pain detection and improved clinical decision support.

title: Comparative evaluation of traditional, machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid models for short-term wind speed forecasting in Colombo, Sri Lanka
abstract: Short-term wind speed forecasting is critical for optimizing wind-dependent operations in Sri Lanka. However, existing studies lack comprehensive comparisons across different time series forecasting frameworks and insufficiently examine performance differences between univariate and multivariate approaches. This study addresses these gaps by evaluating traditional time series models (ARIMA, ARIMAX, VAR), machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Regression), and deep learning models (Feed Forward Neural Network, Long Short-Term Memory, Convolutional Neural Network) for daily wind speed forecasting in Colombo, Sri Lanka. A residual-correction hybrid framework combining the optimal standalone XGB with deep learning models (XGB-FNN, XGB-LSTM, XGB-CNN) is systematically evaluated for the first time in the Sri Lankan wind speed forecasting context. Meteorological data from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2023, encompassing ten atmospheric variables, were analyzed. Model hyperparameters were optimized using Grid Search CV, Random Search CV, and Optuna with time series cross-validation. All residual-correction hybrid models used Optuna-tuned XGBoost, which is the optimal standalone model, as the primary model. The XGB-CNN with Optuna-tuned CNN achieved the best numerical performance with MSE of 0.5172, RMSE of 0.7192, MAE of 0.5432, and R 2 of 0.7855. Subsequent Diebold-Mariano testing and Multiple-Comparison Correction via Model Confidence Set confirmed that, although all hybrids showed numerically improved performance over the standalone XGBoost model, these improvements were not statistically significant. This suggests that both the optimal standalone XGBoost model and the proposed hybrid forecasting frameworks constitute robust and reliable approaches for forecasting in the present study. The most influential features identified were minimum, maximum, and average temperatures, precipitation, wind direction, southwest monsoon season, cloud cover, previous-day wind speed, previous-day sea level pressure, current and previous-day relative humidity, and surface pressure change from the previous day.

title: Exploration the influence of electron donor engineering on frequency-dependent nonlinear optical properties of anthraquinone-based chromophores: a DFT-ML approach
abstract: Recently, non-linear optical materials (NLO) have gained significant attention due to their applications in photonics, optical communication, and signal processing. Herein, anthraquinone core-based chromophores (APCD1–APCD7) were designed via donor engineering for efficient nonlinear optical materials. Their structural and optoelectronic properties were calculated by density functional theory and time dependent density functional theory (DFT/TD-DFT) at M06/6-311G (d, p) level. The designed chromophores (APCD1–APCD7) showed red-shifted absorption spectrum (380.89–466.58 nm ) and reduced HOMO LUMO energy gap of 1.99 − 3.81 eV . The density of states (DOS), transition density matrix (TDM) and natural bond orbital (NBO) analyses revealed efficient charge redistribution. Moreover, the designed compounds exhibited enhanced NLO responses, with APCD1 showing the strongest second-order NLO response, including β(− 2ω;ω,ω) of 7.11 × 10⁻²⁷ esu , whereas APCD5 exhibited the most pronounced third-order NLO response, with γ DFWM of 3.10 × 10⁻³¹ esu and n₂ of 5.01 × 10⁻¹⁴ cm²/W at 532 nm . Machine learning analysis established the structure–property relationship of the energy gap, identifying PEOE VSA 11, EState VSA 10, and BCUT2D VSA 11 as the most influential descriptors. Synthetic accessibility analysis indicates the practical feasibility of the designed chromophores, highlighting their potential for advanced photonic and optoelectronic applications.

title: A RAG-enhanced multi-agent LLM/VLM framework for auditable and region-aware structural health monitoring of a historic masonry structure
abstract: Historic masonry structures require monitoring workflows that are non-destructive, interpretable, and robust to field variability. This paper presents a proof-of-concept, RAG-enhanced structural health monitoring (SHM) workflow demonstrated on a single historic masonry minaret case study, in which a manager–orchestrator coordinates signal analysis, visual analysis, and cross-modal fusion. Vibration data from four sensors installed on this minaret are processed through a reproducible pipeline that includes data cleaning, PSD-based baseline characterisation, adaptive windowing, robust normalisation, and anomaly screening with a 1D convolutional autoencoder trained on healthy reference data (Measurements 1–12), followed by evaluation on Measurements 13–20. Localisation is strengthened through relation-based autoencoders on sensor pairs and sensor-to-zone damage mapping. In parallel, a VLM analyses sensor-linked inspection images from the same case study, while a curated retrieval-augmented structural memory package for the monitored minaret (geometry, materials, baseline dynamics, FE notes, and inspection playbook) supports context-aware interpretation. A three-agent decision layer (Agent A: LLM+RAG, Agent B: VLM+RAG, Agent C: fusion + RAG) reconciles agreements and conflicts between signal- and image-derived evidence to produce case-specific global and zone-level risk assessments. The study compares with-RAG and without-RAG analysis modes within this single deployment and reports structured, traceable outputs, including JSON artefacts, per-image findings, per-sensor summaries, narrative reports, and final risk maps. Its main contribution is to demonstrate how signal-derived anomalies, image-derived evidence, and retrieval-grounded structural memory can be combined within a traceable multi-agent SHM workflow for one monitored historic masonry minaret.

title: Joint molecular optimization for efficient virtual screening via machine learning
abstract: Joint molecular optimization serves as the central focus of this research, which explores the synergistic integration of machine learning (ML) and virtual screening (VS) for drug discovery. This study addresses these limitations by integrating molecular docking and ML to predict and balance multiple molecular properties concurrently. Traditional VS methods often fall short by primarily targeting single molecular properties, such as binding affinity, overlooking the necessity of simultaneously optimizing multiple crucial parameters like ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) profiles. Key objectives include developing and evaluating multi-objective optimization strategies and employing ML models (e.g., logistic regression, SVM, neural networks) to enhance predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. This research balances efficacy and safety metrics to refine VS and demonstrates the effect of combining these strategies on benchmark data. This work contributes a controlled, reproducible framework and an explicitly defined multi-objective prioritization procedure intended to support more efficient and transparent virtual screening, offering valuable insights for researchers in drug discovery, computational chemistry, and ML. Claims of reduced clinical attrition or improved clinical success would require prospective experimental validation and lie beyond the scope of this computational study.

title: Imaging-based biological age estimation predicts competing mortality risk in lung cancer screening
abstract: Lung cancer screening (LCS) participants have a high competing risk of non-lung cancer related death, which limits screening benefit. We hypothesized that imaging-based biological age can identify individuals at higher risk of non-lung cancer mortality. Low dose computed tomography scans from a large LCS trial were retrospectively analyzed. Bone density loss, muscular fat infiltration, vascular calcification, and visceral fat mass were calculated using segmentations from a nnU-Net based deep learning segmentation model. Each participant’s age gap, defined as the difference between their estimated biological age and chronological age, was estimated with disease course mapping using a Bayesian mixed-effects model. Disease course map construction used all available longitudinal scan data, whilst individual biological age prediction used baseline scan data only. The performance of age gap as a parameter in competing risk models for non-lung cancer related death versus lung cancer diagnosis was evaluated, following the TRIPOD + AI reporting guideline. We included 29,745 scans from 12,478 participants in the final analysis. Median follow-up was 5 years, representing 58,284 person-years at risk. Multivariable survival models of competing risks were constructed, including the estimated age gap. The subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) for each decade of age gap for non-lung cancer related death was higher (sHR = 2.0, 95% CI 1.8–2.3), compared to lung cancer diagnosis (sHR = 1.3, 95% CI 1.2–1.5). Addition of age gap improved model concordance of non-lung cancer death compared to a model with clinical variables alone (pooled C-index = 0.69 vs 0.73, difference + 0.04, 95% CI 0.03–0.04, p < 0.001). Biological age estimation using an imaging-based disease progression model improves prediction of non-lung cancer related death in lung cancer screening.

title: Isolating the exposomic impact of acute war and displacement within chronic crisis using multimodal, AI-enabled phenotyping
abstract: Wars often unfold within contexts of prolonged instability, yet little is known about how acute conflicts interact with cumulative exposomic adversity to shape mental health processes. Here we studied clinical and subclinical symptoms in a Lebanese sample across three groups—one assessed before the 2024 war and two assessed after, with or without displacement—within a shared background of chronic crises. Using a multimodal, AI-enabled approach combining clinical assessments, narrative coding, and large-scale linguistic and emotional profiling of life stories, we show that mental health burden does not scale linearly with acute war or displacement. Despite higher cumulative exposure, war-time groups did not exhibit higher PTSD or depression than pre-war participants, and resilience was lowest among non-displaced individuals. In contrast, narrative organization showed non-linear reconfiguration: displacement was associated with enhanced temporal structuring but reduced global causal coherence, whereas acute war exposure without displacement amplified autobiographical reasoning and explicit self-change. AI-based analyses further revealed emotional blunting rather than emotional overload, alongside increased linguistic complexity decoupled from symptom severity. By enabling scalable analysis of life narratives, this approach isolates acute vs chronic effects and reveals sub-clinical adaptations not captured by symptom measures alone, that can inform healthcare and policy in conflict-affected regions.

title: Surrogate-assisted machine learning framework for performance enhancement of Rb2CuSbF6 perovskite LEDs with MoO3/WO3 charge transport layers
abstract: Machine learning has become an impressive method to speed up the design and performance prediction of optoelectronic devices, by making the exploration of efficient high-dimensional and highly nonlinear parameter spaces. In this paper, we propose a surrogate-assisted machine learning model to train a performance enhancement of lead-free Rb 2 CuSbF 6 perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) using MoO 3 and WO 3 as hole- and electron-transport layer, respectively. This is done by physics-based simulations of devices to undertake a systematic parametric sweep of fourteen important material and device parameters producing over 11,000 samples and provides the variation in four important performance measures indicating electrical and optical efficiency. Several machine learning regression models are developed and tested to build a good surrogate model that is sufficiently accurate to predict the nonlinear interactions among all input parameters and the performance of the device. The trained surrogate model is subsequently used for rapid prediction and design-space screening across the multidimensional parameter space, enabling identification of high-performing combinations of transport-layer properties at substantially lower computational cost than repeated physics-based simulations. The suggested framework has a strong predictive potential and rapid prediction action plan in the design and development of perovskite LEDs. This paper shows how surrogate-assisted machine learning solutions can be an efficient and scaled route to creating high-efficiency, environmentally common-place lead-free perovskite light-emitting devices.

title: A blockchain-enhanced CNN architecture for robust anomaly detection in industrial and IoT cyber-physical systems
abstract: Cyber–physical and network attacks are becoming commonplace in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments, with the potential to disrupt operations, compromise safety, and potentially impact the reliability of security evidence. In this study, a modified CNN (mCNN) framework is proposed to detect anomalies with robust, auditable capabilities by incorporating blockchain technology. The detector is based on the following building blocks: dilated convolutions to capture temporal dependencies in industrial process data, multi-branch feature extraction, dataset-adaptive input structuring, and a compact classifier to model heterogeneous patterns in IoT traffic. Anomalies detected are turned into signed and hashed event records and sent to a permissioned Hyperledger Fabric workflow. They test the framework on SWaT and N-BaIoT and validate their results with three baselines: Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and LSTM, and compare them with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC. The proposed CNN is designed under the adopted protocol, and the F1-scores obtained on SWaT and N-BaIoT are 0.977 and 0.951, respectively. An incremental ablation study quantifies the contributions of dilation, multi-branch fusion, windowing, and structured input representation. The findings advocate for the use of customized CNN models for anomaly detection in heterogeneous IIoT applications, and blockchain stress testing, adversarial robustness, constrained-device profiling, and model-specific explainability are key aspects that need to be assessed in the future.

title: Machine learning–driven strength prediction and optimal waste glass powder dosage for concrete exposed to high temperatures
abstract: This study explores the synergistic effects of the addition of waste glass powder (WGP) and elevated temperatures on the mechanical behavior of concrete, and proposes a machine-learning-based framework for mixture design optimization. Six concrete mixtures containing 0–50% WGP were tested for compressive, flexural, and splitting tensile strengths over the temperature range 24–600 °C, and the results consistently showed an optimal WGP dosage of 10–20% at room temperature and a pronounced degradation in these strengths above 400 °C. To model the strength evolution across the entire WGP-temperature space, a physics-aware data augmentation method and a multi-output Random Forest surrogate model are developed and validated using mixture-wise three-fold cross-validation, parity plots, Y-randomization tests, SHAP-based interpretability analysis, and bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification. The validated surrogate is then combined with NSGA-II to determine WGP dosages that simultaneously maximize room-temperature strength, high-temperature residual capacity, and material efficiency. Both prospective within-domain experimental validation showed close agreement between the surrogate predictions and independently measured responses. Contour maps and optimization results also consistently show that the 10–20% WGP dosage offers the best trade-off between initial strength and thermal resilience. The results demonstrate the two-fold role of WGP as a micro-filler in improving ambient performance and as a thermally sensitive phase governing degradation mechanisms at elevated temperatures. Therefore, this work presents a validated ML-based framework and practical design charts for optimizing WGP-modified concrete for fire-exposed or high-temperature applications. SEM analyses of the glass powder-reinforced concrete sample exposed to 600 °C showed an increase in cracks and voids in the microstructure; EDX results indicated Ca enrichment with the dominance of O (51.49%), Ca (20.78%), and Si (8.17%); FT-IR spectrum showed the disappearance of the ~ 3400 and ~ 1650 cm⁻¹ bands and the weakening of the ~ 950–1000 cm⁻¹ band, confirming C–S–H degradation; and XRD analysis revealed a decrease in amorphous humps and the prominence of crystalline peaks, indicating that the structure became more crystalline and brittle at high temperature. TGA results indicated that room-temperature-cured samples exhibited higher mass loss and progressive degradation at low temperatures, whereas samples pre-exposed to 600 °C exhibited reduced mass loss and enhanced thermal stability, owing to prior dehydration and microstructural reorganization.

title: Predicting nitrogen dioxide column density from the International Wealth Index with a convolutional neural network in Africa
abstract: In the pursuit of improving socioeconomic living conditions of their populations, many nations struggle to meet their nationally determined contributions (NDCs) under the Paris agreement, and that shortfall makes accountability for emissions reductions critical. The long atmospheric lifetimes of key gases such as carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) hinder traditional greenhouse gas (GHG) monitoring, because what any one place emits adds only a small excess to a large, well-mixed background. Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) behaves differently: it is short-lived and highly variable in space and time, so satellite instruments resolve its patterns close to source regions. Across the African continent, mapped temporal correlations between NO 2 and CO 2 are moderate in magnitude but spatially structured and consistently positive. Although we do not use that association to mechanically convert NO 2 observations into CO 2 , we report it as contextual evidence towards NDCs. Given this context, this study asks the following question: to what extent can socioeconomic development at the neighbourhood scale predict NO 2 column densities (the amount of NO 2 in the air column above that neighbourhood) across Africa? We apply a convolutional neural network (CNN) to gridded International Wealth Index (IWI) estimates and to NO 2 observations from the tropospheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI), and obtain an average predictive accuracy of \(R^2\) = 0.56 across the African continent. Because IWI can be projected forward, we also present an illustrative 2030 scenario as a methodological demonstration of the relationship between socioeconomic development and NO 2 trajectories. These findings indicate that gridded wealth estimates carry predictive information about NO 2 column density in Africa. Such estimates offer a lightweight and scalable screening tool that complements process-based atmospheric monitoring rather than replacing it.

title: An explainable two stage framework for spatial temporal traffic accident prediction and injury severity classification
abstract: Traffic accidents pose severe risks to public safety, yet existing injury severity prediction models often overlook spatial-temporal dynamics. This study proposes a two-stage framework integrating spatial-temporal analysis with machine learning to enhance prediction accuracy and interpretability. In the first stage, a Graph Convolution Network-Long Short-Term Memory (GCN-LSTM) model predicts daily accident counts across administrative regions, incorporating the predictions normalized as relative frequencies as features for injury severity classification. The second stage, which classifies the injury severity of accidents that have occurred, employs a stacking ensemble model with four tree-based classifiers, selecting the best-performing configuration based on performance metrics. Experimental results on a real-world dataset demonstrate the framework’s superiority over traditional methods. The GCN-LSTM model reduces mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE) by 18.4% and 3.6%, respectively, compared to the state-of-the-art Spectral Temporal Graph Neural Network (StemGNN). The stacking model with Random Forest as the meta-learner achieves an 87% accuracy in severity prediction. SHAP-based interpretability analysis reveals key factors influencing injury severity, providing actionable insights for traffic safety management. This study offers an interpretable approach to injury severity prediction, supporting data-driven decision-making in accident prevention and emergency response.

title: Freeze-thaw model for compressive strength of flowable solidified soil based on machine learning
abstract: Freeze-thaw cycling is a critical factor triggering durability degradation of flowable solidified soil in cold-region engineering, and its damage evolution process is affected by multi-factor coupling with obvious nonlinear characteristics. Based on experimental compressive strength data of flowable solidified soil under freeze-thaw cycles, four influencing factors, namely solidifier dosage (SD), admixture dosage (AD), water-solid ratio (WS) and freeze-thaw cycle number (F-T), are selected as input variables. Four machine learning algorithms including Decision Tree (DT), BP Neural Network (BP), Support Vector Regression (SVR) and XGBoost are adopted to establish freeze-thaw damage prediction models for the compressive strength of flowable solidified soil. The SHAP interpretable framework is further employed for feature sensitivity analysis to quantify the contribution and nonlinear effect of each input factor on prediction results. The results reveal that the DT model suffers severe overfitting with drastic error fluctuations on the test set; BP and SVR achieve a high test‑set R 2 yet show noticeable prediction deviations; the ensemble tree model XGBoost presents well‑balanced fitting capacity and satisfactory overall prediction stability with low error dispersion. SHAP analysis indicates the feature importance ranking: F-T > SD > AD > WS. Freeze-thaw cycle number (F-T) acts as the dominant control factor, and high/low values of each factor impose distinct positive and negative effects on model outputs. The proposed modeling and interpretive analysis method can provide technical references for rapid prediction of mechanical indices of similar flowable solidified soil specimens and identification of primary influencing factors.

title: Gait freezing onset and termination prediction in Parkinson disease using shank sensor acceleration data
abstract: Motor impairment Freezing-of-Gait (FoG) is associated with reduced mobility leading to falls usually occurring in advancing Parkinson’s disease (PD). Cueing techniques have been successfully used to alleviate the event. Although, FoG prediction is extensively studied but only paucity of work includes event termination detection. Together with freezing, unfreeze event prediction is advantageous to reduce long-term cueing effects. The focus of carried work is to propose a machine-learning based framework for prediction of freeze and unfreeze events. Based on the Freeze Index (FI), a relabelling scheme is developed to represent four gait states, that are, no-FoG, pre-FoG, FoG, and pre no-FoG using publicly available Daphnet dataset, comprising of 10PD patients. Using nine extracted features from the shank sensor, Random Forest model achieved an accuracy of 95.5% using segmentation window of 2s. While episode-independent GroupKFold (5-fold) and subject-independent evaluation reported accuracy of (91.2 ± 0.9)% and (86.2 ± 4.0)% respectively representing more stricter independence constraints to generalize across episodes and, unseen subjects. Following feature selection, a reduced set of five shank features are obtained using 2s segmentation window and accuracy of 96.2% is achieved. At event level, 197 of 237 annotated FoG episodes are successfully identified at onset, corresponding to per-episode sensitivity of 83.12%. The predicted termination transitions achieved 63.6% cue-deactivation accuracy. These results demonstrate that single shank sensor can provide information for both FoG onset and termination with relatively low sensing and feature-processing requirements. However, framework requires clinical validation and its effectiveness for real-time cueing following prospective validation on larger and more diverse PD population.

title: Optimized energy efficient cluster based routing protocol for real time communication in 5G enabled VANETs using reinforcement learning
abstract: The fusion of fifth generation (5G) communication technologies with Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) provides the possibility to achieve low latency and reliable communication for intelligent transportation systems. But with high mobility of the vehicles, the frequent topology change, variable link quality, growing network density, and energy limitation, the traditional routing protocols are facing major challenges. These limitations can result in excessive control overhead, route instability, increased communication delay, and inefficient energy utilization. To overcome the above issues, this study presents an Optimized Energy-Efficient Cluster Based Routing Protocol (OEECRP) for real-time communication in 5G based VANETs by adopting Reinforcement Learning (RL) technique. The suggested framework combines the weighted dynamic clustering, energy and mobility based cluster-head selection, energy-adaptive routing with Q-learning and 5G quality of service. The cluster heads are selected by a weighted process that calculates the residual energy (40%), mobility stability (30%), and 5G link quality (30%). The Q-learning algorithm assesses network states such as vehicle density, battery level, link stability and communication delay for making intelligent routing decisions. The protocol was tested with simulation experiments in MATLAB R2023a with the 5G Toolbox and Communications Toolbox under urban vehicle network conditions with vehicle densities of 50–200. The performance metrics of OEECRP were compared with that of AODV, DSR, DSDV, GPSR, and LEACH with respect to energy consumption, end-to-end delay, packet delivery ratio (PDR), packet loss ratio and throughput. The results reported show that OEECRP kept the energy consumption in the range of 21.3 ± 0.8 to 45.4 ± 1.6, the end-to-end delay in the range of 38.5 ± 1.2 to 59.3 ± 1.9 ms and PDR in the range of 96.7 ± 0.5 to 89.1 ± 0.9 for the vehicle densities evaluated. Throughput increased from 452.1 ± 12 to 592.6 ± 20 kbps. Based on these results, the use of a hybrid approach between energy-adaptive clustering and reinforcement-learning-based routing for enhancing the VANET communication performance under different network densities seems promising. Practical deployment performance has to be further validated via repeated experiments, real mobility traces and hardware based testbeds.

title: Machine learning-based prediction of 90-day tensile strength in geopolymer concrete under varying input-variable scenarios
abstract: Accurate prediction of the long-term tensile strength (TS) of geopolymer concrete remains a complex challenge owing to the nonlinear and interactive nature of the governing parameters. This study develops and comparatively evaluates four machine-learning models linear regression (LR), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF) and support-vector regression (SVR) to predict 90-day tensile strength from a suite of physicochemical and mixture-related variables. Eleven systematically designed input scenarios were formulated to quantify the influence of different feature combinations on predictive performance. The results demonstrate a pronounced dependence of model accuracy on input configuration. Early scenarios that employed limited variable sets yielded only moderate performance (R² ≤ 0.885, with most models below 0.86), whereas the optimal configuration (S11), which incorporates water absorption (WA), ground-granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS), nano-silica, pH and bulk density (BD), substantially enhanced predictive capability. Among the models, DT achieved the highest test accuracy (R² = 0.984, RMSE = 0.751) together with the smallest generalisation gap (training R² = 0.988), indicating strong predictive performance within the investigated dataset and limited evidence of overfitting under the applied validation procedures. RF and SVR also delivered high predictive performance (R² = 0.964 and 0.956, respectively), while LR exhibited comparatively lower accuracy, underscoring the importance of nonlinear modelling approaches. Permutation-importance sensitivity analysis identified WA as the dominant influential parameter (mean ΔR² = 0.911), followed by GGBS (0.588) and nano-silica (0.277), indicating that WA and GGBS were the strongest predictors of TS within the trained model, consistent with though not a direct proof of their established physical roles in porosity and geopolymeric gel formation. Collectively, the findings indicate that the integration of advanced tree-based learning algorithms with comprehensive input characterisation provides a promising and computationally efficient framework for modelling the long-term tensile behaviour of geopolymer concrete within the range of mixtures examined; broader industrial application will, however, require external validation on independent datasets and formal uncertainty quantification.

title: Physics-guided explainable machine learning for predicting temporal scour evolution around hybrid spur dikes under unsteady flood hydrographs
abstract: Accurate prediction of local scour around river-training structures during flood events remains a major challenge because scour evolution is governed by highly nonlinear interactions among hydraulic conditions, structural permeability, sediment transport, and time-dependent bed morphology. Although machine learning has recently improved scour prediction, existing studies have primarily focused on equilibrium scour under steady flow conditions and have largely treated predictive models as black boxes, limiting physical interpretation. This study develops an explainable physics-guided machine learning framework for predicting the temporal evolution of normalized scour depth around hybrid spur dikes (Bandal-like) under unsteady flood hydrographs. A laboratory dataset comprising 1,308 observations collected under nine hydrograph scenarios with different peak discharges, hydrograph durations, and permeability ratios was used to train and evaluate four regression algorithms, including Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Regression, and CatBoost. Hyperparameters were optimized using GridSearchCV with five-fold cross-validation, and a physics-guided cumulative-maximum constraint was incorporated to maintain temporal consistency of the predicted cumulative scour envelope by preventing nonphysical decreases. Among the investigated models, CatBoost achieved the highest predictive performance on the independent testing dataset, with \({R}^{2}=0.9110\) , RMSE = 0.0504, and MAE = 0.0343, and successfully reproduced the principal characteristics of temporal scour evolution across the investigated flood hydrographs. Explainable artificial intelligence analyses using CatBoost Feature Importance, Permutation Feature Importance, and SHAP consistently identified relative time ( \(t/{T}_{b}\) ) as the dominant predictor, followed by structural permeability ( \({R}_{a}\) ), while SHAP interaction analysis revealed nonlinear and condition-dependent relationships among hydrograph position, relative discharge, flow depth, and structural permeability. In particular, the predictive contribution of relative discharge became more pronounced near peak-flow conditions, while the influence of permeability varied with hydraulic loading and hydrograph stage. The proposed framework combines predictive performance with interpretable model-based insights and physics-guided temporal consistency, providing a complementary approach to conventional scour assessment within the investigated experimental domain.

title: Rapid reconstruction-free classification from Lissajous sparse sampling using deep learning
abstract: Non-raster laser scanning techniques such as Lissajous scanning provide mechanically efficient alternatives to conventional raster scanning, but typically require computationally expensive image reconstruction before automated analysis. This reconstruction step offsets many of the speed and efficiency advantages of sparse scanning and is a bottleneck in real-time imaging systems. Here, we demonstrate that accurate object recognition can be performed directly from one-dimensional Lissajous intensity measurements without reconstructing an intermediate image. In our proof-of-concept work, optimized Lissajous scan trajectories were used to sparsely sample MNIST handwritten digits, generating one-dimensional signal representations containing 50, 100, 200, or 500 measurements. These signals were classified using one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, and k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and compared with conventional reconstruction-based image classification pipelines using both pre-trained and retrained convolutional neural networks. The proposed 1D-CNN achieved 98.60% classification accuracy using only 500 sampled measurements while classifying 10,000 test images in 0.68 s. Reconstruction-based image classifiers achieved slightly higher peak accuracy (99.34%) but required more than 150 s to reconstruct and classify the same dataset. Across all evaluated models, direct signal-domain classification reduced end-to-end computational cost by more than two orders of magnitude while maintaining comparable or slightly diminished classification performance. These findings demonstrate that image reconstruction is not a prerequisite for accurate object recognition from sparsely sampled Lissajous measurements and establish reconstruction-free deep learning as an efficient framework for intelligent laser-scanning systems. The proposed approach has potential applications in LiDAR, optical coherence tomography, endoscopic imaging, image-guided surgery, and other computational imaging systems where rapid inference and reduced computational overhead are critical.

title: Lightweight anomaly detection via knowledge distillation from ensemble teachers
abstract: This paper proposes a knowledge distillation-based anomaly detection method that employs a heterogeneous Isolation Forest ensemble as the teacher and a lightweight neural network as the student. The student learns the teacher’s soft labels by minimizing the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence. Evaluated on three categories from the MVTec 3D-AD dataset (bagel, carrot, and cookie), the teacher achieves a macro-average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.6406, whereas the student, with 2.010 million parameters in the multilayer perceptron (MLP) head and an approximately 0.051 ms detector-head inference time per image (both excluding the ResNet-50 backbone), achieves a macro-average AUROC of 0.5937 and delivers an approximately 11.6-fold detector-head inference speedup over the teacher ensemble. Compared with representative deep learning baselines (RD4AD and PatchCore), the proposed method achieves moderate accuracy with lower detector-head latency and a smaller detector-head model footprint (excluding the backbone). These results suggest that knowledge distillation can serve as an effective compression technique, transferring ensemble knowledge to a lightweight student with a measurable accuracy trade-off. The benefit of distillation is category-dependent: the student outperforms the teacher on one category but exhibits performance degradation on the others. Moreover, the No-KD ablation (student trained without KD) achieves a higher macro-average AUROC (0.6057 vs. 0.5937), indicating that soft-label distillation is a viable compression strategy rather than a universal performance enhancer. The conditions under which distillation improves or degrades performance are discussed.

title: Integrated sensor engineering and AI-assisted peptide design to target the Zika virus NS2B-NS3 protease
abstract: Zika virus NS2B-NS3 protease (ZVP) is an essential enzyme for viral replication and a promising antiviral drug target. However, peptide-based inhibitor design remains challenging. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining a recombinant FRET-based protease sensor with AI-driven peptide inhibitor design. The engineered PEprot ZIKV sensor, containing the ZVP cleavage sequence between two fluorescently labeled domains, enabled quantitative activity assays. PEprot ZIKV showed ~ 5.5-fold higher catalytic efficiency ( k cat / K m = 49 ± 7 × 10 6 M −1 s − 1 ) and a lower K m (4 nM) than a chemically synthesized substrate (22 nM) bearing the same cleavage sequence, with comparable catalytic turnover. Structural hotspot mapping of 53 ZVP crystal structures and multiple sequence alignment of flaviviral polyprotein motifs guided de novo peptide generation using RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN. Computational filtering (docking, AlphaFold-3 co-folding, MD simulations and MM/PBSA) prioritized short peptides for testing. Biochemical screening with PEprot ZIKV identified three candidate inhibitors, with peptide 715 showing the strongest activity (IC 50 = 214 µM), followed by 630 and 701. Structure-guided peptide elongation improved 630-derived variants (e.g., 630_03, IC 50 = 224 µM) but reduced potency for 701- and 715-derived sequences. This integrated approach offers a generalizable framework to accelerate the discovery of peptide inhibitors against ZVP and other viral proteases.

title: Long-term associations between land-surface indicators and dust-storm occurrence along the margins of the Taklimakan Desert
abstract: Land-surface change and atmospheric variability jointly shape dust activity in arid regions. We examined land-cover transitions, station dust-storm records, a Sentinel-1 backscatter index, meteorological variables from the fifth-generation European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts reanalysis (ERA5) and dust diagnostics from the Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2) along the margins of the Taklimakan Desert. Within the mapped domain, grassland increased from 9.45% in 1990 to 10.59% in 2023, while barren land decreased from 86.45% to 82.30%. Annual dust-storm-day trends were negative at 21 of 30 stations over available 1990–2024 records, and Sentinel-1 index trends were positive at 22 stations during 2015–2024. Mixed-effects path analysis of 3,804 station-month observations showed that the Sentinel-1 index was negatively associated with modelled dust emission (standardized coefficient = − 0.191; 95% confidence interval: −0.289 to − 0.043). The normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and friction velocity had the highest training-set feature importance in the random forest analysis.

title: Machine learning-based thorium normalization in airborne gamma-ray spectrometry for enhanced critical mineral exploration
abstract: Airborne gamma-ray spectrometry (AGRS), also known as radiometric surveying, is one of the most cost-effective large-scale methods for geological mapping, critical mineral exploration, and radiometric anomaly detection through the measurement of potassium (K), uranium (eU), and thorium (eTh) in rocks and weathered materials. However, the identification of radioelement anomalies is often affected by factors such as soil moisture variability, precipitation, and radiation attenuation. While primary single channel maps (K, eU, and eTh) reflect bedrock composition, secondary maps derived through mathematical operations among channels can highlight geochemical processes and modify radiometric contrast. Thorium is an important radioactive element in AGRS due to its relative geochemical stability and its relevance to critical mineral and nuclear energy-related systems and has therefore been widely used to normalize potassium and uranium variations. This study proposes a target-informed, machine-learning-based methodology for normalizing thorium concentrations using a Random Forest regression model to derive a model-estimated thorium reference response. The resulting reference response is then used to calculate relative normalized deviations and enhance thorium radiometric contrast in airborne gamma-ray spectrometry data. In this study, thorium is treated as a relatively stable reference component, and thorium-derived feature transformations, including squared thorium values and radiometric ratios (eTh 2 /eU and eTh/(eU + eTh)), are deliberately combined as part of a target-informed nonlinear normalization procedure. The squared thorium term emphasizes elevated thorium responses, whereas the ratio-based variables represent complementary relationships between thorium and uranium. The model was trained and evaluated using high-resolution AGRS data, and the resulting normalized products were analyzed in a Geographic Information System (GIS) to assess their geological relevance. The resulting model-estimated thorium reference surface response was used to derive normalized thorium values, modifying the spatial contrast of the original eTh response and highlighting spatially coherent thorium variations. Results indicate that the proposed feature transformations provide complementary radiometric information that may support geological interpretation and the identification of areas potentially associated with thorium enrichment and REE-bearing materials, demonstrating the potential of machine learning as an exploratory tool for radiometric data analysis and geological exploration.

title: Perceptually indistinguishable retinal OCT synthesis and objective computational framework for detection of synthetic images
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly deployed in medical imaging to mitigate data scarcity, enable scalable model development, and simulate disease progression; however, as synthetic data approaches photorealism, it introduces a critical vulnerability: the inability to reliably distinguish synthetic from authentic clinical data. In imaging-centric health systems, undetected synthetic data may erode dataset integrity, obscure provenance, propagate bias, and compromise reproducibility and regulatory auditability. Despite these risks, rigorous evaluation of synthetic image detectability remains limited. To this end, we synthesize high-resolution (512 × 512) retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) B-scans using four representative generative architectures, a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN), a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM), R3GAN, and a Latent Diffusion model (LDM) trained on 88,500 images from the AIREADI dataset and systematically evaluate their perceptual realism and structural fidelity. In particular, perceptual indistinguishability is assessed through two blinded human reader studies involving four retinal specialists, comprising a naïve and post-familiarization evaluation for WGAN-generated images and an independent evaluation of DDPM-generated images. In parallel, we introduce an objective computational framework predicated on gradient-derived (Sobel) representations, with downstream dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis (PCA) and support vector machine based (SVM) classifier, to probe latent structural divergences within feature space. Across both reader studies, retinal specialists demonstrated limited ability to distinguish synthetic from real OCT images. Classification accuracy remained near chance both before (59.5%) and after familiarization (56.5%) for WGAN-generated images, while DDPM-generated images yielded a similar near-chance accuracy (50.3%), indicating that perceptual indistinguishability was observed for both adversarial and diffusion-based image synthesis. In contrast, the proposed objective computational method achieved 99.93%, 99.63%, 99.91%, and 99.83% classification accuracy for WGAN, DDPM, R3GAN, and LDM-generated images, respectively on independent test datasets, demonstrating near-perfect discrimination between real and synthetic images. These findings delineate a fundamental disjunction between human perceptual judgment and computational detectability of synthetic medical images. Although generative models yield clinically plausible OCT scans, they encode latent structural signatures that remain imperceptible to expert readers yet are robustly recoverable with objective computational analysis.

title: Metaheuristic optimized and explainable machine learning for predicting the compressive strength of lightweight foamed concrete
abstract: Lightweight foamed concrete (LFC) can provide reduced structural dead load and enhanced thermal performance, however the compressive strength of LFC is determined by the complex nonlinear interactions between the mixture constituents, density and testing age, which makes the prediction and proportioning of the product difficult. This study addresses this challenge through leakage-resistant machine learning combined with metaheuristic optimization and explainable artificial intelligence. A literature-derived database of 993 observations was divided by mix-design group into 795 development records representing 276 groups and 198 unseen-test records representing 69 independent groups, with no overlap. Random forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) models, together with their Leopard Seal Optimizer (LSO), Harris Hawks Optimizer (HHO), and Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA) optimized variants, were assessed using 10-fold grouped cross-validation and a completely held-out test set. SHAP and PDP-ICE analyses were subsequently applied to the best-generalizing model. LSO-XGB achieved the strongest grouped out-of-fold performance ((R 2 = 0.888); RMSE = 3.93 MPa), whereas HHO-XGB performed best on unseen data ((R 2 = 0.875); RMSE = 4.10 MPa), reducing the baseline-XGB RMSE by 4.1%. HHO-XGB also produced a median absolute error of 0.82 MPa, with 95.96% and 97.47% of predictions within 5 and 10 MPa, respectively. Binder was the dominant predictor, contributing 45.4% of the global SHAP importance, followed by measured density at 16.9%. The proposed framework within the represented data domain can support preliminary LFC mixture screening and guide locally validated, multi-objective experimental designs balancing strength, density, cost, and environmental impact.

title: BioInteract combines residue-level cross-attention with protein-language and physicochemical priors for interpretable drug–target interaction prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug–target interactions (DTIs) can support the prioritisation of candidate pairs, yet published models are usually compared through numbers quoted across papers whose protocols differ, and their attribution outputs are rarely accompanied by an explicit statement of where the model may be trusted. We present BioInteract, a DTI framework combining a chemistry-aware molecular graph encoder, an ESM-2/physicochemical protein residue encoder with a configured domain-label channel, and bidirectional cross-attention, and we evaluate it inside a matched-protocol benchmark on the Davis kinase inhibitor dataset in which every model is trained with one shared partition, seed, optimiser, schedule and threshold rule. The comparison is a three-model ladder that changes one component at a time, so that adding the frozen ESM-2 representation and then replacing concatenation with cross-attention can be read separately. Both steps help, but by protocol-dependent amounts: the protein language model adds 0.120 and 0.063 AUPRC under the random and Target-ID-held-out protocols, whereas cross-attention adds 0.067 and 0.201 AUPRC under the same two protocols. A breadth check across two further architecture families places these differences in context: on the random split the five architectures tested fall within a narrow band, so the controlled Target-ID-held-out ladder carries the informative contrast. We audit chemical and sequence similarity across all partitions, evaluate exact-sequence-grouped cold-start protocols, and report leakage-aware diagnostic controls. On a strict exact-entity-novel BindingDB cohort, whose construction is documented as a complete row-level filtering waterfall for both the curated-articles snapshot and the full BindingDB release, the frozen Davis checkpoint achieved an AUROC of 0.560 and an AUPRC of 0.340; an applicability-domain analysis attributes this limited transfer principally to ligand and target novelty relative to Davis. The attribution analyses generate hypotheses about model-relevant atoms and residues, but, in line with evidence from models trained with explicit non-covalent interaction supervision, unsupervised attention is not treated here as a recovered interaction mechanism. BioInteract therefore contributes an audited, reproducible and domain-of-applicability-aware DTI reference rather than a new architectural principle.
