title: Physics-informed neural operators for rapid electric field prediction in transcranial magnetic stimulation of healthy and tumor subjects
abstract: Accurate and rapid prediction of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-induced electric fields is essential for personalized clinical applications, from individualized therapy in major depressive disorder to presurgical functional mapping in neuro-oncology. Yet conventional finite element methods are often too computationally expensive for interactive use. Existing deep learning surrogate models partly address this limitation but are largely constrained to fixed voxel-grid representations that cannot naturally accommodate the irregular geometry of subject-specific head meshes. We present the first physics-informed neural operator (PINO) for subject-specific prediction of vector TMS electric fields, built on a mesh-native dual-encoder architecture that jointly encodes head anatomy and coil configuration. By incorporating a curl-based regularization term aligned with the curl-free nature of the TMS secondary field, the PINO model promotes physical consistency as a soft regularizer alongside data-driven supervision. Trained on 75 subjects from the IXI dataset, the framework was evaluated across four independent held-out test datasets, including healthy subjects from two additional MRI cohorts and, for the first time in learning-based TMS electric-field prediction, tumor patients. The resolution-agnostic formulation generalizes across subjects, coil types, and spatial resolutions without retraining, predicting vector electric fields on approximately 300,000 gray matter volume nodes in under 100 ms on a consumer-grade GPU. Across all test datasets within the focality-50% region, the PINO model achieved median center-of-gravity errors of 0.39–0.43 mm, RMSE of 0.12–0.16 V/m, and mean angular deviations of 6.7°–7.3°, with performance within or below the error ranges reported by recent deep-learning approaches. At the selected 5% physics-loss weighting, curl loss decreased by 9.1% relative to the data-only model, while RMSE and MAD increased by only 1.6% and 1.3%, respectively. These results suggest that physics-informed neural operators provide a scalable technical foundation for rapid gray-matter electric-field approximation, supporting future studies on real-time electric-field-guided TMS workflows

title: Bayesian optimization-driven machine learning for compressive strength prediction of hybrid fiber-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete
abstract: The use of recycled coarse aggregate (RCA) in concrete provides a sustainable approach to reducing construction and demolition waste, but predicting its compressive strength (CS) is challenging due to complex interactions among binder composition, supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), fibers, and mix proportions. This study develops and compares seven Bayesian optimization (BO) based machine learning (ML) models to predict the CS of hybrid fiber-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete (HFRRAC). A dataset of 281 experimental samples with 14 input variables, including OPC, FA, GGBS, water content, aggregate proportions, and fiber characteristics, was used for model training and evaluation. Performance was assessed using R 2 , RMSE, MAE, and MAPE. The results show that ensemble and boosting methods outperform the conventional approaches evaluated in this study. On the held-out testing subset, the best-performing BO-GP-GBQR model achieved a training R 2 of 0.9959 and a testing R 2 of 0.9348, with a testing RMSE of 3.5675 MPa, MAE of 2.4883 MPa, and MAPE of 8.03%. SHAP analysis identified water content, OPC, and GGBS as the most influential parameters. The proposed framework enables accurate and interpretable prediction of 28-day CS and can support preliminary mixture screening for HFRRAC containing recycled coarse aggregate and hybrid fibers.

title: Transfer learning improves the prediction of ligand binding sites at protein–membrane interfaces
abstract: Membrane-exposed ligand binding sites in membrane proteins are emerging as important modulatory targets in drug discovery, however, their prediction remains challenging due to limited structural data. Here, we present DeepPocket-Mem, a deep learning-based approach that applies transfer learning to a convolutional neural network originally developed for soluble protein binding sites. A curated dataset comprising 605 protein–ligand complexes was used to fine-tune the components responsible for ranking candidate binding sites and predicting their shapes, followed by validation using measures of binding-site localization and spatial overlap. While transfer learning of the classification module alone did not improve discrimination between binding and non-binding sites, fine-tuning of the segmentation module enhanced pocket localization and increased the number of correctly identified sites among top-ranked predictions, as reflected by improved success rates based on distance center-to-center (DCC) and discretized volume overlap (DVO). Further improvements were achieved by restricting training to drug-like ligands with confirmed biological activity, underscoring the importance of biologically relevant data for model performance. Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of transfer learning for binding site prediction under data-limited conditions and establish DeepPocket-Mem as a useful tool for identifying membrane-embedded binding sites. Concurrently, they highlight the need for expanded structural datasets to further improve prediction accuracy.

title: Deep learning-assisted sustainable design of a multi-substrate 2.4 GHz wearable IoT antenna
abstract: Wearable antennas are essential components of modern Internet of Things (IoT) systems, enabling wireless communication for body-centric, healthcare, environmental-monitoring, and smart-textile applications. Deep learning provides an effective means of accelerating antenna design and optimization under complex material and operating conditions. This paper presents a deep learning-assisted and sustainability-oriented framework for designing a compact 2.4 GHz wearable IoT antenna implemented on three representative substrates: FR4, Rogers laminate, and felt-based textile. A unified slotted microstrip patch topology is adopted to enable a consistent comparison between rigid and flexible antenna realizations while highlighting trade-offs among impedance matching, bandwidth, mechanical flexibility, and material characteristics. A multi-substrate full-wave electromagnetic dataset containing approximately \(1.09\times {10}^{5}\) samples is generated in CST Microwave Studio by varying the principal geometrical parameters, substrate descriptors, and operating frequency over the 2.0–3.0 GHz range. A fully connected deep neural network surrogate is trained to predict the reflection coefficient from antenna geometry, substrate properties, and operating frequency, achieving an RMSE of 0.8500 dB and \({R}^{2}=0.9553\) on the held-out sample-level test partition. A separate geometry-level holdout evaluation is also conducted using six antenna configurations whose complete frequency responses are excluded from training and validation. The optimized antenna designs are fabricated on the three substrates and experimentally evaluated through calibrated reflection-coefficient measurements. For the felt-based textile prototype, additional measured reflection-coefficient responses under on-arm bending and progressive surface-wetting conditions demonstrate stable impedance matching around the 2.4 GHz ISM band. Radiation patterns, realized gain, radiation efficiency, on-body behavior, and specific absorption rate are evaluated using full-wave simulations only; no experimental over-the-air radiation validation is claimed. The simulations predict broadside radiation behavior and simulated SAR values below the applicable international safety limits. An equivalent parallel RLC model is also introduced to support the physical interpretation of substrate-dependent impedance behavior. The results indicate that the proposed surrogate-assisted framework enables rapid, substrate-aware antenna design and reduces dependence on repeated full-wave simulations. The felt-based implementation provides a practical compromise among simulated electromagnetic performance, flexibility, reduced substrate mass, and wearable suitability.

title: Representation learning for low-data protein fitness prediction using sequence–structure embeddings and graph neural networks
abstract: Accurate prediction of mutational fitness effects remains challenging in low-data protein engineering settings, where experimentally characterized variants are limited. Although recent protein language models and structure-aware neural networks have demonstrated strong performance on large-scale datasets, the relative importance of structural information, pre-trained embeddings, and optimization strategies under data-constrained conditions remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we investigate a graph-based framework that integrates AlphaFold2-derived protein structures, Masked Inverse Folding with Sequence Transfer (MIF-ST) embeddings, and graph neural networks for protein fitness prediction using a dataset of 152 TEM \(\beta \) -lactamase variants. Through controlled ablation experiments, we systematically evaluate the effects of structural quality, feature richness, pre-trained embeddings, and automated hyperparameter optimization across both random train–test splits and mutation-specific splits requiring generalization to unseen mutations. Under standard random splits, simpler feature representations perform competitively because training and test samples follow similar distributions. In contrast, under mutation-specific distribution shift, models incorporating structural information and pre-trained sequence–structure embeddings achieve considerably stronger predictive performance and improved generalization. Among the evaluated configurations, the full framework combining AlphaFold2, MIF-ST, and Optuna achieved the highest overall performance across the evaluation datasets. These findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of structure-aware representations depends strongly on the evaluation regime and highlight the importance of mutation-specific generalization when designing data-efficient protein fitness prediction frameworks.

title: Machine learning and Weibull-based reliability analysis of impact-resistant geopolymer concrete with construction demolition waste and natural fibers
abstract: This study presents a novel impact-resistant geopolymer concrete (GPC) incorporating construction and demolition waste powder, brick waste powder, slag, recycled concrete aggregates (RCA), and natural fibers (banana, jute, and pineapple) to simultaneously enhance its mechanical performance, impact resistance, and sustainability. Unlike previous studies that primarily focused on compressive strength, this study integrates experimental evaluation, microstructural characterization, machine learning, and Weibull reliability analysis to assess both the impact strength performance and reliability of GPC. By addressing the brittleness and performance variability associated with high RCA content, this study provides a practical strategy for developing durable, low-carbon concrete within the framework of a circular economy. This study examined the strength of natural-fiber-based geopolymer concrete using slag, construction demolition waste powder, brick waste powder, and RCA (0, 25, 50, 75%, and 100%). Banana, pineapple and jute fibers were used at 0.75% by volume. These combinations were mixed and tested for the compression and impact strengths of a total of 20 mixtures. In addition, microstructural analysis was performed on the GPC. Machine learning and the Weibull distribution were used to analyze the performance and reliability of the impact strength. The results showed that increasing RCA content substantially reduced impact resistance, with reductions of 45.6–57.3% in first-crack impact resistance and 54.4–62.7% in failure impact resistance for the fiber-reinforced mixtures. Pineapple-fiber-reinforced GPC exhibited comparatively stable post-cracking performance, with the ductility index remaining within 1.81–2.01 across the investigated RCA levels. The Weibull analysis demonstrated that fiber incorporation reduced the variability of impact resistance and provided more stable reliability characteristics under repeated impact loading. The XGBoost model showed good predictive capability, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.80 on the testing dataset, with root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error values of 11.05, 9.39, and 19.54%, respectively. Shapley additive explanations analysis indicated that natural coarse aggregate and pineapple fiber were the most influential variables affecting the predicted impact resistance, followed by superplasticizer dosage, RCA content, and fiber volume fraction.

title: A machine learning-based platform for predicting the potential energy of small molecules
abstract: Accurate estimation of molecular potential energy after energy minimization is vital for the rational design of targeted therapeutics. In this study, we present a machine learning platform that leverages sophisticated neural network architectures to predict the potential energy of small molecules. Accurate prediction of molecular potential energy can facilitate the computational characterization of drug- and gene-delivery-related molecules and support molecular modeling workflows. Our methodology involves designing and evaluating deep learning models, including convolutional neural network–bidirectional long short-term memory architectures, with and without multihead attention mechanisms. These models are trained on a comprehensive dataset comprising small molecules structures. By utilizing atom-wise sequential representations that preserve key geometric and chemical information, our approach effectively estimates potential energies and surpasses traditional descriptor-based machine learning methods. The integration of attention mechanisms enhances model generalization by capturing complex structural relationships, thereby streamlining virtual screening processes. Comparative analyses against existing benchmarks demonstrate the efficacy of sequence-based neural networks in molecular energy prediction, paving the way for more efficient drug discovery and polymer informatics. This platform offers a robust, computationally efficient tool for virtual screening and energy estimation of candidate molecules, supporting the advancement of targeted therapeutics through rapid molecule prioritization based on predicted potential energies.

title: Autonomous labeling of surgical resection margins using a foundation model
abstract: Assessing resection margins is central to pathological specimen evaluation and has profound implications for patient outcomes. Failure to achieve clear margins significantly increases the risk of local recurrence and may necessitate adjuvant therapies such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy. However, margin assessment faces multiple procedural challenges, including human error during manual tissue margin labeling (physical inking), tissue shrinkage and distortion from fixation and processing, and thermal damage from cautery that obscures cellular features, all of which can compromise accurate margin identification. We demonstrate a virtual inking network (VIN) that localizes the resection margin on whole-slide images (WSIs), producing a standardized, ink-free margin map that helps mitigate limitations of physical inking and enables accurate and reproducible margin measurements. VIN uses a frozen foundation model as the feature extractor and a compact two-layer multilayer perceptron trained for patch-level classification of cautery-consistent features. The dataset comprised 120 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained slides from 12 human tonsil tissue blocks, resulting in ~ 2 TB of uncompressed raw image data, where a board-certified pathologist provided boundary annotations. In blind testing with 20 slides from previously unseen blocks, VIN produced coherent margin overlays that qualitatively aligned with expert annotations across serial sections. Quantitatively, region-level accuracy was ~ 73.3% across the test set, with errors largely confined to limited areas that did not disrupt continuity of the whole-slide margin map. Our results suggest that VIN is capable of capturing cautery-related histomorphology, offering a potential ink-free margin delineation for digital pathology workflows. These proof-of-concept results warrant further validation of VIN as a tool for margin localization in larger, clinically representative cohorts.

title: Integrating ventilation assessments with IoT monitoring to evaluate indoor air quality in elementary schools of San Luis Potosí, México
abstract: Indoor air quality (IAQ) is often neglected in schools of the Global South. Carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) serve as key indicators of ventilation and exposure risk. This study employed a two-pronged approach to evaluate IAQ in elementary schools of the San Luis Potosí Metropolitan Area, Mexico. Ventilation rates were quantified in 106 spaces across 53 schools. Continuous IAQ monitoring (CO 2 , PM 2.5 , temperature, relative humidity) was conducted using low-cost Air Sentinel monitors in a convenience sample of 11 schools during cold and hot seasons. Machine learning models forecasted CO 2 concentrations one hour in advance, and the Wells-Riley model estimated airborne infection probability (AIP). IAQ was classified as poor, acceptable, and excellent in 1.3%, 31.5%, and 67.2% of classrooms, respectively. During the cold season, 97.7% of classrooms maintained CO 2 within 400–1000 ppm; in the hot season, 67.7% fell within this range and 1.2% exceeded 2000 ppm. The strongest CO 2 forecasting performance occurred in the hot season, while PM 2.5 forecasts failed in both seasons, AIP increased monotonically during the first two hours of class in both seasons. We conclude that integrating ventilation assessments with continuous IoT monitoring provides a comprehensive approach to characterizing IAQ in resource-constrained settings.

title: Knowledge distillation-based lightweight generative large language models for standardized quality control of Chinese radiology reports
abstract: Radiology reports, which document radiologists’ imaging observations and diagnostic conclusions from CT, X-ray and MRI scans, deliver core imaging evidence for clinical diagnosis and therapeutic planning. Inaccurate or disordered reports may lead to misdiagnosis and delayed intervention, posing risks to patient safety. Radiology reports are essential for clinical decision-making, yet Chinese radiology reports frequently exhibit logical inconsistencies, incomplete content, non-standardized descriptions, and formatting errors, while manual quality control remains time-consuming and inconsistent. Large teacher models can provide task-specific supervision but are difficult to deploy locally, whereas smaller models require adaptation to this clinical text task. We developed a teacher-supervised, locally deployable 4B language-model system for rule-based textual quality control of Chinese radiology reports. Among the three evaluated teacher APIs, Doubao-seed1.6-non-thinking achieved the highest macro-precision of 0.94, under the study’s precision-prioritized selection. Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 emerged as the optimal student model, achieving a macro-averaged precision of 0.90, recall of 0.49, and F1-score of 0.62. Under the deployment conditions of this study, it yielded an observed inference speed improvement of over 40-fold. Real-world clinical validation demonstrated that the lightweight model attains an alert acceptance rate of 0.74 in authentic clinical scenarios, suggesting it can serve as an adjunct for human radiologist review.

title: Multi-view context learning for human-object interaction detection
abstract: Understanding how humans interact with objects in complex visual scenes is fundamental to human-centric artificial intelligence. Yet, current Human-Object Interaction (HOI) detection frameworks often falter when faced with visual occlusions, vague interaction semantics, and scenarios that extend beyond predefined categories. We present Multi-View Context-Aware Disentangled Interaction Network (MCD-Inet), a unified framework designed to robustly detect HOIs under these challenging, open-world conditions. Our approach integrates a novel Multi-View Context Fusion mechanism that synthesizes fine grained spatial cues and broad semantic information across instance, interaction, and global levels. To decouple the learning of object localization from interaction semantics, we introduce a Disentangled Interaction Decoder, enabling clearer task specific representations. Complementing this, our Bilateral Knowledge Adaptation module bridges high-resolution spatial features from the visual backbone with abstract semantics from a pre-trained vision language model. To overcome the challenge of occluded interactions, we design an Occlusion-Robust Enhancement module, which extrapolates missing regions and mines contextual cues to recover interaction evidence. Finally, MCD-INet leverages multi-modal prompts incorporating both textual templates and visual exemplars to extend its detection capabilities to unseen HOI triplets. Extensive evaluations on HICO-DET, V-COCO, and the HICO-Ambiguous datasets confirm the superiority of our approach, achieving a new state-of-the-art mAP of 40.7% and demonstrating significant resilience in occluded and zero-shot scenarios. MCD-INet offers a powerful step toward generalizable, context-aware HOI detection in real-world visual environments.

title: A quantum-informed gradient catalyst layer architecture for freeze-resistant proton exchange membrane fuel cell cold startup via DFT guided machine learning
abstract: Cold start represents a critical barrier to automotive PEMFC commercialization, as product water from the oxygen reduction reaction freezes rapidly at sub-zero temperatures, blocking catalyst active sites and transport pathways. This work proposes a quantum-mechanically guided hydrophilic-hydrophobic gradient catalyst layer architecture optimized for freeze-resistant cold startup at − 20 °C. We utilize the Density Functional Theory (DFT) results to use N-doped carbon and MoS 2 quantum dots useful interfaces to perform a systematic analysis of the water binding energies, ice nucleation barrier, and diffusion coefficient of a surface on the material. The Q-ICE-CL framework follows a five-stage workflow: (1) DFT quantum-mechanical calculations establish water-surface interaction descriptors for N-doped carbon/MoS₂ interfaces; (2) hybrid XGBoost-GNN machine learning models trained on DFT data enable inference-time composition screening within the established design space; (3) gradient catalyst layer architecture is designed using DFT-derived wettability parameters; (4) COMSOL Multiphysics simulations pre-validate the design before physical fabrication, substantially reducing experimental iterations; and (5) experimental cold-start testing validates the fabricated gradient catalyst layer. The calculated values of quantum parameters inform the design of a three-zone gradient architecture in which the membrane-side and proton-transport zone is mildly hydrophilic (1.5% N-doped), the core zone compartment offers mixed-wettability microchannels (3% N + 8% MoS \( {\text{}}_{2}\) ) and the gas diffusion interface is hydrophobic (5% N -doped). The hybrid XGBoost-GNN ensemble achieves R² = 0.881 (MAE = 2.14 s, n = 126 test compositions) using composition-structural inputs only, representing genuine independent predictive capability; the full-feature ensemble including DFT-linked descriptors that also participate in label construction achieves R² = 0.946 (MAE = 1.24s, n = 126 test compositions) and functions as a physics-informed emulator of the DFT-to-device performance chain rather than an independent predictor. Simulations of the gradient design using COMSOL Multiphysics has been performed for future time saving purpose which reveal that the gradient design provides a 108% increase in the freeze-delay time (17.1s) compared to baseline (8.2s), and a 52% decrease in time-to-0 °C self-heating threshold (12.0s) compared to baseline (25.0s), reduce ice formation (41.7% reduction in ice area fraction, and a 97% cold-start success rate at − 20 °C (29 of 30 trials), and tolerate is 5% of performance loss after 200 freeze-thaw cycles (compared to conventional Pt/C catalyst layers). These findings establish quantum-controlled microarchitectures as a significant advance toward reliable sub-zero PEMFC operation. This multi-scale pipeline represents one of the first frameworks to integrate DFT-computed ice nucleation descriptors with ML-accelerated screening specifically for cold-start catalyst layer optimization.

title: A multimodal machine learning framework for assessing moisture and thermal damage in asphalt binder aggregate systems
abstract: Moisture and thermal degradation of asphalt binder and aggregate interfacial bonds is a major precursor to stripping, adhesion loss, and premature pavement deterioration, but conventional mixture level indicators often fail to capture early interface damage. This study develops a multimodal learning framework for post-conditioning diagnostic assessment of durability loss by integrating binder rheology, aggregate surface characteristics, conditioning variables, contact angle measurements, and image derived damage descriptors. A 720-record experimental dataset was assembled using eight asphalt binders, six aggregate sources, five conditioning states, and three replicates. Target outputs included pull off adhesion strength, retained adhesion index, moisture damage probability, failure mode, interfacial durability score, and critical conditioning class. Mean pull off adhesion strength decreased from 722.0 kPa to 453.1 kPa after saline thermal aging, while retained adhesion declined from 100.0% to 61.7%. Contact angle increased from 77.4° to 101.9° and debonded area ratio increased from 5.0% to 31.8%, confirming progressive wetting related and morphological damage. For post test diagnostic inference, the Multimodal Transformer and CatBoost fusion model achieved R² values of 0.984 and 0.968 for adhesion strength and retained adhesion, moisture damage classification accuracy of 0.96, and failure mode macro F1 of 0.90. The reported multimodal performance therefore characterizes already conditioned interfaces and should not be interpreted as prospective prediction before environmental exposure or mechanical testing.

title: Multi-class Alzheimer’s disease classification using VGG19 transfer learning with hybrid Harris Hawks Optimization and random forest
abstract: Accurate cognition-state classification of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), and Cognitively Normal (CN) is essential for early evaluation of the disease. Existing deep-learning approaches often retain redundant features, depend on dataset-specific configurations, and provide limited methodological optimization. This study proposes a transfer-learning-based MRI classification framework integrating spatial and intensity normalization, histogram equalization, double bilateral filtering, VGG19-based deep feature extraction, Harris Hawks Optimization with Simulated Annealing (HHO-SA) for feature selection, and Random Forest (RF) classification. The framework was implemented using Python and PyTorch and evaluated on the ADNI1 Complete 1Yr 1.5T dataset, containing 2,294 MRI observations from 639 subjects. Subject-level partitioning was employed to minimize data leakage. The proposed framework achieved 98.70% accuracy, 98.55% macro-precision, 98.93% macro-recall, 99.28% macro-specificity, 98.73% macro-F1, and 99.40% macro-ROC-AUC. Compared with the strongest reported benchmark accuracy of 98.20%, this study developed into 0.50%. The findings demonstrate effective retrospective three-class MRI classification and provide a reproducible computational framework for AD research.

title: Heterogeneous graph transformer with slot-based message passing for node classification
abstract: As a widely utilized data structure, heterogeneous graphs can accurately model complex structures and multi-typed relationships, finding extensive applications in social network analysis, recommendation systems, knowledge graphs, and biomedical analysis. Node classification supports these applications by identifying entity categories or functional roles. However, during the message-passing process, mapping different types of nodes into a unified representation space often leads to cross-type feature confusion, resulting in the loss of type-specific semantic information. To address this issue, this paper proposes the HGT-Slot model. First, the model employs a type-aware Slot initialization to construct type-specific representation spaces for different node types, preserving their unique semantic attributes. Subsequently, a Slot attention mechanism is employed during the message-passing phase to preserve heterogeneous semantic information through different Slot channels. Meanwhile, the Transformer architecture is leveraged to enhance interactions among node representations, thereby improving the representation capability of the model. Finally, a Slot aggregation mechanism integrates the Slot representations for local prediction, which is fused with the global prediction from the Transformer branch for classification. Experiments on three datasets show that HGT-Slot achieves the best mean Macro-F1 and Micro-F1 scores among the compared methods for node classification.

title: Dynamic fusion and robust downsampling for remote sensing object detection
abstract: In remote sensing imagery, complex backgrounds and scale variation make small objects difficult to detect. To address this issue, we propose an SRFD-CAFM (Shallow Robust Feature Downsampling - Convolution and Attention Fusion Module) framework, which is an improved RT-DETR (Real-Time Detection Transformer). It integrates CNN and Transformer to balance local and global information. A dynamic weight allocation (DWA) module adaptively regulates feature contributions, while the Shallow Robust Feature Downsampling (SRFD) module preserves fine-grained shallow information to mitigate small-object feature loss. Experiments on multiple datasets show a 1.6-point mAP50–95 improvement over the baseline, confirming the model’s capability in complex scenes and small object detection.

title: Unsupervised learning on advanced diffusion MRI metrics for clinical characterization of migraine
abstract: Current migraine classification does not fully capture its clinical heterogeneity, and no objective biomarkers are available for diagnosis or progression. Neuroimaging, especially Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), offers promising biomarkers; however, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) oversimplifies diffusion properties, motivating the development of advanced approaches compatible with clinical routine. We applied unsupervised machine learning to diffusion MRI data to explore patient stratification and evaluate whether sophisticated diffusion techniques, such as AMURA, provide information complementary to DTI. A total of 107 patients with migraine (56 chronic [CM], 51 episodic [EM]) were included. Diffusion metrics from 48 white matter regions were extracted using standard DTI parameters and advanced AMURA descriptors, alone or combined with DTI. After dimensionality reduction and feature selection, unsupervised clustering was performed using K-means, Agglomerative, and Spectral algorithms. Two clusters consistently emerged, each characterized by distinct clinical features. DTI mainly separated patients based on chronicity-related features, particularly time since onset of CM, and showed an incremental longitudinal association with topiramate response. AMURA-based clusters were associated with migraine frequency, disease duration, and medication overuse headache. These results position the combination of advanced diffusion descriptors and unsupervised learning as an exploratory framework for migraine characterization requiring independent validation.

title: XCAT-UIR: explainable cross-attention guided ConvNeXt-transformer framework for underwater image restoration systems
abstract: Underwater images play a significant role in ocean exploration, but they frequently suffer from major loss of image quality due to light absorption and scattering in underwater conditions. However, underwater image restoration remains a challenging issue because of various distortions. The primary cause of information degradation includes wavelength-dependent color attenuation, light scattering effects, and blurring of objects. Currently, deep learning methods are widely utilized for image enhancement, leveraging the concept that hidden features can be learned to improve the image quality. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning methods limits the understanding of how the model produces its restoration outputs. This study presents an Explainable Cross-Attention Guided ConvNeXt-Transformer for Underwater Image Restoration (XCAT-UIR) model. The major objective of the proposed XCAT-UIR approach is to increase the visibility, correct color distortions, preserve fine details, and improve the overall quality of degraded underwater images. The proposed approach initially performs preprocessing to improve image quality for further analysis. Subsequently, ConvNeXt and Swin Transformer techniques are employed to extract local texture and global contextual information from the preprocessed images to enhance the feature understanding. The integration of convolution-based and transformer-based feature extraction networks improves the representation capability of the restoration model. Besides, the Cross-Attention Fusion model is used to integrate local features from ConvNeXt and global features from Swin Transformer to generate discriminative fused feature representations. Furthermore, Residual Reconstruction Blocks reconstruct the enhanced underwater image from the fused features while preserving important details and reducing information loss. Lastly, Grad-CAM and cross-attention maps are used to enhance visual evidence for restoration-relevant areas and local-global feature interactions. To ensure the improved performance of the proposed model, a widespread experimental analysis is performed using a benchmark dataset. An extensive comparison study emphasized that the proposed model has gained significant performance over recent methods in terms of different measures, indicating its superiority in underwater image restoration.

title: Explainable machine learning for identifying nonlinear associations between street vitality and the built environment in a Historic District
abstract: Historic districts exhibit fine-grained spatial variation, while street vitality may relate nonlinearly to the built environment. Using 213 micro-sampling points in the Lihuangpi Road Historic District, Wuhan, this study integrates heritage location, functional facilities, transport accessibility, street networks, frontage characteristics, and streetscape visual features. OLS, GAM, and XGBoost were compared, while SHAP, LOWESS, and spatial validation were used to assess nonlinear associations, model interpretation, and reliability. Under nested random validation, XGBoost achieved R² values of 0.474, 0.490, and 0.460 for overall, weekday, and weekend vitality, respectively, outperforming GAM and OLS. However, spatial GroupKFold reduced these values to 0.012, 0.084, and 0.052, with further deterioration as training–test separation increased. In the original ten-predictor models, Distance Heritage Core ranked first (29.7%–30.0%); after adding X and Y coordinates and distance to the study-area boundary, its importance decreased to 10.6%–11.3% and its rank fell to third or fourth, indicating that part of its apparent contribution reflected general spatial position. The results show that explainable machine learning can reveal nonlinear within-area associations, but random-validation performance should not be interpreted as spatial transferability. The framework supports micro-scale diagnosis and cautious, heritage-compatible renewal in historic districts.

title: Carbon accounting method for industrial sectors at prefectural level: the case of Shanxi Province
abstract: Accurately quantifying carbon dioxide (CO₂) generation from industrial sectors at the prefectural level is both critically important and highly amenable to methodological improvement. This study develops a systematic, machine learning–enhanced framework for precise sectoral CO₂ generation estimation and robust imputation of missing data. Utilizing this framework, an extensive carbon accounting analysis is performed for Shanxi Province, a major energy production hub in China, encompassing 30 industrial sectors across its 11 prefectural regions during the years 2007 to 2022. Furthermore, the resulting dataset is used to characterize the spatial distribution and sectoral heterogeneity of industrial CO₂ generation. This study advances the existing literature along four dimensions: (i) it achieves carbon accounting at a significantly finer spatial and sectoral resolution; (ii) it introduces a more sophisticated, algorithm-driven accounting framework grounded in state-of-the-art machine learning techniques; (iii) it incorporates a broader spectrum of energy types and explicitly accounts for sector-specific variations in carbon emission factors across energy sources; and (iv) it implements a rigorous reclassification of industrial sectors alongside nuanced, deflation-adjusted treatments of monetary indicators to ensure temporal consistency and comparability of industrial carbon dioxide generation estimates over time.

title: A multi task deep learning framework for automated health condition prediction from retinal fundus images using hybrid attention and explainable AI
abstract: Although retinal fundus imaging is a non-invasive tool to assess systemic and fundus pathology, current deep learning algorithms are mostly single-task, lack clinical interpretability and are unable to handle acquisition variation between different domains. These constraints limit their clinical utility: when a patient comes to the clinic for fundus screening, they could also be diabetic, have glaucoma, AMD, and increased cardiovascular risk, with each disease having retinal vascular biomarkers that require a patient to be tested for in the clinic, which must be managed within a framework of common, interpretable, and generalizable models rather than a pipeline of independent models. To solve these problems, we suggest a multi-task deep learning network that simultaneously classifies DR severity (five-class), glaucoma likelihood (binary), AMD stage (four-class) and cardiovascular risk (binary) from a single retinal fundus image using a single forward pass. It adopts an EfficientNet-B4 convolutional backbone pretrained on the ImageNet dataset, a six-layer multi-head self-attention Transformer encoder (d_model = 512, h = 8), a novel dual-branch spatial-channel attention module that builds on, but significantly expands, the CBAM module, and four task-specific output heads that are optimized using the homoscedastic uncertainty-weighted multi-task loss following the formulation of Kendall et al. Per-task anatomical explanations are produced by back propagating the CNN backbone via Grad-CAM in the anatomical space. The proposed model was evaluated on EyePACS, APTOS 2019, Messidor-2 and RIM-ONE v3 and achieved an accuracy of 94.7%, AUC = 0.978, sensitivity = 93.2% and specificity = 95.8% while being statistically better than all single task models (DeLong test, p < 0.01, Bonferroni corrected). Under the reported experimental setting, the zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation achieves AUC ≥ 0.951, which is promising for its performance across datasets. Grad-CAM saliency maps are anatomically similar to established clinical grading criteria for each disease. The four task-specific heads share a single architecture and produce four outputs in one forward pass, but no individual patient in the training corpora had verified ground-truth labels for all four conditions simultaneously; the model is trained on partially labelled, multi-source data via a masked multi-task loss, and the cardiovascular output is an AVR-derived image-based surrogate rather than a validated clinical cardiovascular diagnosis. This proposed framework could be considered for an additional potential step toward the future when it comes to multi-disease fundus screening with an interpretable single-model solution, if it is assessed and approved at an independent multi-centre level and by regulatory bodies.

title: Physics-guided deep learning inference of intramural slow-conduction depth from simulated epicardial optical mapping
abstract: Epicardial optical mapping integrates fluorescence over depth, making intramural slow conduction difficult to localize from surface signals alone. We present a simulation-based proof-of-concept study coupling monodomain electrophysiology and Monte Carlo photon transport to generate epicardial optical action potentials (OAPs) from slow-conduction layers in a 5 mm ventricular wall. In an initial 71-case depth sweep with fixed layer properties, 5-fold cross-validation of a one-dimensional residual network gave \(r=0.963\) , \(R^2=0.916\) , and RMSE \(=0.298\) mm, with reduced performance beyond approximately 3 mm. We then varied start depth (0.5–3.5 mm), thickness (0.15–0.50 mm), and conductivity multiplier (0.15–0.4) in a 279-case factorial study. Training the same architecture on this expanded dataset and using grouped-depth cross-validation, in which every substrate variant at each test depth was withheld, retained predictive depth information across all tested combinations ( \(r=0.852\) , \(R^2=0.717\) , RMSE \(=0.476\) mm), although accuracy varied with layer thickness and conductivity. Previously acquired rabbit optical and depth-stepped microelectrode recordings showed behaviour consistent with the simulated signals but were not used to train or quantitatively validate the estimator. These results demonstrate that simulated OAP morphology contains recoverable information about slow-layer depth across the tested variations in layer thickness and conductivity.

title: Dispositional pessimism selectively predicts engagement with system-blame conspiracy theory around COVID-19 on social media
abstract: Understanding why some individuals engage with conspiracy theories online remains a central challenge in misinformation research. In this study, we analyzed data from 2,506 U.S.-based Twitter users linked to over 7.7 million of their social media engagements, focusing on six COVID-19-related conspiracy theories. Using machine learning classification of ecologically valid behavioral tracking and multilevel modeling, we investigated whether self-reported dispositional optimism and pessimism, along with experimentally measured judgment bias, could predict interest in conspiracy-related content. Our results revealed that dispositional pessimism was selectively associated with engagement with one of the six conspiracy theories examined - specifically, the narrative that “ The virus and response to it are aimed at creating economic instability and benefiting large corporations .” The remaining five theories showed no such association, and neither dispositional optimism nor judgment bias predicted engagement with any of the six narratives. These findings suggest that dispositional pessimism may increase susceptibility to conspiracy theories that emphasize systemic threats, while leaving others unaffected. This underscores the role of affective-cognitive dispositions in shaping engagement with conspiratorial narratives and real-world digital behavior.

title: Transformer-based architectures for anomaly detection in solar-wind integrated energy infrastructures
abstract: The growing incorporation of variable solar and wind power in electrical grids leads to serious issues concerning reliability due to the complexity of spatial and temporal behavior caused by factors like variations in environmental conditions, degradation of equipment, failures of sensors, and exceptional operating conditions. Therefore, we develop an innovative transformer-based deep-learning approach for anomaly detection in integrated solar-wind energy systems using real-life multivariate time series datasets from a renewable energy facility situated in Kayathar, Tamil Nadu, India. The framework proposed in this paper consists of data preparation and normalization, sliding window conducted as a set of sequences, anomaly data creation based on domain knowledge, transformer encoder enhanced with multi-head self-attention technology and the attention mechanism-based data interpretation. The effectiveness of the framework is compared with LSTM, GRU and CNN-LSTM using MSE, accuracy and ROC-AUC. The obtained results indicate the sufficient performance of the transformer model with the lowest MSE value of 0.00641 in comparison to 0.00831, 0.00859 and 0.00792 achieved for LSTM, GRU and CNN-LSTM respectively. The transformer model has also achieved the value of accuracy equal to 95% together with ROC-AUC of 0.89. However, at the default classification threshold, this accuracy was driven almost entirely by the majority (normal) class, and the model failed to identify any of the 10 labelled anomalies in the confusion-matrix evaluation (recall = 0% for the anomaly class), reflecting a severe 18.8:1 class imbalance in the test set. The correlation and attention analysis performed in the study shows that the model is capable of revealing significant interdependence among various environmental parameters and renewable power generation rates such as solar radiation and solar energy production ( r = 0.84) and wind speed and wind energy production ( r = 0.90).

title: Improved HCV genotyping based on sequence encoding and feature integration
abstract: Genomic sequence classification is an important task for understanding viral genetic variability and supporting genotype identification, particularly for viruses such as the Hepatitis C Virus (HCV). In this study, we evaluate the effectiveness of different sequence encoding techniques, supplementary genomic descriptors, and class-balancing strategies for HCV genotype classification under a stricter CD-HIT-EST cluster-aware evaluation protocol designed to reduce sequence-identity leakage. Four encoding methods were investigated, namely Frequency Chaos Game Representation (FCGR), k-mer encoding, one-hot encoding, and label encoding. These representations were evaluated using multiple machine learning models, including XGBoost, Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). To address class imbalance, SMOTE was applied, while GC content and GC skew were included as supplementary compositional descriptors. Overall, FCGR and k-mer encoding outperformed one-hot and label encoding. The best result was achieved using k-mer encoding with XGBoost and SMOTE, obtaining a macro F1-score of 0.890, accuracy of 0.922, macro precision of 0.866, macro recall of 0.925, macro specificity of 0.990, and MCC of 0.893 under the CD-HIT-EST cluster-aware evaluation setting. The statistical analysis showed that SMOTE had a clear positive effect on classification performance, particularly for the Random Forest model, while GC-based descriptors provided additional interpretability but did not show a statistically significant improvement in the k-mer-based experiment. Overall, this study demonstrates the importance of selecting appropriate sequence encodings and class-balancing strategies for machine-learning-based HCV genotype classification. The findings provide a comparative basis for future work on sequence-based classification tasks in virology and computational genomics.

title: Deployment of edge-lightweight AI vertical models in multimodal anomaly detection and energy optimization of tech-long production line
abstract: Aiming at the problems that the abnormal state of high-speed liquid packaging production lines is difficult to identify in time, the computing power of edge controller is limited, and the energy consumption regulation and condition monitoring are separated from each other, a multimodal lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) system embedded in Tech-Long production controller is constructed; this realizes the collaborative optimization of abnormal operation window identification and energy consumption of the whole line. First, this study collects vibration, acoustic, and thermal signals from the bottle blowing, filling, and packaging sections; it also constructs cross-sectional anomaly characterization through time synchronization, feature-level alignment, and hierarchical fusion. Subsequently, Feather Convolutional Neural Network (FeatherCNN) is reconstructed using kernel fusion, channel compression, and 4-bit Integer (INT4) quantization to reduce model computation and storage load; thus, the network can adapt to resource-constrained Advanced RISC Machine (ARM) edge controllers. Finally, a dual-layer control chain is built, composed of continuous basic energy-saving and anomaly risk-weighted correction, so that anomaly scores influence the updates of temperature zones, valve openings, and heat-sealing parameters via dynamic weights and adjustment gains. The experimental results demonstrate that the anomaly window recognition accuracy of multimodal FeatherCNN reaches 0.931, which is superior to traditional machine learning models, deep learning baselines and various single-modal structures. The lightweight processing reduces Floating-Point Operations (FLOPs) from 3.42×10⁹ to 0.58×10⁹, a decrease of approximately 83%. The inference latency of the complete model on the ARM controller is shortened from 18.63 milliseconds (ms) to 7.41 ms. Under the controlled conditions of fixed production line speed, material specifications, and statistical windows, the dual-layer collaborative control has reduced the overall energy consumption of the whole line by 26%. The results show that multimodal anomaly identification, model lightweighting, and energy-saving parameter tuning can work together in the same edge decision chain. The framework verifies the feasibility of resource-constrained controllers supporting abnormal monitoring and energy consumption regulation of the entire packaging line; meanwhile, it provides an engineering reference for edge intelligent deployment of similar high-speed liquid packaging lines.

title: SpecLLM: LLM-based VNIR spectral interpretation
abstract: Visible and near-infrared (VNIR) spectroscopy identifies materials from characteristic spectral bands, and spectroscopists interpret spectra by features such as peak positions and intensities. Recent machine-learning and foundation models for hyperspectral data are highly effective but return numerical outputs or latent representations rather than such feature-level descriptions. Meanwhile, LLM-based spectral approaches have mostly provided raw numerical sequences. We present a method for making spectroscopic data accessible to large language models (LLMs) through compact, feature-based representations. Instead of supplying full spectra as comma-separated values (CSV), JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), or extensible markup language (XML), the proposed approach extracts summary statistics and discriminative extrema. It serialises them as either natural language or structured JSON. We evaluate prototype-based substance classification in two complementary scenes from an open-access VNIR hyperspectral blood dataset. For the selected models, compact feature representations were substantially more effective than raw numerical encodings, but less effective than a Random Forest operating on raw spectra. The natural-language format provides a human-readable, inspectable serialisation of compact spectral evidence and reduces prompt length compared with full-spectrum encodings. We also compared natural language and JSON feature representations and found them broadly comparable.

title: Dynamic weighted federated contrastive learning for robust medical image classification under heterogeneous data
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, AI-driven medical image classification has attracted considerable attention in recent years. However, increasingly stringent data privacy regulations have significantly restricted data sharing among medical institutions, making it difficult for traditional centralized learning frameworks to effectively exploit distributed medical data resources. As a privacy-preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, federated learning enables multiple institutions to collaboratively train models without directly exchanging raw data. Nevertheless, federated learning still faces several critical challenges in practical applications, including heterogeneous data distributions and model bias caused by non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dynamic weighted learning method based on federated contrastive learning. Different from approaches that focus solely on local representation optimization or employ fixed aggregation weights, the proposed framework couples supervised contrastive local training with loss-feedback-based multi-factor client weighting, thereby jointly controlling local representation drift and server-side model aggregation. Specifically, contrastive learning is integrated into the federated learning framework by jointly leveraging local and global model representations for supervised contrastive optimization. This strategy effectively mitigates the distribution discrepancy among different clients and gradually aligns local models with the global model as communication rounds progress. Furthermore, during global aggregation, a loss-feedback rule is introduced to accept the candidate global model parameters and aggregation weights only when the candidate loss-feedback value decreases. In addition, a multi-factor weighted aggregation mechanism is introduced to comprehensively evaluate client contributions based on multiple factors, thereby assigning larger aggregation weights to local models that are more beneficial to global model optimization. Experiments were conducted on an osteoporosis knee X-ray dataset and a COVID–Pneumonia–Normal chest X-ray dataset under IID and different Non-IID settings. Under severe Non-IID conditions, the proposed method achieved accuracies of 92.12% and 96.27%, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 98.31% and 97.68%, and F1 scores of 90.92% and 93.22% on the two datasets, respectively. Comparisons with representative federated learning methods and the static-weighting ablation setting demonstrate that the proposed method maintains competitive classification performance and stable training behavior under heterogeneous client distributions.

title: Molecule-aware machine learning for predicting absorption and emission of benzothiadiazole derivatives
abstract: Predicting the absorption and emission wavelengths of 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (BTD) derivatives across diverse solvents from molecular structure alone remains challenging, and conventional random-split validation can obscure whether models truly extrapolate to new chemical structures or merely interpolate solvent effects for known ones. By enforcing a molecule-aware train–test split, in which all solvent measurements of any given chemical structure are held out together, we show that champion-model \(R^2\) falls by approximately 27–29 percentage points relative to random splitting, revealing that high random-split accuracy primarily reflects reliable prediction of solvent-induced spectral shifts rather than generalisation to unseen BTD structures. Within this framework, replacing binary with count-based Morgan fingerprints raises single-split \(R^2\) from 0.747 to 0.941 for absorption and from 0.797 to 0.916 for emission, an improvement rooted in the ability of count fingerprints to encode the recurrence frequency of donor substructures, a key determinant of intramolecular charge-transfer character. A systematically optimised deep neural network reaches \(R^2 = 0.954\) for absorption on its best of twenty random initialisations (mean \(0.83 \pm 0.12\) ), the highest value reported for this dataset, yet the molecule-aware benchmark confirms that this performance does not translate to structure-level extrapolation. Comparative evaluation of graph neural networks, multi-task learning, extended descriptor sets, and ensemble methods confirms that none outperforms the count-fingerprint approach at this dataset size. Feature-importance analysis identifies tertiary amine substitution as the dominant structural driver and solvent polarity as the strongest single feature for emission (ranked first or second in all four model/encoding combinations examined, versus 8th–13th for absorption), an asymmetry consistent with the stronger solvatochromism of relaxed charge-transfer states. These results offer practical guidance for computational screening: the models are well suited to solvent selection for known dyes, whereas the design of genuinely new structures demands expanded structural diversity in the training set.

title: XAI-driven analysis of influencing factors in streamflow-based flood forecasting via fine tuned MTV19Anet
abstract: An accurate and timely flood prediction that relies on streamflow information is important for developing an early warning system to minimize the negative effects of floods. This paper proposes a new Steam flow-based Flood prediction model using a Fine-tuned MTV19ANet architecture (SFFPM-FTA). The novelty of proposed model integrates an Enhanced Normalization Technique (enNormT) that effectively reduces the impact of large outliers. It also employs an improved entropy-based feature extraction method to enhance prediction robustness. The hyperparameters are optimized using an Improved Wolverine Optimization Algorithm (IWoOA) with SHAP, an explainable AI technique to insights into model interpretability. The study also includes the visual representation of steam flow, where normal flow and flooded flow are visually represented over river areas. The experimental analysis shows that the proposed SFFPM-FTA model obtains high performance compared to other prediction models with respect to various error measures. The proposed model demonstrates minimal errors in streamflow-based flood forecasting through improved normalization during preprocessing and enhanced entropy-based feature extraction. Compared with other baseline methods, the proposed method demonstrates superior performance, with reductions of 55.26% in MAE, 64.56% in MAPE, 83.45% in MSE, and 57.30% in RMSE, respectively. In addition, the model achieves NSE of 0.988, KGE of 0.963, and R² of 0.986, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately capturing streamflow dynamics. Overall, the proposed SFFPM-FTA improves flood forecasting accuracy and provides reliable and interpretable streamflow predictions.

title: Integrating hippopotamus optimization algorithm into machine learning frameworks for predicting suspended sediment concentrations
abstract: The vertical distribution of sediment concentration is a fundamental component of sediment transport hydraulics, directly impacting the estimation of sediment loads in riverine and channel systems. Therefore, accurate characterization of this distribution remains a critical challenge in hydraulic engineering. To address this, advanced intelligent modeling techniques offer a robust pathway for reliable prediction. This study evaluates the performance of six distinct modeling approaches—ORELM, ORELM-HOA, GPR, GPR-HOA, GMDH-ANFIS, and GMDH-ANFIS-HOA—to predict the relative sediment concentration distribution (C/C a ​). Results indicated that the integration of meta-heuristic optimization significantly enhances the predictive precision of the GMDH-ANFIS, ORELM, and GPR frameworks. Comparative analysis reveals that the GMDH-ANFIS-HOA model achieved the highest predictive accuracy, yielding an RMSE of 0.0434 and R 2 of 0.9747 during the training phase, and an RMSE of 0.0424 and R 2 of 0.9727 during the testing phase. The GPR-HOA model followed as the second-best performer. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis identified the relative depth (y/D) as the most dominant factor influencing model accuracy. These findings demonstrate that the optimized GMDH-ANFIS-HOA model provides a reliable and efficient computational tool for engineers and hydrologists, facilitating improved design and management of irrigation canals, river engineering projects, and sediment-related environmental assessments.

title: Multi-task deep learning framework for brain tumor classification and segmentation using ensemble feature extraction
abstract: Brain tumors are one of the most severe neurologic diseases, and their early and proper diagnosis is critical in developing treatment plans. MRI is often used in tumor detection; however, the manual examination is time-consuming and susceptible to human error. While deep learning algorithms have contributed to more automated brain tumor detection, there have been challenges in their implementation. For example, most methods implement classification and segmentation operations separately which increases the computational burden. In light of this challenge, this paper presents a multi-tasking deep learning architecture to detect brain tumors while incorporating both tumor segmentation and classification into one framework. Specifically, the model adopts an ensemble feature extraction technique through the use of ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B5, and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) along with attention-based modules to extract a wide range of features. A dynamic weighting process will be used to achieve effective fusion of the extracted features. In addition, classification will be the first step, and if a tumor is detected, then the U-net++ segmentation will be initiated. Experiments conducted using public MRI dataset yielded impressive results with a classification accuracy rate of 99.84%, dice coefficient of 91.22%, and IoU of 89.01%.

title: An innovative framework for student adaptability prediction using discriminant-based classification, feature selection, and sensitivity analysis
abstract: Accurately predicting student adaptability is essential for enhancing academic performance and personal development. The present study presents a classification-based approach utilizing Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) to predict student adaptability. To enhance model performance, the Turbulent Flow of Water-based Optimization (TFWO) and Giant Armadillo Optimization (GAO) algorithms are employed. The dataset, consisting of 1,205 student records with demographic, educational, and socio-economic attributes, is split into training and test sets. The two best-performing hybrid models undergo a sensitivity analysis using the FAST approach. Experimental results demonstrate that the QDA model optimized with GAO (QDGO) achieves the highest classification accuracy of 0.975, outperforming other model configurations. These findings underscore the potential of optimized classification models in student adaptability prediction, providing valuable insights for educational institutions. Future studies can explore additional hybrid models and larger datasets to further refine predictive accuracy.

title: An interpretable model for efficient and robust runoff forecasting via causal-linear attention and adaptive KAN decoding
abstract: Accurate runoff prediction is essential for water resources management, flood control, and disaster mitigation. However, existing deep learning models often face challenges in efficiently modeling long sequences, representing nonlinear runoff responses, and providing interpretable predictions. To address these issues, this study proposes LiTKAN, a hybrid runoff forecasting model integrating Temporal Causal Encoding (TCE), Global Linear Attention (GLA), and a KAN-based Nonlinear Decoder (KND). The proposed model combines temporal information representation, efficient long-range dependency modeling, and adaptive nonlinear mapping. Specifically, TCE incorporates temporal structural information into runoff sequences; GLA reduces the computational complexity of attention-based dependency modeling from O(N²) to O(N), enabling efficient long-sequence feature extraction; and KND employs learnable B-spline basis functions to characterize nonlinear runoff responses and provide data-driven interpretability. To evaluate LiTKAN under different forecasting configurations, this study conducted experiments across dual temporal scales and four representative basins with different hydrological characteristics, including multi-source meteorological-driven forecasting and univariate runoff forecasting scenarios. Results show that LiTKAN achieved competitive prediction performance under the evaluated conditions, with NSE values ranging from 0.878 to 0.994 across the four basins. The model also demonstrated improved representation of extreme runoff variations compared with baseline models. In terms of computational efficiency, the linear attention mechanism reduced runtime and GPU memory consumption compared with the standard Transformer while maintaining high prediction accuracy. Ablation experiments and interpretability analyses revealed that different model components contribute differently under different forecasting scenarios, and the nonlinear response patterns extracted by KND were generally consistent with known hydrological characteristics. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of integrating efficient sequence modeling, nonlinear representation, and data-driven interpretability for multi-timescale runoff forecasting.

title: Hybrid dual attentional-based pyramidal deep learning model for liver tumor detection
abstract: Liver tumors are life-threatening diseases that occur due to the rapid growth of liver cells and even result in a chronic condition. Nevertheless, conventional liver tumor detection struggled with the limitations of poor robustness, difficulties in identifying the complex boundaries, and inconsistent segmentation. Hence, the research introduced a hybrid dual attention-based pyramidal deep convolutional network and deep belief network (HDPCBN) for accurate liver tumor detection. Significantly, the HDPCBN approach deployed a pyramidal architecture to learn deep hierarchical features and intricate patterns of the tumor effectively. Moreover, the integration of the dual attention technique gathers the long-range relationships of both spatial and channel dimensions for accurate liver tumor detection. In addition, the HDPCBN model learns the local patterns and edges from the images, thereby leading to precise tumor detection. The Hybrid deep flow features (HDF2) extraction gathers the discriminative and textural features of the tumor, which significantly reduces the training complexity and leads to accurate tumor detection. Experimental results indicate that the HDPCBN framework obtains exceptional performance, reporting the specificity of 93.77%, accuracy of 96.52%, sensitivity of 97.89%, balanced accuracy of 95.83%, and Macro F1-score of 96.67%, while outperforming the other state-of-the-art methods.

title: Input-data perturbation in groundwater level prediction: a controlled experiment on accuracy–reliability trade-offs among data augmentation and Bayesian-type uncertainty estimation methods
abstract: Groundwater is a major water resource for irrigation and domestic use, especially in arid and semi-arid regions where freshwater is scarce and the total amount of rainfall is limited. Hence, monitoring both quality and quantity parameters of this source is necessary for optimal water resources management, environmental studies, and ecosystem modeling, as well as ecological planning. Groundwater level (GWL) variation is influenced by numerous driving factors, both natural and human-induced. Such external impacts introduce considerable uncertainty into GWL variations, which should be taken into account in hydrological modeling processes of a catchment. This study reports a controlled perturbation experiment that assessed how prescribed input-data errors in GWL drivers (e.g., meteorological variables) propagated to GWL predictions. As the imposed perturbations were synthetic rather than derived from the measurement-error characteristics of the source records, the analysis was framed as a robustness and error-propagation assessment rather than as a validated quantification of total predictive uncertainty. Three data augmentation methods (jittering, frequency domain, and test-time augmentation (TTA)) and an IBUNE-type multiplicative stochastic input perturbation, derived from the integrated Bayesian uncertainty estimator (IBUNE) framework but implemented here without its Bayesian inference step, were applied to introduce Gaussian noise at various levels into the meteorological input variables. The Random Forest (RF) model was then used to predict GWL on a daily time step using these augmented datasets, and an unperturbed RF model sharing the same chronological partition and hyperparameter configuration was used as a baseline (test NSE = 0.885, RMSE = 0.034 m). All reported accuracy indices refer to the ensemble-mean prediction series, whereas coverage and interval-width indices refer to the corresponding 95% ensemble intervals. Jittering and IBUNE provided higher point accuracy levels (with NSE and RMSE values of 0.87 and 0.036 m, respectively) while providing narrower uncertainty bands with low 95% coverages (18.0–24.1% for jittering and 34.1–36.8% for IBUNE). Frequency-domain augmentation produced moderate accuracy (NSE = 0.83 and RMSE = 0.041 m) while improving reliability (approximately 61% coverage) through wider bands. TTA presented the highest coverage (60.7% at 10% noise, rising to 83.6% at 40% noise) with wide intervals and reduced accuracy under higher noise levels. The results revealed that the jittering and IBUNE methods presented the highest prediction accuracy, while TTA produced the highest uncertainty coverage (inclusion rate). The frequency-domain method showed the most balanced trade-off between accuracy and uncertainty. Measured against the unperturbed baseline, none of the four schemes improved point accuracy. Each scheme reduced NSE, by as little as 0.004 for jittering at 10% noise and by as much as 0.066 for TTA at 40% noise, so the wider intervals were purchased with accuracy rather than gained alongside it. Because no configuration approached the nominal 95% level, the reported intervals should be read as measures of perturbation-induced spread rather than as calibrated predictive uncertainty.

title: Characteristics and simulation of ozone pollution in Haikou City under combined effects of meteorological factors and pollutants
abstract: Ozone (O 3 ) pollution has become a central concern in regional air-quality management. Using environmental monitoring and co-located surface meteorological observations for Haikou from 2016 to 2024, we examine nine-year variations in the daily maximum 8-h average O 3 concentration (O 3 -8 h) Twelve routinely measured air pollutants and meteorological variables were used as inputs to three models—random forest (RF), XGBoost, and LightGBM—to simulate and verify O 3 -8 h in 2024. Over the study period, O 3 -8 h increased at 1.61 µg (m 3 a) −1 . Haikou averaged 9.1 days of light O 3 pollution per year, with an overall exceedance rate of 2.49%. Seasonally, O 3 -8 h was highest in autumn, followed by winter and spring, and lowest in summer. The monthly cycle was bimodal, peaking at 78.7 µg m −3 in April and 101.3 µg m −3 in October. O 3 -8 h correlated positively with PM 10 and PM 2.5 ( r = 0.67 and 0.64). All three models reproduced the 2024 temporal pattern but underperformed for extreme values. RF performed best (RMSE = 21.35 µg m −3 , MB = − 5.29 µg m −3 , MNB = − 0.40%, and R 2 = 0.566), indicating stronger applicability for dynamic O 3 simulation in Haikou. The results provide a basis for ozone early warning and air-quality management in tropical coastal cities.
