title: Predictive modeling and optimization of eco-friendly cementitious grouts containing waste marble dust for semi-flexible pavements
abstract: Semi-flexible pavements integrate the advantages of flexible and rigid systems through a porous asphalt layer filled with cement-based grout; however, their high cement consumption raises environmental concerns. This study aims to optimize eco-friendly cementitious grouts incorporating waste marble dust (WMD) using machine learning techniques based on 72 experimental mixtures. The dataset included water–cement ratios (0.35–0.50), WMD content (0–25%), grout flow, and compressive strengths at 7 (CS_7d) and 28 days (CS_28d). Five machine learning models, including artificial neural networks (ANN), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) were developed and evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), coefficient of determination (R 2 ), and adjusted R 2 . Among these, the decision tree model demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy with R² = 0.994 and MAE = 0.266 MPa. Explainable artificial intelligence methods, including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and partial dependence plots (PDPs), identified 7-day compressive strength as the most influential parameter, as it provides an experimentally measured representation of the early-age strength development of the grout. Results indicate that increasing water–cement ratio and marble dust content reduces CS_28d. Model-based optimization allowed up to 32% cement replacement at a 0.4 water–cement ratio with 0.5% superplasticizer, while higher ratios reduced replacement efficiency. The findings demonstrate the potential of WMD as a partial cement replacement in semi-flexible pavement grout, supporting waste valorization and reducing cement demand while providing a data-driven approach for sustainable mixture design.

title: Comparative drying kinetics and quality analysis of dried tomatoes through improving air distribution in a bin-type solar dryer versus conventional systems
abstract: Tomato is considered among widely consumed horticulture crops which provide essential nutrients and antioxidants to the human body. Being perishable crop, tomatoes require to dry for preservation. Solar drying provides a facility to dry the perishable crops efficiently and at low cost. These dryers are categorized for their efficiency and drying mechanism. In this study a Bin type solar dryer (BSD) with improved air distribution system was compared in terms of quality of dried product, moisture removal rate, thermal efficiency and techno-economic analysis with tray type solar dryer (TSD) and conventional type solar dryer (CSD). Three air velocities V 1 (1.5 ms −1 ), V 2 (2.5 ms −1 ), V 3 ((3.5 ms −1 ), and three different slice thickness S 1 (3 mm), S 2 (5 mm) and S 3 (7 mm) were selected for evaluation. Page model, Henderson and Pabi model, Modified Henderson and Pabi model, Midili-Kucuk model, Logarithm model and Approximate Diffusion Model were selected to study the kinetics of drying process in three drying systems. The moisture content of tomato slices was reduced from 89.63 to 9.95%. The results revealed with higher drying rate tomato slices dried in BSD had higher color changes than TSD and CSD. BSD exhibited better drying performance than TSD and CSD. Slice thickness directly affected the drying performance as with increase of slice thickness, drying rate was reduced. At optimum velocity (V 2 ), BSD took 10–12 h, TSD took 14–16, and CSD took 16–18 h to dry the tomato slices depending upon thickness. BSD, TSD and CSD had 19.17, 16.83 and 15.42% thermal efficiency respectively which support the improvement in design for better drying results. The specific energy consumption was 1.86, 2.12 and 2.31 kWh/kg water for BSD, TSD and CSD respectively. With four model parameters, Midili-Kucuk model had better fit with experimental data than other models with R 2 of 0.9998, χ 2 of 0.0002 and RMSE of 0.0048. The techno-economic analysis proves the economic feasibility of BSD with higher drying capacity and lower drying time with payback period of 1.10 years. BSD offers a sustainable and economically viable solution for small-scale farmers. Future integration of AI and thermal storage could further enhance drying efficiency, reducing postharvest losses and improving food security.

title: Structure-guided design and dynamic evaluation of VP4-targeting siRNAs against rotavirus A
abstract: Rotavirus is a major cause of severe diarrheal disease in children under the age of five, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, with no currently available antiviral therapeutics and treatment being largely supportive. In this study, we developed an integrative in silico approach to design and evaluate siRNAs targeting conserved mRNA transcript of the VP4 gene of Rotavirus A across six geographically diverse countries. Candidate siRNAs were screened using established design rules, target accessibility assessment, regression-based scoring with off-target filtering and thermodynamics analysis. Three optimized siRNAs were selected and structurally evaluated through AlphaFold 3-based modeling of RISC-associated protein–siRNA complexes with independent validation using Boltz-2. The predicted interactions showed conserved binding within TRBP and AGO2 domains, corroborating efficient RISC compatibility. Molecular dynamics simulations (100 ns) showed stable conformational behavior of AGO2–siRNA–mRNA complexes, with low RMSD values (~ 0.2–0.5 nm) and limited residue fluctuations (< 0.2 nm). MM/PBSA analysis showed that siRNA02 exhibited the most favorable AGO2 binding free energy (-453.62 kJ/mol), suggesting enhanced RISC stabilization, whereas siRNA01 demonstrated the strongest target mRNA interaction (-60.63 kJ/mol), indicating superior target recognition. Comparative dynamic analyses identified two siRNAs as the most balanced candidate for AGO2 mediated VP4 silencing based on structural compatibility, reduced conformational fluctuations, and stable interactions. These findings provide a rational computational basis for VP4-targeted siRNA development, facilitating experimental validation.

title: Early and reliable short-video news verification through event-aware shot modeling and cross-modal evidence fusion
abstract: Short-video news combines titles, images, speech, and captions, allowing misleading narratives to emerge from individually authentic components. Whole-video aggregation and undifferentiated fusion can obscure when discrepancies arise and whether their sources are reliable. We present EASE-Fact, a framework for content-based news screening that models ordered visual units under an explicit observation boundary. A causal event-evolution transformer captures title-conditioned transitions, while a reliability-aware router models typed cross-modal relations and distinguishes inconsistent evidence from absent or unreliable sources. The Core model supports complete-video classification and a separately trained streaming configuration with prefix-local preprocessing and committed transcripts. The Full model adds temporally admissible historical debunking records and preserves the Core prediction when usable evidence is unavailable. Chronological and event-disjoint evaluations, matched comparisons, online first-crossing alerts, component ablations, and manual localization assess the framework’s performance and practical boundaries. The findings support temporal structure and source-quality modelling, while statistical uncertainty and event-exclusion analyses qualify comparative and retrieval gains. EASE-Fact provides inspectable diagnostics for news communication and editorial prioritization; benchmark predictions and internal conflicts remain distinct from independent determinations of factual truth.

title: A unified deep learning framework for multi-lesion detection in diabetic retinopathy using fundus images
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR), an ocular disease caused by diabetes, is a significant cause of vision impairment. Early and accurate detection of different types of retinal lesions, including Microaneurysms, Haemorrhages, Soft Exudates and Hard Exudates, is essential for DR diagnosis and prevention of associated vision loss. Conventional manual analysis of retinal fundus images is subjective and time-consuming, requiring specialized clinical expertise. Automated diagnostic systems can alleviate these issues and assist clinicians with objective analysis and improved outcomes. This work focuses on simultaneous detection of different lesion types in DR, through a unified framework. In particular, the U-Net architecture is employed for multi-lesion segmentation due to its ability to preserve fine structural details using its encoder-decoder design. Additionally, an Adaptive Batch Scaling (ABS) strategy is employed, wherein the batch size is dynamically adjusted across training epochs, based on the validation Dice score, to optimize pixel-level segmentation accuracy. The performance of U-Net is compared with other DL-based segmentation models such as Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network, YOLOv8, and Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network architectures, in terms of its ability to accurately segment and identify diverse DR lesions in retinal fundus images. Validation is performed on two different publicly available DR datasets, i.e., Indian Diabetic Retinopathy Image Dataset (IDRiD) and Diabetic Retinopathy Detection Dataset (DDR). Specifically, DDR dataset is used for training the model, which is tested separately on each of the two datasets – DDR and IDRiD, to assess intra-dataset and cross-dataset generalization. Performance metrics including accuracy, Dice score, Intersection over Union (IoU) and mean average precision (mAP), are used to evaluate the performance of the models. The findings reveal that the U-Net architecture demonstrates superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 0.925, Dice score of 0.771, IoU of 0.748 and mAP of 0.647. The results demonstrate the potential of semantic segmentation models, particularly U-Net, in automated DR screening. The proposed unified multi-lesion detection system enables simultaneous detection of multiple DR lesions in a single-pass reducing computational overhead, while maintaining reasonable detection performance. The system is envisaged to serve as a reliable tool in DR screening workflow, facilitating early diagnosis and timely intervention, thereby reducing the burden of DR-related vision worldwide.

title: Mine ecological assessment and prediction based on RSEI and a multi-neural-network framework
abstract: The Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) maps ecological quality by integrating greenness, wetness, dryness, and heat. However, because it is calculated from observations acquired at the target date, the RSEI is retrospective: it identifies ecological change after it occurs but does not itself forecast the next period. Moreover, the linear construction of RSEI through principal component analysis does not explicitly capture nonlinear temporal interactions between ecological indicators and external environmental drivers. To address these limitations, this study develops a staged convolutional neural network–long short-term memory–backpropagation neural network (CLB) framework for ecological assessment and one-step-ahead prediction in the Wangpo Mine Field, Shanxi Province, China. The framework assigns the three networks complementary roles: CNN extracts features from multivariable time series, LSTM models temporal dependence and predicts the target-period variables, and BP fuses the predicted remote-sensing indicators with climatic, topographic, and spatial variables to estimate the target-period RSEI one step ahead. Landsat-8 imagery from 2015 to 2020 was used to quantify ecological change; data from 2015 to 2019 were used for model development, and 2020 was reserved for testing. The mean RSEI increased by 12.1%, from 0.6136 to 0.6879, accompanied by an expansion of excellent-quality areas and a contraction of poor-quality areas. For the held-out 2020 data, the predicted RSEI grades were consistent with those calculated from Landsat-8 imagery, with grade-specific accuracies of 87.3–94.1%. By coupling feature extraction, temporal forecasting, and nonlinear multivariable fusion, the CLB framework may provide a methodological reference for one-step-ahead ecological-quality prediction in mining areas.

title: Data-driven insights into stainless steel pitting corrosion through large-scale literature mining and database construction
abstract: Pitting corrosion is one of the most prevalent and detrimental forms of localized corrosion in stainless steels exposed to chloride-containing environments. Its initiation and propagation are governed by the combined effects of alloy composition, environmental conditions, and experimental parameters. Although a substantial body of experimental data has been accumulated through decades of research, these data remain largely dispersed across the scientific literature, limiting their accessibility for large-scale statistical analyses and data-driven investigations. To address this challenge, this study proposes a large language model (LLM)-based framework for structured data extraction and database construction from scientific literature. By decomposing the complex information extraction process into multiple subtasks, including experimental condition extraction, pitting potential extraction, and data alignment, the framework enables the automated acquisition and integration of experimental data from unstructured scientific documents. Using the proposed framework, 12,792 candidate publications retrieved using a broad stainless-steel pitting corrosion search strategy were processed, resulting in a structured extraction output containing 36,095 experimental records. The database encompasses key information, including alloy compositions, environmental parameters, and pitting potentials. Stainless-steel-specific descriptive and statistical analyses were subsequently conducted using material-screened subsets of the extracted records. Data quality evaluation demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves strong aggregate performance in structured information extraction from complex scientific texts, while stage-specific validation indicates that pitting-potential extraction and normalization remain more challenging than the overall field-level extraction task. Statistical analysis of the resulting database reveals that existing studies are predominantly focused on room-temperature, neutral chloride environments, as well as austenitic and duplex stainless steel systems. Furthermore, partial correlation analysis revealed conditional associations between the investigated variables and pitting potential. Among these variables, molybdenum exhibited the strongest positive conditional association, whereas temperature showed a negative conditional association. Chloride ion concentration showed only a weak negative association. These trends were generally consistent with established corrosion knowledge and therefore provided a scientific plausibility check for the statistical patterns observed in the constructed database. This work highlights the potential of large language models for knowledge extraction and automated database construction from corrosion-related scientific literature. The proposed framework provides a reusable data resource and technical pathway for corrosion informatics research, while establishing a foundation for future data-driven studies on corrosion mechanism discovery, performance prediction, and materials design.

title: Cost-aware evaluation of time-series foundation models for urban air-quality and temperature forecasting
abstract: Cities with the greatest need for hyper-local air-quality and weather forecasts often have the shortest data records and the tightest compute budgets. The usual responses, searching for a tiny architecture or transferring from data-rich cities, assume foundation models are too heavy, an assumption more often adopted than tested. Across 29 cities and two domains (hourly PM2.5 and 2 m temperature), under pre-specified protocols with measured energy and a cost-adjusted decision rule, we compare all three. On PM2.5 three zero-shot foundation models spanning two families and a 4.3-fold size range are statistically indistinguishable from the tuned specialist in mean absolute scaled error (MASE 0.659-0.662 vs. 0.692 under deployable causal covariates) and formally equivalent to one another. The specialist’s apparent temperature edge (0.533 vs. 0.792) depends heavily on covariate timing: 0.638 with covariates carrying measured 24-h forecast error, 0.745 with only values knowable at the forecast origin. Perfect foresight therefore distorts the cross-domain comparison, as it can in any benchmark using future covariates. Transfer learning never significantly beats zero-shot at any budget. Under frequent retraining the untrained model uses roughly ten times less measured energy, though a once-trained specialist eventually amortizes. Where models are refreshed often, downloading one now matches training one.

title: The impact of a synchronized multimodal AI interface configuration on consumer experience journey and satisfaction
abstract: With the rapid integration of multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) into digital interfaces, understanding how combined visual, auditory, and textual cues influence consumers' experience journeys and satisfaction has become critically important for both scholars and practitioners. While prior research has examined individual modalities in isolation, the comparative effects of a specific rich multimodal interface configuration versus a minimal-modality baseline across different stages of the consumer journey remain underexplored. This study draws on cue utilization theory, presence theory, and the customer journey framework to investigate how exposure to a synchronized multimodal AI interface (text + voice + animated avatar) versus a text-only interface affects consumer satisfaction through three experimentally induced journey stages: search, evaluation, and post-purchase. A between-subjects online experiment (N = 320 recruited; 312 retained after screening) was conducted using a simulated e-commerce platform where participants interacted with an AI shopping assistant featuring either text-only or synchronized text-voice-avatar cues. Results from SEM indicate that the synchronized multimodal interface was associated with higher perceived diagnosticity and immersion, which in turn were related to higher satisfaction across all three stages. The configuration–satisfaction contrast was largest for evaluation satisfaction (Cohen’s d = 1.58, 95% CI [1.33, 1.83]); the indirect-effect patterns via perceived diagnosticity and immersion were statistically consistent with, but not demonstrative of, the proposed pathways. We emphasize that the two conditions differ not only in synchronization but also in modality count, anthropomorphic cues, and social presence; accordingly, all findings are interpreted as pertaining to the interface configuration as a whole, not to integration quality as an isolated construct. Theoretical contributions include extending cue utilization theory in the form of a speculative conjecture and identifying stage-specific patterns. Managerial implications suggest that e-commerce platforms should consider synchronized multimodal cue design, particularly during product comparison phases in simulated and early deployment contexts, and should be regarded as preliminary pending field validation.

title: Meteorological forecasting of respiratory diseases incidence with geospatial and machine learning methods
abstract: Weather conditions play a significant role in shaping human health, particularly in the incidence of respiratory diseases. This study proposes a workflow to predict hospital admissions related to respiratory conditions by integrating heterogeneous environmental and health data sources. A 15-year time series of meteorological data was combined with geographic and demographic information to derive biometeorological indices associated with hypoxia and hyperoxia. To account for spatial variability, three clustering techniques—k-means, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), and Spatial ’K’luster Analysis by Tree Edge Removal (SKATER)—were applied to define intra-provincial regions for targeted data extraction from raster models. These approaches were compared with conventional aggregation at the provincial level. Interpretable machine learning models, specifically tree-based algorithms, were used to evaluate predictive performance. The proposed spatial clustering strategies achieved comparable or improved performance relative to the baseline approach. Experiments conducted in three Spanish provinces (Cantabria, Madrid, and Valencia) yielded mean absolute errors ranging from approximately 5.4 to 8.2 cases per million inhabitants, depending on the province. Results highlight the relevance of spatially refined environmental data in improving predictive accuracy. The integration of geospatial data, meteorological models, and machine learning provides an effective framework for forecasting respiratory disease incidence. This approach supports the development of early warning systems and risk management strategies based on environmental monitoring. In this article we present how to gather, transform and model datasets from several data sources to predict hospital admissions of respiratory diseases. We also draw the importance of geographical distribution of population in order to determine the appropriate method to extract meteorological data.

title: Human-centered evaluation of data visualization understanding in vision-language models
abstract: Data visualization understanding, which requires integrating visual, numerical, and linguistic inputs, poses fundamental challenges to multimodal reasoning. Recently developed vision-language models (VLMs) are promising candidates for modeling the computations that underlie human data visualization understanding. However, whether they are useful as scientific models depends not only on whether they produce correct answers, but also on whether they approximate the patterns of responses that people produce on the same tasks. This distinction has been ignored in recent evaluations of VLMs, which typically only report overall model performance (accuracy) without direct comparison to human behavioral patterns . Here we introduce a human-centered evaluation protocol that compares VLM and human responses on the same set of visualization understanding items. We apply this protocol to eight VLMs across six assessments: five established tests of human visualization literacy, plus one designed specifically for evaluating VLMs. Models performed worse than humans on average, and this gap persisted even under lenient criteria. Moreover, while relative performance across items was somewhat correlated between models and humans, all models produced error patterns that were reliably distinct from those of humans. We envision our evaluation protocol helping to identify artificial systems that might serve as promising scientific cognitive models of how humans reason about data visualizations.

title: Advancing automatic classification of single fine particles via multimodal deep learning framework
abstract: The accurate identification and classification of single fine particles are essential for understanding emission sources, atmospheric processes, and their subsequent impacts on climate and health. However, this task remains challenging due to the highly diverse and overlapping physicochemical characteristics of various particle types. Conventional single particle analysis relies heavily on manual interpretation, which is inherently slow, subjective, and limited in scalability. To overcome these limitations, this study implemented a multimodal deep learning fusion framework that classifies fine particles into seven distinct types: dust (206), fly ash (64), metals (164), organic-rich (551), sea spray (91), soot (299), and sulfur-rich (247), by simultaneously fusing three modalities (morphology, size, and elemental composition). A comprehensive dataset of 1,622 single particles, collected from diverse emission sources and ambient environments, was utilized for model development and evaluation. Three multimodal fusion strategies were systematically evaluated: early fusion (concatenating all modalities at an early stage), traditional joint fusion (integrating independently extracted features), and attention-based fusion (dynamically focusing on the most informative features within and across modalities). The attention-based fusion architecture achieved the highest predictive performance, yielding an overall accuracy of 89.6%, a sensitivity of 0.90, and a specificity of 0.98. Furthermore, an interpretability analysis revealed that the model’s classification decisions were predominantly governed by distinctive elemental composition and morphological patterns. By rapidly classifying thousands of individual particles within minutes, this automated, high-throughput framework provides a highly scalable solution for single-particle analysis, thereby facilitating a more profound understanding of atmospheric aerosol sources, transformation mechanisms, and their broader climate and health impacts.

title: A calibrated-domain DEM–machine learning assessment of asphalt concrete stiffness and micromechanical response
abstract: Asphalt concrete is a heterogeneous composite whose stiffness and damage response depend on aggregate contacts, binder-mediated bonding, air voids, force chain evolution, and progressive bond failure. This study presents a calibrated-domain assessment of an AC-16C mixture using three two-dimensional Discrete Element Method contact/bond formulations: the linear parallel bond, soft-bond, and contact-bond models, together with a machine-learning stiffness surrogate. The 160 records constitute a hybrid laboratory–DEM/parametric dataset within a single AC-16C domain, rather than 160 physically distinct mixtures. The DEM outputs were used to interpret the contact forces, particle displacement, bond breakage, coordination number, energy dissipation, and fracture localization. The Linear Parallel Bond Model produced the stiffest response because it transferred both force and moment; the Soft-Bond Model represented gradual softening and energy dissipation and the Contact-Bond Model exhibited earlier localized bond failure. The machine learning models used uniaxial compressive strength, indirect tensile strength, dynamic modulus, and Poisson’s ratio to predict the experimental elastic modulus; DEM-derived descriptors were not included as predictors. Using a 112/24/24 training, validation, and holdout partition, Random Forest and XGBoost achieved holdout R 2 values of 0.940 and 0.928, respectively, whereas the ANN/MLP was less stable, with an R 2 of 0.847. Because the dynamic modulus dominated the feature importance, the high predictive accuracy primarily reflected the stiffness-variable collinearity within the calibrated domain. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as internal calibrated-domain interpolation rather than external validation or evidence of a general microstructure–property relationship. Broader application requires physically independent mixtures, complete DEM reproducibility information, three-dimensional verification, raw data disclosure, and measured runtime comparisons.

title: Global context integration for pharmacologically robust preclinical sleep stage classification
abstract: Sleep stage classification from electrophysiological signals is essential for studying brain function in preclinical neuroscience, yet models often fail to generalize across subjects and experimental conditions, particularly under pharmacological interventions that alter neural and muscular activity. We propose a robustness-oriented deep learning framework that integrates multi-branch feature extraction, global contextual representation, sequence modeling, and training strategies designed to reduce sensitivity to subject- and treatment-specific variability. The approach is evaluated on a large rodent dataset comprising over one million annotated EEG and EMG segments collected from multiple animals across several pharmacological conditions. It achieves strong classification performance, substantially outperforming both classical methods and standard deep learning baselines. Notably, the model maintains stable performance across treatments, showing minimal degradation when trained on limited conditions, and remains effective even with relatively small amounts of annotated data. These findings demonstrate that accurate and robust sleep stage classification is achievable despite pronounced experimental variability. The proposed framework reduces reliance on extensive annotation and improves the reliability of automated sleep analysis, supporting more scalable and reproducible preclinical research.

title: Identification of genes associated with a macrophage polarization-related transcriptional signature as biomarkers for tendinopathy based on bioinformatics analysis
abstract: Tendinopathy is a common overuse-induced musculoskeletal disorder characterized by chronic pain, collagen disorganization, and immune cell infiltration. Macrophage polarization plays a critical role in tendon inflammation and tissue repair, but its diagnostic potential in tendinopathy remains largely unexplored. We utilized two publicly available gene expression datasets, GSE26051 and GSE180836, sourced from the GEO database, serving as the training and screening cohorts, respectively. Importantly, differential expression results from GSE180836 contributed to candidate gene discovery, and this cohort was therefore not used as a validation cohort; the only independent validation of the biomarkers was performed by RT-qPCR in a clinical cohort. Genes associated with a macrophage polarization-related transcriptional signature were integrated with weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and differential expression analysis to identify differentially expressed genes associated with a macrophage polarization-related transcriptional signature (MPTSGs). Three machine learning algorithms—LASSO, SVM-RFE, and Boruta—were employed to screen for candidate biomarkers. A diagnostic nomogram was constructed and validated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and calibration curves. Additionally, functional enrichment, immune infiltration, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)/Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA), and drug-gene interaction analyses were conducted. Three biomarkers (PTCHD1, NEURL1, and ST8SIA5) were identified through integrative bioinformatics analysis and were significantly downregulated in the training cohort (GSE26051). In the independent clinical cohort (n = 30), RT-qPCR analysis confirmed that PTCHD1 and NEURL1 were significantly down-regulated in tendinopathy samples compared to controls (both P < 0.01). ST8SIA5 also exhibited a downward trend, although the difference did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.074). The nomogram model achieved an AUC > 0.7 with good calibration. GSEA revealed their involvement in key signaling pathways, including PI3K-Akt and ECM-receptor interaction. A total of 16 potential therapeutic compounds were identified via drug-gene network analysis. Our study identifies PTCHD1 and NEURL1 as robust biomarkers associated with macrophage polarization in tendinopathy, and provides new insights into its immunopathogenesis and therapeutic targeting. ST8SIA5 is proposed as a potential candidate showing a consistent trend, warranting further investigation in larger cohorts.

title: Evaluating SynthSR for MRI harmonization and quantitative analysis of hippocampal volume in autoimmune neurologic diseases
abstract: Variability in acquisition protocols limit the use of retrospective clinical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for quantitative analysis. SynthSR is an AI tool that harmonizes heterogeneous brain scans into synthetic 1-mm isotropic structural images. We evaluated SynthSR performance in autoimmune encephalitis (AE) and mimics. This multicentre study included 102 patients from the Australian Autoimmune Encephalitis Consortium, and 28 controls, comparing high-resolution reference standard T1-weighted structural scans against low-resolution (n = 27) or contrast-enhanced counterparts (n = 76), with one patient having both. Images were processed via SynthSR, with hippocampal volume measured using FastSurfer. SynthSR processing systematically overestimated hippocampal volume, with high inter-individual variability. Nevertheless, relative consistency between SynthSR-processed and original reference standard remained high (ICC = 0.88, 95% CI 0.74–0.94). Contrast enhancement did not substantially alter performance, but inclusion may require caution. While agreement between synthetic images derived from low-resolution scans and reference standard was moderate (ICC = 0.75, 95% CI 0.36–0.90), agreement with SynthSR-processed reference standard was excellent (ICC = 0.90, 95% CI 0.76–0.96). Longitudinally, no statistically significant difference in volumetric change was detected, although wide limits of agreement indicated substantial individual-level variability. SynthSR facilitates harmonization of heterogeneous MRI for group-level volumetric analyses, provided a consistent processing pipeline is maintained. However, it is not reliable for individual-level patient assessments.

title: Explainable machine learning reveals a compact, low-dimensional geometric basis underlying sheet and skeletal TPMS architected materials
abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) architectures constitute one of the largest and most diverse families of architected materials, yet the geometric principles governing their mechanical and thermal behavior remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate fourteen TPMS topologies spanning both sheet- and skeletal-based realizations and characterize their geometry through a set of sixteen physically interpretable descriptors. Combining finite element simulations with explainable machine learning, we establish descriptor hierarchies for the effective mechanical and thermal properties across the TPMS design space. Surface area and compactness emerge as universal descriptors shared by both architecture classes, while descriptors of diminishing importance differ between sheet and skeletal networks, reflecting distinct manifestations of geometric heterogeneity. Despite these differences, a unified four-descriptor representation is identified that accurately predicts Young’s and shear moduli, thermal conductivity, as well as uniaxial and shear yield limits across all topologies for both network classes with coefficients of determination exceeding \(R^2=0.93\) . Interestingly, both principal component analysis (PCA) and the nonlinear Levina-Bickel intrinsic dimension estimator reveal that the geometric descriptor space and the associated performance space collapse onto a compact, nearly two-dimensional manifold, indicating that the apparent complexity of TPMS architectures arises from a remarkably low-dimensional organization. These findings provide a unified framework, applicable across sheet- and skeletal-based network classes, for interpretable modeling and materials informatics of TPMS architected materials, and establish a compact basis for future inverse-design methodologies.

title: Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and transcriptome analysis to explore uric acid–related biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms in preeclampsia
abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a pregnancy-specific syndrome that occurs after 20 weeks of gestation. Abnormal uric acid metabolism may play a pivotal role in the onset and progression of PE. This research aimed to extensively analyze and pinpoint biomarkers related to uric acid in PE and elucidate their potential molecular mechanisms. Data related to PE and uric acid were obtained from the public databases. Biomarkers were selected and validated through differential expression analysis, machine learning algorithms, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and expression level validation. Moreover, a nomogram was applied to construct a uric acid-related predictive model for PE. Enrichment analysis, immune infiltration analysis, molecular regulatory network, drug prediction, and molecular docking were performed to further verify the regulatory roles of biomarkers. Furthermore, the expression patterns of biomarkers in core cells were investigated using dataset GSE173193. Finally, validation of biomarkers expression was performed by western- blotting and qRT-PCR. Overall, four biomarkers (ENG, JAK1, LEP, and SLC6A8) were identified as significantly associated with uric acid in PE. A predictive nomogram based on these biomarkers showed promising apparent diagnostic performance in the GSE35574 cohort. The biomarkers were significantly enriched in the “housekeeping genes”, “mitochondria”, and “signaling by Robo receptors”. Notably, JAK1 was positively correlated with gamma delta T cells, while SLC6A8 was negatively correlated with gamma delta T cells. Subsequently, 348 microRNAs (miRNAs) (like hsa-miR-4486) and 25 transcription factors (TFs) (like CTCF, TBP, and MAFK) were associated with the biomarkers. Molecular docking predicted favorable interactions for the reported biomarker-compound pairs. Moreover, ENG, JAK1, and SLC6A8 exhibited relatively high expression in extravillous trophoblasts (EVT). Finally, the results of qRT-PCR and Western blot showed that the mRNA and protein expressions of ENG, SLC6A8, and LEP in placental tissues from the PE group were higher than those in the control group, while the mRNA and protein expressions of JAK1 were lower in the placental tissues of the PE group compared to the control group, which is consistent with the expression patterns observed in the RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets. Four uric acid-related biomarkers (ENG, JAK1, LEP, and SLC6A8) were identified in PE, providing preliminary molecular clues and a theoretical reference for further mechanistic exploration and the screening of potential therapeutic targets of PE.

title: Liquid neural network-driven intelligent topology perception and path anomaly diagnosis for Ipv6 smart grids
abstract: The deployment of Segment Routing IPv6 (SRv6) in smart grids introduces highly dynamic topologies and continuous-time telemetry streams. Traditional discrete-time Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) struggle to process these asynchronous, irregularly sampled data streams without suffering from severe discretization information loss, limiting their real-time diagnostic capabilities. To resolve this, this paper proposes an intelligent topology perception and path anomaly diagnosis framework driven by Liquid Neural Networks (LNNs). The novelty of this work lies in formulating network state transitions as continuous-time dynamics governed by Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs). This approach natively accommodates irregularly sampled telemetry data without discretization, allowing the network’s internal states to dynamically adapt to transient anomalies. Furthermore, we design a multi-task learning architecture that unifies real-time topology inference and probabilistic fault forecasting into a single end-to-end framework. Experimental evaluations on a simulated IPv6 smart grid demonstrate the objective superiority of the proposed model over state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, the LNN framework achieves a 98.0% F1-score in topology awareness (outperforming Informer by 2.5%), reduces the False Positive Rate (FPR) in anomaly detection to 4.7%, and provides an Early Warning Time (EWT) of 8.5 s, which is a 13.3% improvement over the best baseline model. Comprehensive ablation and scalability studies further validate the computational feasibility and robustness of the LNN framework under high data-missing rates, providing a highly reliable monitoring mechanism for mission-critical power networks.

title: Feature driven machine learning framework for accurate and computationally efficient remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Accurate estimation of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is essential for improving the reliability, safety, and cost-effectiveness of electric vehicles (EVs). Although several machine learning models have been reported for RUL prediction, many require extensive feature engineering or high computational effort, which limits their practical use in battery management systems. This work presents a predictive machine learning framework that balances prediction accuracy with computational efficiency. The proposed framework uses sensor-derived features from the NASA battery degradation dataset. The data are first preprocessed through exploratory data analysis and normalization to improve their quality. Feature analysis identifies the maximum discharge voltage and the minimum charge voltage as the two most influential indicators of battery degradation. These features are then used to train three regression models, namely k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Random Forest (RF). The models are evaluated using multiple statistical performance metrics. Among them, the RF model delivers the best overall performance with a coefficient of determination ( \(R^{2}\) ) of 0.9421 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 77.47. The kNN model achieves comparable prediction accuracy while requiring less training time. However, the SVR model exhibits lower prediction accuracy incurring higher computational cost. The proposed framework is further validated using independent battery datasets, where the predicted RUL closely follows the observed degradation trend. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach provides accurate, reliable, and computationally efficient RUL estimation, making it suitable for real-time battery health monitoring and predictive battery management in electric vehicles. In the future, this framework has the potential to contribute to effective and scalable battery health management systems. Furthermore, it could be extended to deep learning and adaptive models to be used under diverse operating conditions.

title: Natural-language prompting builds and operates an open-source software workflow for virtual drug-discovery
abstract: Virtual docking and free-energy calculations can accelerate drug discovery, but practical use requires structural chemistry expertise, complex parameter selection and software integration. Here we show that iterative dialogue with an artificial intelligence (AI) coding assistant, OpenAI Codex, can guide a non-specialist scientist to build and operate a scripted, auditable computational workflow without direct coding. The assistant provided structural chemistry guidance and assembled an integrated pipeline for structure retrieval and preparation, binding-site definition, ligand preparation, virtual docking, interaction analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) and alchemical relative binding free-energy calculations. It also built a script generator for launching, monitoring and interpreting workflow runs. We tested the workflow on public cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) benchmarks. After primary docking and multi-seed hit refinement, the active-ligand fraction increased from 1.73% in the input library to 80% in the ten-candidate handoff set (46.4-fold over input); a short MD stage acted as a structural quality-control gate on the leading candidates. Docking and hit refinement also generalized to human immunodeficiency virus reverse transcriptase and kinesin family member 11 benchmarks. In a CDK2 free-energy benchmark, the workflow achieved root-mean-square error = 0.66 kcal/mol and Pearson r = 0.90. Prompt-guided AI can orchestrate computational drug-discovery workflows for non-specialists while the underlying calculations remain the work of established external software and every run remains auditable.

title: Physics aware joint low light and color correction for underwater image enhancement
abstract: The underwater images suffer from low illumination, absorption and scattering varies with the wavelength, poor visibility, low contrast and severe color distortion. These degradations have a negative impact on applications for underwater vision like marine exploration, object recognition and autonomous navigation. To overcome these difficulties, a Physics-Aware Joint Low-Light and Color Correction (PA-JLCC) framework to enhance underwater images has been developed. The proposed approach is lightweight, interpretable and does not require extensive training, in contrast with deep learning-based approaches. The framework estimates ambient light level, builds a depth-aware attenuation proxy by using the logarithmic color ratio, and computes a preliminary transmission map from an underwater image formation model, which is further improved by a total variation regularization. The radiance of the scenes is then reconstructed by model-based inversion, enhanced by multi-scale local contrast enhancement and Gray-World color balancing to improve the visual clarity, maintain structural details and restore natural color appearance. Extensive experiments are conducted on synthetic and real-world underwater benchmark datasets to evaluate the visual and quantitative performance of the proposed PA-JLCC framework. Specifically, the proposed approach achieves the reported Underwater Image Quality Measure (UIQM) and Underwater Color Image Quality Evaluation (UCIQE) results, which not only reflect improved perceptual image quality but also improved color fidelity and underwater contrast in various underwater environments. In addition to this, the computational complexity of the proposed algorithm is linear, O(N), where N denotes the number of pixels, making the framework computationally efficient for image enhancement applications. The efficiency and interpretability of the proposed approach make it applicable to underwater image enhancement systems.

title: EEG-based Alzheimer’s disease detection using two-branch multi-scale deep learning with integrated gradients-guided channel selection
abstract: Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is critical for timely intervention and clinical monitoring. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive, low-cost, and portable alternative to neuroimaging. However, existing traditional and deep learning (DL)-based methods often face challenges related to computational cost, representational complexity, and practical deployment. In this work, we propose Fused-MSCA-2B, a two-branch multi-scale channel-attentive 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) for EEG-based AD detection. The model processes broadband multichannel EEG directly as temporal sequences and combines multi-scale temporal convolution, residual learning, squeeze-and-excitation channel attention, and feature-level branch fusion. Specifically, Branch A uses MSCA blocks with kernel configurations \((3,5,9)\) and \((3,5,7)\) to capture local and medium-range temporal dependencies, whereas Branch B uses \((5,9,15)\) and \((3,5,9)\) to capture broader and higher-level temporal patterns. The branch-level embeddings are fused and passed through dense classification layers to generate AD/HC posterior probabilities. A key component of the proposed model is an explainable AI-guided reduced-channel selection strategy. Integrated Gradients (IG) is used to rank EEG channel relevance from validation data, enabling the EEG montage to be reduced from 19 to 12 channels. We evaluated the proposed model using two benchmark datasets. The IG-guided Top-12 configuration achieved 98.60% ± 1.18% recording-level accuracy while reducing the EEG montage from 19 to 12 channels. As a supporting ablation analysis, the Fixed Top-12 configuration achieved 98.40% ± 0.73% accuracy, further confirming the effectiveness of the IG-guided reduced-channel selection strategy. The results demonstrate that the proposed XAI-guided Fused-MSCA-2B framework supports robust EEG-based AD detection with a compact and practical electrode configuration, showing strong performance with reduced channel sets.

title: Comparative dielectric and physicochemical assessment of surfactant-free TiO2 and SiO2 nanofluids for high voltage transformer mineral oil
abstract: This study compares semiconductive TiO 2 and insulating SiO 2 nanoparticles as separate, surfactant-free additives to the same transformer mineral oil under a matched preparation and testing framework. The novelty is not the first use of nanofluids, but the controlled head-to-head evaluation of two electronically distinct oxide classes while minimizing the protocol differences that commonly prevent direct comparison across published studies. Five low loadings (0.01–0.10 wt%) were screened for kinematic viscosity, moisture content, and room-temperature AC breakdown voltage; relative permittivity and DC conductivity were additionally characterized from 30 °C to 90 °C. TiO 2 produced the largest measured AC breakdown improvement, 22.16% at 0.10 wt%, whereas SiO 2 reached its maximum improvement, 15.00%, at only 0.01 wt%. At 0.10 wt%, TiO 2 also produced a larger viscosity and DC-conductivity penalty than SiO 2 , revealing a clear performance trade-off between dielectric strengthening and charge transport. The results therefore provide a comparative concentration-selection map: semiconductive TiO 2 favors higher-loading breakdown enhancement, while insulating SiO 2 achieves its optimum response at trace loading with a smaller conductivity increase. These conclusions are restricted to the investigated concentration and test windows; quantitative long-term stability, temperature-dependent breakdown, thermal/oxidation performance, and oil-paper ageing remain necessary before transformer implementation.

title: A machine learning model for early season wildfire risk in Ghana’s Guinea savannah assessing discrimination, operational prevalence, spatial transferability, and CMIP6 climate scenarios
abstract: Tropical savannas account for most of the world’s burned area, and West Africa is a centre of both current fire activity and projected future risk, yet the northern Guinea Savannah of Ghana still lacks a locally calibrated early season fire risk tool. This study develops and critically evaluates a machine learning fire risk model for the November to January window on a 1 km grid over 2001 to 2024, using MODIS fire products, ERA5-Land reanalysis, CHIRPS precipitation, FLDAS multi-depth soil moisture, MODIS vegetation indices, SRTM topography, drought indices, and human access layers into 123 engineered features. Five algorithms were compared under a temporal split with spatial cross-validation. Discrimination was high on the held-out period, with tree ensemble AUC of 0.960 to 0.962 and overlapping bootstrap confidence intervals, and pairwise DeLong tests showing the leading gradient boosting models to be statistically comparable. Three methodological findings frame the contribution. First, because fire is rare at the cell month scale, threshold-dependent skill measured on a class balanced sample overstates operational performance: a base rate correction to the operational prevalence of about 1.7% reduces precision to roughly 0.12 to 0.14, so the model is a screening rather than an alerting tool. Second, feature attribution does not identify a single dominant driver; temperature range, population density, precipitation and soil moisture memory, and vegetation state jointly govern predicted risk, and a spatial ablation experiment shows that removing the five most influential static predictors lowers AUC by only about 0.013, indicating that most skill derives from time varying environmental variables rather than spatial memorisation. Third, CMIP6 scenario experiments suggest higher late century risk under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 but are reported as illustrative because tree ensembles cannot extrapolate beyond their training envelope and human drivers were held fixed. The framework offers a transferable template for evidence based, honestly evaluated fire risk screening in West African savanna landscapes.

title: Station-specific variability and short-term forecasting of a particulate air-quality index using machine learning in Charleroi, Belgium
abstract: Air-quality management in urban–industrial environments require reliable assessment of particulate pollution and realistic evaluation of forecasting performance. This study examined temporal variability and short-term predictability of a particulate air-quality index at Marchienne-au-Pont, Charleroi and Lodelinsart in Belgium. The analysis included 206,184 half-hourly observations collected during 2020–2023. Quality control identified a probable inconsistency in the recorded PM 2.5 and PM₁₀ fields, which was addressed through a reproducible provisional reconstruction. k-nearest neighbours, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost and a Neural Network—were evaluated using expanding-window validation and an independent 2023 test period. The four-year mean particulate index was highest at Marchienne-au-Pont (35.13), followed by Lodelinsart (31.62) and Charleroi (28.60). PM 2.5 determined the index in 67.63–74.84% of observations, whereas PM 10 determined 25.16–32.37%. Tree-based models produced contemporaneous testing R 2 values above 0.999 because the target was mathematically derived from the simultaneous particulate predictors. Separate future-forecast experiments therefore provided the principal operational assessment. One-hour forecasts achieved R 2 values of 0.857–0.920, decreasing to 0.551–0.641 at 6 h and 0.270–0.335 at 24 h. Compared with persistence, Gradient Boosting reduced RMSE by 5.80–6.29% at 1 h, 15.31–17.19% at 6 h and 12.41–12.96% at 24 h. These findings demonstrate the importance of data-quality verification, chronological validation and explicit separation of contemporaneous index estimation from genuine future forecasting. Because monitoring-agency confirmation of pollutant identity and processing history was unavailable, the reconstructed concentrations and derived results remain provisional.

title: A spatio-temporal graph neural network model for predicting economic impact of sports events and analyzing regional synergy effects
abstract: Major sporting events reshape economic activity in host cities and their surroundings through channels that input-output, computable general equilibrium, and spatial econometric tools capture only in part, because each of these tools fixes multipliers or adjacency rules before it sees the data. This study develops ST-GAT, a spatio-temporal graph attention network that forecasts a monthly regional activity index around event cycles and learns inter-regional coupling from data, with gravity-based priors entering as side information rather than as fixed weights. The forecasting target combines card-transaction consumption with night-time light intensity at the prefecture-month level; the model therefore predicts event-period activity and does not estimate welfare or causal effects. Its architecture couples attention-weighted graph convolution with multi-scale gated temporal convolution and a synergy-regularized objective, and a downstream routine turns the learned attention into a directional synergy matrix. We evaluate the framework on eight Chinese host environments, which involve fourteen host or co-host prefectures among 96 prefectural nodes observed monthly from 2014 to 2024. Averaged over five random seeds, ST-GAT lowers RMSE by approximately 25% relative to STGCN at a six-month horizon. The margin narrows against DCRNN, ASTGCN, and Graph WaveNet: the Graph WaveNet comparison ( p = 0.032) survives a Holm adjustment across seven baselines but not a Bonferroni bound, so we treat it as provisional. The advantage widens at longer horizons and persists when the pandemic window is excluded. Three exploratory patterns follow, each a property of the fitted model rather than an estimated effect. Legacy half-life rises monotonically with pre-event fixed-asset investment across the eight environments, although part of this association may be mechanical because investment is also a model input. Suzhou, Foshan, and Langfang act as predictive hubs in the attention network without hosting an event. Perturbing policy-alignment information moves the synergy output roughly twice as far as perturbing transport accessibility, a contrast that motivates, but cannot substitute for, a causal test. We therefore present ST-GAT as a forecasting and hypothesis-screening tool that indicates which co-hosting, industrial, and infrastructure relationships deserve dedicated causal evaluation.

title: Integrating disulfidptosis patterns and machine learning identifies a novel diagnostic signature for endometriosis
abstract: Endometriosis (EM) is a heterogeneous gynecological disorder with incompletely understood molecular mechanisms. Disulfidptosis, a recently identified form of programmed cell death, has not been systematically explored in EM. Gene expression profiles from the GSE51981 dataset were analyzed to investigate disulfidptosis-related genes (DRGs) and immune characteristics in EM. Consensus clustering identified molecular subtypes, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was performed to screen subtype-associated genes. Four machine-learning algorithms were subsequently compared to establish an optimal diagnostic model, which was further evaluated in two independent external datasets and validated at the expression level using RT-qPCR experiments. EM tissues showed abnormal DRG expression patterns and immune infiltration. Two disulfidptosis-associated molecular subtypes with distinct immune features and biological pathways were identified. The Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) algorithm showed the best performance and generated a five-gene signature comprising BTBD2 , SLC4A2 , SSC5D , LPPR2 , and SRGAP2C . External validation, calibration, decision curve analysis, and nomogram evaluation provided complementary evidence supporting the potential diagnostic utility of the signature. RT-qPCR provided partial expression-level validation of selected genes within the five-gene signature in EM patients. Disulfidptosis-related molecular heterogeneity is associated with immune remodeling in EM. The five-gene signature provides a potential diagnostic tool and new insights into EM mechanisms.

title: Potential role of PDLIM1 in the tumorigenesis of acute myeloid leukemia: a comprehensive bioinformatics and in vitro study
abstract: PDLIM1 has been associated with the development of multiple malignancies, but its expression profile and clinical relevance in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) have not been fully characterized. In this study, publicly available datasets were analyzed to assess differences in PDLIM1 mRNA expression between AML samples and healthy controls, while its protein abundance was preliminarily examined by immunohistochemistry. CCK8 and Transwell assays were used to evaluate the effects of PDLIM1 on the proliferation, invasion, and migration of AML cells. The molecular functions of PDLIM1 were investigated using an integrated multi-omics framework that included weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, immune cell infiltration assessment, and functional enrichment analysis. Molecular docking was also performed with AutoDock Vina to estimate the binding affinities of PDLIM1 for candidate compounds, and the highest-ranking binding conformations were visualized using PyMOL. PDLIM1 was markedly upregulated in AML tissues compared with healthy control tissues, with a standardized mean difference of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.53–1.29). This result was preliminarily validated by immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining. Clinicopathological analysis indicated that elevated PDLIM1 expression was associated with greater proportions of blasts in the bone marrow and peripheral blood, as well as increased peripheral white blood cell counts. CCK8 and Transwell assays revealed that overexpression of PDLIM1 significantly enhanced the proliferation, invasion, and migration abilities of AML cells. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrated that PDLIM1 was primarily enriched in leukemia stem cell (LSC) and AML cell populations, indicating that it may serve as a molecular marker for LSCs. WGCNA identified 332 genes related to PDLIM1 expression. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analysis further revealed significant enrichment of these genes in several biological pathways, including focal adhesion. Potential small-molecule agents associated with PDLIM1 expression were subsequently screened through the Gene Set Cancer Analysis database. The highest-ranked compounds were A-770041, afatinib, WZ-1-84, dasatinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, saracatinib, and WH-4-023. Among these compounds, A-770041 exhibited the lowest predicted binding energy, and local docking visualization identified multiple intermolecular interactions at favorable distances, suggesting that it may be the most promising candidate ligand among those evaluated. Collectively, these findings indicate that PDLIM1 is markedly upregulated in AML and LSCs and may represent a potential therapeutic target.

title: Spatial metabolomics-guided deep learning framework for dissecting immune evasion mechanisms in fungal infection microenvironments
abstract: Invasive fungal infections cause high mortality in immunocompromised patients, yet the spatially organized metabolic circuits that enable pathogens to evade host immunity remain poorly understood. Here we present an integrated computational–experimental framework coupling high-resolution spatial metabolomics with attention-enhanced deep learning to dissect immune evasion mechanisms within fungal infection microenvironments. We constructed a spatial metabolic atlas from MALDI-MSI and DESI-MSI data acquired on murine invasive pulmonary aspergillosis tissue sections, identifying 1,847 reproducible metabolite features across histologically distinct tissue compartments. A multi-scale convolutional network with fused channel and spatial attention modules was designed for automated segmentation of infection core, immune infiltration zone, and a transitional boundary zone, not previously resolved spatially in this infection model, that is enriched in immunosuppressive metabolites including kynurenine, prostaglandin E₂, and gliotoxin, achieving a mean Dice coefficient of 0.887 against expert pathologist annotations. To reconstruct the dynamic regulatory wiring underlying immune evasion, we developed a variational graph autoencoder coupled with neural ordinary differential equations, which inferred temporally evolving metabolite–immune interaction networks across 24, 48, and 72 h post-infection with an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.782 against KEGG and Reactome benchmarks. Network analysis ranked kynurenine as the highest-centrality hub metabolite at 48–72 h, and Neural ODE interpolation placed a putative metabolic tipping point between 36 and 48 h, marked by abrupt activation of tryptophan catabolism edges and a concurrent loss of Th1-associated signaling connectivity. Ablation experiments showed that the dual attention mechanism contributed the largest gain in segmentation and the second-largest in network inference, after the Neural ODE temporal coupling. This framework offers a hypothesis-generating, data-driven paradigm that recasts immune evasion as a spatially encoded and temporally dynamic process, and it yields prioritised candidate targets and therapeutic windows that remain to be tested by perturbation experiments before any antifungal intervention strategy can be built on them.

title: Automatic music emotion tag generation for short-video platforms: a self-supervised audio-lyric fusion network with valence-arousal regularization
abstract: Background music serves as a primary carrier of emotional narrative on short-video platforms, where hundreds of millions of user-generated clips are uploaded daily and organized, searched, and recommended largely through metadata. Emotion-related tags, however, are still produced mainly by manual annotation or by generic audio taggers that were never designed for fifteen-to-sixty-second clips recorded in uncontrolled environments. This paper addresses the problem of automatic music emotion tag generation for short-video platforms, a setting characterized by truncated clips, ubiquitous audio degradation, and unreliable lyric availability. To tackle these challenges, we propose SALF-Net, a self-supervised audio-lyric fusion network specifically designed to be robust to modality absence and input noise. The audio branch adapts a music-domain self-supervised transformer encoder to clip-level inputs through masked segment sampling and statistics pooling, while the lyric branch encodes automatically transcribed or metadata-provided lyrics with a pretrained language model. A gated cross-modal fusion module with modality dropout keeps the system functional when lyrics are missing, which is common for instrumental tracks and noisy recordings. A multi-task objective jointly optimizes multi-label tag prediction and valence-arousal regression, so that the psychological structure of emotion space acts as a regularizer for tag geometry. Experiments on the mood and theme subset of MTG-Jamendo, on the DEAM dimensional emotion benchmark, and on a newly constructed short-video test collection of 30,000 clips show that the proposed model reaches a precision-recall AUC of 0.389 and an ROC-AUC of 0.921, outperforming strong self-supervised baselines by a clear margin, while a distilled student variant preserves 95% of this quality at 2% of the teacher’s latency. The results indicate that accurate, robust, and deployable emotion tagging is feasible at short-video scale without relying on platform-private annotation budgets.

title: Physics-informed graph attention networks for multi-objective optimization of double skin façades: a climate-responsive framework for operational carbon reduction
abstract: This study introduces a physics-informed and climate-responsive optimization framework of Double Skin Façade (DSF) design to reduce the operational CO 2 emissions and preserve thermal and ventilation functions. The method combines building energy simulations and a Physics-Informed Graph Attention Network (PI-GAT) surrogate model and a multi-objective NSGA-II algorithm. The PI-GAT model outperforms conventional machine learning methods (ANN, RF, and XGBoost) by achieving higher accuracy and improved robustness, particularly under nonlinear and extreme design conditions, due to the incorporation of physical constraints governing airflow and heat transfer. The model is tested on two opposite climates: Tashkent (cold-dominant) and Najran (hot-arid). Findings show that optimum DSF schemes are capable of decreasing operational CO 2 emissions by 13–23% and 8–20% in comparison with baseline scenarios, respectively. Pareto analysis shows that there are unique climate-dependent trade-offs in which ventilation needs to be tightly regulated in cold climates but improved in hot climates to attain carbon-efficient operation. Overall, the proposed PI-GAT-NSGA-II framework is a credible and computationally efficient method of climate-adaptive and low-carbon design of façades.

title: The chain mediating roles of career planning and future time perspective between AI literacy and employment anxiety among higher vocational college students
abstract: Against the background of artificial intelligence (AI) reshaping the labor market, employment anxiety among higher vocational college students is becoming increasingly prominent. Grounded in Career Construction Theory, this study aims to explore the relationship between AI literacy and employment anxiety among Chinese higher vocational college students, with a specific focus on the chain mediating roles of career planning and future time perspective. A total of 1,234 students from five industry-featured higher vocational colleges in Jiangxi Province, China, were surveyed using self-report scales measuring AI literacy, employment anxiety, career planning, and future time perspective. The relationships among these variables were tested using the PROCESS macro (Model 6) for SPSS. The results indicated that (1) all variables were significantly correlated with one another; (2) AI literacy exhibited a significant positive total association with employment anxiety, which decomposed into a substantial positive direct association and a negative total indirect association; (3) AI literacy exerted a significant negative indirect association on employment anxiety through three pathways, namely, the independent mediating roles of career planning and future time perspective, and their chain mediating role, while the total association remained positive. These findings suggest that while higher AI literacy may heighten students’ awareness of labor-market disruptions, its negative indirect associations with employment anxiety operate through enhanced career planning and future orientation. It is recommended that higher vocational colleges consider integrating AI literacy education into career guidance programs, strengthening students’ career planning competencies, and cultivating a long-term future orientation, so as to potentially strengthen the anxiety-buffering pathway associated with AI literacy.

title: Whale-optimized elman neural network for predicting moisture content during seaweed drying in a v-groove hybrid solar dryer
abstract: Traditional sun-drying methods for seaweed face many challenges, such as moisture content, weather conditions, and inconsistent drying rates. This study addresses the needs of Malaysian seaweed farmers for a dependable and effective drying process by a v-Groove Hybrid Solar Dryer (v-GHSD). Data on seaweed was obtained using smart farming technology sensors attached to the v-GHSD. There are 29 main drying parameters, and by adding the second-order interaction, the parameters increased to 435 parameters to capture interaction effects. For non-linear and high-dimensional data, traditional models cannot handle the problem. Then, we applied the Elman Neural Network (ENN) based on the Whale Optimization Algorithm, support vector regression, ENN, and partial least squares regression methods to develop the predictive models. From the results, the hybrid WOA-ENN model is better, with the root mean square error of prediction of 0.0710, a correlation coefficient of 0.9974, and the relative percent deviation of 3.1165.

title: Prior knowledge informed neural network based on Basquin’s formula for predicting fatigue life
abstract: This study introduces a prior knowledge-informed neural network (PKiNN) for predicting material fatigue life. The prior knowledge module generates data adhering to S-N curve characteristics, while a pure data-driven module assesses factors like stress concentration from notches. By merging these outputs through a single-layer fully connected neural network, fatigue life predictions are obtained. Experimental validation confirmed PKiNN’s superior extrapolation capabilities compared to traditional machine learning (ML) approaches. Moreover, PKiNN’s predictive performance is less dependent on specific training data set choices, distinguishing it from current informed ML methods.

title: Multi-omic analysis of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC)
abstract: Millions of patients surviving COVID-19 infection develop post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), a debilitating condition that severely disrupts quality of life. Limited data exists on PASC patient peripheral blood multi-omic landscape. We enrolled 155 individuals with self-reported PASC who were compared with 100 acutely ill COVID-19 patients and with 44 healthy subjects. State-of-the-art mass spectrometry and next-generation leukocyte RNA sequencing were conducted in the blood samples of these participants. PASC status was associated with failure to regain a healthy baseline molecular status in these patients and aberrations in multiple biological pathways, including sphingolipids, chromatin-associated processes, and others. A machine learning algorithm trained on patients’ data produced 9 top entities allowing PASC diagnosis with a mean precision-recall area under the curve (AUC) of 0.97. An interface tool was generated to facilitate rapid access to the presented data and enable further analyses. This work provides new mechanistic insights into PASC through integrated multi-omic and machine learning analyses, establishing a robust exploratory framework and data resources to guide future biomarker validation and clinical meta-analyses.

title: Mamba-enhanced RT-DETR for ship detection in optical remote sensing images
abstract: Ship detection from optical remote sensing images remains challenging due to cluttered sea–land backgrounds, large scale variations, low-contrast small targets, and dense ship occlusion. Existing detectors struggle to balance global modeling capability, detection precision, and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a Mamba-enhanced Real-Time Detection Transformer (RT-DETR) framework for high-precision ship detection and identification. First, a Mamba-based Deformable Spatial Attention (Mamba-DSA) backbone is proposed to integrate linear-time state-space feature modeling and deformable spatial attention, which strengthens ship-specific feature representation and suppresses background interference. Second, a Context-Guided Spatial Feature Reconstruction Feature Pyramid Network (CGRFPN) is designed to enhance multi-scale context awareness and rectangular region calibration, effectively reducing missed detections in dense ship scenes. Third, a Spatial-to-Depth Depthwise Convolution (SPD-DWConv) module is developed to enhance small-target features without introducing excessive computation overhead. Experiments on HRSC2016, NWPU VHR-10, and DOTA-v1.5 datasets show that the proposed method outperforms the baseline RT-DETR by 9.0% in precision, 16.5% in recall, 19.0% in mAP@50, and 14.1% in mAP@50:95. The proposed method achieves strong robustness and efficiency, showing high practical value for maritime monitoring, port security, and emergency response.
