title: Integrated hierarchical fusion of GRU and meta-features for enhanced identification and interpretation of calcium ion inhibitors
abstract: The flow of calcium ions across cell membranes is essential for a wide range of physiological processes, including hormone secretion, epithelial function, the maintenance of electrochemical gradients, and the generation of electrical impulses. Calcium ion inhibitors have emerged as promising therapeutic agents for the treatment of various conditions such as cancer, muscle weakness, renal dysfunction, endocrine disorders, impaired cell function, and cardiac arrhythmias. Therefore, accurate identification and characterization of these inhibitors is crucial in regulating ion flow through calcium channels. In this study, we develop a neural network-based model for the identification of calcium ion inhibitors. To construct a comprehensive predictive framework, we employed seven peptide-encoding strategies and five distinct machine learning classifiers, resulting in 35 baseline models. From each, we extracted 35-dimensional probabilistic outputs and 35-dimensional predicted class labels, which were concatenated into a unified 70-dimensional meta-feature vector. In addition, we used the AAindex matrix to encode the physicochemical and biostructural properties of the peptide sequences. A gated recurrent unit (GRU) model was applied to capture long-range dependencies within this matrix, producing another 70-dimensional feature vector. The two 70-dimensional vectors were then concatenated into a final 140-dimensional representation, integrating physicochemical, biostructural, biochemical, and sequence-derived features. This 140D feature vector was used to train a two-layer multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier. On the independent test set, our proposed model (PredCaII) achieved an accuracy of 0.941, MCC of 0.883, and AUC of 0.990, outperforming the state-of-the-art Multi-Branch-CNN method (accuracy: 0.751, MCC: 0.431, AUC: 0.766) and all individual baseline models. Furthermore, we assessed the interpretability and robustness of the model using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) and Integrated Gradients. These interpretability analyses provided deep insight into the model’s decision-making behavior, highlighting the most influential compositional and physicochemical characteristics. The experimental results demonstrated the proposed method offers a powerful and interpretable computational framework for the discovery and screening of potential calcium ion inhibitors.

title: Identifying prevalent multimorbidity and its correlates in a low- and middle-income country: a machine learning analysis
abstract: Multimorbidity, the coexistence of two or more chronic conditions, presents growing challenges for health systems in low- and middle-income countries. Neighbourhood socioeconomic conditions are widely assumed to contribute to multimorbidity risk beyond individual characteristics, but this contribution has not been quantified in sub-Saharan Africa. We estimated how much neighbourhood socioeconomic context adds to the identification of prevalent multimorbidity, over and above individual characteristics and place of residence, and compared machine learning with conventional regression for this task. We analysed cross-sectional data from 6,177 adults aged 15 years and older in 691 primary sampling units in the 2016 South Africa Demographic and Health Survey. Multimorbidity was defined as two or more of twelve chronic conditions ascertained by biomarker measurement, self-reported diagnosis or reported treatment. Predictors were classified by temporal status as structural, behavioural, or illness-concurrent; the primary model excluded illness-concurrent variables because current medication use is itself a criterion for ascertaining two of the outcome conditions. We compared 18 supervised algorithms with three regression comparators using repeated ten-fold cross-validation grouped by primary sampling unit, with sampling weights applied in the evaluation of all algorithms and in the fitting of those that accept observation weights. Discrimination was estimated from pooled out-of-fold predictions with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals. We assessed subgroup sensitivity, false-negative rate and calibration across wealth, age, sex, residence and province. Multimorbidity affected 2,628 participants (weighted prevalence 40.0%). The primary model achieved an area under the curve of 0.776 (95% CI 0.760–0.793), sensitivity 0.599 (0.568–0.631) and specificity 0.785 (0.764–0.804). Adding neighbourhood socioeconomic indicators to a model already containing individual characteristics, province and urban/rural residence changed discrimination by 0.001 (95% CI -0.001 to 0.002); the neighbourhood-level intraclass correlation was 0.027. Machine learning offered no advantage over conventional regression: multilevel logistic regression with a primary-sampling-unit random intercept achieved an identical area under the curve of 0.776 (0.761–0.793), and the total spread across the five best-performing algorithms was 0.004. Including illness-concurrent predictors inflated discrimination by 0.031 (0.025–0.036). Although accuracy was similar across subgroups, sensitivity ranged from 0.00 in adults aged 15–24 years to 0.95 in those aged 65 and over. In a weighted analytic sample drawn from a nationally representative South African survey, neighbourhood socioeconomic context contributed negligibly to identifying prevalent multimorbidity once individual characteristics and place of residence were accounted for, and flexible machine learning offered no discriminative advantage over an appropriately specified multilevel regression. Reported performance of multimorbidity models is materially inflated by predictors that reflect existing disease. Because these data are cross-sectional, the model identifies prevalent rather than incident multimorbidity, and comparable subgroup accuracy conceals near-total failure to identify affected younger adults.

title: Predicting walking recovery after traumatic cervical spinal cord injury with machine learning: a multicenter cohort study
abstract: This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of various ML models—Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression (LR), Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), and Decision Tree (DT)—in predicting walking recovery after TCSCI. The goal is to develop a robust, personalized predictive model using demographics, injury characteristics, peripheral inflammatory blood biomarkers, and neuroimaging factors metrics. A retrospective cohort of 468 TCSCI patients treated between 2016 and 2022 was included. Patients were divided into training (235), testing (99), and validation (134) groups. Key prognostic features, including demographic data, injury characteristics, peripheral inflammatory blood biomarkers, and MRI features were collected. Several ML models were developed and validated using the training cohort, and performance was assessed in both internal (testing cohort) and external (validation cohort) validation cohorts. Model performance was evaluated using area under the curve (AUC) with 95% DeLong confidence intervals, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and Brier score for calibration. The study demonstrated that all six ML models successfully predicted walking recovery after TSCI. Among the models, the RF model exhibited the highest performance in the training cohort, achieving perfect AUC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV. However, its performance slightly decreased in the validation cohort, AUC of 0.990 (95% CI 0.977–1.000). The LR model showed stable and reliable performance across all cohorts, making it a solid option for predicting recovery. The SVM, DT, and LASSO models also exhibited strong predictive abilities, though with slight variations in performance across cohorts. However, the KNN model showed the lowest overall accuracy and NPV. ML models, particularly RF and LR, offer robust tools for predicting walking recovery in patients with TCSCI. While the RF model performed best in the training cohort, the LR model demonstrated consistent and reliable results across all cohorts, suggesting its potential for clinical application. Meanwhile, the SVM, DT and LASSO models also showed strong performance. These models could aid in personalized rehabilitation planning, improving clinical decision-making and patient prognostication.

title: Blockchain-enhanced SDN framework with deep unfolding spatial frequency attention network and pine cone optimization for smart city IoT cybersecurity
abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) in smart cities has revolutionized services by connecting numerous devices to deliver intelligent applications. However, this interconnected environment also exposes IoT networks to severe cybersecurity risks, including data breaches, intrusions, and advanced persistent threats. Traditional detection mechanisms often struggle with high-dimensional traffic, noisy data, missing values, and evolving attack patterns, which significantly reduce their reliability. Moreover, ensuring secure and tamper-proof storage of detection outcomes in large-scale IoT system s remains a major challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-enhanced IoT cybersecurity framework for smart cities, utilizing a software-defined networking framework with a Deep Unfolding Spatial-Frequency Attention Network and Pine Cone Optimization (DUSFAN-PCO). Initially, input data is collected from UNSW-NB15 and CIC-IDS2017 datasets. The collected data are pre-processed using Diffusion Models for Missing Value Imputation (DMMVI) to handle noise and missing values. Next, Carpet Weaver Optimization (CWO) is applied to select the most informative attributes. These selected features are then fed into the Deep Unfolding Spatial-Frequency Attention Network (DUSFAN), which classifies IoT network traffic into normal and multiple attack categories through real-time anomaly detection. To further enhance detection accuracy, Pine Cone Optimization (PCO) is used to fine-tune DUSFAN’s weight parameters. Finally, the results are securely stored and managed using a Blockchain-Based Secure PBFT Lightweight Consensus (SPBFT-LC), ensuring immutability, transparency, and trust among IoT nodes. The proposed DUSFAN-PCO framework achieves an accuracy of 99.20% on UNSW-NB15 and 99.48% on CIC-IDS2017, with F1-scores of 99.52% and 99.50%, and ROC values of 0.99–1.00 across both datasets. Coupled with high blockchain-based security integrity (> 99%), it ensures robust, real-time, and reliable detection of IoT network intrusions, making it highly suitable for secure and resilient smart city IoT environments.

title: Multi-criteria prioritized reinforcement learning for autonomous underwater vehicle navigation in 3D multi-node environments
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are increasingly used as mobile data collectors in underwater wireless sensor networks, where navigation must balance task completion, obstacle avoidance, communication performance, and energy efficiency. This study develops a Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework with Multi-Criteria Prioritized Experience Replay (MC-PER-TD3). The replay priority combines normalized temporal-difference error with a goal-proximity heuristic; energy consumption is incorporated into the reward and data-collection evaluation rather than the replay priority. A soft potential-field reward and a time-window-based waypoint escape-transition mechanism are further used to guide continuous navigation. Across six training seeds and 60 deterministic-policy evaluation episodes per seed, MC-PER-TD3 achieved 100% mission success with zero observed collisions. Relative to uniform-replay TD3, the mean successful path length decreased from 13.188 ± 3.885 m to 10.985 ± 0.436 m and task time from 6.911 ± 1.511 s to 5.654 ± 0.257 s. A standard TD-error-only PER-TD3 baseline achieved 50% mission success, whereas the combined TD-error-plus-goal replay achieved consistent completion across all six training seeds. Additional zero-shot tests under observation noise, current perturbations, fixed and randomized obstacle layouts reveal condition-dependent robustness and clear failure boundaries. In UWSN evaluation, MC-PER-TD3 achieved the highest mean energy efficiency, while TD3 retained the highest throughput, indicating a throughput-energy trade-off rather than universal dominance.

title: Nutritional profiling and nutrient quality scoring of microgreens cultivated in India
abstract: Micronutrient deficiency remains a major public health challenge in India, where dietary diversity is often limited among low-income populations. Microgreens, young edible seedlings harvested at the two-true-leaf stage (7–21 days post-germination), have recently gained traction as potentially nutrient-dense functional foods. However, systematic compositional data for commercial varieties of Microgreens grown in India remain scarce. In this study, sixteen commonly consumed vegetable species from five botanical families (Brassicaceae, Amaranthaceae, Asteraceae, Apiaceae, and Compositae) were cultivated under controlled polyhouse conditions in Bihar, India. They were evaluated for vitamin C, crude fiber, protein, total phenolic content (TPC), DPPH (2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl) radical scavenging activity, FRAP (ferric reducing antioxidant power) assay, and mineral content (calcium, iron, zinc, and potassium), as well as oxalate, an antinutritional factor. All analyses were conducted in three independent replicates. Data were expressed as mg 100 g −1 fresh weight (FW) for vitamin C, protein, oxalate, and TPC, and mg 100 g −1 dry weight (DW) for minerals. The data were statistically analyzed using a Completely Randomized Design with three replicates. Radish, kale, broccoli, and fenugreek were the richest sources of vitamin C (85.77–97.88 mg 100 g −1 FW), while celery, parsley, palak, and spinach were the richest sources of calcium (320.14-410.15 mg 100 g −1 DW). The crude fiber content of broccoli microgreen (11.95 g 100 g −1 DW) and cabbage microgreen (11.48 g 100 g −1 DW) was good. Low oxalate content across all microgreen species (15.89–55.14 mg 100 g −1 FW) suggests safe consumption levels. The composite Nutrient Quality Score (NQS) and Antioxidant Index (AI) were calculated using Min-Max normalized values to enable cross-species comparison. Palak, broccoli, fenugreek, and kale ranked highest in NQS, driven primarily by their vitamin C, crude fiber, and iron content. These findings provide a systematic nutritional reference for microgreens grown in India and illustrate how NQS can be applied to comparative dietary assessment.

title: Electroencephalographic gamma correlates with pain intensity attenuation in a prospective longitudinal study using an AI-powered digital device for pain self-management
abstract: Chronic low back or neck pain is one of the most common neurological disorders in the US. Electroencephalogram (EEG) is a leading noninvasive approach to identify biomarkers for chronic pain, but its validation in clinical settings remains limited by methodological challenges, including variable feature selections, subjective removal of EEG artifacts, and reliance on population-level analyses. In this single center, prospective, longitudinal study, we investigated the relationships among EEG features, patient-reported clinical outcomes via validated Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMS) questionnaires, and daily self-management of pain-associated physical activity via a newly developed AI-powered mobile application Paindrainer PDCC (Paindrainer AB, Lund, Sweden) in patients with chronic pain undergoing standard care. In total, twenty patients with chronic lower back or neck pain were enrolled and evaluated during 3 visits over a 12-week period. Results show significant improvements in pain score, physical function, and pain interference scores over time, whereas mean EEG power spectral density across all electrodes and frequency bands was statistically insignificant at the group level between the three visits. However, logistic regression analysis revealed significant nominal inverse correlations between pain score reduction and gamma power changes (averaged globally and localized to the right temporal and left frontal regions), though these failed to retain significance after multiple comparison correction. Logistic regression showed a statistically significant correlation between increased EEG gamma oscillations (1 Hz bins) and decreased pain intensity in the right temporal EEG electrodes. These exploratory analyses suggest that improvements in self-reported pain outcomes in chronic pain patients undergoing standard treatments and complemented with digital-based behavioral interventions correlate negatively with measurable changes in EEG spectral features, which need further validation in future studies with larger cohorts.

title: DAF-EfficientNetV2: distribution-aware feature enhancement for plant leaf disease recognition in complex environments
abstract: Plant leaf diseases in complex natural growing environments are characterized by significant scale variation and morphological heterogeneity, which pose severe challenges to the feature representation capability and inference efficiency of recognition models. Although existing convolutional neural networks have achieved certain progress in disease recognition tasks, they are still constrained by inherent local inductive bias, resulting in limited capability in modeling long-range dependencies and bridging the semantic gap across hierarchical features. To address these issues, this paper proposes a plant leaf disease recognition model termed DAF-EfficientNetV2 (Distribution-Aware Feature-enhanced EfficientNetV2) based on the EfficientNetV2-S backbone. Under the premise of maintaining parameter efficiency and fast inference of the backbone network, the proposed model introduces an integrated Global–Local Semantic Fusion Module (GMSF). Through a spatially orthogonal global modeling strategy, the module efficiently captures cross-region lesion correlations within a single computational unit, and, together with an adaptive semantic calibration mechanism, effectively alleviates the semantic inconsistency among features from different levels. As a result, the model’s panoramic perception capability for scale distortion and complex lesion morphologies is significantly enhanced. In addition, a Shuffle Attention feature re-calibration mechanism is incorporated, which jointly optimizes channel-wise and spatial responses through a “group–parallel–reassemble” strategy, guiding the model to focus on diagnostically valuable lesion regions while suppressing redundant noise from complex field backgrounds in a computationally efficient manner. Furthermore, a lightweight cross-scale aggregation strategy is adopted to achieve efficient integration and alignment of features at different resolutions. Experimental results on the Plant Pathology 2020-FGVC7 and Plant Pathology 2021-FGVC8 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves classification accuracies of 95.43 ± 0.51% (best 96.14%) and 88.39%, respectively, outperforming existing mainstream approaches and validating the effectiveness and robustness of DAF-EfficientNetV2 in complex plant disease recognition tasks. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/mayue0606/DAF-EfficientNetV2 .

title: AI-quantum hybrid channel modeling and noise mitigation for 5G/6G wireless networks: the AQCME framework
abstract: Channel estimation is one of the most fundamental and performance-limiting operations in fifth-generation (5G) and emerging sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks, where ultra-massive MIMO arrays, millimetre-wave and terahertz carrier frequencies, and non-Gaussian hardware-induced noise combine to render classical least-squares and minimum mean squared error estimators inadequate. Deep learning has narrowed the performance gap, yet it offers no information-theoretic guarantee on how close any particular network architecture is to the fundamental noise floor. This paper introduces the AI-Quantum Channel Modeling and Estimation (AQCME) framework, which integrates variational quantum circuits, quantum signal processing, and a quantum eigenspace denoising operator into a unified trainable architecture for simultaneous channel estimation and noise suppression in MIMO-OFDM systems. The defining theoretical result is a quantum Cramer-Rao lower bound on normalised mean squared error, grounded in the quantum Fisher information matrix of the encoded channel state, together with a rigorous proof that the AQCME estimator approaches this bound as training data grows – to the best of our knowledge the first constructive achievability result of its kind in the wireless channel estimation literature. The framework is supported by formal analysis of quantum channel state preparation, quantum kernel universality with an explicit barren-plateau trainability discussion, ergodic spectral efficiency, Nakagami-m outage probability, and convergence of the hybrid quantum-classical gradient descent. Monte Carlo simulations over 50,000 channel realisations, reported with 90 percent confidence intervals throughout, validate every theoretical prediction. Ablation studies across circuit depths and qubit counts, a hardware-noise sweep over gate error rates from 1e-4 to 1e-2, and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis confirm robustness. At 20 dB signal-to-noise ratio, AQCME reduces normalised mean squared error by 4.8 dB over MMSE and by 2.1 dB over the best deep learning baseline; under emulated near-term noisy quantum hardware conditions it still outperforms MMSE by 2.6 dB. All quantum results in this work are obtained by exact classical statevector emulation of the variational circuit; no physical quantum processor was used, and reported hardware-noise behaviour is modelled by a depolarising channel. Spectral efficiency improves by up to 22.4 percent in massive MIMO scenarios, the URLLC outage target of 1e-5 is met at 6.2 dB lower signal-to-noise ratio than with MMSE, and inference complexity scales logarithmically with antenna count rather than quartically as with MMSE matrix inversion.

title: Unraveling nonlinear ecosystem water use efficiency dynamics and environmental drivers across Iran using remote sensing and XGBoost-SHAP
abstract: Understanding how ecosystems regulate the trade-off between carbon assimilation and water loss is essential for assessing ecohydrological stability in water-limited regions. This study investigated ecosystem water use efficiency (WUE) dynamics across Iran from 2001 to 2025 using an integrated framework combining multi-source remote sensing datasets, polynomial trend analysis, optimized eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Morris global sensitivity analysis (Morris GSA). A polynomial regression approach was employed to characterize linear and nonlinear WUE trends across Köppen–Geiger climate zones and land cover types. In addition, XGBoost-SHAP-Morris GSA modeling identified dominant climatic and environmental drivers, characterized their nonlinear effects, and quantified WUE sensitivity. The results indicated that valid WUE estimates covered approximately 44% of Iran’s total area, of which 23.75% experienced significant long-term WUE trends, with increases (20.39%) substantially exceeding decreases (3.36%). Linear trends were the dominant pattern, covering 17.1% of this area (72.2% of all significant trends), while nonlinear trends accounted for 6.6% of this area. The magnitude of significant WUE trends ranged from –0.97 to 0.90 g C m −2 mm −1 decade⁻ 1 , with increasing trends mainly distributed across western, southwestern, and northern coastal Iran, particularly along the Zagros and Alborz mountain ranges, where changes were more associated with changes in GPP than ET. Among land cover types, grasslands (11.9%) and croplands (5.8%) showed the largest proportions of significant WUE trends. The XGBoost–SHAP analysis revealed that NDVI (50.98% relative contribution), LAI (19.81%), and solar radiation (17.44%) were the dominant factors explaining the variability of WUE. The Morris GSA indicated that modeled WUE responses were primarily sensitive to NDVI (24.00% relative sensitivity, μ* = 0.827), followed by air temperature (20.35%, μ* = 0.701) and solar radiation (16.52%, μ* = 0.569), whereas LST, soil moisture, and wind speed exhibited comparatively weaker overall sensitivity. This study characterizes WUE dynamics across Iran and identifies key environmental factors associated with WUE variability, providing insights into ecosystem water-use dynamics in water-limited regions.

title: A hybrid artificial intelligence framework for three-dimensional electromagnetic field mapping using airborne measurements in general aviation
abstract: The increasing electrification of aircraft systems and development of autonomous aviation technologies increase the need for accurate characterization of electromagnetic field (EMF) distributions under operational conditions. However, dense three-dimensional EMF measurements in aviation environments are difficult to obtain because airborne observations are typically sparse, irregularly distributed, and collected under varying flight conditions. Here, we present an artificial intelligence-based framework for three-dimensional reconstruction of the electric field component of EMF from real-world airborne measurements in general aviation. The study uses more than 80 h of measurements collected during operational activities involving four aircraft types and a low-cost, high-sensitivity sensing platform recording synchronized electric-field and geospatial data over the 1-8000 MHz frequency range. Geostatistical and machine-learning approaches, including Kriging, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, and Exact Gaussian Processes, were evaluated for three-dimensional field reconstruction. Based on this comparison, we developed a hybrid Deep Gaussian Process Kolmogorov-Arnold Feature Extractor (DGKAN), combining nonlinear feature representation with probabilistic spatial modeling and uncertainty estimation. DGKAN achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 0.0381 and a mean squared error of 0.0071, reducing the mean absolute error by approximately 27.6% relative to the strongest baseline model. These results demonstrate that combining Kolmogorov-Arnold representations with probabilistic Gaussian Process modeling enables accurate reconstruction of three-dimensional electromagnetic field distributions from sparse airborne measurements. The proposed framework provides a data-driven approach for electromagnetic environment assessment in general aviation and establishes a basis for further development of intelligent EMF monitoring and prediction methods under operational flight conditions.

title: Robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework with complex entropy-aware and wavelet convolution
abstract: In adverse weather conditions such as fog, haze, rain, and snow, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) small object detection faces decreased accuracy due to reduced image quality and blurred object features, which seriously affects the reliability of low-altitude detection tasks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework based on unsupervised domain adaptation with a teacher-student self-training paradigm. The proposed framework introduces complex entropy-aware attention and wavelet convolution to enhance target representation under severe weather degradation. Aiming at the domain distribution differences in multi-weather scenarios, the framework alleviates such differences through more robust category-level prototype matching and global statistical characteristic learning based on DATR (domain adaptive detection transformer model). First, to alleviate feature uncertainty introduced by adverse weather noise, we design a complex entropy-aware attention mechanism that estimates channel-wise Shannon entropy and assigns adaptive weights according to feature information concentration. Instead of simply emphasizing uncertain responses, the proposed mechanism suppresses high-entropy ambiguous features while preserving low-entropy discriminative representations that remain more reliable under weather-induced degradation. Next, to solve the limitations of traditional convolution in capturing the global context of small objects and distinguishing objects from noise, we propose to use wavelet convolution to leverage frequency-domain multi-scale decomposition and large receptive fields, strengthening the capture of global context for small objects and improving the distinction between objects and noise through frequency filtering. Finally, to further improve the stability of teacher model evolution under cross-weather domain shifts, we design a grouped EMA (exponential moving average) strategy. Unlike conventional Mean Teacher or BYOL frameworks that employ a globally fixed decay coefficient, the proposed strategy dynamically adjusts grouped parameter updating rates according to feature adaptation requirements, providing a more flexible optimization trajectory for domain adaptation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves UAV small object detection performance under several adverse weather domain-shift scenarios, while showing promising robustness against weather-induced feature degradation.

title: A multi-task learning approach for consumer sentiment classification and emotion detection via behavioral data
abstract: Sentiment analysis captures overall opinion polarity, but it often fails to reveal the key emotions that drive consumer behavior. The recognition of both sentiment and emotions provides crucial information to uncover underlying drivers of consumers behavior and brand loyalty. These important insights enable businesses to detect emerging issues, refine products and services, and personalize consumer experiences. This study proposes a multi-task approach that performs sentiment classification and emotion detection tasks based on consumer reviews and corresponding ratings. To this end, we propose Consumer Sentiment and Emotion Modeling ( COSMO-MT ), a deep learning-based multi-task model for sentiment classification and emotion detection. It begins with an input layer followed by embedding layers that provide sentiment-specific, emotion-specific, and shared embeddings from the input text. Each embedding is processed through shared layers consisting of CNN, BiLSTM, and attention mechanisms. Moreover, several auxiliary features are incorporated into the shared layers to provide explicit linguistic information. The outputs of the shared layers are then passed to task-specific layers for sentiment classification and emotion detection. Finally, corresponding dense and output layers generate predictions for both tasks. We evaluate the efficacy of the proposed COSMO-MT model on two publicly available datasets. It significantly outperforms existing studies and baseline methods.

title: Evaluating and enhancing the geotechnical properties of clay–wood ash and clay–sawdust composites using RSM and ANN
abstract: This study examines the mechanical and geotechnical performance of expansive clayey soil stabilized with sustainable agro-industrial by-products. The experimental program evaluates the effects of incorporating wood sawdust (WS) and wood ash (WA) at dosages of 2% to 10%, both individually and in combination with a fixed 2% addition of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC). Comprehensive laboratory characterization included Atterberg limits, methylene blue value, hydrometer analysis, compaction characteristics determined by the Standard Proctor test. Direct shear testing was conducted to determine cohesion (c) and the internal friction angle Φ), while California bearing ratio (CBR) and unconfined compressive strength (UCS) were evaluated as key mechanical properties. Soil responses were modeled using response surface methodology (RSM) and artificial neural networks (ANNs). The mixture containing 8% WA and 2% OPC showed the greatest mechanical improvement relative to the untreated natural clay baseline, increasing CBR by 389.34% and UCS by 335.50%. while significantly enhancing shear strength parameters. Both ANN/Genetic Algorithm (GA) and RSM/Desirability function effectively identified mixes that maximized CBR and UCS, although ANN/GA provided superior prediction accuracy and closer alignment with the model-based optimum. These findings support the use of optimized clay-based biocomposites incorporating WA, WS, and OPC for sustainable foundation engineering, soil stabilization, and pavement subgrade enhancement.

title: Integrated transcriptomics and network toxicology suggests core targets and potential mechanisms of aspartame-related breast carcinogenesis
abstract: Aspartame (APM) is a globally prevalent low-calorie artificial sweetener. Although its long-term health risks have garnered increasing attention, the potential molecular targets and pathways linking APM exposure to breast cancer remain largely unexplored. In this study, we integrated network toxicology and transcriptomics with multiple computational approaches, including machine learning, molecular docking, and clinical validation, to predictively prioritize candidate targets and pathways potentially involved in APM‑related breast carcinogenesis. We acquired 226 APM targets and 1973 breast cancer genes, from which 46 overlapping potential targets were extracted. Functional enrichment analyses revealed that these targets were mainly enriched in biological processes related to cell proliferation and migration, as well as multiple cancer‑associated signaling pathways, including transcriptional misregulation in cancer, TNF, and IL-17. Using a multi-algorithm machine learning model, we further prioritized 5 core targets with favorable diagnostic performance and stable predictive ability. SHAP analysis was performed on the core targets, and virtual gene knockout was conducted for the gene with the most significant contribution. Finally, TCGA datasets further confirmed the differential expression of these core targets across breast cancer subtypes and normal tissues. Collectively, these computational findings provide a prioritized list of molecular candidates and a hypothesis‑generating basis for future experimental and mechanistic studies on APM and breast cancer.

title: A glycolysis-associated four-gene risk model for prognosis and immune microenvironment characterization in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has a dismal prognosis and profound metabolic reprogramming, yet the role of glycolysis-associated genes (GRGs) remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to develop a glycolysis‑associated prognostic model and explore its association with the tumor immune microenvironment (TME). We curated 760 GRGs from MSigDB and performed consensus clustering to identify molecular subtypes. Using WGCNA integrated with three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, Random Forest, and SVM-RFE), we constructed a GRGs risk score model and validated it across multiple independent cohorts. Its correlation with prognosis, genomic alterations, immune infiltration, and in silico drug sensitivity was comprehensively evaluated. Experimental validation was conducted in clinical specimens and HCC cell lines. Two distinct GRGs-based subtypes were identified, with cluster B exhibiting worse prognosis and significant enrichment of cell cycle, glycolysis, EMT, and PI3K‑AKT‑mTOR pathways. A four-gene risk model ( CBX1 , DNMT1 , GAS2L3 , KPNA2 ) was constructed. The risk score demonstrated moderate prognostic performance as an independent prognostic factor and correlated with advanced AJCC stage, higher tumor mutational burden, and an immunosuppressive TME characterized by increased Tregs and M0 macrophages. A nomogram incorporating the risk score showed moderate predictive accuracy and clinical net benefit. Experimental validation supported upregulation of all four genes in HCC tissues, and knockdown of CBX1 or GAS2L3 markedly suppressed cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. The GRGs risk model demonstrates clinical applicability and net benefit in terms of prognostic stratification and immunophenotype characterization in HCC patients, offering a potentially useful tool for risk assessment and personalized management.

title: Data-driven and physics-guided neural approaches for LCR circuit modeling: a comparative analysis
abstract: This study compares a data-driven recurrent (RNN–LSTM) predictor with physics-guided neural networks for the forced charge response of a series LCR circuit whose resistive term carries a Caputo fractional memory of order 0.6. The reference trajectory is generated by an explicit Sumudu transform–Adomian decomposition recursion. In an independent recomputation, the magnitude of component 50 on the 1001-point grid is \(3.43018\times 10^{-20}\) , and the maximum residual under extended-precision evaluation is approximately \(1.69974\times 10^{-9}\) . A product-trapezoidal solver exhibits second-order convergence. With a chronological split before sequence windowing, the reported experiments evaluate one-step and autonomous LSTM prediction, a data-only network, networks penalized by an integer-order residual, and a fractional physics-informed network (fPINN). Across five seeds, teacher-forced LSTM prediction gives a test charge RMSE of \(0.01537\pm 0.00369\) , whereas autonomous rollout gives \(0.16095\pm 0.04806\) . The fPINN with the residual enforced over the whole interval gives \(2.15109\times 10^{-4}\pm 2.03608\times 10^{-4}\) , compared with \(0.05414\pm 1.84137\times 10^{-4}\) for the integer-order residual. The mean test RMSEs of the three feedforward variants without a residual on the test interval range from 0.39211 to 0.92453. These differences reflect the information and prior knowledge supplied to each model rather than an intrinsic ranking of architectures. The data are synthetic and noise-free, and only one parameter set and a short extrapolation interval are studied.

title: Prediction of asphaltene onset pressure and precipitation amount using tree-based stacking–blending ensemble meta-learners: a flow assurance perspective
abstract: Flow assurance is critical to reliable oil production, and asphaltene precipitation is among its costliest threats, damaging the near-wellbore region, cutting output, and forcing expensive remediation. Equation-of-state models describe it rigorously but need detailed fluid characterization and heavy computation. This study aims to predict asphaltene onset pressure (AOP) and precipitation amount, as two separate regression tasks, from routinely available reservoir data. We compiled 483 AOP and 408 precipitation measurements from the literature, trained XGBoost, Random Forest, LightGBM, and Extra Trees, and combined them through stacking and blending with a Huber meta-learner. Tuning used 5-fold cross-validation on training data only, and all metrics come from a held-out test set. An ensemble performed best in each task: Stacking-Huber for AOP (R2 = 0.991, MAPE = 1.65%) and Blending-Huber for precipitation amount (R2 = 0.988, MAE = 0.0298), though margins over the best base learners were small. C1 and C5 mattered most for AOP, and pressure and bubble point pressure for precipitation amount, in line with thermodynamic expectations. These findings support rapid screening of asphaltene risk when detailed equation-of-state characterization is unavailable and can inform inhibitor design. When coupled with the pressure and temperature profile along the wellbore, the models can be used to estimate the depth at which precipitation begins and the amount of asphaltene precipitated, within the compositional range of the training data. The main challenge is generalization: records from one source may fall in both training and test sets, so scores reflect the compiled data, not unseen oils. Future work should use source-wise validation on independent datasets, cover gas-injection conditions, and embed thermodynamic constraints through physics-informed models.

title: Cutting-edge trends in drought prediction and mitigation using ensemble learning and augmented XAI: a meteorological study
abstract: Drought affects more than 60% of India's population, reducing agricultural productivity, straining water resources, and threatening socioeconomic stability. This study proposes an interpretable one-month-ahead meteorological drought prediction framework by integrating class-weighted ensemble machine learning with SHAP and LIME explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Historical meteorological observations (1972–2022) obtained from the Zenodo climate database were analyzed for 49 districts across five drought-prone Indian states (Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka). After generating lagged meteorological features (t − 1 to t − 6) and addressing severe class imbalance (7.07% drought events), multiple machine learning classifiers were evaluated. The class-weighted XGBoost model (scale_pos_weight ≈ 11.90, without SMOTE) achieved the best overall performance on the independent 2016–2022 test dataset, with an accuracy of 95.7%, macro precision of 84.7%, macro recall of 81.0%, macro F1-score of 82.7%, and a PR-AUC of 0.647 on the highly imbalanced test set (outperforming both unweighted training and SMOTE-based approaches). SHAP and LIME consistently identified lagged Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), lagged precipitation, vapour pressure, and wet-day frequency as the most influential drivers of drought occurrence. Exploratory temporal analysis further revealed declining wet-day frequency in Karnataka, increasing vapour pressure in Andhra Pradesh, and substantial climatic variability across the study regions. The proposed framework combines accurate drought prediction with transparent model interpretation, providing a practical decision-support tool for district-level drought early warning, water resource management, and climate-resilient agricultural planning in India.

title: Reducing boundary conditions for the Thomas–Fermi equation using a hybrid q-deformation and neural network method
abstract: This study introduces a hybrid \(q\) -calculus and artificial neural network framework for the Thomas–Fermi equation of free positive ions. Its contribution is a construction in which \(q\) -deformation combines the terminal derivative and terminal-value conditions, representing three classical boundary conditions by two constraints in the deformed problem. A boundary-compatible trial solution embeds the transformed constraints, allowing training to focus on the \(q\) -differential residual. For fixed \(q<1\) , the result is a deformed approximation with a classical limit as \(q\rightarrow 1\) . Experiments across nine ionization degrees and five seeds compared the \(q\) -ANN with a benchmark, a soft-constrained PINN, and an undeformed hard-constrained classical ANN. The \(q\) -ANN produced lower RMSE than the PINN in 42 of 45 matched runs and a lower median RMSE ( \(0.004127\) versus \(0.015044\) ), although two outlying outcomes caused mean RMSE to favor the PINN and paired tests did not establish a difference. Against the hard-constrained classical ANN, the \(q\) -ANN produced lower RMSE in 44 of 45 comparisons, indicating that the observed performance is not attributable solely to exact constraint embedding. The pointwise \(q\) -ANN was approximately \(102\) times slower than the vectorized PINN. The framework provides a new boundary-transformation strategy while retaining initialization sensitivity and computational cost as limitations.

title: From reconstruction to interpretation: zero-setup deployable model for multi-phase segmentation of X-ray tomography data
abstract: X-ray tomography enables the nondestructive characterization of materials, and recent advances in micro-CT imaging technology have accelerated the acquisition and reconstruction of volumetric data. However, rapid scientific interpretation remains limited by image segmentation, which typically requires manual thresholding, user prompting, or material-specific model training before meaningful analysis can begin. We present a zero-setup deployment framework for multi-phase segmentation of synchrotron X-ray tomography data that produces interpretable segmentations of previously unseen tomography datasets without user prompting, manual parameter tuning, or additional retraining during deployment. The framework combines a material-agnostic deployment strategy based on reusable attenuation- and morphology-based mask categories, including background, sample, bright regions, dark-gray regions, light-gray regions, and porosity, with a pretrained semantic segmentation network to generate rapid first-pass segmentations within minutes of reconstruction. In inference-time benchmarks, the framework segmented a 500-slice \(\:2560\times\:2560\) volume in 67.1s and a 2000-slice volume in 253.5s using four A100 GPUs. Unlike conventional deep learning pipelines that require dataset-specific annotations and retraining, the proposed approach can be applied immediately to new scans, enabling rapid assessment of experimental quality and preliminary microstructural analysis during ongoing beamline experiments. Users can subsequently refine or fine-tune the generated masks when application-specific segmentation is required. Experiments on held-out and qualitatively evaluated synchrotron micro-CT datasets suggest that the framework produces consistent and physically meaningful first-pass segmentations on new tomography datasets while substantially outperforming conventional intensity-based thresholding. By bridging the gap between high-speed data acquisition and immediate interpretation, the proposed framework enables near real-time beamline feedback and supports scalable AI-assisted scientific imaging workflows.

title: Quantifying nonlinear thresholds of grey-green space morphology on urban carbon metabolism across local climate zones: a machine learning study in Changchun city
abstract: Urban grey-green spaces play a critical role in regulating carbon metabolism by influencing atmospheric CO₂ concentration (XCO₂) and net primary productivity (NPP). However, the heterogeneous drivers of carbon metabolism across different Local Climate Zones (LCZs) remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated Changchun, China, by integrating LCZ classification, multidimensional morphological indicators, and interpretable machine learning. Based on typical urban development patterns and morphological contrasts, LCZ 1–3 were aggregated into a compact built-up group (hereafter the LCZ 1 group), while LCZ 6 (open low-rise) was retained as an independent group; these two groups were selected as representative zones. CatBoost-SHAP models were developed to reveal nonlinear relationships between urban morphology and carbon metabolism. Results showed that grey-space characteristics (B_CORE, BD, BH) dominated carbon metabolism in LCZ 1, contributing over 55%, whereas green-space and climatic factors (VFC, ACH, MAT) played greater roles in LCZ 6. Context-dependent nonlinear turning-point characteristics were identified: in LCZ 1 group, response changes occurred around B_CORE ≈ 2.0 and over BH range of 10–40 m; in LCZ 6, VFC around 0.65 and B1 around − 0.25 showed distinct turning points. Identical indicators showed different association across LCZs, highlighting context-specific planning. This study provides an integrated LCZ-based interpretable machine-learning framework to characterize localized nonlinear responses and support low-carbon urban planning.

title: Regional synergetic effects of ice and snow consumption based on a BERT neural network
abstract: This study takes Harbin Ice-Snow World as a key case and develops an integrated framework based on a BERT neural network and regional economic analysis to quantify and analyze regional synergy associated with ice-snow consumption. The framework integrates semantic features with structured indicators to construct a regional synergy intensity model using approximately 12,000 consumer reviews and multidimensional statistical data from 15 regional nodes. Five-fold cross-validation and a three-expert consistency assessment (Fleiss’ Kappa = 0.84) were conducted. The results showed that the model achieved strong performance in predicting synergetic relationships, with an F1-score of 0.87, significantly outperforming baseline models based on advanced large language models such as Llama-3-70B and the ablation variants. Harbin was identified as the “absolute core” of the network, with a weighted centrality of 4.52. Based on quantitative topological indicators, including network density and path strength, the synergetic patterns were classified into the “Heilongjiang Core Agglomeration Zone,” the “Jilin-Liaoning-Hebei Functional Complementarity Zone,” and the “Long-Distance Characteristic Linkage Zone.” This study provides a new perspective for understanding the spatial organization of the ice-snow industry and offers data-driven decision support for formulating cross-regional collaboration policies.

title: Multi-bitplane edge detection of skin lesion contours in dermoscopic images
abstract: In dermatological medical image analysis, edge detection is critical for skin disease diagnosis. Precise edge information provides a vital basis for subsequent disease assessment. However, existing grayscale gradient-based edge detection methods exhibit poor visual effects when extracting features of complex skin textures, often due to interference from noise and inability to obtain complete, clear edge images, while deep learning-based methods suffer from heavy reliance on large annotated datasets and high computing costs. To improve the visual quality of edge detection for skin images and extract clear, complete skin edges, we propose the training-free, lightweight Skin Lesion Contour Detection (SLCD) method. It integrates Haar wavelet transform denoising and 3 × 3 circular structuring element morphological processing for two-stage preprocessing of skin images. The processed image uses 3 Most Significant Bit (MSB) planes, and edge detection is performed on each bit plane separately. Each bit plane is processed by the 3 × 3 neighborhood adaptive analysis based on local standard deviation and average gradient to get the edge image, and the resulting edge images are fused to generate the final detection result. Experiments on the Skin Image Edge Detection Test (SIEDT) dataset show that SLCD achieves an average F1-score of 0.718, Jaccard index of 0.575, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.733. All of which are the best among the compared methods. The SLCD can effectively extract true skin edges and mitigate noise interference in skin images, providing a training-free and lightweight alternative that offers better edge detection performance than traditional operators while avoiding the heavy data and computational requirements of deep learning models in resource-limited skin image analysis scenarios. This study provides multi-bitplane fusion-based novel concepts and methods for edge detection in skin images. It delivers diagnostic value by providing high-precision lesion contours, supporting analysis of skin lesions, early diagnosis, and surgical planning, and improving the reliability of clinical decision-making in dermatology.

title: Ontology-guided neuro-symbolic convNeXtV2–swin transformer for explainable cytological classification of papillary thyroid carcinoma
abstract: The cytological assessment of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) relies on microscopic evaluation of cellular and nuclear morphology. Subtle cytomorphological differences, interobserver variability, and specimen heterogeneity can complicate interpretation. This study developed an explainable hybrid ConvNeXtV2–Swin Transformer framework that integrates fine-grained cytological representation with broader spatial-context modeling for PTC classification. ConvNeXtV2 provides fine-grained nuclear and cellular representations, whereas Swin Transformer captures broader contextual relationships across cytological regions. These complementary representations support classification and subsequent pathology-informed interpretation of nuclear, architectural, and stromal evidence. Interpretability combines Biomarker-Guided Attention Modeling, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM)-style quantitative attribution analysis, and ontology-guided post-classification semantic interpretation. On the independent test set, the hybrid framework achieved 96.19% accuracy, 96.16% sensitivity, and 96.16% specificity. Precision was 95.27%, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) reached 0.9702. External testing achieved 91.4% accuracy, 91.0% sensitivity, 92.0% specificity, and 94.0% precision. Quantitative attribution analysis showed greater activation heterogeneity and stronger localized responses in PTC tissue. Non-PTC tissue showed broader and more uniform responses associated with preserved follicular morphology. The neuro-symbolic component subsequently organized compartment-level responses according to predefined thyroid cytopathology relationships. These outputs provide pathology-informed computational interpretation without constituting independent biomarker detection or expert-equivalent pathological reasoning.

title: Artificial Intelligence, climate policy uncertainty, and renewable energy transition: nonlinear evidence on sustainable energy resilience
abstract: The transition toward renewable energy is central to achieving sustainable development and climate mitigation objectives. At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI) and climate governance have emerged as critical forces shaping the pace and resilience of clean energy transformation. Despite growing attention to these factors, limited evidence exists regarding their nonlinear and asymmetric influences on renewable energy performance. This study investigates the asymmetric effects of AI development and climate policy uncertainty (CPU) on renewable energy transition using monthly data spanning 2013 to 2023. Employing a nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) framework, AI and CPU are decomposed into positive and negative partial shocks to capture heterogeneous short-run and long-run responses. The empirical results reveal pronounced asymmetries in the renewable energy transition process. Negative shocks to AI development generate larger and more persistent adverse effects on renewable energy performance than positive AI shocks generate benefits, indicating that disruptions in digital innovation substantially weaken the resilience of sustainable energy systems. Likewise, adverse climate policy uncertainty shocks exert stronger and longer-lasting impacts than favorable policy developments, increasing investment risk, delaying clean energy deployment, and weakening confidence in long-term low-carbon planning. Dynamic multiplier analysis confirms gradual adjustment toward long-run equilibrium, highlighting the presence of transition costs and delayed adaptation mechanisms within renewable energy markets. Furthermore, financial conditions and conventional energy prices significantly influence renewable energy performance through market-based transmission channels. Overall, the findings demonstrate that resilient renewable energy transitions depend on sustained technological innovation, stable climate governance, and supportive financial environments. By uncovering the asymmetric interactions between AI, policy uncertainty, and renewable energy dynamics, this study contributes to the emerging literature on sustainable development and offers policy insights for strengthening energy transition resilience and accelerating progress toward long-term decarbonization goals.

title: Schizophrenia classification from multichannel EEG using EEGNet with SHAP and Grad-CAM
abstract: Schizophrenia affects cognition, perception and neural information processing. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive and relatively low-cost way to study these changes. This study evaluates two deep learning models for separating paranoid schizophrenia patients from healthy controls using the public RepOD resting-state EEG dataset, which contains 14 patients and 14 healthy controls recorded from 19 electrodes at 250 Hz. To prevent participant level data leakage, all final testing kept participants separate using Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) and Stratified Group 5-Fold validation. The three-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) used Short-Time Fourier Transform representations (STFT), while EEGNet used the channel-time EEG epochs directly. At the reference settings used for the final controlled analysis, EEGNet gave an accuracy of 0.750, F1-score of 0.767, Cohen’s kappa of 0.497 and AUC of 0.797 under LOSO validation. Under Stratified Group 5-Fold validation, the corresponding values were 0.679, 0.695, 0.357 and 0.757. EEGNet showed stronger performance than the 3D-CNN, particularly under Stratified Group 5-Fold validation, where the 3D-CNN achieved a kappa of 0.011. Participant-based bootstrap confidence intervals quantified the uncertainty associated with the 28-participant cohort. Additional tests of learning rate (LR) and STFT resolution confirmed that the 3D-CNN was sensitive to model settings and fold composition. A separate ICA cleaning test showed that removing likely artifacts did not correct the weak 3D-CNN stratified result, while EEGNet performance improved after cleaning. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) were used to examine which EEG channels and signal regions influenced the model decisions. The XAI results were clearer for EEGNet, while SHAP and Grad-CAM assigned different rankings to individual electrodes. These findings provide a basis for further validation using larger and independent datasets.

title: Durability and impact resilience of OPS coir fibre reinforced concrete with experimental insights and machine learning predictions
abstract: The impact and crack resilience are critical parameters for assessing concrete under dynamic loading, while durability governs its long-term resistance to deterioration from weather and chemical attack. Oil Palm Shell (OPS) is a promising sustainable lightweight aggregate with the potential for enhanced impact and durability performance. This study investigates the durability, impact and crack resilience of OPS concrete reinforced with coir fibre, focusing on fibre length and slab boundary conditions. Durability was further assessed under varying curing ages and conditions. Experimental testing utilised 300 mm square slabs of 30 mm thickness subjected to low-velocity impact loading, complemented by machine learning (ML) predictions using SVM and ANN. The ML models predicted responses at crack initiation, with optimal responses identified through a graphical optimisation technique. Findings demonstrated notable improvements in impact and crack resilience, proportional to fibre length and support configurations. Peak performance of up to 135 Joules and 631 N/mm 2 was achieved with 50 mm coir fibre under four support configurations, with fibre effects most pronounced in simply supported slabs. The ML models effectively predicted the impact and crack responses, with the ANN achieving the highest predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.76), followed by SVM-Linear. The durability assessment revealed up to 97% reduction in permeability in water-cured specimens, attributed to pore sealing and potential blocking due to the continued hydration process. Overall, the OPS–coir fibre reinforced concrete exhibited enhanced impact resilience and durability, suitable for application in sustainable construction where durability and impact resistance are of primary importance.

title: Revealing gut microbiome signatures in inflammatory bowel disease
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), is a chronic gastrointestinal disorder characterized by immune dysregulation and microbial imbalance. This study presents a gut microbiome analysis of Kazakhstani IBD patients, comparing stool microbiota from 132 IBD patients and their 132 non-IBD relatives using 16S rRNA sequencing. The results revealed a significant reduction in microbial diversity and distinct dysbiosis patterns in UC and CD. UC was associated with an overrepresentation of pathogenic genera (e.g., Streptococcus, Haemophilus ), while CD exhibited increased abundance of metabolically adaptive taxa (e.g., Olsenella, Flavonifractor ). Functional profiling revealed an increase in predicted pathways related to oxidative stress response and antibiotic biosynthesis, together with a reduction in steroid biosynthesis and bacterial motility pathways in UC. Random forest models using microbial and functional features achieved good classification performance (AUC = 0.83 and AUC = 0.75, respectively), identifying candidate diagnostic biomarkers. Correlation analyses linked microbial shifts with systemic inflammation (CRP, ESR), disease duration, and depressive symptoms, suggesting possible involvement of the gut–immune–brain axis. These findings underscore the microbiome’s diagnostic and therapeutic potential in IBD and highlight the need for personalized, microbiota-directed strategies tailored to regional microbial profiles.

title: Multidimensional behaviors-enhanced dual-path collaborative knowledge tracing model with forgetting perception
abstract: Current mainstream knowledge tracing methods suffer from problems such as coarse-grained of behavior analysis, insufficient mining of knowledge topological relationships, weak integration of spatiotemporal features, and lack of personalized forgetting modeling. This paper proposes a multidimensional behavior-enhanced dual-path collaborative knowledge tracing model, MEDKT, focusing on the synergistic integration of multidimensional behavior analysis and spatiotemporal features. The model adopts a hierarchical modular architecture for fine-grained knowledge tracing. First, it constructs a multidimensional behavior representation system that integrates explicit and implicit learning states, and employs gated residual structures together with adaptive weights to suppress temporal noise for behavior modeling and exercise representation learning. Second, a GNN-Transformer dual-branch encoding architecture is constructed, relying on graph structure to mine knowledge topology, using Transformer to capture long-term temporal patterns, and updating graph node weights through temporal attention to achieve deep fusion and bidirectional enhancement of spatiotemporal features; Subsequently, branch weights are allocated through adaptive gating fusion, and a knowledge-point-level memory decay strategy is designed based on the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve to characterize learners’ differentiated knowledge mastery and forgetting characteristics, thereby improving the knowledge tracing effect. Validation experiments in this paper are conducted on three public datasets, namely ASSIST09, ASSIST12 and Junyi. ROC-AUC, ACC, PR-AUC, F1 and RMSE are selected as evaluation metrics. Among them, PR-AUC measures the global probability ranking capability of the model, while F1 characterizes the hard classification performance under a fixed threshold of 0.5. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior overall performance compared with state-of-the-art baseline models: it yields better results in terms of ROC-AUC, ACC, PR-AUC and RMSE. A slight reversal is only observed for the F1 metric on the ASSIST09 dataset. This phenomenon is a non-significant fluctuation caused by threshold sensitivity and does not undermine the overall superiority of the model. On the ASSIST09 dataset, ROC-AUC increases by 0.81% points, ACC rises by 0.15% points, PR-AUC improves by 0.61% points, and RMSE decreases by 1.05. On the ASSIST12 dataset, ROC-AUC is boosted by 0.93% points, ACC increases by 1.04% points, PR-AUC improves by 0.57% points, and RMSE drops by 0.71. On the Junyi dataset, ROC-AUC rises by 1.56% points, ACC increases by 0.03% points, PR-AUC improves by 0.34% points, and RMSE is reduced by 0.16. Ablation experiments and visualization analysis further confirm the empirical effectiveness of each functional module. This model can provide reliable technical support for learning analytics and personalized learning guidance in online education scenarios.

title: A hybrid artificial neural network approach to forecasting CO₂ emissions in the United States under policy uncertainty and energy consumption
abstract: This study applies an advanced hybrid artificial neural network framework to predict total CO₂ emissions in the United States using monthly data from 1986M1 to 2025M12. Natural gas consumption, economic policy uncertainty, monetary policy uncertainty, oil prices, and renewable energy consumption are employed as predictors of emissions dynamics. The study compares the conventional multilayer perceptron with hybrid MLP models optimized using Tunicate Swarm Optimization, Moth-Flame Optimization, the Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm, the Sine Cosine Algorithm, and the Gaussian Mutation Specular Reflection Learning with Local Escaping Operator–based Artificial Electric Field Algorithm. It further extends the existing MLP-GRLEO-AEFA framework by integrating kernel regularization, thereby developing the MLP-KR-GRLEO-AEFA model. Model performance is evaluated using separate training and testing samples and assessed through NNSE, R², MSE, RMSE, MSLE, and MAE. Robustness is further examined using benchmark functions, convergence analysis, Friedman ranking, Wilcoxon tests, residual diagnostics, observed-versus-predicted plots, and permutation feature importance. The results show that the conventional MLP achieves the strongest training performance, MLP-SCA records the best out-of-sample testing performance, and MLP-KR-GRLEO-AEFA provides the strongest aggregate full-sample performance. Permutation feature importance also identifies the predictors that contribute most strongly to U.S. CO₂ emissions prediction. Based on these findings the study provides a reliable framework for forecasting U.S. CO2 emissions and supporting climate and energy-policy decisions.

title: Identification of complement system-related biomarkers in immunoglobulin A nephropathy through machine learning and single-cell data analysis
abstract: Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is associated with complement dysregulation, but complement-related molecular markers remain incompletely defined. We integrated bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE93798 training; GSE37460 validation), a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (GSE171314), machine-learning feature selection, functional enrichment, immune deconvolution, and a preliminary qRT-PCR assessment to identify candidate complement-system-related biomarkers. Among 25 differentially expressed complement-related genes, LASSO, SVM-RFE, and Boruta jointly prioritized A2M, C3AR1, COLEC11, SERPINA1, and IL1B; A2M, C3AR1, and SERPINA1 showed consistent cross-cohort expression patterns and AUCs > 0.7. A three-gene ANN classifier achieved an apparent training AUC of 1.000 and an external-validation AUC of 0.959, although overfitting remains possible. Functional analyses associated the candidates with ECM-receptor interaction and propionate-metabolism signatures. CIBERSORT and exploratory single-cell analyses suggested macrophage-related associations, but the single-cell dataset included only one healthy control. Archived summary-level qRT-PCR measurements from 5 patients with IgAN and 5 living-donor controls showed higher mean A2M and C3AR1 expression in IgAN tissue; these measurements are presented descriptively because participant-level raw values and the original statistical-test output were not available for independent reanalysis. These findings support A2M, C3AR1, and SERPINA1 as candidate IgAN biomarkers requiring validation in larger, clinically annotated cohorts.

title: An explainable swarm-optimized hybrid GRU–Transformer framework with wavelet-based spatial–temporal feature modeling and activation function analysis for rainfall classification across Pakistan’s climatic regimes
abstract: Accurate rainfall occurrence prediction is essential for climate risk management, flood preparedness, and water resource planning, particularly in climatically diverse regions such as Pakistan. This paper develops and compares a multi-phase classification of rainfall based on daily IMERG precipitation data over six representative Pakistani cities spanning very low-, moderate-, and high-rainfall regimes, i.e., Gharo, Gilgit, Islamabad, Karachi, Swat, and Turbat. The research follows a four-stage modeling process: (i) a baseline set of ensemble-learning models; (ii) a hybrid GRU–RNN model on 30-day temporal sequences with 19 engineered features; (iii) a GRU–RNN optimized with Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and the Tiki-Taka Algorithm (TTA); and (iv) a swarm-optimized hybrid GRU–Transformer using wavelet-based spatio-temporal features (W-ST). Four ensemble methods, namely Bagging, Boosting, Voting, and Stacking, were used in the initial phase to classify next-day rainfall. Findings show ensemble models perform well in low-rainfall cities in terms of overall accuracy because of the effect of class imbalance, while predictive performance is more balanced in moderate- and high-rainfall areas. In the second stage, a hybrid GRU–RNN model on 30-day temporal sequences and 19 engineered features showed good discrimination ability across the climatic regimes, with better rainfall-event classification in Karachi and Gharo among the low-rainfall cities and balanced classification in Gilgit and Swat. The analysis of activation functions also showed that ReLU is more effective in highly imbalanced low-rainfall conditions, whereas Tanh is more stable and balanced in moderate and heavy rainfall conditions. The third stage involved optimization of the GRU–RNN using the proposed TTA framework to improve the stability of the classification process, achieved by adding VMD-based multi-scale signal decomposition and adaptive hyperparameter tuning. The optimized framework achieved strong performance across cities, including Karachi (ACC = 0.944, F1 = 0.624, ROC–AUC = 0.885), Gharo (ACC = 0.927, F1 = 0.596), Gilgit (ACC = 0.772, F1 = 0.589, ROC–AUC = 0.834), and Swat (ACC = 0.656, F1 = 0.556). In the fourth stage, to enhance predictive performance, a swarm-intelligence-based hybrid deep-learning system combining W-ST, STFM, HGRA, DTGAM, GRU, and Transformer modules was developed using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Glowworm Swarm Optimization (GSO). Empirical findings show that PSO offers greater performance stability in most cities, especially Gharo, Karachi, Islamabad, and Swat, whereas GSO can offer better localized performance in Gilgit and Turbat. The activation-wise assessment shows that Tanh-based networks consistently generate better F1-scores and ROC–AUC values, whereas ReLU provides slightly more accurate results in extreme class-imbalance situations. In general, the proposed PSO/GSO hybrid framework achieved high classification performance across a variety of climatic regimes. The highest overall performance was achieved with GSO–Turbat in the Tanh configuration (ACC = 0.9617, F1 = 0.754, ROC–AUC = 0.956), followed by PSO–Turbat (ACC = 0.9583). PSO-based configurations in Gharo and Karachi were highly stable, with accuracies of 0.9392 and 0.9351, respectively. In moderate-rainfall regions, Gilgit achieved optimal performance with GSO–ReLU (ACC = 0.9064, F1 = 0.806, ROC–AUC = 0.953), while Islamabad performed best with PSO–Tanh (ACC = 0.8838, F1 = 0.782, ROC–AUC = 0.927). In all cities, ROC–AUC values were high (≈ 0.90–0.95), indicating strong discrimination ability between rain and non-rain events. The explainability analysis conducted using SHAP revealed wavelet-derived components, lagged rainfall variables, persistence measures, and seasonal encodings as the top predictors, suggesting that the proposed framework captures physically significant rainfall dynamics rather than spurious ones.
