title: HAFI-DTA: an interpretable multimodal framework for drug-target affinity prediction based on hierarchical attention guidance and feature iterative interaction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target affinity (DTA) is a core technical step in high-throughput drug screening and targeted drug discovery, which directly affects the efficiency of candidate compound mining and the control of research and development costs. Traditional experimental methods are difficult to meet the requirements of high-throughput screening, while existing deep learning-based models generally suffer from bottlenecks such as shallow fusion of multi-source heterogeneous features, insufficient mining of interactive features, and inadequate generalization robustness. To address these issues, we propose HAFI-DTA (Hierarchical Attention-Guided and Feature Iterative Interaction for Multimodal Drug-Target Affinity Prediction). Specifically, our framework employs a hierarchical attention mechanism to guide the fusion of multi-source heterogeneous features, and combines a two-layer GRU with iterative interaction to capture the deep correlations among features. Experimental results on the KIBA and Davis datasets demonstrate that the proposed HAFI-DTA model achieves overall performance comparable to the current state-of-the-art, while delivering stable and modest improvements in both CI and MSE metrics. Moreover, under the most challenging drug–target double cold-start scenario, our model attains the best performance, exhibiting excellent generalization robustness. In addition, interpretability analysis shows that the model can automatically focus on the key residues of the real binding pockets of proteins, providing an important basis for subsequent drug design and binding mode research.

title: Histopathology image classification based on ensembles of highly compact features
abstract: In this paper, we present a method for extracting highly informative yet compact features from histopathological images, which at the same time enable their classification with high accuracy. These types of concise features are very valuable due to the ever-increasing size of datasets as well as the sheer size of histopathology scans. To meet these requirements, we propose new methods for extracting features from the combinations of inner layers of deep neural networks DenseNet-161 and ResNet-152, as well as DINO derived from vision transformers. This is followed by the construction of the subspaces with the help of the principal, as well as neighborhood component analysis. This method creates new features: PCA/NCA-DenseFeats, PCa/NCA-ResFeats, and PCA/NCA-DINO. We then further improve their performance through domain-trained extraction models. The collected results show that the classification accuracy of these features becomes stable even after several-fold reduction of the dimensionality of the baseline features. This means that there is no need to use long representation vectors, and features even several times shorter can be used for classification with almost no information loss. In addition, we propose the multi-architecture ensemble of classifiers orchestrated by the error-correcting output codes method, which utilizes features extracted from three different domain-finetuned models with different architectures: ViT Small, ResNet-152, and DenseNet-161. The proposed solution allows for an increase in accuracy by up to almost 7pp compared to the baseline. The classification vector consumes only 180 float16 values, which is significantly smaller than many other published methods. This reduces the memory required to store features and enables faster classification of these representations. The proposed method was evaluated on the BreakHis breast cancer dataset (achieving 95.39% at 40X, 92.07% at 100X) and the Kather colorectal cancer dataset (97.1%), demonstrating its generalizability and applicability.

title: An integrated wireless sEMG framework with Bayesian-optimized machine learning for multi-task locomotor classification and neuromuscular characterization
abstract: Wearable surface electromyography (sEMG) systems show strong potential for real-time gait analysis, yet few frameworks combine wireless acquisition, standardized normalization, and optimized machine learning within a single validated pipeline, leaving their joint contribution to subject-independent locomotor recognition unclear. This study developed and validated a custom wireless sEMG framework combining hardware design, normalization evaluation, and Bayesian-optimized machine learning for locomotor-task classification and neuromuscular characterization. An ESP32-based system recorded tibialis anterior, soleus, and gastrocnemius lateralis activity in 25 healthy participants during level walking, stair ascent, and ramp ascent. Signals were bandpass filtered (20–500 Hz), rectified, and used to extract 120 time-, frequency-, and time–frequency-domain features. Three normalization strategies, three feature-selection methods, and eight Bayesian-optimized classifiers were evaluated via an exploratory participant-level split, nested 5 × 5 cross-validation, leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) validation, and an independent test set. Task-dependent EMG differences were significant with large effect sizes (η 2 = 0.183–0.708, p < .001). Level walking was the most electromyographically distinct task, while stair and ramp ascent were similar yet separable; ramp ascent showed multi-muscle co-activation at mid-stance and peak soleus activity at toe-off (50.7 ± 6.2% MVC). Genetic Algorithm feature selection with Z-score normalization gave the best single-split performance (logistic regression: 98.33% accuracy; SVM: 96.33%). Under the stricter LOSO regime, random forest reached 89.02% accuracy with 44 features, while a correlation-pruned 17-feature subset matched or exceeded this across all classifiers—best with SVM (92.40%)—achieving an 85.8% dimensionality reduction from the original feature space (61% relative to the 44-feature set) with no loss in mean accuracy. Two deep-learning baselines (1D-CNN, BiLSTM) achieved comparable LOSO accuracy (91.39% and 87.72%), confirming the feature-based pipeline captures the signal’s discriminative structure without end-to-end deep architectures. These findings support an interpretable, compact, subject-independent framework for multi-task locomotor classification, though broader clinical validation is still needed.

title: A drone-assisted deep learning framework for disaster assessment in real time and emergency response
abstract: Disasters affect citizen safety, municipal infrastructure, and the economy, making disaster management vital and difficult. Rapid urban expansion and climatic extremes have increased big catastrophe frequency and complexity. Situational awareness and quick decision-making are needed. In catastrophes, traditional evaluation methods may not give accurate and timely information owing to enormous volumes of data and quick changes. Due to these restrictions, this research offers an AI system for real-time catastrophe assessment and response using drones and the Adaptive Convolutional-Transformer Fusion Network. Convolutional feature extraction and attention-based temporal modeling allow ACTF-Net to grasp sequential interactions and dynamic spatial patterns in high-dimensional catastrophic data. Adaptive Relevance Filtering and Contextual Scaling Transformation increase data dependability and feature relevance, enabling noisy or missing data learning. Testing regularly shows that ACTF-Net outperforms previous systems like BERT and CapsNet. F1-score is 0.981, area under curve is 0.993, and catastrophe severity prediction rate is 0.96. The model’s consistent performance across datasets of different sizes across time supports real-time applications. The proposed method uses multimodal drone data, powerful preprocessing, and novel metrics like the Contextual Sensitivity Index and Temporal Stability Score to reliably categorize and assess catastrophe severity using multiple labels. The results indicate that ACTF-Net may improve situational awareness, resource usage, and response time in high-risk crisis situations.

title: Climate-related shifts in fire-weather regimes across heterogeneous mountain ecosystems: long-term spatiotemporal assessment in the Alborz mountains
abstract: Climate change is intensifying fire-weather activity globally, yet the extent to which ecosystem structure modulates fire-weather regimes in complex mountain environments remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate contrasting responses of forested and non-forested landscapes to climate-driven fire weather in the Alborz Mountains (1980–2025). Using high-resolution Fire Weather Index (FWI) data, combined with nonparametric trend analysis, structural breakpoint detection, spatial hotspot analysis, and a supplementary machine learning-based statistical extrapolation, we identify a pronounced divergence in fire-weather dynamics across land-cover types. Non-forested areas exhibit up to approximately threefold higher mean annual frequencies of high-FWI days compared with forested areas at the high fire-danger threshold (FWI ≥21.3), together with stronger historical increasing trends, whereas Hyrcanian forests exhibit comparatively muted responses. These differences are consistent with the combined influence of contrasting land-cover environments and the prevailing climatic and topographic gradients across the Alborz Mountains, with forested regions generally experiencing lower fire-weather exposure under their current environmental setting. Spatial analyses reveal persistent and intensifying hotspots concentrated in the western Alborz, alongside a marked west–east gradient in fire-weather evolution. Abrupt shifts detected during the mid-to-late 1990s, particularly around 1996 and 1999, indicate potential transitions in regional fire-weather regimes, although their relationships with large-scale climatic variability require further investigation. As a supplementary analysis, historical fire-weather patterns were statistically extrapolated to 2026–2035, indicating relatively higher frequencies in non-forested summer landscapes. These estimates represent statistical continuation of historical temporal patterns rather than climate projections or deterministic predictions of future wildfire occurrence. Overall, the results highlight pronounced spatial contrasts in climate-driven fire-weather conditions among different land-cover environments. These patterns reflect the combined influence of land-cover distribution, regional climatic gradients, and topographic setting rather than the independent effect of land cover alone.

title: Evaluation of age-friendly public space renovation in older residential communities based on AHP and AIGC —a case study of Shaolin Community, Quanzhou, China
abstract: Using Shaolin Community in Quanzhou, China, as a case, this study examined artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) for early-stage design and evaluation of age-friendly public-space renovation. A four-criterion, 16-indicator system was developed through literature and policy review, field investigation, and professional consultation. A 15-member specialist panel applied the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) to determine weights. A separate 15-member evaluation panel, including six older resident representatives, then rated six scheme sets generated by Dreamina AI, MidJourney, and Stable Diffusion for five public-space nodes. Infrastructure Renovation received the highest criterion weight, while accessible facilities, cultural atmosphere, environmental sanitation, spatial accessibility, and quality of life ranked highly among the indicators. Within the case-specific workflows, the two Stable Diffusion scheme sets received the highest composite scores. Panel B ratings showed high concordance in scheme ordering (Kendall’s W = 0.931, p < 0.001), and the complete ranking remained unchanged across 64 one-at-a-time weight-perturbation scenarios (± 10% and ± 20%). Structured weighting made the screening criteria for AIGC concepts more explicit than an undifferentiated visual appraisal. However, the study covered one community, six scheme sets, limited resident participation, and platform-specific workflows, and no probabilistic uncertainty analysis was performed. The findings therefore should not be generalized beyond this setup. The integrated workflow is presented as preliminary conceptual-design decision support, not evidence of general tool superiority or implementation performance.

title: A reconfigurable architecture for CNN acceleration using line buffers
abstract: Computer vision (CV) is experiencing a rapid increase in real-time applications driven by neural network (NN) processing. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are the core architecture of advanced CV applications based on artificial intelligence (AI) for autonomous driving, facial recognition, object detection, and information decryption. However, huge computational complexity and continuous memory bandwidth requirements restrict the efficient hardware implementation of CNNs on FPGA platforms. In this paper proposes a reconfigurable systolic CNN architecture using line buffers for enhancing the resource utilization and reducing delay. The proposed architecture dynamically reconfigured to CNN layer requirements, and line buffers improve the data reuse and reduce redundant memory access. In addition, reconfigurable adder and pooling structures are designed to increase the flexibility of accumulation and down sampling operations, supporting various kernel sizes and layers in CNNs. The proposed reconfigurable architecture is hardware-efficient through control signals and adapts to all CNN layers. FPGA implementation of this proposed reconfigurable architecture is performed using LeNet CNN architecture layers. This flexible and low-cost reconfigurable systolic CNN architecture achieves a 15.25% reduction in LUTs utilization, 75% improvement in throughput, and 2.44% reduction in computational delay in LeNet CNN. The implemented LeNet CNN using proposed reconfigurable architecture is suitable for high performance and hardware efficient CNN applications.

title: A hybrid ANN-metaheuristic framework for vibration-based identification of orthotropic parameters in GFRP laminated plates
abstract: Glass-fibre-reinforced polymer (GFRP) composite plates are widely used in engineering structures, yet their numerical modelling is challenging because their material properties can vary due to anisotropy, manufacturing variability, and uncertainty in input parameters. This study develops a fast numerical framework for vibration-based finite element model updating and inverse identification of orthotropic material properties in GFRP composite plates using analytical modal reference data. A baseline finite element model was developed in Abaqus and compared with modal results obtained using Classical laminate plate theory. To reduce the high computational cost of repeated finite element simulations during model updating, an artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate model was trained on parametric FE data and coupled with genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimisation (PSO), and slime mould algorithm (SMA) optimisation methods. The novelty of the study lies in comparing these ANN-assisted optimisation frameworks with direct GA-Abaqus-Python updating under the same modal identification problems. Pearson correlation-based sensitivity analysis showed that the longitudinal elastic modulus E x was the dominant parameter affecting the modal response, with sensitivity values ranging from approximately 0.62 to 0.80. In the representative updated model, ANN-SMA achieved the lowest average frequency-prediction error of 2.289%, compared with 3.821% for the conventional GA-Abaqus-Python updated model. However, statistical analysis over 50 independent runs showed that ANN-PSO provided the best robustness, with the lowest mean frequency error, smallest standard deviation, and lower runtime than ANN-SMA. The ANN-assisted methods reduced the computational time from approximately 5.830 h to 6.617–42.409 s. These results show that ANN-assisted model updating provides an efficient numerical approach for vibration-based material-property identification in composite structures.

title: Phytochemical-based quality control of cayenne pepper using spectroscopic monitoring of lycopene content and antioxidant capacity
abstract: Quality control in cayenne pepper fruit is important for maintaining product consistency. The research aimed to evaluate lycopene content and antioxidant capacity as the main indicators of cayenne pepper quality. Visible-near infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy is an emerging technology that can predict lycopene content and antioxidant capacity non-destructively, accurately, and quickly. Spectral data (381–1065 nm) were analyzed using support vector machine regression to develop the calibration model. Reference data on lycopene and antioxidant capacity were determined using spectrophotometry method. The results displayed a robust association between spectra and reference data. The calibration model for lycopene content and antioxidant capacity generated sufficient performance in terms of accuracy. For both parameters, the models showed correlation coefficient ( R ) ≥ 0.85, root mean square error of calibration (RMSEC) ≥ 17.61, root mean square error of cross validation (RMSECV) ≥ 42.01, and ratio of prediction to deviation (RPD) ≥ 1.95. Based on these results, it further strengthens that Vis-NIR technology was able to non-destructively assess lycopene content and antioxidant capacity. In the food and postharvest industries, the developed method shows promise for fast quality screening, automated grading, and real-time monitoring. Additionally, Vis-NIR spectroscopy’s rapidity and non-destructive nature make it scalable for industrial uses, especially in precision agriculture and contemporary quality control systems. These findings support the potential of non-destructive technology as an alternative for the quality control system of cayenne pepper quality in the agricultural and food industries.

title: CNN model-based image classification for canine brain MRI abnormalities
abstract: Diagnostic imaging represents one of the most promising clinical applications of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the customised convolutional neural network (CNN) SepNetDense for distinguishing between normal and abnormal canine brain magnetic resonance images (MRIs), with the aim of enhancing diagnostic efficiency and assisting radiologists in identifying abnormal images. The dataset comprised T1-weighted (T1w) pre- and post-contrast sequences in transverse, sagittal, and dorsal planes from 550 dogs, collected from four universities. Dogs were included if they had a complete clinical diagnosis confirmed either through histopathology or in accordance with current clinical consensus. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 444), a validation set (n = 53), and a test set (n = 53). Each MRI was labelled on a slice-by-slice basis as normal or abnormal. The model was trained on 205 normal imaging datasets (e.g., extracranial aetiologies, idiopathic epilepsy, paroxysmal dyskinesia) and 239 abnormal ones (e.g., neoplasms, inflammatory lesions, other pathologies). The model correctly predicted 74% of the true normal slices in the test set as normal and 73% of the true abnormal as abnormal. A ROC analysis of the model’s prediction at the patient level revealed that, at a threshold of 51% abnormal slices per patient, the model reached an optimal balance of 83% sensitivity (95% CI 67–91%) and 78% (95% CI 54–91%) specificity, with a balanced accuracy of 80% (95% CI 69–92%). ANCOVA revealed that the CNN’s classification performance was influenced by multiple biological, technical, and institutional factors. Lesion diagnosis, institutional setting, and breed size had significant large effects, whereas body weight showed a significant medium effect. Significant interactions with large effect sizes were also observed between diagnosis and institute, as well as between breed size and weight. Additionally, a distinct pattern was observed in the distribution of prediction categories along the anatomical axes, with a trend towards better CNN performance in the central quartiles across all MRI sequences. Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of CNN-assisted triage of canine brain MRI studies and highlight diagnosis, institutional setting, breed size, and body weight as key determinants of model performance, emphasising the importance of heterogeneous datasets for the development of robust veterinary AI applications.

title: Machine learning-driven inverse design of high-hardness multi-principal element alloys through symbolic regression
abstract: Conventional trial-and-error metallurgical approaches fail to efficiently develop high-hardness multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs), limited by poor physical interpretability of existing machine learning (ML) hardness prediction models and the lack of targeted inverse composition optimization. This work establishes a closed-loop physics-informed ML framework integrating symbolic regression (SR), CatBoost surrogate modelling and multi-metaheuristic optimization to address the two core bottlenecks. A comprehensive descriptor library is constructed by integrating elemental fractions, pymatgen-derived atomic physicochemical properties and classical Hume-Rothery metallurgical parameters, which quantitatively captures lattice distortion, electronic effects and phase transformation mechanisms governing alloy hardness. Genetic programming-based symbolic regression automatically extracts three nonlinear descriptors that encode standardized physicochemical variables, reducing the original 39-dimensional feature space by 33% and remarkably elevating predictive accuracy. The SR-enhanced CatBoost model achieves a test-set coefficient of determination R 2 = 0.885 and RMSE = 77.2 HV, far outperforming traditional semi-empirical formulas and baseline ML models. SHAP analysis verifies that the three SR features contribute 52% of total predictive weight, explicitly elucidating non-monotonic hardening responses including hardness saturation under excessive atomic size mismatch and the trade-off between bulk modulus and dislocation storage capacity. A triangulated inverse design pipeline combining genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization and whale optimization algorithm is deployed to maximize Vickers hardness under four- and five-principal-element constraints. Cross-algorithm convergence shows stability of the search under a shared surrogate rather than global optimality. The 22 candidates that clear the physical screen and the domain test span 716.6-783.1 HV. Refractory W and Mo act as primary strengthening elements, while moderate Al addition enables simultaneous lightweighting and possible precipitation hardening. This integrated framework unifies interpretable forward hardness prediction, mechanistic analysis and targeted compositional inverse design, drastically cutting experimental screening costs. Future research will incorporate processing and microstructural variables to realize multi-objective optimization balancing hardness, density and ductility.

title: Integrating causal knowledge with satellite and glider data: a novel framework for marine water quality simulation
abstract: This study presents a causally informed machine-learning framework for jointly estimating coastal marine variables by incorporating prior structural assumptions into model training. The causal-informed neural network (CINN) uses an expert-specified directed acyclic graph (DAG) and model-based feature-perturbation effects as regularization targets; it is designed for prediction and does not identify causal effects from the observational data. The framework combines satellite remote sensing data with high-resolution in-situ glider measurements from the upper 0–2 m to jointly estimate temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, and chlorophyll-a. Under acquisition-date-blocked five-fold cross-validation, in which all observations from the same acquisition date were kept in the same fold, CINN achieved R² values of 0.961, 0.905, 0.898, and 0.725, respectively, and a uniform-average multi-output R² of 0.872. Regularization-weight, matched-input, and output ablations assess predictive sensitivity, while bootstrap intervals and Diebold–Mariano tests quantify uncertainty in the reported observation-level comparisons.

title: Methodological audit and empirical evaluation of a lightweight whole-volume 3D CNN for preterm brain injury classification
abstract: This study uses methodological auditing to evaluate a proof-of-concept engineering pipeline for classifying radiological severity groups of preterm brain injury (BI) from T2-weighted MRI in the dHCP cohort. Its primary contribution is methodology-driven empirical discovery rather than a new neural-network architecture. GloResNet combines a standard ResNet-10 backbone, MedicalNet initialization, whole-volume array resizing, mixup, and array-axis-0-reversal probability averaging, hereafter referred to as axis-0-reversal averaging; no new CNN block is proposed. The audit identifies concrete mechanisms by which small-cohort imaging results can be overstated, including unit-of-analysis drift, fold-assignment non-traceability, post hoc model-selection bias, and ranking across incompatible evaluation protocols. Building on this framework, we report the first fair, traceable comparison between a de novo trained Vision Transformer (ViT) and a domain-adapted lightweight 3D CNN on a public preterm brain injury dataset. When all sources of bias are controlled, the lightweight CNN achieves comparable or superior performance to ViT, challenging the prevailing assumption that larger, more complex architectures are always preferable in low-data regimes. Applying the audit to the historical evidence also showed that the archived GloResNet mean fold accuracy of \(69.12 \pm 7.42\%\) was calculated over 180 scan records from 128 subjects, including repeated scans, without retained subject identifiers or out-of-fold predictions. The historical archive is therefore reported separately from the fair, traceable server-side comparison. A separate, auditable subject-level input-representation experiment did not demonstrate superiority of whole-volume input. The resulting minimum reporting standard requires an explicit statistical unit, traceable subject-level folds, retained out-of-fold predictions, prespecified selection rules, and transparent comparator conditions. These internal estimates do not establish clinical screening performance or external generalizability. The source code is available at https://github.com/ICL-SUST/GloResNet-Preterm-Brain

title: Explainable hybrid ensemble framework for lung cancer classification using deep CNNs and random forest
abstract: Lung cancer is still a significant cause of cancer death in the world. Thoracic computed tomography (CT) classification can be helpful in earlier diagnosis and better patient management. However, many deep-learning techniques require large annotated datasets, large amounts of computational resources and the techniques are not easily interpretable. This manuscript introduces a comprehensible hybrid approach to multiclass lung cancer classification based on two different transfer-learning backbones, DenseNet169 and MobileNetV2. They used several ensemble techniques to combine their class-probability outputs. For qualitative visual explanations of the image regions contributing to each prediction, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was applied to the image after inference. The framework was evaluated with two publicly available thoracic CT datasets that include both benign and malignant, normal and non-small-cell lung cancer categories. The accuracy of the Random Forest stacker for the Chest CT dataset was 99.50% and 99.54% for the IQ-OTH/NCCD dataset. The results show that DenseNet169 and MobileNetV2 complementary probability outputs could be used as an effective decision-fusion method in lung cancer classification from different datasets with different class structures and diagnostic categories. The Grad-CAM technique also made the model predictions more transparent by identifying image areas that influenced the prediction. In general, the proposed framework presents a practical and comprehensible method for automated lung cancer classification, and serves as a valuable guideline in future studies regarding the development of robust, explainable, and clinically relevant computer-aided diagnosis in medical imaging.

title: Econometric-prior-guided multi-head attention with application for interpretable multi-horizon financial forecasting
abstract: Reliable financial forecasting requires both predictive accuracy and transparent model behavior. This study presents Economic-Loss Guided Multi-Head Self-Attention (ELG-MHSA), a transformer framework that regularizes three attention heads toward distinct econometric and statistical priors: GARCH-based conditional variance, a trailing moving-average target for mean reversion, and a one-sided trend estimate. The priors are constructed separately within each causal input window and are normalized over eligible historical positions only, preventing future information from entering training or evaluation. The proposed losses are optimized jointly with the forecasting objective without changing the transformer encoder structure. Experiments on VIX Futures, FRED-MD, and Binance BTC-USD compare ELG-MHSA with GARCH(1,1), EGARCH, a standard multi-head transformer, and the Temporal Fusion Transformer. The reported results are interpreted as descriptive performance differences unless accompanied by formal uncertainty estimates. The framework is intended to improve the economic interpretability of attention while retaining multi-horizon predictive capacity.

title: Risk model for predicting mortality risk in patients with cerebral infarction: a cohort study using the MIMIC-IV database
abstract: Cerebral infarction represents a significant health threat, causing mortality and long-term disability. This study investigated prognostic variables associated with cerebral infarction and developed a risk model to predict mortality, thereby offering new strategies to enhance patient care and improve overall outcomes. Participants were selected from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database, covering the period 2008–2019. The study population comprised patients with cerebral infarction admitted to the intensive care unit. Univariate Cox regression analysis, proportional hazards assumption testing, machine learning (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression), and multivariate Cox regression analysis were performed to identify prognostic variables. Based on these variables, a risk model was developed and subsequently evaluated. After excluding ineligible individuals, 109 patients with cerebral infarction were included. The anion gap [hazard ratio (HR) = 1.1040, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.0070–1.2110, P = 0.0356], platelet count (HR = 0.9965, 95% CI = 0.9939–0.9990, P = 0.0072), and glucose concentration (HR = 1.0050, 95% CI = 1.0000–1.0090, P = 0.0483) were identified as prognostic variables. A risk model utilizing these prognostic variables classified patients into high- and low-risk cohorts, with high-risk patients displaying lower survival probabilities. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated the strong predictive performance of this risk model, with all areas under the curve exceeding 0.7. The study identified the anion gap, platelet count, and glucose concentration as prognostic variables for cerebral infarction. The findings underscore the potential of the risk model to enhance clinical decision-making and management for patients with cerebral infarction.

title: Solar-powered VANET architecture for sustainable and smart traffic management in arid regions
abstract: Energy-autonomous roadside communication is essential for sustainable intelligent transportation systems (ITS), particularly in arid regions that combine abundant solar resources with highly dynamic traffic demand. Existing solar-powered vehicular ad hoc network (VANET) approaches typically treat roadside unit (RSU) placement, activation scheduling, and traffic prediction as separate problems, limiting their ability to coordinate long-term infrastructure siting with short-term communication demand and energy availability. This paper presents an integrated solar-powered VANET framework that coordinates these spatial and temporal decisions within a unified architecture. A Discrete Grey Wolf Optimization (D-GWO) method performs spacing-aware RSU siting by maximizing traffic coverage, network centrality, and solar harvesting potential while penalizing redundancy. A Traffic-Aware Duty Cycling (TADC) controller regulates RSU operation through traffic hysteresis, battery state-of-charge guards, and minimum dwell times. A Joint Activation Score (JAS) couples long-term site utility with runtime activation, and a Random Forest-based traffic anticipation module enables proactive scheduling; the Activation Timeliness Gain (ATG) metric quantifies the resulting improvement in activation timing. Trace-driven simulations on the Ha’il City road network, using measured solar irradiance and real traffic data, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves packet delivery ratios (PDR) of 94.5–97.9%, reduces end-to-end delay (E2ED) by 7–35 ms, and lowers per-RSU energy consumption by 20–33% relative to representative baselines, while maintaining fully off-grid operation under the evaluated conditions. Predictive assistance further advances RSU activation by up to 2.1 min during traffic surges without additional energy cost. These results show that coordinated spatio-temporal design can simultaneously enhance communication reliability, responsiveness, and energy efficiency, supporting the feasibility of energy-autonomous VANET operation under the evaluated Ha’il topology, traffic densities, irradiance trace, and log-distance radio model.

title: A machine learning-based web application aids Kawasaki disease diagnosis and predicts its outcomes
abstract: Unless Kawasaki disease (KD) is promptly treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), patients may develop IVIG-unresponsiveness and aneurysm. We analysed 628 KD and 155 KD-like cases to develop machine learning models for having KD (i.e., being diagnosed with KD), IVIG-unresponsiveness and aneurysm formation. We applied LASSO logistic regression to illness-day-indexed data incorporating family/previous histories and laboratory variables (e.g., neutrophils, total bilirubin, C-reactive protein, and AST). Optional inputs included BNP, IgG, fibrinogen, and echocardiographic Z scores. On Day 4, all models achieved AUCs > 0.7 in the test dataset: having KD (0.779), IVIG-unresponsiveness (0.772), and aneurysm formation (0.710). On Day 5, the model achieved a positive predictive value > 90% for having KD. When combined with predictions of unresponsiveness or aneurysm, 90% of complicated KD cases were identified. These models were implemented in a web-based and intranet-integrated application, enabling early diagnosis and risk stratification of KD across resource-limited and resource-rich settings.

title: SCLC-SBT: a spectral-bilinear transformer for small cell lung cancer histopathology image classification
abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is among the most lethal thoracic malignancies, and timely and accurate histopathological classification is critical for guiding treatment decisions. Existing deep learning approaches face difficulty simultaneously capturing the high-frequency nuclear texture features characteristic of SCLC—such as hyperchromatic salt-and-pepper chromatin and dense nuclear moulding—and the long-range spatial dependencies of tissue organisation, limiting classification reliability. To address these challenges, this study proposes SCLC-SBT, a hierarchical Spectral-Bilinear Transformer for automated SCLC histopathological image classification. The network deploys re-parameterizable Hybrid-Conv Blocks (HCB) with frequency-domain Spectral-Channel Attention (SCA) in the first three stages to extract fine-grained multi-scale local features, and employs a novel Dual-Branch Conv Linear Integration Transformer (DBCLIT) in the deepest stage to jointly model local morphology and long-range dependencies via bilinear selective state space modelling. Evaluated on a 1,974-image binary classification benchmark comprising Normal and SCLC tissue patches, SCLC-SBT achieves 0.9697 accuracy (95% CI 0.9495 to 0.9865), 0.9728 F1-score, and 0.9971 AUC, attaining the best point estimate among eleven compared architectures including DeiT, MLP-Mixer, DaViT, and CAFormer on five of the seven reported metrics. Bootstrap confidence intervals and pairwise McNemar’s tests indicate that this advantage is statistically significant relative to five of the eleven baselines. Relative to the six strongest baselines, DeiT, MLP-Mixer, CAFormer, Swin-T, and the tied PoolFormer and DaViT pair, the difference is not statistically significant at \(\alpha =0.05\) on the 297-sample test set, so SCLC-SBT is best interpreted as achieving competitive to superior accuracy at a substantially better accuracy-efficiency trade-off while maintaining competitive model efficiency with approximately 17 M parameters and 7.0 G FLOPs. The results demonstrate that integrating spectral-domain channel recalibration with bilinear state space modelling provides an effective inductive bias for SCLC histopathological feature learning.

title: Metabolic syndrome and colorectal cancer share GPAT3 and PLAU as candidate genes: Mendelian randomisation, machine learning, single-cell knockout and docking
abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) associates with colorectal cancer (CRC), but the direction and linking nodes are unresolved. We integrated bidirectional Mendelian randomisation (MetS as a latent genetic liability), MetS–CRC transcriptomic intersection, machine-learning prioritisation, immune deconvolution, single-cell virtual knockout and docking. MR supported a MetS-to-CRC effect (inverse-variance-weighted OR = 1.231, 95% CI 1.052–1.439, P = 0.0093); the reverse direction was non-significant and, with only seven instruments, inconclusive. The transcriptomes shared 200 co-differentially expressed genes, 36 within a TNF/NF-κB prior set from MSigDB hallmark founder sets. Of seven hubs retained by all three algorithms, GPAT3 and PLAU were significant in both GSE10950 and TCGA/GEPIA2, GPAT3 being directionally concordant between the MetS and CRC contrasts and PLAU concordant only across tumour platforms. GPAT3 virtual knockout perturbed blood-vessel morphogenesis, extracellular-matrix organisation and myeloid activation. PLAU correlated most strongly with tumour neutrophils ( r = 0.376). Docking of three ligands against the PLAU catalytic domain predicted binding for all three, strongest for AGB (N-(1-adamantyl)-N′-(4-guanidinobenzyl)urea) and amiloride. These findings are consistent with a causal MetS-to-CRC direction (robust to MR-PRESSO outlier correction and MR-RAPS, and placed in context by multivariable MR) and nominate GPAT3 and PLAU as candidate nodes for testing.

title: RSTNet: sandstorm image enhancement using a residual saturation and transmission estimation network
abstract: The degradation of sandstorm images is diverse, as it encompasses color casting and dark and dim conditions. In addition, because the structural degradation of sandstorm images involves imbalanced color channels, an image may seem yellowish or reddish. Moreover, when an image is obtained, because the atmosphere contains various hazy particles such as sand, the sand in the image may seem hazy. The existing sandstorm image enhancement methods improve the image’s color components and mitigate the hazy effect. However, an artificial color component may appear when the enhanced color channels are imbalanced. Therefore, in this paper, an effective color balancing method using convolutional neural networks and image saturation is proposed because image saturation is strongly related to color information. Additionally, a color-balanced image may be hazy because of the presence of hazy particles; thus, in this paper, hazy images are enhanced using transmission networks for dehazing. Overall, a sandstorm image enhancement method using a convolutional neural network that estimates residual saturation and a transmission estimation network (RST-Net) is proposed. The enhanced images obtained using the RSTNet appear natural, and the RSTNet is verified to be suitable for enhancing degraded sandstorm images.

title: Non-volatile, compact, and broadband multimode matrix vector multiplication for photonic neuromorphic computing
abstract: Matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) is a fundamental operation in artificial neural networks. While conventional electronic implementations of MVMs face bottlenecks in speed and energy efficiency, here, we design an ultra-compact (185 μm × 21 μm) non-volatile photonic MVM engine leveraging mode division multiplexing (MDM) with the fundamental and first-order transverse magnetic modes. The architecture integrates a multimode-interferometer power splitter (0.98 dB insertion loss), a directional-coupler (de)multiplexer (≈ -10 dB crosstalk suppression, 0.87 dB insertion loss), a weighting core comprising four independently programmable weighting paths, each containing five Ge 2 Sb 2 Se 4 Te 1 (GSST) phase-change cells in series, giving twenty cells in total. By electrically programming individual GSST cells between amorphous and crystalline states, the device supports 1296 distinct matrix configurations with an extinction ratio of 11.29 dB and 17.3 dB for TM0 and TM1 modes, respectively. Electro-thermal simulations indicate ultrafast and reversible switching using a 5 V and 33 ns pulse for crystallization, while a 12 V and 5 ns pulse triggers melting and rapid quenching for amorphization. The non-volatile nature of GSST eliminates static power consumption, enabling energy-efficient operation. The complete MVM exhibits a total insertion loss of 2.76 dB and 3.64 dB at 1550 nm for TM0 and TM1 modes, respectively. This device maintains functionality across a 40 nm bandwidth (1540–1580 nm), offering a scalable pathway for energy-efficient, MDM-enabled photonic computing.

title: An adaptive transformer-based model with entropy-driven knowledge distillation for single-channel EEG REM sleep detection
abstract: Accurate detection of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep is critical for neurophysiological monitoring and early identification of sleep-related disorders. An entropy-driven adaptive knowledge distillation framework integrated with a lightweight Transformer was developed to support robust REM sleep detection from single-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. By dynamically adjusting temperature scaling and distillation weighting based on teacher–student entropy, the proposed approach explicitly models uncertainty inherent in REM sleep. When evaluated under subject-independent cross-validation on three public datasets (Sleep-EDF, ISRUC-Sleep, and MASS), the proposed model outperformed CNN, LSTM, and standard Transformer baselines, achieving an average accuracy of 93.2% and an F1 score of 92.8%. Moreover, the distilled student model reduced training time and memory usage by approximately 30%, indicating potential suitability for future optimization toward real-time and wearable EEG applications. These results suggest that uncertainty-aware adaptive distillation may support accurate and computationally efficient REM sleep detection from single-channel EEG under subject-independent experimental conditions.

title: A multi-source earth observation and artificial intelligence framework for unsupervised water-use anomaly screening in Mediterranean agriculture
abstract: Reliable screening of agricultural water-use anomalies over large areas remains challenging because verified event labels and field observations are rarely available. We present AI4WaterGuard, a multi-source Earth Observation and artificial intelligence framework for unsupervised water-use anomaly screening across Cyprus. Using 617,862 records from 1,974 centroids across six hydrological years, six primary detector families were assessed under nested temporal cross-validation with training-consistent scaling, validity-aware scoring, and harmonised temporal support. Among the five centroid-sequence detectors, the convolutional neural network autoencoder showed the strongest response to the strong-reference controlled synthetic proxy, achieving Average Precision of \(0.893\pm 0.130\) and Proxy F1 of \(0.880\pm 0.100\) . The spatially explicit convolutional long short-term memory variational autoencoder was evaluated at finer land-pixel-sequence granularity and interpreted descriptively. Across five perturbation patterns and three severities, the convolutional neural network autoencoder achieved an equal-scenario mean Average Precision of 0.342, declining to 0.088 for weak perturbations. These synthetic metrics quantify controlled-proxy sensitivity, not field-validated detection performance. Operational post-processing on 1,157 WorldCover-eligible centroids combined threshold sensitivity, 1,000 exact-count randomisations, a primary Top-50 inspection-prioritisation queue with a nested Top-20 high-priority subset, and common-cadence spatiotemporal events. The resulting screening priorities require independent administrative and field evidence to establish physical cause or legal status.

title: Experimental enhancing drug solubility in supercritical CO₂ using modifiers: Modeling and machine learning prediction
abstract: The experimental determination of the solubility of aripiprazole (APZ) in supercritical carbon dioxide (SC-CO 2 ) containing ethanol and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) was conducted at temperatures ranging from 308 to 338 K and pressures from 12 to 30 MPa. The measured mole fraction solubility of ethanol ranged from 2.95 × 10 − 5 to 1.03 × 10 − 4 , while that of DMSO ranged from 4.59 × 10 − 5 to 1.38 × 10 − 4 . These results demonstrate that DMSO provides superior solubility enhancement. The maximum enhancement factor achieved was approximately 33 relatives to pure SC-CO₂. The experimental were then correlated using six semi-empirical models: The Sodeifian-Sajadian, González et al., Jouyban et al., Garlapati-Madras, MST, and Soltani-Mazloumi models. The Sodeifian-Sajadian and González et al. models were found to give the best correlations in terms of AARD%, R adj, and AICc, respectively, for DMSO and ethanol. In addition, multilayer perceptron (MLP) and support vector regression (SVR) models were developed to predict APZ solubility. The MLP model demonstrated superior predictive capabilities, with AARD values of 0.85% and 1.30% for the ethanol and DMSO systems, respectively. The experimental data and predictive models provide a reliable foundation for designing and optimizing supercritical pharmaceutical particle engineering processes.

title: Identification of artificially ripened banana by chemical agent using gas sensor array
abstract: Fresh fruits are consumed for the necessary vitamins, minerals, fiber, and proteins to keep ourselves healthy. The banana is a common and healthy fruit produced around the year in Bangladesh and many countries in the world. Bananas are often artificially ripened by chemical agents, which is injurious to health. Therefore, detecting artificially ripened bananas (ARB) has become important in ensuring food safety and quality. A novel non-destructive approach to identify ARB by analyzing electronic signals acquired by a gas sensor array in response to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted from bananas is proposed in this paper. An automated data collection system is designed, which consists of a gas sensor array, a data acquisition device, and LabVIEW. Four machine learning (ML) models, namely logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), decision tree (DT), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), have been utilized to analyze the sensor data and classify the bananas into both binary and day-wise (ripening stages) classification of artificially and naturally ripened banana (ANRB) tasks. Among the four models, XGBoost achieved the best performance on binary classification of ANRB with 97.03% and 95.05 ± 2.98% test and 10-fold cross-validation (CV) accuracy while incorporating important features. As for the day-wise classification, the SVM model performed best, obtaining 99.94% test accuracy and 99.92 ± 0.05% CV accuracy (utilizing all features). Moreover, this study is the first investigation of ANRB detection using VOC response, which also outperforms existing hyperspectral imaging-based ANRB classification in a substantially cost-effective manner. Overall, this study contributes to the advancement of food safety technologies by providing a non-destructive technique, an alternative to destructive solutions, for ARB detection.

title: Multi-scale representation contrastive learning for multivariate time-series anomaly detection
abstract: In recent years, multivariate time series anomaly detection has received growing attention due to its broad relevance in real-world applications. Nevertheless, accurately identifying anomalies in large-scale time series remains challenging. Many existing methods partition time series into patches to model temporal information, but single-scale patching cannot simultaneously capture complex dynamics at multiple granularities. Moreover, multivariate time series often exhibit strong coupling and complex interactions across sensor channels, such that anomalies may propagate across channels and disrupt dependency structures. To address these challenges, we propose a multivariate time series anomaly detection method based on Multi-scale Representation Contrastive Learning (MsRCL). Specifically, MsRCL performs multi-scale patch decomposition and learns complementary representations from two views, multi-scale intra-patch and multi-scale inter-patch, to capture local dynamics at different temporal scales, cross-segment dependencies, and temporal patterns such as trends and periodicity. In addition, we design a channel-aware attention mechanism that strengthens salient channel correlations and suppresses weakly correlated noise, enabling adaptive modeling of cross-channel dependency structures and improving the representation of cross-channel coupled anomalies. Experiments on five real-world multivariate time series datasets show that MsRCL delivers effective performance gains over the mainstream alternatives.

title: Identification of a natural product derived NaV1.5 sodium channel modulator through integrated machine learning and molecular modeling
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia, and the voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.5 represents a key therapeutic target. However, currently available sodium channel blockers are associated with proarrhythmic liabilities, underscoring the need for safer alternatives. This study aimed to develop an integrated computational framework to identify novel natural product–derived NaV1.5 modulators. A curated dataset of 1512 NaV1.5 inhibitors from ChEMBL was used to train LightGBM, XGBoost, and Random Forest classification models using optimized hybrid feature selection strategies. Model performance was evaluated using scaffold-based splitting and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC). The optimized models were applied to virtually screen 100,404 natural compounds from the COCONUT database. Top-ranked hits were further analyzed using molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM/GBSA binding free energy calculations, and in silico ADMET profiling. The best-performing model (LightGBM) achieved an MCC of 0.66 on the external scaffold-based test set. Virtual screening identified 10 candidate compounds. Among them, Piperaduncin C exhibited favorable docking scores, stable interactions during molecular dynamics simulations, and a more favorable predicted binding free energy compared to quinidine. ADMET analysis suggested comparatively low predicted hERG liability and limited CYP2D6 inhibition. This integrated computational strategy identified Piperaduncin C as a potential NaV1.5 modulator. While experimental validation is required, these findings support its consideration as a natural product–derived scaffold for further antiarrhythmic drug development.

title: Deep learning mitigates batch effects in Raman spectroscopy
abstract: Raman spectroscopy is widely used for its ability to provide rich molecular-level information from biological samples. However, the high sensitivity of Raman spectra can also unintentionally encode extraneous information, such as patient identity, instrument-specific signatures, environmental conditions, and sample handling protocols. This hidden structure, referred to as the batch effect, poses increasing challenges in machine learning applications, where it can lead to model overfitting, poor generalization, and even privacy risks when datasets are shared. In this work, we investigate the presence and impact of the batch effect in a Raman spectroscopy dataset derived from glioma tumor samples. We show that deep learning can accurately predict patient identity from individual spectra, revealing strong bias patterns in the data. To mitigate this issue, we explore several approaches and introduce an algorithmic framework based on adversarial deep learning. Our method effectively reduces the influence of confounding sample-specific signals while preserving information relevant to tumor classification. These findings highlight the need for careful bias control in Raman-based AI pipelines and provide tools to support more robust applications in biomedical spectroscopy.

title: Identification of NUDT6 and LINGO1 as candidate genes for nCRT-associated signatures to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer patients
abstract: Rectal cancer is a highly prevalent cancer worldwide and a common cause of cancer death. Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) is the first choice for advanced rectal cancer. In this study, we used bioinformatics approaches to explore candidate genes affected by nCRT in rectal cancer. A total of 26 samples of rectal cancer patients were collected and divided into the Treatment group (14 patients who received nCRT) and the Control group (12 patients who did not receive nCRT). candidate genes were selected by high-throughput sequencing, differential expression analysis, machine learning algorithms, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and gene expression analysis. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) was used to trace the enrichment pathways of these candidate genes. Additionally, the relationship between immune cells and these candidate genes was explored. A nomogram and molecular regulatory network were constructed based on the selected candidate genes. The quality of sequencing data was high for all samples. Overall, 35 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were discovered. Among them, NUDT6 and LINGO1 were identified as candidate genes with high discriminative ability (both with area under the curve (AUC) > 0.8). A nomogram with satisfactory exploratory performance was constructed. NUDT6 was significantly enriched in the ribosome and oxidative phosphorylation pathways, and was significantly positively correlated with Megakaryocyte-Erythroid Progenitor (MEP) and T helper cell 1 (Th1 cells), and significantly negatively correlated with Myocyte cells. LINGO1 was significantly enriched in the proteasome pathway and significantly positively correlated with Erythrocytes. Additionally, drug prediction analyses indicated that valproic acid was most highly associated with NUDT6, while bisphenol A is most closely linked to LINGO1. In this study, NUDT6 and LINGO1 were identified as potential candidate genes significantly associated with the Treatment group (patients who received nCRT) compared to the Control group (patients who did not). These findings may offer exploratory insights into the molecular correlates of nCRT treatment in rectal cancer. Moreover, as this study relies on a single-center convenience sample, these findings require further validation in multi-center prospective cohorts.

title: AI awareness relates to university students’ boundaryless career through the parallel mediation of intrinsic motivation and future job insecurity
abstract: The in-depth penetration of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has reshaped career forms and the structure of the labor market, exerting a profound impact on university students’ cognition and orientation towards career development. Based on the conservation of resources theory and self-determination theory, we conducted three studies—an experimental study and two survey studies—to explore correlational linkages between AI awareness and university students’ boundaryless career. Studies 1 and 3 consistently demonstrated that AI awareness is indirectly associated with boundaryless career through the parallel mediating pathways of intrinsic motivation and future job insecurity. Study 2 provided experimental evidence that heightened AI awareness increases both intrinsic motivation and future job insecurity. This research enriches the application scenarios of boundaryless career theory in the context of technological change, deepens the understanding of the mechanism linking technological perception to youth career psychology, and offers practical implications for career guidance in universities.

title: Development of an automated method for audiometric data extraction and analysis using voting optical character recognition
abstract: Hearing loss affects over 1.5 billion people worldwide, significantly impacting language development, quality of life, and economic independence. Research on audiometric data, such as pure tone audiometry (PTA), the speech reception threshold (SRT), and the word recognition score (WRS), is essential for understanding and preventing hearing loss. However, this data is frequently stored as image files within electronic medical records (EMRs), thus requiring manual extraction for research use. Manual extraction is time-consuming, costly, and prone to errors, limiting data utility and impeding large-scale data acquisition. In this paper, we propose an automated extraction method for audiometric report images using Tesseract optical character recognition (OCR) and an improved voting OCR (VOCR) algorithm. VOCR mitigates OCR variability by removing symbols (e.g., “dB,” “%”) and using tabulated data, generating multiple OCR candidates per cell and utilizing a voting mechanism to select reliable values. Our results indicate that VOCR achieves an image-level accuracy of 97.60% and high accuracy across all audiometric data categories, including PTA (99.95%), SRT (98.95%), WRS % (98.05%), and WRS stimulus (99.80%). The voting-based accuracy metric allows for the assessment of reliability, enabling a targeted review of areas with low consensus. This method has the potential to be employed in web-based data collection services, supporting real-time, standardized data management and reducing the need for manual extraction, making it a valuable tool for otolaryngological research.

title: Structured human resource development with AI support is associated with higher expert rated recruitment task quality among education graduates
abstract: Graduate employability programmes are usually evaluated with self-report measures. We compared a structured human resource development programme supported by generative AI with career guidance matched on topics, duration and facilitator contact. Twelve intact cohorts of graduates seeking education-sector posts in Guangdong, China (N = 186), were allocated as whole units, six per condition, crossed with institution, facilitator and schedule. Blinded experts gave a global rating (0–100) of recruitment-task materials produced on site, under invigilation and without AI, before and after the programme. Ratings were made without a pre-specified rubric, which limits their interpretation. Among 168 participants with post-test data (overall attrition 9.7%), the adjusted difference favoured the AI-supported programme by 5.38 points (95% CI 2.76 to 8.01; d = 0.60) and was stable across eight specifications. Four new self-report scales showed smaller differences (d = 0.12 to 0.29), none significant after Holm correction; each scale could detect only differences of about d = 0.4. The effect on expert ratings exceeded the mean effect on self-report by 0.37 standard deviations (95% CI 0.10 to 0.63). Component analyses were exploratory. The design cannot separate the contribution of AI from structured practice and feedback.

title: Mapping soil salinity and prediction uncertainty across different depths using quantile regression forests
abstract: Accurate assessment of soil salinity across the soil profile is necessary for sustainable agricultural management, yet conventional surface-based observations often provide limited information about subsurface salinity conditions. This study developed a depth-resolved digital soil mapping framework to predict soil electrical conductivity (EC) across five standard depth intervals (0–25, 25–50, 50–75, 75–100, and 100–125 cm) in Shandong Province, eastern China. A total of 617 soil profiles were used, and continuous profile observations were harmonized into standard layers using equal-area quadratic spline functions. Environmental covariates representing spectral salinity characteristics, vegetation conditions, climate, and terrain attributes were compiled at a 30-m spatial resolution. Principal component analysis was applied to reduce multicollinearity among predictors, and Quantile Regression Forest (QRF) models were implemented to estimate EC and its 90% prediction intervals. Model accuracy was evaluated using repeated 10-fold cross-validation. The results showed a clear decline in predictive performance with increasing depth: the coefficient of determination decreased from 0.79 in the 0–25 cm layer to 0.51 in the 100–125 cm layer, whereas RMSE increased from 0.142 to 0.295 dS m⁻¹. Surface EC predictions were mainly driven by salinity-sensitive spectral indices, including SSIB, CSI, and SC, while the contribution of these variables weakened in deeper layers. Conversely, topographic wetness index, valley depth, relative slope position, and climatic variables became increasingly important below 50 cm, suggesting a shift from predominantly spectral controls near the surface to hydro-topographic and climatic regulation at depth. Higher EC values were generally predicted in the eastern and southeastern parts of the study area, whereas uncertainty was more pronounced in western and central transitional zones. The findings demonstrate the value of integrating depth-specific environmental information with probabilistic machine learning to produce spatially explicit, uncertainty-aware maps of soil salinity for improved monitoring and site-specific land management.
