title: Practical prediction of concrete compressive strength using an interpretable enhanced linear regression model
abstract: Reliable estimation of concrete compressive strength is essential for quality control in civil engineering. While complex machine learning models offer high accuracy, their lack of transparency limits practical adoption. This study develops an interpretable linear regression model in which cement, slag, and fly ash are represented as total binder content and slag-to-binder ratio, raw age is replaced by its natural logarithm, and water-to-cement ratio is retained alongside superplasticizer and aggregate contents. Using a publicly available dataset of 1,030 concrete mixtures, the final model achieved a full-data R 2 of 0.821 and, under nested GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by unique mixture design, a mean outer-fold R 2 of 0.805 (SD = 0.018), RMSE of 7.30 MPa, and MAE of 5.62 MPa. Multicollinearity was controlled, with a maximum variance inflation factor of 6.35 and a condition number of 4.97. All predictors were statistically significant ( p < 0.001), and the maximum Cook’s distance was 0.0217. Benchmarking against tuned Random Forest (nested R 2 = 0.884) and XGBoost (nested R 2 = 0.882) indicated that while ensemble methods offer higher accuracy, the proposed linear model retains interpretable coefficients and provides a transparent screening tool for preliminary strength estimation within the range of the studied dataset.

title: Hybrid local–global vision transformer framework for robust plant disease detection in precision agriculture
abstract: Correctly identifying plant diseases has significant consequences for sustainable agricultural productivity as well as for national and global food security. Even though traditional convolutional neural networks have achieved great success detecting diseases using images, the receptive field is inherently limited which in turn limits the ability simply to model long-range dependencies. However, vision transformers can capture global relationships but often fail to maintain fine-grained local texture information that may be critical for distinguishing subtle symptoms caused by diseases variably. To mitigate these issues, we introduce ViT-LGFNet, a Hybrid Local-Global Fusion Vision Transformer that uses local convolutional feature extraction along with global self-attention encoding. The proposed architecture is built with the following proposed modules: a Local CNN Stem module for learning fine textures followed by a Transformer Encoder module for modeling contextual features. We propose a dual Cross-Attention Fusion Module that performs bi-direction direction exchanges between local and global tokens to increase the discriminative ability for the hybrid representation. The PlantVillage dataset results demonstrate ViT-LGFNet mean validation accuracy of 95.15% ± 0.74 across multiple runs, with a best-case performance of 96.28%. Grad-CAM and Attention Rollout maps were placed for visualization purposes, demonstrating that the model accurately attends to the disease-affected part of an image. The proposed model offers a reliable and explainable benchmark for plant disease recognition and shows potential for application in smart farming systems and AI-based crop health monitoring applications.

title: Identification and validation of key genes related to innate immune cell barrier in type 2 diabetes mellitus: transcriptome and single-cell combined analysis
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) constitutes a significant global public health issue, characterized by insulin resistance and progressive functional decline of pancreatic β-cells. The regulatory role of innate immune cell barrier (ICB)-related genes (ICBRGs) in the progression of T2DM remains unclear. This study aims to identify the key ICBRGs associated with T2DM, elucidate their regulatory mechanisms and clinical significance, and provide molecular targets for precise therapeutic interventions. Initially, T2DM-related transcriptome datasets were downloaded from public databases, with GSE15932 serving as the training set and GSE26168 as the validation set, along with the single-cell dataset GSE268210. Candidate genes were obtained by screening the intersection with ICBRGs through differential expression analysis. Subsequent identification of key genes was conducted using various machine learning algorithms, such as XGBoost and Random Forest (RF). In-depth exploration of gene functions involved immune infiltration analysis, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis, encompassing aspects such as cell communication and pseudotemporal analysis. Finally, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was employed to validate the expression of the identified key genes. Three key genes were successfully identified: CEBPA, ELANE, and TGFB1. Immune infiltration analysis revealed significant correlations of these genes with immune cells, particularly monocytes and CD4 + memory T cells. GSEA results indicated co-enrichment of these genes in critical metabolic pathways, including the insulin signaling pathway. Single-cell analysis confirmed that monocytes play a pivotal role in T2DM, exhibiting the highest communication probability with B cells. Pseudotime analysis demonstrated dynamic expression patterns of the key genes during the differentiation of monocytes. RT-qPCR validation indicated significant upregulation of CEBPA and ELANE in T2DM blood samples, while TGFB1 exhibited an increasing trend that did not reach statistical significance. CEBPA, ELANE, and TGFB1 may contribute to the pathogenesis of T2DM through monocyte-related immune regulation. CEBPA and ELANE demonstrated consistent experimental validation, while TGFB1 is proposed as a candidate biomarker that warrants further confirmation in larger clinical cohorts.

title: Retinal layer thickness prediction from smartphone fundus imaging for early glaucoma detection
abstract: Glaucoma progression leads to the loss of ganglion cells, which results in the thinning of retinal layers. Retinal layer thickness is a biomarker for monitoring glaucoma progression. Glaucoma is detected using the thickness of OCT images based on the RNFL layer and fundus images based on optic nerve damage. Continuous glaucoma monitoring requires both screening methods for effective treatment. However, OCT devices are high-cost, non-portable, require specialized operators, and are susceptible to artifacts and media opacities, which reduce their suitability for routine, large-scale screening, particularly in resource-limited settings. To address this clinical accessibility gap, an MPIML framework is proposed. The framework uses the Glauco Twin dataset, which consists of both fundus and OCT image data features. From the dataset, RNFL layer thickness is predicted from fundus image data features. This method of prediction avoids frequent OCT screening. In this proposed study, a smartphone-based 2D fundus image is used for measuring RNFL thickness. As the current cohort comprises 23 patients, this work is presented as a pilot feasibility study intended to demonstrate technical and clinical feasibility rather than population-level clinical validity. In this study, a multimodal physics-informed machine learning (MPIML) framework is proposed for the measurement of retinal layer thickness. The framework uses (I) the Glauco Twin dataset, which consists of segmented OCT and smartphone-based fundus image features such as structural, vascular, and biomechanical features for the same glaucoma patient's left and right eye. The MPIML framework consists of Segmentation-Modified TransUNet, which segments OCT images with 2-layer boundary segmentation of RNFL and ILM. A Modified SegFormer algorithm segments the optic disc, optic cup, blood vessels, and macula region for estimating indirect RNFL measurements. Finally, the MPIML model is used to classify glaucoma progression as normal, suspect, and glaucoma. The MPIML framework achieves a classification accuracy of about 94.3%, an AUC of 0.95, and RNFL thickness prediction is done for 3.1–3.4 µm length. In this pilot feasibility study, smartphone-based fundus image data with the MPIML model effectively predicts RNFL thickness and improves the detection of early-stage glaucoma progression, motivating a larger, multicenter validation study.

title: The impact of artificial intelligence on corporate innovation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a key driver of technological progress and industrial transformation, yet empirical evidence on how AI promotes corporate innovation remains limited. Using online job posting data of Chinese listed companies from 2014 to 2024, this study constructs a firm-level measure of artificial intelligence and examines its impact on corporate innovation. The results show that artificial intelligence significantly promotes corporate innovation. Further analyses indicate that artificial intelligence enhances corporate innovation by increasing R&D investment and enriching firms’ knowledge diversity, thereby facilitating knowledge creation and knowledge recombination. The positive effect is more pronounced among non-state-owned enterprises and firms operating in non-high-tech industries. Grounded in the knowledge-based view, this study demonstrates how artificial intelligence expands firms’ knowledge bases and promotes knowledge creation and recombination, thereby extending the knowledge-based view of corporate innovation and providing new firm-level evidence on the innovation effects of artificial intelligence.

title: Integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing analysis reveals paraptosis-related biomarkers and immune microenvironment regulation in triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most aggressive subtype of breast cancer with limited targeted therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Paraptosis, a non-apoptotic programmed cell death modality characterized by endoplasmic reticulum dilation and mitochondrial swelling, plays a critical role in tumor suppression and chemosensitivity. However, the molecular mechanism of paraptosis-related genes (PRGs) in TNBC progression and immune microenvironment remodeling remains poorly defined. As a pivotal calcium release channel on ER, ITPR3 is speculated to participate in endoplasmic reticulum stress and paraptosis execution, but its diagnostic value and regulatory role in TNBC have not been systematically elucidated. Two TNBC datasets were downloaded from the GEO database. PRGs were intersected with TNBC differentially expressed genes, and six hub genes were screened using random forest, SVM-RFE and multivariate logistic regression. ROC curve, nomogram, calibration curve and decision curve analysis were applied to evaluate the diagnostic value of hub genes. Furthermore, external validation in the independent TCGA-TNBC cohort was performed to further verify the robustness and diagnostic efficacy of this six-gene diagnostic model. Consensus clustering was used to classify TNBC into subtypes, followed by immune infiltration and inflammatory cytokine correlation analysis. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was performed to identify key modules and perform Gene Ontology (GO) / Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis. Single-cell transcriptomics was used to explore the cell-type-specific expression patterns of ITPR3 . We used the TIMER and HPA databases to verify the mRNA and protein expression levels of ITPR3 across pan-cancers and breast tissues. Finally, qRT-PCR, CCK-8 and EdU assays were conducted to verify the expression and biological function of ITPR3 in TNBC cells. A total of 13 differentially expressed PRGs were identified, and six hub genes including ITPR3 , CASP3 , CCR4 , CDKN3 , LPAR1 and MYLK were finally screened. The six hub genes and the combined diagnostic model exhibited satisfactory diagnostic performance. TNBC was divided into two distinct subtypes with significant differences in clinical features, immune cell infiltration and inflammatory cytokine levels. WGCNA identified two core modules closely correlated with subtypes, which were enriched in cell cycle, DNA replication, p53 signaling pathway and platinum drug resistance. Single-cell analysis confirmed that ITPR3 was highly expressed in tumor epithelial cells. In vitro experiments confirmed that ITPR3 was highly expressed in TNBC cell lines, and knockdown of ITPR3 markedly inhibited cell proliferation. This study reveals the expression characteristics and immune regulatory roles of hub PRGs in TNBC. The constructed diagnostic model has good predictive value, and TNBC subtypes present obvious heterogeneity in clinical and immune landscapes. ITPR3 is upregulated in TNBC and can promote tumor cell proliferation, which may serve as a candidate diagnostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target for TNBC.

title: Language-based assessments for experienced well-being: accuracy and external validity across behaviors, traits, and states
abstract: While language is central to human communication, psychological science has relied on self-reported rating scales for decades because it was difficult to quantify language effectively. Large language models (LLMs) have changed that in recent years. Here, we used LLMs with machine learning to compare traditional ratings against language-based responses (short essays and descriptive words) of experienced well-being over 12 weeks from 764 individuals from an overburdened population highly exposed to emotional experience, U.S. hospitality workers. While accuracies were comparable by internal criterion (across 9 affective traits; words r = .53 vs. .51 for ratings), both language formats doubled the ratings’ accuracy (up to r = .18 and .24 for words and essays, respectively) across 24 external criteria: traits, demographics, and behavior. Beyond improved accuracy, language responses offered psychological insights: words provided concise emotional nuances, whereas essays encompassed broad life contexts. Though each language-based format differed in strengths and weaknesses, both demonstrated greater information-richness than traditional rating scales.

title: Process effect prediction method based on visual generative models
abstract: This study aims to develop a conditional visual generation model that maps process-structure relationships, generating scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of metallographic microstructures under specified conditions based on input process parameters for process improvement reference. The Omni-loss is used to optimize the conditional discriminator/generator. A MAE-CGAN model was proposed to demonstrate the fidelity of generated microstructures and their correlation with applied processing methods. The model integrating visual transformer and Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGAN) offers several advantages: the CGAN framework theoretically supports modeling any material system; trained generators can produce specific microstructure images under designated process conditions. And the prediction datasets are evaluated using quantitative indicators proposed in previous work. The results showed that the pre-trained Masked Auto-Encoder (MAE) model demonstrated robust critical structural feature extraction capabilities with the relatively small image dataset. The quantitative analysis of existing samples yielded results consistent with the expert evaluations, and the generated samples hold great potential for guiding future experimental settings.

title: Design and implementation of an automated Drosophila locomotor assay using computer vision tracking
abstract: Drosophila has long served as a powerful model for investigating locomotor behavior, using geotaxis assays to generate valuable insights into genetics, aging, and neurobiology. Nonetheless, its use has been constrained by subjective scoring, modest throughput, and challenges in reproducibility. We developed and validated an integrated hardware–software platform that enables automated, high-resolution locomotor analysis across 12 vials in parallel. The system integrates 3D-printed mechanical components, Raspberry Pi–based video acquisition, and programmable environmental controls to ensure standardized conditions. A deep learning pipeline segments vials with near-perfect accuracy (IoU > 0.95), while computer vision algorithms quantify climbing trajectories, velocity, and positional zone occupancy at 60 frames per second. The end-to-end workflow converts raw video into time-resolved metrics, supports sex-specific aggregation, and incorporates advanced statistical analyses, including Linear Mixed Effects regression, harmonic mean p-values, and Mann–Whitney U tests. Relative to manual scoring, this automated pipeline yields 2.8-fold faster processing and about 800-fold higher data density. Application of the platform uncovered reproducible phenotypes of multiple genotypes. For example, in circadian Clock out mutation, males displayed progressive climbing deficits with age, whereas females maintained age-resilient trajectories. Moreover, male Clock out exhibited a reduced locomotor performance compared to age-matched control ( w 1118 ) males; however, female Clock out showed subtle reduction in locomotor performance. Additionally, glial-specific knockdown of PolG , encoding the DNA polymerase gamma catalytic subunit, revealed striking sex-dimorphic aging patterns: females outperformed controls at older age in Glaz-driven line and at younger age in Elav-driven line, while males exhibited a marked decline. To promote broad adoption, a user-friendly Python interface (Tkinter GUI) enables accessibility independent of computational expertise. Collectively, this standardized, high-throughput framework advances the resolution of genotype-, age, and sex-dependent locomotor dynamics, offering new opportunities in aging, circadian biology, and neurodegeneration research.

title: A machine learning framework for solar cell design optimization and efficiency prediction
abstract: This study applies machine learning (ML) to the design of tin-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs) to reduce dependence on exhaustive device simulation. Ten regression algorithms were trained on 4428 SCAPS-1D simulations covering 27 device architectures, predicting efficiency (η), open-circuit voltage (V OC ), short-circuit current density (J SC ) and fill factor (FF) from the absorber, electron and hole transport layer materials, absorber thickness, and band-edge densities of states. CatBoost performed best, reaching R 2 of 0.999990 and RMSE of 0.0126% points for η on a random 80:20 split. Accuracies of this kind are common in this literature, so we examined what they measure. The dataset is a dense sweep of a deterministic solver, so random partitioning, including ten-fold cross-validation, leaves near-identical configurations on both sides of the split. Withholding whole architectures raised the error by one to two orders of magnitude. The models are therefore reliable for interpolation within characterised architectures, not for extrapolation to unseen ones. Training on random subsets showed that 480 simulations, 10.8% of the grid, recovered the correct architecture and the optimum in all ten repeats. The best configuration, FASnI 3 with SnO 2 and Cu 2 O at 660 nm, reaches 28.87% efficiency (V OC 1.086 V, J SC 30.01 mA cm⁻², FF 88.55%).

title: Integrated experimental and machine learning analysis of nano-MQL assisted turning of AA7075-T6
abstract: This study comprehensively investigates the machinability performance of dry cutting, minimum quantity lubrication (MQL), and nanoparticle-modified minimum quantity lubrication (nano-MQL) methods in turning AA7075-T6 aluminum alloy. Tool wear mechanisms were evaluated using SEM/EDS analyses; surface roughness, cutting forces, and energy consumption were compared under different cutting parameters. In addition, the obtained data were predicted and evaluated using machine learning-based correlation maps and random forest models. The results demonstrated that the cutting environment plays a decisive role in machining performance. The nano-MQL application reduced the build-up edge (BUE) height at the cutting edge by approximately 29% compared to dry cutting and presented a more stable wear morphology compared to MQL. Surface roughness values ​​were measured at their lowest levels under nano-MQL conditions for all cutting parameters; an improvement of 12–20% compared to dry cutting and 3–10% compared to MQL was achieved. The cutting forces were reduced by an average of 8–19% in the nano-MQL environment compared to dry cutting, while energy consumption savings ranged from 10–53%. The nano-MQL strategy demonstrated high performance and energy efficiency in turning AA7075-T6 alloy by reducing tool wear, improving surface quality, and lowering cutting forces and energy consumption.

title: Structured generative AI preparation and classroom belonging in a six-class randomized trial
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may support independent preparation without necessarily strengthening students’ connections to the classroom. We examined a structured instructional protocol combining AI exploration, confidence reflection, unresolved question generation, and instructor responsiveness. Following baseline assessment, six intact undergraduate class sections at one Chinese university were randomized equally, with three sections and 110 students assigned to each condition. Assessments were conducted in Weeks 1, 6, and 12, and the intervention began in Week 2. Recomputed item means were analyzed using equally weighted section-level contrasts with four degrees of freedom, supplemented by exact randomization tests. At Week 12, the between-condition difference in classroom belonging change was 0.361 (95% CI 0.145 to 0.576; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.029). The corresponding differences were 0.282 for emotional engagement, − 0.497 for reactance to teacher guidance, and − 15.24 points for the confidence–performance discrepancy index (CPDI). Exact two-sided randomization p values were 0.100 for all primary contrasts, the minimum attainable with six balanced sections. Exploratory individual-level pathway and effect-modification analyses were treated as hypothesis-generating because only six sections were observed and the pathway estimates were sensitive to measurement timing. Overall, the structured protocol showed promising differences in classroom belonging and related outcomes, but inference remains limited by the small number of randomized sections, parametric model assumptions, and the preliminary discrepancy measure. The findings therefore concern the combined instructional protocol rather than an isolated effect of GenAI or an established psychological mechanism.

title: RNA processing factors are associated with microglial heterogeneity and intercellular communication in ischemic stroke
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and long-term disability globally, with dysregulated RNA processing implicated in its pathogenesis. This study aimed to identify the key genes associated with RNA processing factors (RNAPF) in IS using integrated transcriptomic analyses. Microarray data from human blood (GSE16561 and GSE58294) and single-cell RNA sequencing data from mouse brain tissue (GSE174574) were analyzed. Candidate genes were screened via differential expression analysis and intersected with RNAPF-related genes. Machine learning algorithms identified feature genes, followed by diagnostic validation and functional characterization. Immune infiltration was characterized at the transcriptomic level, whereas cellular heterogeneity was examined at single-cell resolution. To avoid pseudoreplication, all statistical inferences from single-cell data were elevated to the biological replicate level (n = 3 per group). Cell type and microglial subtype proportions were compared using sample-aggregated Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Using RT-qPCR technology, we conducted a preliminary assessment of expression differences in key genes in a small-scale clinical sample set (n = 5 per group), providing preliminary support for this bioinformatics finding. A total of 12 candidate RNA processing-related genes were identified, with RNASEL and SRPK1 established as potentially key genes via machine learning and validation cohorts. A nomogram integrating both genes demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy. Functional enrichment linked key genes to neuroinflammation pathways, such as Toll-like receptor and chemokine signaling. Immune dysregulation was observed, with RNASEL/SRPK1 positively correlating with M0 macrophages and neutrophils. Single-cell analysis revealed microglia as a cell type of interest. At the sample level (n = 3 per group), microglia showed a decreasing trend in IS (24.40% vs. 21.51%,). Microglial subtype analysis revealed a marked reduction in MG_Homeostatic_Slc2a5 (88.50% → 15.60%) and significant expansion of MG_IEG_Egr1 (3.75% → 46.74%) and MG_Postnatal-PAM_Spp1 (0.05% → 21.22%) in IS. Pseudobulk DESeq2 analysis demonstrated that RNASEL was significantly downregulated (log2FC = − 1.127, padj < 0.001) while SRPK1 was significantly upregulated (log2FC = 0.599, padj < 0.001) in IS microglia. Cell–cell communication analysis highlighted enhanced monocyte–microglia interactions. RT-qPCR analysis in a small but clinically characterized cohort (n = 5 per group) preliminarily supported the key gene-expression patterns observed in the bioinformatics analyses, although these findings require validation in larger cohorts. RNASEL and SRPK1 may serve as candidate RNAPFs whose altered expression is associated with immune dysregulation and microglial reprogramming in IS. Microglial subtype-specific changes and altered intercellular communication networks provide hypotheses for further mechanistic investigation.

title: Predicting hypertension risk using machine learning, deep learning, and quantum neural network models: a comparative evaluation
abstract: Hypertension is a major public health problem and an important risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Early identification of patients at risk of hypertension can support timely prevention and clinical assessment. This study developed and compared statistical, machine learning, deep learning, and quantum neural network (QNN) models for hypertension prediction using clinical data from 624 patients at District Headquarters Hospital, Faisalabad, Pakistan. The proposed framework involved data preprocessing, K-nearest neighbor imputation, chi-square-based feature selection, feature scaling, and synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) for class balancing. Logistic regression was used as a statistical reference, while SVM, random forest, XGBoost, Naive Bayes, ANN, SVM with PCA, DNN, and QNN were evaluated. Stratified 10-fold cross-validation was used to assess model performance using accuracy, F-measure, AUC, precision, recall, specificity, and maximum probability of correct decision (MPCD). The DNN model achieved the highest accuracy (95.77%), while the QNN achieved the highest AUC (95.40%), precision (96.26%), and recall (94.76%). Naive Bayes showed the lowest accuracy (83.40%). The QNN was included as an exploratory hybrid quantum-classical approach using a simulated quantum circuit, and the results do not imply a quantum advantage over classical models. Overall, the evaluated models showed promising predictive performance for hypertension classification in the study population. Further evaluation using independent populations, external validation, and prospective clinical studies is needed before considering their use in routine clinical practice.

title: Predicting 1-year outcomes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction from preoperative physical performance using machine learning: an exploratory study
abstract: This study aimed to develop machine learning (ML) models to predict 1-year outcomes after primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) using preoperative variables. A retrospective cohort of 75 patients who underwent ACLR between 2016 and 2023 was analyzed. Preoperative features included demographic characteristics, treatment-related variables, isokinetic muscle performance, and patient-reported outcome measures. One-year outcomes were defined as return to pivoting sports (RTS; Tegner activity level ≥ 6) and achievement of the patient acceptable symptom state (PASS; International Knee Documentation Committee score ≥ 75.9). Variables identified in univariable logistic regression were used for ML model development. Multiple algorithms were trained and evaluated using 3-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and Brier scores. Among the models, the random forest algorithm demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.832 for RTS and 0.815 for PASS. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified younger age and greater preoperative flexor strength of the uninvolved limb as the most important predictors. In this exploratory study, ML models incorporating preoperative clinical and physical performance variables showed promising potential for predicting 1-year outcomes after ACLR. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and lack of external validation. The models should therefore be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than ready for clinical implementation, and require further validation in larger, independent cohorts. Key Terms : anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, machine learning, RTS, patient acceptable symptom state.

title: Anatomy-guided U-Net deep learning for sparse-view chest CT reconstruction using spatially varying RTV regularization
abstract: Sparse-view computed tomography (CT) reconstruction remains a challenging inverse problem due to severe undersampling artifacts, noise amplification, and the difficulty of preserving anatomical structures while reducing image degradation. Conventional regularization-based methods often require manual parameter adjustment and rely on spatially uniform priors, whereas deep learning approaches may provide limited interpretability or insufficient integration of physical constraints. In this study, we propose SvRTV-UNet, a physics-guided deep learning framework that integrates a U-Net architecture with spatially variant Relative Total Variation (SvRTV) regularization for adaptive sparse-view chest CT reconstruction. The proposed framework simultaneously performs anatomical segmentation and predicts reconstruction parameters, including the regularization strength (λ) and tissue-specific weighting parameters (A 1 and A 2 ), directly from image quality characteristics. A homoscedastic uncertainty-based multi-task learning strategy is employed to automatically balance segmentation, parameter estimation, and reconstruction objectives without manual loss weighting. In addition, anatomy-aware confidence maps derived from segmentation accuracy and edge information enable tissue-dependent regularization for improved structural preservation. Compared with conventional iterative reconstruction methods, model-based regularization approaches, and representative deep learning methods, SvRTV-UNet demonstrated improved reconstruction performance across quantitative metrics. The quantitative and qualitative results obtained demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared with the evaluated approaches. By integrating physics-based constraints with anatomy-guided adaptive regularization, SvRTV-UNet offers an interpretable framework that adapts to varying acquisition conditions without view-specific retraining.

title: Aerodynamic optimization of Gurney flap parameters for a Formula 1 wing using experimental and coupled GA-ANN-CFD methods
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive numerical and experimental investigation of the aerodynamic performance of Gurney flaps applied to an inverted multi-element airfoil representative of a Formula 1 front wing. A coupled Genetic Algorithm & Artificial Neural Network & Computational Fluid Dynamics (GA-ANN-CFD) framework is developed and applied to a three-element airfoil at a Reynolds number of 500 × 10 3 . Four baseline configurations, defined by flap orientation (vertical and surface-normal) and geometry (solid and slotted), are independently optimized, yielding eight optimal designs. The results demonstrate that flap height is the dominant parameter governing downforce generation, with maximum-height configurations increasing downforce by up to 11.24%, albeit with a moderate reduction in aerodynamic efficiency. In contrast, smaller-height slotted configurations provide a more favorable balance between downforce and drag. The experimental investigation evaluates nine Gurney flap geometries, combining three heights (1.5%, 3%, and 5% chord) and three installation angles (54°, 72°, and 90°), over Reynolds numbers ranging from 250 × 10 3 to 500 × 10 3 . Surface pressure measurements and wake velocity profiles reveal that increasing flap height significantly enhances pressure differentials and wake momentum deficit, leading to higher downforce. Overall, the results identify flap height as the primary design parameter governing downforce generation, while installation angle and slotting provide secondary control over aerodynamic efficiency and wake characteristics.

title: CAT-GAN-UKF: uncertainty-aware spatiotemporal reconstruction for resilient urban air-quality monitoring under partial observability
abstract: Urban air-quality monitoring networks are inherently incomplete: measurements disappear intermittently, sustained outages occur, and the reliability of the remaining evidence changes with pollutant, location, temporal regime, and network state. We present CAT-GAN-UKF, an uncertainty-aware framework for multivariate reconstruction under partial observability that combines nonlinear spatiotemporal state propagation, adversarial learning of context-dependent uncertainty, and masked recursive Bayesian updating. Pollutant-specific conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial networks with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) are trained on signed empirical process- and observation-residual distributions derived exclusively from the chronological training period. Monte Carlo variance of generated residuals defines time-varying diagonal \(Q_t\) and \(R_t\) , which are injected into a nonlinear network UKF. The primary model uses causal temporal, lagged, rolling, missingness, and spatial context; temperature and humidity are evaluated only in a sensitivity analysis because they did not improve reconstruction in this benchmark. The evaluation uses 153,260 hourly station-time records from an OpenAQ-derived 2024 New York City metropolitan-area dataset. After predefined quality control, 27 of 33 monitoring locations were retained. All learned parameters are fitted on training data only; a separate validation interval is used for pollutant-specific multiplicative interval calibration, and the held-out test period is never used for fitting or calibration. Robustness is assessed under four random-masking levels, four contiguous outage lengths, and an empirical-gap replay protocol whose outage-length distribution is learned from naturally occurring training-period gaps. Each stress test is repeated over 30 masking seeds. CAT-GAN-UKF is compared with matched linear KF, fixed-covariance UKF and heuristic adaptive UKF baselines, as well as Extra Trees, random forest, histogram gradient boosting, multilayer perceptron, ridge, lasso, persistence, and temporal means. CAT-GAN-UKF significantly improves RMSE over adaptive UKF in seven of nine scenarios, linear KF in all nine, Extra Trees in all nine, and persistence in eight of nine after Holm correction. Relative to a strong fixed-covariance UKF, point-estimation accuracy is generally comparable rather than uniformly superior; however, CAT-GAN-UKF reduces average 95% interval width by approximately 38% across the nine scenarios while retaining mean empirical coverage near 95%. Spatial coupling is the dominant structural contribution: removing it increases RMSE by approximately 5.9% under 10% random masking and by 42.7% under a 24-hour outage. Conversely, adding meteorological covariates worsens RMSE throughout the sensitivity analysis. These findings establish an uncertainty-efficient research framework for spatial reconstruction under degraded sensing; real-time latency, memory use, and resource-constrained deployment feasibility were not evaluated.

title: Shapley-guided token pruning for real-time remote sensing scene classification on edge devices
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) excel at remote sensing scene classification, but the quadratic cost of self-attention hinders real-time inference on edge platforms such as on-board satellite and UAV payloads. Token pruning accelerates ViTs, yet mainstream methods rank tokens by attention scores, whose reliability is contested, so aggressive pruning may discard predictively important patches. We instead adopt the axiomatically grounded Shapley contribution as the pruning criterion. To keep its exponential cost out of inference, Shapley values are estimated offline as supervision, and a lightweight head (about 0.10 M parameters) is trained through ranking distillation to reproduce their ranking, so the deployed path performs no Shapley computation; pruning is hierarchical (layers 4/7/10) with a calibrated early-exit recalibrated after pruning. On NWPU-RESISC45 (DeiT-S backbone), the criterion learned by this head follows the offline Shapley ranking more faithfully than attention does (Spearman rho = 0.641 vs. 0.401), with a higher Insertion AUC and a lower Deletion AUC. On a Jetson Orin Nano with TensorRT, latency and per-image energy fall by 24.18% and 32.27% versus the unpruned model. Accuracy at 0.7 retention is 93.04%, 0.53% points above attention pruning; however, with only three paired seeds this comparison is marginal (paired t-test, p = 0.067), and an observed-effect diagnostic power calculation gives only 0.51 at alpha = 0.05. Accordingly, no statistically decisive accuracy improvement is claimed. The contribution is therefore framed as a more faithful pruning criterion and a favourable accuracy-latency trade-off under a single-backbone, single-remote-sensing-benchmark setting, rather than as a general accuracy advantage.

title: Switching thermal cycle modulation and cycle feature fusion for mixed gas concentration prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of methane and acetylene concentrations supports insulation condition assessment and fault diagnosis in power equipment. Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors offer compact, low-cost sensing, but cross-sensitivity limits their accuracy in mixed-gas concentration prediction. To improve prediction accuracy while simplifying temperature modulation hardware, a Switching Thermal Cycle Modulation (STCM) device and a Cycle Feature Fusion Network (CFFNet) are developed. STCM uses a timer-based circuit to periodically switch the sensor heaters on and off, producing temperature variations that induce periodic changes in gas response waveforms. CFFNet uses cycle means and fixed cosine projections to represent response intensity and waveform shape, respectively, and a Transformer encoder to model their temporal relationships across cycles during gas exposure and recovery. Performance was evaluated using nested leave-one-batch-out cross-validation on STCM and constant-temperature (CT) datasets, each comprising five acquisition batches. On the STCM dataset, CFFNet achieved mean coefficients of determination (R 2 ) of 0.9973 for methane and 0.9974 for acetylene, outperforming all four baseline models on this metric for both gases. Compared with CT, STCM improved concentration prediction accuracy across all evaluated models, demonstrating the value of modulation-induced response information for distinguishing gas concentrations. Ablation experiments supported the complementary roles of cycle mean and shape features, with cross-cycle temporal modeling providing a greater improvement in methane prediction. These results support combining simplified temperature modulation with cycle feature modeling to improve gas concentration prediction under the evaluated conditions.

title: Evaluating the real-world accessibility of open-source deep learning models for retinal vessel segmentation in optical coherence tomography angiography
abstract: Accurate segmentation of retinal vasculature in optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) images underpins disease diagnosis and monitoring. While numerous open-source segmentation algorithms are available, an optimal solution remains elusive. This study evaluates and compares the real-world usability and performance of open-source deep learning-based vessel segmentation models across a diverse dataset comprising healthy and diseased eyes. The selected models are standardised in training and performance settings. Model usability is assessed against a range of software engineering criteria defined by the International Organisation for Standardisation. Performance is evaluated on the publicly available OCTA-500 and ROSE-1 datasets using the Dice coefficient of similarity (Dice) and Intersection over Union (IoU). We show that, within the evaluated sample, considerable variability exists in the quality and usability of open-source models, which may limit the practical integration and adoption of some tools within clinical research workflows. Common shortcomings include incomplete or missing dependency documentation, limited portability across systems, hard-coded file paths, and missing scripts or modules. Among the reviewed models, FRNet most closely met the requirements of international software engineering quality standards. In addition to its strong usability profile, FRNet consistently achieved high Dice and IoU across all evaluated datasets. Beyond identifying a reliable OCTA vessel segmentation model, this study highlights a gap between open-source development practices and their practical use in clinical research. While open-source frameworks support reproducibility and translation, explicit usability and quality criteria are needed to ensure real-world adoption.

title: CBAT-Net: a unified CNN–BiLSTM–MultiHead transformer architecture for joint Q3/Q8 protein secondary structure prediction
abstract: Protein Secondary Structure Prediction (PSSP) remains one of the core challenges in computational biology relevant to a variety of important applications such as drug design, protein engineering and understanding of disease mechanisms. Although some recent deep learning methods have shown remarkable performance, the simultaneous prediction of the 3-state (Q3) and 8-state (Q8) secondary structure with high accuracy is not achieved yet. A novel unified architecture of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks (BiLSTM) and Multi-Head Transformer mechanisms is demonstrated to effectively predict the Q3/Q8 protein secondary structure together. Our architecture is based on a hierarchical structure that combines features extracted by layers of attention mechanisms. We obtain full mathematical models for gradient flow optimization, and present a new dual-task loss function with adaptive weights. The performance of CBAT-Net is tested on benchmark datasets (CB513, CASP12, CASP13, CASP14 and TS115); it outperforms the existing methods by 23.8% and 4.7% in Q3 and Q8 accuracy (Q3 = 86.71%, Q8 = 78.42% on CB513), respectively. The performance is confirmed as better by the statistical significance test ( p < 0.001). Ablation studies have shown that the whole architectural composition has a significant impact on the final performance. CBAT-Net is an important improvement in the field of protein secondary structure prediction that shows that it is possible to successfully learn both local and global information from a protein sequence with hybrid architectures that indicate suitable inductive bias. It discusses Hyper Learning, deep learning architecture, convolutional neural network, bidirectional LSTM, multi-head attention, Transformer architecture, features of the dataset, and Protein Secondary Structure Prediction.

title: An explainable hybrid transformer–CNN framework for multi-class brain tumor classification from MRI images
abstract: The identification of brain tumors through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) requires effective methods that provide precise results because these results determine clinical choices. The study presents a classification system based on hybrid Transformer-CNN technology which classifies brain tumors into multiple types by using tumor segmentation and deep feature extraction and explainable artificial intelligence. The preprocessing of MRI images involves several steps which include skull stripping and CLAHE-based contrast enhancement and normalization and data augmentation and resizing to create high-quality images that maintain uniformity for model input. The TransUNet architecture performs tumor region segmentation by integrating convolutional neural networks with transformer-based attention systems which enable it to recognize both nearby and distant contextual details. The system generates segmentation masks which enable region-of-interest (ROI) feature extraction through DenseNet121 that has been pretrained on ImageNet while the final classification layer gets removed and global average pooling produces discriminative feature representations. The system uses an attention-based feature refinement method to improve feature representation followed by a regularized fully connected deep classifier which includes batch normalization and dropout for four-class classification of tumors. Model interpretability is achieved using Grad-CAM++ and attention visualization, enabling clear identification of tumor-related regions and improving model transparency. Experimental evaluation demonstrates high classification performance, achieving accuracies of 98.54% for meningioma, 98.65% for glioma, 99.45% for pituitary tumors, and 99.56% for no-tumor cases. These results indicate that presented TransUNet–DenseNet121 approach offers an accurate, reliable, interpretable method for detection of brain tumors automatically from MRI scanned images.

title: Integrated oculomics and lipidomics characterise cross-sectional retinal–lipidomic associations in a generally healthy biobank population
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading global cause of mortality, yet current risk stratification methods may fail to capture early, subclinical vascular changes. Previous studies have rarely integrated retinal microvascular characteristics with comprehensive serum lipidomic profiles as potential indicators of cardiovascular health. In this study, we applied an imaging–omics framework that combines deep learning-derived retinal microvascular traits with serum lipidomic data to explore retinal-lipidomic association patterns using higher-dimensional serum lipidomic profiling alongside quantitative retinal vascular phenotypes. To our knowledge, this represents one of the first large-scale, covariate-adjusted correlation analyses of retinal microvascular phenotypes and serum lipidomics in a generally healthy biobank population. Retinal phenotypes were quantified using automated image analysis tools, while serum lipid profiling was performed using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with electrospray ionisation high-resolution mass spectrometry. Modest but statistically significant age- and sex-adjusted partial correlations were observed, particularly between average artery width, vessel density, and lipid subclasses such as triacylglycerols, diacylglycerols, and ceramides. These relationships are biologically plausible in the context of microvascular–metabolic remodelling but should be interpreted as exploratory association signals rather than evidence of causality or clinical prediction. By linking quantitative retinal vascular phenotypes to annotated serum lipidomic features, this study characterises retinal–lipidomic association patterns relevant to microvascular–metabolic variation. This integration provides an imaging–omics workflow for identifying candidate association signals that connect automated retinal vascular phenotypes with circulating molecular profiles. Future longitudinal and outcome-linked studies will be important to assess the temporal stability and clinical relevance of these association patterns.

title: A novel LLM-based GPT-neo transformer with machine learning architecture for promoters prediction in Agrobacterium
abstract: Promoters are vital for the initiation of gene transcription, and their accurate uncovering in bacterial genomes is crucial for the progression of genetic and biotechnological research. This research introduces an innovative approach for detecting promoters in Agrobacterium tumefaciens, integrating a large language model (LLM)-based GPT-Neo transformer with Random Forest (RF) feature engineering and traditional machine learning methodologies. The GPT-Neo model was initially used to tokenize nucleotide sequences and produce high-dimensional embeddings that include the structural and interactional characteristics of promoter regions. The embeddings function as input for the RF classifier, which conducts probabilistic feature extraction to provide augmented feature vectors, therefore enhancing the model’s prediction capabilities. The integration of LLM-based feature extraction with RF feature engineering results in substantial performance enhancements, with the model attaining an accuracy of 97% and an AUC of 0.99, surpassing conventional methods. Furthermore, the use of the Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) rectifies class imbalances, hence providing equitable sensitivity and specificity. This methodology signifies a considerable progress in promoter prediction, providing a solid foundation for prospective applications in bacterial genomics and bioinformatics.

title: Zhixin: dataset construction and instruction fine-tuning for LLM-based mental disorder diagnosis
abstract: Automatic diagnosis of mental disorder from chief complaints is an appealing but challenging task. Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown rich knowledge and strong reasoning ability in medical domain. However, mental disorder diagnosis based on chief complaints requires highly specialised knowledge. Lack of corresponding resources hinders LLMs performance on this task. To address this problem, we collect 6,780 complaint-diagnosis pairs spanning 29 different types of mental disorders from a specialized hospital as the dataset. Meanwhile we conduct detailed data cleansing and manual proofreading to protect the privacy. On this basis, we propose the model named Zhixin , a LLM for mental disorder diagnosis fine-tuned on the proposed dataset. The experimental results show that Zhixin outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of automatic evaluation. It surpasses 3-shot DeepSeek-R1 by 18.54 \(\%\) on Overall Accuracy . Meanwhile, human evaluation results show that the generated response from Zhixin ensures the Accuracy , Safety and Professionalism , which are critical to the diagnosis of mental disorder. In-depth analysis of category-wise performance sheds light on the future research direction, suggesting the focus on relatively rare metal disorders.

title: Artifact-resilient deep learning segmentation for enhanced structural and functional cardiac analysis
abstract: Cardiac imaging is essential in diagnosing heart disease. Imaging methods like x-rays, ultrasound, computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can show the heart in great detail. Given AI’s superior learning capabilities, these imaging approaches can be greatly improved. It is critical to use methods that can withstand artifacts in cardiac MRI when segmenting the ventricle in order to guarantee accurate structural and functional investigation of those tissues. While many have focused on making algorithms better, very few have addressed the problem of artifacts in predictions and how they affect accuracy. To make earlier techniques more resistant to these phenomena, we investigate pretrained network fine-tuning in this work. Our suggested approach makes heavy use of data augmentations designed to resemble such objects. The findings significantly improved the baseline segmentations, with improvements up to 0.06 Dice score and 4 mm Hausdorff distance. Our proposed process consists of three steps: resampling and preprocessing of data and performing normalisation; loading and setting training parameters of a pretrained model; training the loaded model with the data, which is augmented by modifying it in various ways according to intensity and deformations.The 3D data is called volumes, and the pictures are the short-axis slices. We used 3D for data resampling, preprocessing, and normalization, and we used slices for data augmentation. During the segmentation job, our technique primarily focuses on fine-tuning an encoder. We resampled the volumes after orienting them to the canonical orientation. The area of interest was subsequently treated with a crop. After then, the data was divided into two parts: training and validation. Out of the total individuals, 20% were used for validation. Secondly, a histogram was generated from the training data and used to standardize the intensity. Using the aforementioned histogram, we standardize all sets. The data used in our research came from the Extreme Cardiac MRI Analysis Challenge, specifically the Respiratory Motion subset. The results showed a group of five people using the same four breathing intensity throughout the assessment. The ED and ES phases were recorded and labeled by a skilled radiologist for all individuals and breathing intensity.

title: Predicting fluorinated gas solubility in deep eutectic solvents using machine learning and deep learning approaches
abstract: This paper introduces a data-driven framework by deploying machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) architectures to estimate fluorinated gas (F-gas) absorption capacities in deep eutectic solvents (DESs). The proposed approach aims to support the screening and design of DESs for gas capture applications by correlating thermodynamic and molecular descriptors with experimentally measured solubility data. Four predictive models, namely Gradient Boosting (GBoost) and Random Forest (RF) as ML techniques, and TabNet and GrowNet as DL architectures, were developed and compared using a dataset of 440 experimental data points, incorporating temperature, pressure, and critical molecular descriptors of both F-gases and DESs as input parameters. Further evaluation was conducted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis and the leverage approach. DL models, especially GrowNet, demonstrated high accuracy and strong generalization on test data. GrowNet outperformed all others, achieving the lowest test errors (MSE = 0.0046%, R² = 0.9985). SHAP analysis revealed pressure and temperature as the most important variables affecting the model predictions, with critical temperature and acentric factor of F-gases also playing significant secondary roles. The leverage method confirmed model reliability, with over 98% of data points lying within its applicability domain. The results demonstrate that ML- and DL-based methods can provide effective predictive tools for estimating F-gas solubility in DES systems.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influential indicators of coupling coordination between new quality productive forces and high–quality development of the construction industry
abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s ‘Dual Carbon’ goals and the strategic opportunity to develop new quality productive forces (NQPF), coordinated development between NQPF and the high-quality development of the construction industry (HQDCI) has emerged as an important pathway toward regional sustainability. This study examines the coupling coordination degree (CCD) between NQPF and HQDCI across 30 Chinese provinces from 2014 to 2023 and constructs comprehensive evaluation systems for both subsystems. The combined weighting-TOPSIS method is used to measure their development levels. By integrating the CCD model, exploratory spatial data analysis (ESDA), random forest (RF) and SHAP interpretation, this study evaluates coordination levels, reveals spatiotemporal patterns, and identifies influential indicators and regional differences in their model-based contributions. The CCD increased from 0.352 (mild imbalance) in 2014 to 0.453 (near imbalance) in 2023 and displayed an ‘east-high, west-low’ spatial pattern. Moran’s I showed strengthening spatial agglomeration, particularly after 2021. LISA analysis indicated a persistent High-High cluster in the Yangtze River Delta and Low-Low clusters in parts of western China. The RF results show that the ten most influential indicators (e.g., robot installation density, per capita number of patents, number of urban bridges, and technology market turnover) collectively explain 76.69% of the total feature importance. Regional SHAP analysis further uncovers heterogeneous mechanisms: eastern regions rely on intelligent infrastructure integration, central regions on economic scale leveraging scientific-educational resources, western regions require endogenous R&D investment and digital infrastructure and northeastern regions prioritize connotative urban renewal.

title: Hybrid feature pyramid attention and capsule network (FpaNet+CapsNet) for enhanced spatial and contextual feature extraction for improved brain tumor segmentation
abstract: Gliomas are among the most dangerous brain tumors, and their treatment depends on accurately outlining the tumor in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). These outlines are hand-drawn, vary from expert to expert, and are time-consuming to create. Automatic techniques may help, but glioma boundaries are difficult to detect because of the wide variety of shapes, sizes, and contrast. While existing deep learning models address only part of this issue, attention-based networks can capture multi-scale information but may lose spatial relationships in parts of the tumor, and capsule networks can retain these relationships but lose broader context. This study therefore proposes a hybrid model, FpaNet+CapsNet, combining a Feature Pyramid Attention Network and a Capsule Network. The attention module will see the fine details and the context, and the capsule module will preserve the shape and structure of the tumor. Four MRI sequences (T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR) were used for the BraTS2020 model. Patients were split into training (236), validation (59), and test (74) groups prior to pre-processing and augmentation. Both modules proved useful on the test set, achieving Dice scores of 99.05%, 98.05%, and 99.50% for enhancing tumor, tumor core, and whole tumor, respectively, with an overall accuracy of 99.6% and an average HD95 of 2.40 mm. Ablation and statistical tests confirmed the usefulness of both modules, and the model was successful with a Dice score of 0.962 on the unseen BraTS2021 set. These results indicate that the model can accurately and reliably segment gliomas, but requires further clinical validation.

title: Divergent user expectations of conversational AI: a comparative sentiment and thematic analysis of ChatGPT and Replika app store reviews
abstract: Conversational AI apps are increasingly serving two different purposes: instrumental productivity and emotional support. Although both are built on the same underlying language technology, users may evaluate these systems according to different instrumental and relational expectations. This study examines the differences in user evaluation of a task-oriented assistant (ChatGPT) and a companionship-oriented agent (Replika) through computational analysis of the sentiment scoring, NRC emotion analysis, topic modelling, and inferential tests of the 6,000 publicly available app store reviews (3,000 per application). The two applications differed only marginally in overall review polarity, and the direction of the difference depended on the method used: under the Bing lexicon Replika reviews scored slightly higher (M = 0.312 vs. 0.275), whereas under sentimentr ChatGPT scored higher (M = 0.135 vs. 0.102); aggregate polarity was therefore not a robust point of difference between the two corpora. The rating distributions differed significantly between the applications (χ² (4, N = 6,000) = 242.26, p < .001, Cramér’s V = 0.20), with ChatGPT ratings more polarised at both ends of the scale (36.8% vs. 21.7% five-star; 27.4% vs. 23.8% one-star) and Replika ratings more concentrated in the intermediate categories. Once scores were normalised for review length, Replika reviews contained more joy-, anger-, surprise-, and anticipation-associated language, with all effect sizes small; fear-, sadness-, and trust-associated language did not differ significantly between the applications. The coupling between review language and star rating was weaker for the companion application, though the difference was small (App × Rating interaction, partial η² = 0.016); because the two samples span different publication periods, this interaction is reported as provisional. Topic modelling yielded a six-topic solution in which conversation and companionship accounted for 53.6% of Replika reviews against 10.9% of ChatGPT reviews, while task assistance and usefulness accounted for 30.9% of ChatGPT reviews against 1.2% of Replika reviews. Together, the findings are consistent with differences in evaluative framing between the two applications examined in this study, illustrating two representative cases rather than establishing distinct categories of conversational AI systems.

title: Machine learning–enhanced label-free Raman spectroscopy for accurate serum-based detection of early-stage breast cancer via tumor-associated antigens
abstract: Early-stage detection of breast cancer remains a critical challenge for improving clinical outcomes. In this study, an experimentally label-free Raman spectroscopy approach combined with principal component analysis and supervised machine learning is reported for the detection of tumor-associated antigen signatures in serum samples. Raman spectra from early-stage and advanced breast cancer patients, as well as healthy controls, were analyzed alongside recombinant tumor-associated antigen proteins, including \(\alpha\) -1 antitrypsin, peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase A, peroxiredoxin-2, and triosephosphate isomerase-1. Distinct spectral variations were observed in lipid-, nucleic acid-, and protein-related bands. In particular, a characteristic peak at \(\sim\) 519 \(\mathrm {~cm}^{-1}\) , associated with oxidized glutathione and oxidative stress-related structural alterations, was prominently observed in early-stage breast cancer and tumor-associated antigen spectra. Machine learning models trained on principal component analysis-reduced features, including linear discriminant analysis, support vector machine, decision tree, and Naïve Bayes, demonstrated high diagnostic performance, achieving ROC-AUC values above 0.94 for early-stage breast cancer versus controls and above 0.85 for early- versus advanced-stage discrimination. Furthermore, spectral and principal component analysis comparisons revealed partial clustering overlap between early-stage breast cancer samples and tumor-associated antigen proteins, supporting the biochemical relevance of the detected signatures. This integrated spectroscopic and computational approach provides a non-invasive and accurate strategy for early breast cancer detection and stage differentiation, highlighting its potential for clinical diagnostics.

title: Evaluating hv-block cross-validation for dependence-aware model selection in reference evapotranspiration estimation
abstract: Reference evapotranspiration (ET o ) estimation by machine learning techniques, e.g. Random Forest (RF), requires reliable model selection under temporally autocorrelated hydro-meteorological conditions. The hv-block cross-validation procedure 1 has been proposed as an assumption-light, dependence-aware alternative to classical information criteria. On the other hand, its consistency has been criticized because the procedure’s block construction does not satisfy the combinatorial balance of a Balanced Incomplete Block Design (BIBD) on which the original consistency argument relied, so that its theoretical consistency remains unassessed. The present research addressed this gap through a two-phase empirical design. In the first phase, a controlled Monte Carlo simulation (R = 500 replications per autocorrelation strength \(\phi \) ) with a known linear data-generating process was performed to test whether hv-block’s over-selection bias is detectable, persists as sample size scales from n = 4,000 to n = 10,000 and then n = 20,000, and is related to the structural design of the procedure or to autocorrelated noise. In the second phase, the same hv-block framework, using both PACF-based and cyclical exclusion windows, was applied to a real-world, 4000-day ET o dataset from two weather stations in Iran. RF was employed as the base model, and out-of-bag error and 5-fold cross-validation were utilized as temporally naïve benchmarks. As the true input set is unknown for real data, this phase assessed the practical consequences of the criterion choice rather than over-selection. The obtained results revealed that hv-block showed a higher over-selection rate (23–30%) than BIC and AIC at all tested autocorrelation levels, and than 5-fold CV in most configurations. Further, no bias diminishing was detected within the investigated sample-size range ( n = 4000–20,000). Control experiments (ϕ = 0 and h = 0) indicated that the over-selection is mainly associated with the structural design of the procedure (the exclusion gap and the resulting fold geometry and replication imbalance), while the autocorrelated noise showed a secondary role. Nevertheless, the resulting performance accuracy losses were negligible in both the simulation (RMSE differences below 0.002) and real-data applications (RMSE differences lower than 0.01 mm day⁻ 1 at both stations). Overall, while the results partially confirmed the theoretical concern regarding the consistency of hv-block cross-validation, its practical consequences for operational ET o estimation and irrigation water management applications were minimal.
