title: Betta agonistic optimization algorithm: A novel metaheuristic approach for photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for efficient renewable energy integration because of the nonlinear, dynamic, and uncertain characteristics of solar power generation. This paper proposes a novel Evolutionary Memory-Augmented MambaFormer (EvoMem-MambaFormer) optimized using the proposed Betta Agonistic Optimization Algorithm (BAOA) for short-term PV power prediction. The proposed EvoMem-MambaFormer combines selective state-space modeling with memory-guided attention to effectively capture both short-term and long-term temporal dependencies. A Dual Predictive Space Generator is introduced to learn observation-oriented and future-oriented feature representations, while an Error-Adaptive Selective State Evolution mechanism enables recursive memory updates through error feedback. In addition, a Memory Echo Attention Transformer integrates evolved memory states into the attention mechanism to improve temporal feature extraction, and a Quantum-inspired Phase Memory Resonance module enhances the learning of periodic solar generation patterns. The proposed BAOA, inspired by the territorial competition behaviour of Betta fish, is used to optimize the model hyperparameters, improving convergence and forecasting results. Experimental results on a real-world PV dataset demonstrate that the proposed BAOA-EvoMem-MambaFormer attains an RMSE of 7.448, MAE of 4.602, and R² of 0.948, outperforming existing state-of-the-art forecasting models. These outcomes shows that the model provides an accurate, robust, and efficient solution for photovoltaic power forecasting in renewable energy and smart grid applications.

title: HDAR-CNet: hybrid deep learning based spectrum sensing and resource allocation model for cognitive radio networks
abstract: Cognitive Radio Networks require accurate spectrum sensing and resource allocation to efficiently utilize dynamically available spectrum for varying traffic conditions. To address the issues, this research proposed the Hybrid Deep Learning Based Spectrum Sensing and Resource Allocation model for Cognitive Radio Networks (HDAR-CNet) model. Initially, the Multi-size Kernel Recurrent Transformer Network (MKR-TNet) is proposed for spectrum sensing that is designed using Multi-size Kernel Attention and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) based feed forward network of the transformer. Then, the resource allocation strategy is employed using the proposed Sinusoidal Swift Flight Optimization based Deep Reinforcement Learning (2SO-DRL) model. In the proposed DRL model reward estimation is employed by considering the throughput, delay, user priority and penalty to achieve QoS-aware spectrum allocation. Here, the sinusoidal chaotic mapping incorporated in the proposed 2SO algorithm to improve the exploration, avoid the premature convergence and enhances global optimal solution acquisition. The experimental analysis of the proposed HDAR-CNet model based on End-to-End Spectrum Utilization Efficiency and Computation Time acquired the values of 98.9% and 5 s respectively. Thus, the proposed model provides the efficient, intelligent and reliable solution for next-generation wireless communication systems and Cognitive Radio Networks.

title: Physics-informed impedance spectroscopy for diagnosing XLPE cable insulation aging based on a second-order Havriliak-Negami dielectric model
abstract: The dielectric response of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable insulation evolves continuously during aging, yet existing impedance-spectroscopy-based diagnostic methods mainly rely on empirical spectral features and provide limited insight into the underlying dielectric relaxation mechanisms. In addition, conventional sampling-based characterization techniques are destructive and unsuitable for in-service assessment, while existing impedance-spectrum analyses remain inadequate for identifying localized aging. To address these limitations, this study proposes a physics-informed impedance-spectroscopy-based diagnostic framework built upon a second-order Havriliak-Negami (H-N) model. Unlike the conventional single-term H-N model, the proposed formulation explicitly separates interfacial polarization relaxation and dipolar relaxation, enabling the relative responses associated with the two modeled relaxation contributions to be characterized separately. The extracted dielectric parameters are subsequently linked to the source-end input impedance spectroscopy of the cable, from which mechanism-oriented diagnostic indicators are developed to distinguish dominant relaxation processes. For localized aging, a model-matching strategy is further employed to estimate the aging location, and two complementary phase-based indicators are introduced to evaluate the extent and severity of the degraded region. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed framework under the prescribed model conditions. The impedance features exhibit differentiated sensitivities to the two modeled relaxation contributions, while the model-matching approach provides estimates of localized-aging position and the phase-based indicators characterize the spatial extent and nominal severity of the degraded region. By establishing a physical relationship between dielectric relaxation behavior and measurable impedance responses, this study provides a mechanistically interpretable and non-destructive framework for diagnosing XLPE cable insulation aging.

title: Leveraging biased FedSDS as a federated learning strategy for research on non-IID multi-disorder studies
abstract: Federated learning is a powerful approach to overcome privacy and data sharing issues, especially in small sample healthcare settings. However, parameter aggregation strategies, such as FedAvg, are prone to fail in case of non-IID data distributions, which often arise in real-world scenarios. In fact, data provided by different institutions can exhibit systematic heterogeneity across cohorts, such as age, genotype, and life expectancy, reflecting institution-specific biases. Federated Synthetic Data Sharing (FedSDS) represents a valuable solution to the problem of non-IID data. It is a federated learning strategy based on locally generating synthetic datasets from real data and sharing them between the federated clients, avoiding the transfer of real sensitive data. FedSDS is applied to a survival prediction task, performed using a DeepSurv model architecture in 3 different healthcare use cases: Myelodysplastic Syndrome, Low Grade Glioma, and Breast Cancer. We demonstrate that this approach outperforms FedAvg and other strategies based on model parameters optimization in non-IID settings. In particular, the possibility to locally bias shared synthetic data allows preserving the local data distribution of each participating client and significantly improving the performances of federated models. This study shows that biased FedSDS is effective in three different healthcare use cases, such as Myelodysplastic Syndromes, Low Grade Glioma, and Breast Cancer. Our findings suggest that FedSDS may have potential relevance for healthcare applications, as it can support the selection and biasing of samples for dataset augmentation and improve the performance of federated models in non-IID multi-disorder settings. The potential use of this approach for clinical trial cohort selection, however, would require further investigation and dedicated validation.

title: Nonlinear bit-level image encryption method integrating DCGAN-derived dual-branch features and chaotic regulation
abstract: To address the core bottlenecks of insufficient nonlinear adaptive capability of chaotic systems and the difficulty in balancing security and computational efficiency in bit-level transformation for existing image encryption methods, this paper proposes a nonlinear bit-level image encryption scheme combining a dual-branch feature regulation mechanism based on Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGAN) and an adaptive chaotic system. First, a key-controlled dual-branch DCGAN fusion module is constructed to generate cipher keys tightly correlated with plaintext content adaptively. Second, an adaptive Chen chaotic system modulated by plaintext features is designed; comprehensive dynamical analysis verifies its outstanding nonlinearity and randomness. Third, a low-complexity nonlinear bit-level transformation is elaborated to simultaneously achieve powerful confusion-diffusion capability and low computation cost. Experimental results demonstrate that the key space of the proposed method reaches 2 256 , and its security performance outperforms mainstream comparative algorithms. Meanwhile, the computational efficiency is improved by 29.7% compared with traditional DNA-based bit-level schemes, which provides a new perspective for the collaborative encryption of nonlinear dynamics and deep learning.

title: A hybrid EfficientNet-B0-CBAM-Vision Transformer framework for accurate cherry leaf disease classification
abstract: Cherry leaf diseases significantly reduce crop quality and yield, so their early and accurate detection is essential for effective orchard management. However, automated disease classification remains challenging because of high inter-class similarity, subtle visual symptoms, complex backgrounds, and varying illumination in real-world environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework, termed Hybrid EfficientNet-B0 Convolutional Block Attention Module Vision Transformer (HECB-ViT), for accurate and robust cherry leaf disease classification. The proposed architecture integrates the complementary strengths of convolutional neural networks and transformer-based learning to capture both fine-grained local features and long-range global dependencies effectively. Specifically, EfficientNet-B0 serves as a lightweight yet powerful backbone for extracting discriminative local features. At the same time, the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) enhances feature representation by emphasizing disease-relevant spatial regions and informative feature channels. In parallel, the Vision Transformer (ViT) branch models global contextual relationships across the entire leaf surface via multi-head self-attention. The features extracted from both branches are subsequently fused to generate a highly discriminative representation for final disease classification. We evaluated the proposed HECB-ViT framework on a publicly available Cherry Leaf Disease dataset comprising 4,995 images across five classes: Cherry Leaf Scorch, Healthy Cherry Leaf, Cherry Brown Spot, Cherry Purple Leaf Spot, and Cherry Shot Hole Disease. The dataset was split into training, validation, and test sets at 80:10:10. To mitigate class imbalance and improve convergence stability, focal loss and the AdamW optimizer were employed during training. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms baseline and ablation models, achieving an overall classification accuracy of 99% and consistently high precision, recall, and F1 scores across all disease categories. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each architectural component in enhancing classification performance. Overall, the proposed HECB-ViT framework provides a scalable, robust, and efficient solution for automated cherry leaf disease detection, demonstrating strong potential for deployment in precision agriculture and intelligent orchard management systems.

title: Multi-source data-driven prediction of crack-front stress intensity factors using Enhanced-piFNO
abstract: Stress intensity factor (SIF) characterizes the local crack-tip field and the driving force for crack propagation. This study introduces Enhanced-piFNO as an offline neural-operator surrogate for predicting complete SIF distributions along complex crack fronts. The model combines angular positional encoding, low-order one-dimensional spectral mixing, residual identity updates, and mechanics-based regularization in a task-specific architecture. Three data sources are evaluated separately: self-constructed compressor-blade simulations containing three loading paths and Mode I–III SIF responses, SIF labels inverted from externally supplied Digital Image Correlation displacement fields for grouped evaluation under Mode I and Mode II, and selected SIFBench cases for standardized benchmarking. The self-constructed simulation and SIFBench comparisons use DeepONet as the neural-operator baseline, whereas the DIC-derived comparison includes standard FNO. Enhanced-piFNO lowers displayed error peaks in selected Mode-I and Mode-II simulation cases, achieves validation R² values of 0.9977 and 0.9986 for Modes I and II on the grouped DIC-derived labels, and gives the lowest NMAE for all three b/t = 0.5 TT-CC countersunk-hole loading cases. It also gives the lowest normalized \(\:{L}_{2}\) error for the corresponding b/t = 0.05 bearing case.

title: Decoding cerebral vasoregulation: an attention-based BiLSTM framework for elderly ischemic stroke prediction and biomarker identification with clinical associations
abstract: Stroke remains a major cause of mortality and long-term disability among older adults, with risk further increased by age-related decline in cerebral blood-flow regulation and vascular responsiveness. Traditional risk scores often overlook physiological dynamics, necessitating advanced multimodal analysis for early detection and prevention. This study hypothesizes that an attention-based bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) model can accurately classify stroke versus the control group using physiological biosignals while identifying interpretable individual biomarkers associated with cardiovascular risk indicators. In this study, we have used the Cerebral Vasoregulation in Elderly with Stroke (CVES) dataset, comprising multimodal physiological biosignals data (e.g., ECG, arterial blood pressure, cerebral flow velocity, end-tidal \(CO_2\) etc) from 64 elderly participants. The proposed attention-based BiLSTM architecture encodes bidirectional temporal dependencies, applies self-attention for salient feature weighting, followed by dense layers for classification. Model evaluation has employed 5-fold and leave-one-out cross-validation, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for identification of individual biomarkers. The proposed model also identifies an association between physiological and clinical data. We have achieved 98.6% test accuracy, with 0.996 AUC-ROC, 98.8% precision, and 98.9% recall, outperforming baselines like LSTM, GRU, and 1D-CNN. SHAP analysis highlights cardiovascular dominance (e.g., ECG, ABP) as primary biomarkers, with radiative heat loss and middle cerebral artery flow as key discriminators. Clinical analysis revealed age-associated amplification of ECG and CO \(_2\) sensitivities, smoking/alcohol suppression of radiative attributions, and diabetes intensification across signals. The proposed model is also able to predict cardiovascular risk indicators using physiological data with \((R^2) = (0.8467 \pm 0.03)\) . The proposed framework advances proactive stroke-risk assessment by fusing predictive accuracy with interpretable, personalized insights, surpassing literature benchmarks in multimodal integration and translational potential for elderly care.

title: SWT-ResNet-based internal material identification for impacted multilayered cylindrical structures with clearance
abstract: Accurate identification of materials enclosed within multilayer cylindrical structures is challenging without structural disassembly, particularly when assembly clearances induce contact and impact nonlinearities and result in nonstationary vibration responses. To address this problem, a material identification framework integrating the synchrosqueezing wavelet transform and a residual neural network (SWT–ResNet) is proposed. First, vibration responses are measured externally through impact tests, and SWT is employed to generate highly concentrated time–frequency representations through frequency reassignment. A lightweight ResNet is then used to automatically extract multilevel time–frequency features and classify the internal materials. Four materials, namely MJ, AZ31B magnesium alloy, epoxy resin, and polytetrafluoroethylene, are investigated under four impact levels of 5, 10, 15, and 20 g. Three independent repeated tests are performed for each condition, producing 48 original experimental records. To prevent information leakage caused by overlapping sliding windows, the data are partitioned at the original-record level before sample segmentation. The proposed SWT–ResNet achieves an accuracy, macro-averaged precision, macro-averaged recall, and macro-averaged F1-score of 97.50%, 97.56%, 97.50%, and 97.50%, respectively, on the independent test set. Original-record-level three-fold cross-validation yields an accuracy of 96.88% ± 0.63%, demonstrating the stability of the proposed framework. Ablation experiments show that SWT–ResNet outperforms CWT–ResNet, STFT–ResNet, Raw-CNN, SWT–CNN, SWT–SVM, SWT–RF, and PCA–k-means, confirming the contributions of both the highly concentrated SWT representation and residual feature learning. Under Gaussian white-noise conditions of 20, 10, and 0 dB, the corresponding accuracies are 98.5%, 94.4%, and 69.3%, respectively, indicating a certain degree of noise robustness. These results demonstrate that SWT–ResNet can effectively identify internal materials in multilayer cylindrical structures with assembly clearances and provides a feasible nondestructive approach for identifying internal media in complex enclosed structures.

title: Persistent differentiation in rural ecological resilience across functional village types in the Yangtze River Delta
abstract: Understanding ecological differences among functional village types can inform rural revitalization. We analysed 4,126 village units in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) at five benchmark years from 2003 to 2023, using an ecological resilience index (ERI) integrating resistance, adaptability and recovery. Five overlapping functional types were examined through city-adjusted comparisons, spatially validated extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). In 2023, mean ERI was highest for ecological livability (EL; 0.371), followed by rural civilization (RC; 0.366), industrial prosperity (IP; 0.330), effective governance (EG; 0.312) and wealthy life (WL; 0.304). WL villages showed the largest 2003–2023 increase in mean ERI (15.360 × 10⁻³). Functional memberships explained 10.887% of variation remaining after city and year adjustment. Seven of ten city-adjusted pairwise contrasts were significant in all five years after Holm correction. Population and impervious cover were the leading predictive features for 2023 levels, while shortwave radiation, climatic water deficit and nighttime lights were prominent for trends. Spatial out-of-fold coefficients of determination (R²) ranged from 0.585 to 0.788 for levels and from 0.231 to 0.484 for trends. These findings reveal persistent functional differences alongside contrasting temporal trajectories. Integrating functional classification with assessments of resilience levels and changes provides a village-level framework for differentiated ecological assessment and long-term monitoring in rural revitalization.

title: Genetic diversity, phenotypic plasticity, and adaptive capacity of Ziziphus nummularia populations in Iran
abstract: Ziziphus nummularia (Burm.f.) Wight & Arn. (Rhamnaceae) is a medicinally important plant that thrives in arid and semi-arid areas. The native accessions of this species show a highly confined geographical distribution in Iran and exhibit high tolerance to heat, drought, and salinity; hence, they can play an important role in breeding programs related to environmental stresses. Furthermore, these accessions differ significantly in their morphological, fruit, and phytochemical characteristics. Despite various studies assessing the genetic, phytochemical, and morphological diversity of this species in different parts of the world, no comprehensive investigation has examined landscape genetics and the influence of environmental and climatic factors on its adaptive capacity and survival in Iran. Therefore, the present study conducted a gene-ecological analysis of twelve natural populations of Z. nummularia in Iran using different multivariate statistical methods and several modeling approaches, including RDA (Redundancy Analysis), CCA (Canonical Correspondence Analysis), sPCA (Spatial Principal Component Analysis), SEM (Structural Equation Modeling), DEM (Differential Equation Modeling), and RF (Random Forest). The results revealed low to moderate genetic diversity based on SCoT molecular markers among the studied populations while identifying several putatively locally adapted genetic loci. These populations differed significantly in their genetic structure and composition, which were shaped by spatial variables. They exhibited both isolation by distance (IBD) and isolation by environment (IBE). The studied populations also differed in their adaptive capacity and Landscape Adaptive Index (LAI). Random Regression Mixed Model (RRMM) analyses revealed distinct population responses to longitude and latitude, as reflected by both genetic and morphological variation. SEM demonstrated complex interactions among environmental, climatic, genetic, morphological, and soil factors and their collective influence on the adaptive capacity of the studied populations. Furthermore, DEM, SEM, and RF consistently indicated a stable population growth pattern over time. Nevertheless, considering the species’ confined geographical distribution and relatively low genetic diversity, appropriate conservation measures should be implemented to ensure the long-term preservation of these valuable medicinal plant populations.

title: Evaluation of explainable artificial intelligence for subarachnoid hemorrhage detection and outcome modelling using neuroimaging data
abstract: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a life-threatening neurologic emergency. SAH Detection Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Explainable AI (SAHDAI-XAI) is a cloud-based machine learning (ML) model that classifies computed tomography (CT) images as positive or negative for SAH across 8 hemorrhage spaces. Phase 1 of our project used Vertex AI (Google Cloud) automated ML to train models on progressively larger noncontrast head CT datasets (20–300 images), evenly labeled as hemorrhage-positive or hemorrhage-negative. Explainability was applied to images, and the final round evaluated differentiation between hemorrhages and other pathologies. Phase 2 focused on explainability by visualizing predictive features and localizing hemorrhages with the Brain Lesion Analysis and Segmentation Tool for CT (BLAST-CT) model, which segments and quantifies 4 hemorrhage regions. In Phase 1, the first 2 automated ML rounds showed 100.0% precision due to the small dataset size. With larger datasets, third-round precision was 97.9% with 1 false negative, and fourth-round precision was 94.4% with 2 false positives. In Phase 2, after preprocessing using BLAST-CT, topographic hemorrhage maps were generated, with some accurately capturing a large portion of the hemorrhage, while others performed less reliably. SAHDAI-XAI improves transparency in SAH detection by using BLAST-CT visualizations to clarify predictive features and reduce black-box constraints.

title: Modelling farmer engagement with Digital Agro-Advisory Platforms (DAAPs) using an extended TAM framework: evidence from Kisan Sarathi
abstract: Digital Agro-Advisory Platforms (DAAPs) are emerging as vital tools to address gaps in agricultural extension services, particularly in developing economies like India. Kisan Sarathi , implemented by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), represents a pioneering initiative to deliver real-time, multilingual, and location-specific advisories to farmers. Despite its rapid expansion, limited empirical research has examined the behavioural factors driving farmers’ sustained use of such platforms. This study extends the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) by integrating self-efficacy and system quality to investigate determinants of farmers’ usage behaviour of Kisan Sarathi across the Indo-Gangetic Plains. Using stratified two-stage sampling, data were collected from 350 registered farmers in Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and West Bengal. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) and Random Forest techniques were employed. SEM revealed that perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, self-efficacy, and system quality significantly influenced farmers’ attitudes, which strongly predicted behavioural intention and subsequent usage behaviour. Random Forest analysis further identified perceived usefulness, attitude, and behavioural intention as the strongest predictors across states, highlighting regional variations in system quality. The findings underscore the importance of user confidence, system performance, and farmer-centric design. The study contributes to the ICT4Ag literature by advancing TAM with psychological and technical dimensions, while offering insights for policymakers, developers, and extension agencies seeking to design inclusive digital advisory systems and reduce the digital divide in agriculture.

title: Efficient speech enhancement using Harris hawks optimized feature selection and a hybrid Wiener-Bi-GRU model for real-time deployment
abstract: The main challenge in hearing-aid applications is balancing the strict power, memory, and latency limits of battery-powered devices against speech quality. Hearing-aid processors typically operate within a 20–50 mW power budget, 128–512 kB of RAM, and latency below 10 ms. Classical signal processing methods satisfy these constraints but yield limited quality, while deep learning (DL) methods achieve better quality at computational costs unsuitable for embedded devices. This paper proposes a two-stage speech enhancement framework combining Wiener Filtering (WF) preprocessing, Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO)-based feature selection (FS), and a lightweight Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU) with temporal attention. WF removes stationary noise without trained parameters, after which Feature Extraction (FE) generates 352 candidate features spanning time-frequency, spectral, temporal, and pitch representations. HHO reduces this to 42 features using a weighted multi-criteria fitness function that balances intelligibility, quality, and computational cost, achieving 88% dimensionality reduction. The resulting model has 2.18 million parameters and 6.8 ms inference latency. Evaluated on the VoiceBank+DEMAND benchmark, using both an expanded 46,643-sample test set and the standard 824-utterance benchmark test set, the model achieves PESQ of 2.58 to 2.66, STOI up to 0.86, and SI-SDR of 13.9 dB, outperforming classical, metaheuristic, and several deep-learning (DL) baselines while satisfying all target parameter (≤ 3 M), memory (≤ 12 MB), and latency (< 10 ms) constraints. Ablation and multi-seed stability analyses confirm the individual contributions of Wiener preprocessing and HHO-based FS, and paired statistical testing confirms that the improvements over internal baselines are significant.

title: Evaluation of the feasibility of classifying various upper limb movements using multichannel upper-arm sEMG signals
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG)-based upper limb movement recognition studies have primarily focused on signals measured from the forearm or muscles around the wrist. However, the feasibility of using upper-arm sEMG signals as an alternative measurement site for classifying various upper limb movements remains insufficiently investigated. This study evaluated the feasibility of classifying eight upper limb movements, including elbow, forearm, wrist, and hand movements, using five-channel upper-arm sEMG signals. sEMG signals were collected from the biceps brachii long head, biceps brachii short head, triceps brachii long head, triceps brachii lateral head, and brachialis in seven healthy adult males under static and free conditions. Time-domain features were extracted, and classification performance was compared using Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and k-Nearest Neighbors models. Random Forest achieved the highest accuracies of 93.13 ± 0.70% under the static condition and 89.16 ± 1.21% under the free condition. The full feature set and five-channel configuration showed high performance, although lower recall and increased misclassification were observed for hand open and hand close movements under the free condition. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the feasibility of within-subject upper limb movement classification using upper-arm sEMG signals and suggest their potential as a complementary measurement site.

title: Coupled machine learning for urban PM2.5 source apportionment and quantification of associated factors: case study of Heze
abstract: To accurately identify the sources and associated factors of urban atmospheric PM 2.5 , this study took Heze City in Shandong Province as a case and constructed a methodological framework that combines the XGBoost machine learning model with SHAP interpretation analysis. Based on the monitoring data of the atmospheric super station from March 2023 to February 2024 (including conventional pollutants, meteorological parameters, water-soluble ions, carbon components, inorganic elements, and VOCs), the reliability of the data was first verified through chemical mass reconstruction (R 2 = 0.84). Then, the PMF model was used to analyze and identify six types of pollution sources: secondary nitrate (39.4%), secondary sulfate (7.9%), coal combustion source (23.1%), other energy combustion sources (19.3%), dust source (9.1%), and other source (1.2%). Combined with backward trajectory clustering, PSCF, and CWT analysis, the regional transport paths of different source areas were revealed. Among them, the North China Plain significantly contributed to the secondary inorganic salts. The XGBoost model had high fitting performance for PM 2.5 concentration (R 2 = 0.96). The model is primarily used for interpretative factor analysis via SHAP, rather than for future forecasting. SHAP analysis identified CO, relative humidity, temperature, and ethylene as key influencing factors. PM 10 also showed strong SHAP importance. However, PM 10 is a covarying indicator rather than a causal driver. This is because PM 10 contains PM 2.5 by definition. Their strong association also reflects shared responses to meteorological and emission conditions. High humidity, low temperature, and enhanced primary emissions jointly exacerbated the accumulation of pollution. The study demonstrates an integrated application of machine learning and receptor models, providing a scientific basis for the precise source tracing and collaborative control of PM 2.5 in Heze and similar key cities.

title: Genome-inspired AI for extrapolative discovery of high-temperature superconductors
abstract: The discovery of high-temperature superconductors at ambient pressure remains one of the central challenges in materials science. Inspired by the Materials Genome Initiative, we develop an AI-integrated high-throughput screening framework to identify high-Tc superconducting materials and promising elemental genes, while overcoming the extrapolation limitations of prior machine-learning (ML) approaches. Systematic evaluation of ten ML and nine neural-network models identifies functional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architectures as uniquely capable of extrapolative prediction. We introduce the DataG Non-Sc dataset (53,196 materials), addressing the scarcity of non-superconducting data, and develop a novel Functional API neural architecture for improved prediction. Applied across three major crystallographic databases (ICSD, COD, and the Materials Project), the framework identifies 22 previously unexplored ambient-pressure Pu-based superconducting candidates with T c > 50 K (e.g., Pu 2 Co 17 with T c ~ 89 K), alongside over 40 hydrides with predicted T c up to 100 K. The framework independently converges on actinide- and hydrogen-rich systems, two materials families already strongly associated with superconductivity, without prior mechanistic bias. Crucially, all predicted candidates are drawn from existing crystallographic entries, making them immediately accessible for experimental validation, bridging computational screening and laboratory discovery. More broadly, the proposed framework provides a platform for AI-guided discovery of superconducting materials.

title: Emotional and behavioral asymmetries in user responses to virtual versus human influencers
abstract: As AI virtual influencers (AIVIs) proliferate, understanding human-AI emotional engagement is vital for advancing affective computing. To examine whether AIVIs evoke comparable affective responses to human influencers (HIs), we analyzed 156,918 Instagram comments that received 12+ million likes, integratinglarge language model (LLM)-derived knowledge graphs, emotion analysis, and machine learning. HI-directed discourse shows more differentiated emotional expression and a pattern consistent with more cohesive semantic networks than AIVI-directed discourse. AIVI-directed comments are less likely to express positive affect (24.8% vs. 41.5%) and also less likely to express negative affect (5.8% vs. 9.3%), indicating reduced affective expression of either valence rather than heightened negativity. This group-level tendency is not uniform: affective engagement varies substantially across AIVIs, and that variation is more closely associated with positive than with negative expression. Our Multi-Signal Embedding Network (MSEN), incorporating behavioral metrics and OpenAI semantic embeddings, classified influencer types from behavioral, affective and semantic features (F1 = 0.89), outperforming baselines including a state-of-the-art zero-shot LLM. These findings identify a boundary condition for the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm: human-like appearance can elicit social responses without producing affective and semantic response patterns as rich as those elicited by HIs.

title: Comparing SHAP and distributed-lag model summaries of environmental associations with reported malaria cases in three Nigerian states
abstract: Explainable AI is increasingly used to interpret machine-learning models in public health, but is rarely checked against models that estimate environmental exposure–lag relationships directly. We compared the two on identical inputs. We analysed ten years (2015–2024) of routine monthly confirmed malaria cases from three Nigerian states spanning a low-to-high transmission gradient. A regularised LightGBM model trained on lagged satellite rainfall, temperature and vegetation was interpreted with SHAP; a distributed-lag non-linear model fitted to the same predictors provided a reference. The two agreed on which drivers mattered. Agreement on direction was only partial: the mean-absolute SHAP summary is sign-free, and a signed SHAP check matched the reference model on the leading driver (vegetation, positive) but not on rainfall. Agreement on the timing of effects across monthly lags was not reproducible—across rolling-origin resamples it was centred near zero for every driver and, against a permutation null, was not distinguishable from chance. This is consistent with strong collinearity between neighbouring monthly lags, though with only three collinear drivers we cannot isolate collinearity as the cause. Environmental variables did not improve out-of-sample prediction over a seasonal baseline, suggesting gains lie in finer spatial resolution rather than more covariates.

title: A hybrid statistical–machine learning framework for day-ahead electricity price forecasting in smart city environments
abstract: Accurate day-ahead electricity price forecasting, particularly in the context of customer-centric services and emerging smart city infrastructures, is a cornerstone of efficient power market operations, supporting bidding strategies, hedging, and grid reliability. This paper proposes SSXLR, a fault-tolerant hybrid forecasting framework that combines Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous variables (SARIMAX), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) within a 2-out-of-3 voting architecture to capture both linear seasonal trends and nonlinear temporal dynamics while reducing dependence on a single forecasting branch. The proposed method was evaluated using one year of historical data (July 1, 2024–July 1, 2025) from Duke Energy Ohio and Kentucky (DEO&K) within the PJM interconnection. The dataset integrates day-ahead market prices ($/MWh), corresponding load consumption (MW), eleven weather variables, and population growth indicators. The target is the day-ahead price profile for July 2, 2025, consisting of 24-hourly points. Results show that SSXLR achieves more than 30% reduction in Root Mean Squared Error over SARIMAX and XGBoost, respectively. The Mean Absolute Error (MAE) reached 1.196, demonstrating the ability of SSXLR to account effectively for external market drivers and temporal dependencies. These findings highlight the scalability of the proposed framework for regional electricity markets, where accurate day-ahead forecasting can improve operational planning, supply–demand balance, and economic efficiency. The proposed framework is dynamic and region-adaptable, allowing it to be transferred to other smart city or regional energy systems when electricity price, load/consumption, weather, and calendar data are available. Beyond improving predictive accuracy, the 2-out-of-3 voting mechanism provides a fault-tolerant forecasting layer by allowing the final output to be determined from the two most consistent forecasting branches when one branch becomes unavailable or produces an unreliable output.

title: A Caputo fractional physics-informed neural network for Lorenz chaotic systems
abstract: Fractional-order dynamical systems provide an effective mathematical framework for describing nonlinear processes with memory and hereditary effects. Although physics-informed neural networks have demonstrated promising performance for solving differential equations, their application to fractional-order chaotic dynamical systems remains relatively limited. In this study, a Caputo fractional physics-informed neural networks (FPINNs) framework is developed to approximate the fractional-order Lorenz system by incorporating the governing fractional differential equations into a multi-objective loss function. The reference solutions are generated using the Caputo Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM) predictor-corrector method to ensure an appropriate numerical treatment of the fractional derivative. The proposed framework is evaluated for several fractional orders over the considered simulation interval, and its predictive performance is assessed using quantitative error metrics, including mean squared error, mean absolute error, sum of squared errors, and the coefficient of determination. The numerical results demonstrate that the FPINN accurately reconstructs the fractional Lorenz trajectories while maintaining good agreement with the ABM reference solutions. Furthermore, the study investigates the influence of the fractional order on prediction accuracy and computational performance, providing a systematic numerical assessment of the proposed framework. The results indicate that FPINNs constitute an effective and data-efficient approach for approximating nonlinear fractional dynamical systems within the investigated computational setting.

title: OocystMeter, a machine-learning algorithm to count and measure Plasmodium oocysts, reveals a clustering pattern in the Anopheles midgut
abstract: We present OocystMeter, a machine learning-based software developed to automate the segmentation of malaria oocysts from images of mosquito midguts stained with mercurochrome. Existing bioimage analysis tools, including machine learning-based ones, often struggle with the unique staining patterns, complex midgut backgrounds, and variable morphology of oocysts, making the determination of oocyst size and numbers cumbersome. To overcome these challenges, we curated a high-quality dataset comprised of 11,178 Plasmodium falciparum oocysts in Anopheles gambiae midguts annotated by expert parasitologists. Using this dataset, we fine-tuned a Mask R-CNN object detection model to achieve segmentation accuracy comparable to human parasitologists (Spearman’s correlation of 0.998 for oocyst counts and 0.978 for size measurements). Combining tool-assisted expert annotations with spatial analysis, we identified a non-random oocyst clustering pattern, detectable at shorter spatial scales in infections with 4–74 oocysts/midgut. The analyses did not identify a consistent anatomical region or axis that explains this pattern. Our workflow accelerates image-based oocyst counting and size measurement, standardizes image analysis, and provides spatial coordinates for parasitology studies. Manual dissection, staining, mounting, and image acquisition by human scientists remain necessary. OocystMeter is freely available at https://github.com/duopeng/oocystMeter , and as a web-based tool at http://oocystmeter.org/ , offering a valuable resource for researchers investigating the oocyst stage of malaria development.

title: Chinese private university EFL students’ attitude towards iWrite Automated Essay Scoring system: influencing mechanism from perceived interactivity to criticism
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been prominent in our daily lives by means of mobile applications and web search engines. AI-based Automated Essay Scoring (AES) system is playing an increasingly important role in higher education field. This study investigated the relationship between Chinese private university EFL students’ perceived interactivity of iWrite AES system and perceived performance, confirmation, individual innovativeness of AES system, as well as their reflective thinking, and how the variables influence students’ criticism of AES system. Based on a sample of 442 students, the study used Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) for data analysis. The findings indicated that students’ perceived interactivity of AES system is positively related to perceived performance and confirmation. Students’ perceived performance of AES system has a significant influence on students’ confirmation. Furthermore, students’ confirmation of AES system positively affects individual innovativeness, reflective thinking and criticism of AES. And students’ individual innovativeness also positively influences students’ reflective thinking of AES. However, students’ individual innovativeness and reflective thinking of AES system doesn’t have a positive relationship with students’ criticism. This study not only reveals Chinese private university EFL students’ attitudes and experiences towards technological tools but also provide valuable support for enhancing teaching effectiveness and improving teaching methods.

title: Network modeling of science teachers’ perceptions of artificial intelligence integration in science curriculum development
abstract: This study employs psychological network modeling to examine the interrelationships among science teachers’ perceptions of benefits, challenges, and attitudes toward integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools in science curriculum development. A total of 691 Saudi science teachers completed a validated questionnaire. Network estimation using regularization and centrality analyses identified key themes in science teachers’ perceptions of benefits, challenges, and attitudes toward integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools into curriculum development and instructional practices. The estimated network revealed a dense structure. Centrality analyses indicated that curriculum content generation and innovative pedagogical tools were most central, while data processing challenges and algorithmic bias emerged as prominent structural barriers. Centrality metrics identify AI-facilitated curriculum design and innovative pedagogical tools as primary benefits, while challenges such as data processing limitations and algorithmic biases emerge as significant barriers. Teacher attitudes demonstrate ambivalence, characterized by resistance to automating administrative functions alongside guarded optimism for interactive and adaptive learning applications. These insights underscore the imperative to address technical constraints, ethical considerations, and the evolving professional identities of educators to ensure effective AI integration. The study contributes a nuanced, systemic understanding that informs the development of tailored AI tools and support frameworks, ultimately advancing transformative innovation in science education.

title: Generative AI-assisted design problem exploration in interaction design: response disclosure, prompt initiative, and cost-sensitive prompting behavior
abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used in early-stage design exploration, yet experimental evidence is limited on how system-side response disclosure and user-side prompt initiative jointly shape the exploration of design problems that are not yet well defined. In a 2 × 2 within-subject experiment, 48 design students completed four interaction-design tasks involving unfamiliar user groups under one-time versus progressive response disclosure and low versus high prompt initiative, with the composition time of every submission logged. Progressive disclosure was associated with greater perceived understanding change, higher self-reported engagement and germane cognitive load, lower extraneous cognitive load, and more prompts. High prompt initiative showed the same pattern on these four self-reported measures but significantly fewer prompts, reversing the predicted direction; composition time accounted for 18% of the exploration window under high initiative and under 2% under low initiative. Both sets of main effects held after multiplicity correction and adjustment for task and period. An exploratory interaction for germane cognitive load did not survive correction. These findings extend a mixed-initiative view of AI-assisted exploration by identifying response structuring and question formulation as separable design levers. They also indicate that prompt frequency should be interpreted together with the cost of producing a submission.

title: Predicting the number of infant deaths per woman in ethiopia using complementary count regression and machine learning approaches
abstract: Infant mortality remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. Understanding factors associated with cumulative infant deaths and improving their prediction may help identify populations with higher infant-death burdens. This study examined maternal-level counts of infant deaths ever experienced by women in Ethiopia using complementary count-regression and machine-learning approaches. Data from the 2019 Ethiopia Mini Demographic and Health Survey were analyzed among 5,846 women with complete birth histories. The outcome was the cumulative number of infant deaths experienced by each woman. Because the outcome is mechanically related to the number of births, the logarithm of the number of children ever born was incorporated as an exposure offset in the count-regression models and excluded from the machine-learning predictor set. Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP), and zero-inflated negative binomial models were compared using Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. Poisson Random Forest, Extreme gradient boost (XGBoost)-Poisson, and Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM)-Poisson models were evaluated using 70% training and 30% independent testing split, with five-fold cross-validation for hyper-parameter tuning. Predictive performance was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE). The ZIP model provided the best fit among the evaluated count-regression models, with the lowest AIC (2503) and BIC (2544). In the count component, maternal age, household wealth, postnatal care, child vaccination status, maternal education, and place of delivery were statistically associated with the expected number of infant deaths. In the machine-learning analysis, XGBoost-Poisson achieved the best test-set predictive performance, with an MAE of 0.320 and RMSE of 0.570. Region had the largest relative predictive contribution (gain = 0.190), followed by marital status (0.167), maternal age (0.136), education level (0.125), and wealth index (0.117). These variable-importance measures represent predictive contribution and should not be interpreted as causal effects. Cumulative infant-death counts among women in Ethiopia were associated with demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and maternal and child healthcare characteristics. The ZIP model provided interpretable adjusted associations, whereas XGBoost-Poisson provided the best out-of-sample prediction among the evaluated machine-learning models. The findings support the value of combining inferential count regression with count-specific machine-learning methods while emphasizing that predictive importance does not establish causality. Continued attention to maternal education, socioeconomic disadvantage, postnatal care, immunization, and access to appropriate delivery care may help inform child-survival strategies in Ethiopia.

title: Identification of ferroptosis-related key genes influencing synovitis development in osteoarthritis based on machine learning
abstract: This study aims to explore the potential involvement of ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs) in osteoarthritis (OA) synovitis. Synovial tissue samples from 32 OA patients and 32 normal controls were obtained from the GEO database and analyzed to identify differentially expressed FRGs.Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified a gene module significantly associated with OA. To further prioritize candidate genes, three machine learning approaches—Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)—were applied, among which the SVM model demonstrated the best predictive performance.Through integrated analysis, CARS was identified as a candidate key ferroptosis-related gene associated with OA synovitis. Further immune infiltration analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between CARS expression and follicular helper T cell abundance, suggesting a potential association between ferroptosis-related metabolic regulation and immune microenvironment alterations in OA synovial tissue.In addition, competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network analysis indicated that CARS may be regulated by multiple non-coding RNAs, implying a complex post-transcriptional regulatory landscape. Experimental validation using qRT-PCR and Western blot analysis supported the bioinformatics prediction that CARS expression is elevated in OA synovial tissues at both mRNA and protein levels.Overall, this study provides a bioinformatics-based framework for identifying ferroptosis-related gene signatures in OA synovitis and suggests that CARS may serve as a potential candidate biomarker associated with ferroptosis and immune regulation in OA. Further functional studies are required to clarify its mechanistic role.

title: Transformer language models reveal distinct patterns in aphasia subtypes and longitudinal change
abstract: Language impairments in aphasia are characterized by various representational disruptions that may be reflected in discourse production. This research examines the capacity of transformer-based language models, particularly GPT-2, to serve as a computational framework for analyzing variations in aphasic narrative speech. A longitudinal dataset of narrative speech samples collected at six time points from individuals with aphasia (N = 47; baseline cross-sectional sample N = 57) was utilized as part of an intervention study. All transcripts were processed via the GPT-2 language model to obtain activation values from each of the 12 transformer layers. Statistically significant differences in activation values across aphasia subtypes were found at every layer (all p < .001), with the most pronounced effects in the deeper layers. Pairwise Tukey HSD tests revealed consistent distinctions between Broca’s aphasia and both Anomic and Wernicke’s aphasia, suggesting a shared activation profile between the latter two. Longitudinal tests revealed significant changes over time, especially in the final three layers (10–12). These findings suggest that transformer-based activation patterns reflect meaningful variation in aphasic discourse and may align with clinical observations. Overall, GPT-2 provides a scalable tool to model representational dynamics in aphasia and may offer exploratory insights into language representation in aphasic discourse.

title: Mathematical and machine learning analysis of high-density polyethylene thermal degradation
abstract: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) is widely used to characterize polymer degradation, but repeated experiments and conventional single-step kinetic models can become inefficient or inadequate when degradation is nonlinear, multistage, atmosphere-dependent, or evaluated outside the conditions used for calibration. This study developed a machine learning (ML) regression framework to predict the percentage mass remaining during high-density polyethylene (HDPE) degradation. Twenty-five TGA specimens (8–20 mg) yielded 237,154 observations; time, temperature, and initial mass were used as predictors. Random Forest, Extra Trees Regressor (ETR), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), Natural Gradient Boosting (NGBoost), and a multilayer perceptron artificial neural network (MLP–ANN) were compared with a hybrid NGBoost–ETR model. Performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination (R²), mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). The hybrid model achieved R² = 0.999987, MSE = 0.027042, RMSE = 0.164446, and MAE = 0.015879 on the dataset. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) ranked time and temperature as the dominant predictors, while initial mass had a smaller contribution. The optimized point-prediction model was deployed through a Django web interface. The framework provides rapid within-domain interpolation of HDPE TGA profiles; external validation across polymer grades, heating programs, and laboratories remains necessary before replacing experimental TGA.

title: Full-spectrum XGBoost framework for interpretable classification of femtosecond LIBS spectra
abstract: Reliable classification of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) spectra remains challenging when emission signals are weak and strongly fluctuating under low-pulse-energy femtosecond (fs) laser ablation. This study evaluates a full-spectrum machine-learning approach based on eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) using an Al/Si thin-film ablation dataset as a representative binary spectral-classification case. The full raw LIBS spectrum was directly used as the model input, and XGBoost was compared with support vector machine, multilayer perceptron, k-nearest neighbors, and Gaussian Naive Bayes classifiers. Model development and evaluation were performed using processing-point-level data separation, with hyperparameter optimization conducted exclusively on the training dataset using repeated five-fold cross-validation. XGBoost achieved a mean cross-validation accuracy of 99.55 ± 0.26%, an F1-score of 99.48 ± 0.31%, and an AUC of 0.99994 ± 0.00008. On the independent test dataset comprising 612 spectra from 68 processing points, XGBoost achieved 100% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, with an AUC of 1.00000. The classification results remained unchanged at probability thresholds of 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7. The measured single-spectrum inference time was approximately 0.105 ms, substantially shorter than the 10 ms interval between successive laser pulses at 100 Hz. SHAP analysis showed that the most influential wavelength channels were concentrated within the 288–289 nm spectral region and were distributed across multiple neighboring channels rather than being confined to the nominal Si I 288.15 nm wavelength. These results demonstrate accurate full-spectrum classification of the investigated low-signal fs-LIBS dataset while retaining wavelength-level information for model interpretation.

title: RA4KT: a causality-informed explainable reverse attribution framework for knowledge tracing
abstract: With the global digital transformation of education, Knowledge Tracing, the core cognitive modeling module in intelligent tutoring systems, has become a key research focus in educational data mining. However, existing deep learning-based KT models are inherently black-box: while achieving high-accuracy answer performance prediction, they fail to clarify internal decision logic or translate outputs into actionable teaching guidance for students and teachers. Existing KT interpretability methods cannot simultaneously satisfy the core requirements of causality, actionability, pedagogical adaptability, and non-professional accessibility, severely limiting KT’s industrial deployment and compliant application of educational AI systems. To address these research gaps, we systematically establish the conceptual definition, mathematical formalization, and five core attributes of reverse attribution for KT sequence learning scenarios, and propose RA4KT, a model-agnostic post-hoc explainable framework specifically tailored to the sequential characteristics and pedagogical prior constraints of educational scenarios. RA4KT unifies attribution validity, modification minimalism, and pedagogical coherence via a multi-objective loss function integrating knowledge concept prior correlations, enforces intervention actionability through an Actionability Mask hard constraint mechanism, and connects model explanation to teaching intervention via a Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP)-variant post-processing module that generates cognitively aligned ordered teaching paths. Systematic experiments on two large-scale real-world educational datasets (XES3G5M and ASSISTments2017) show that RA4KT outperforms mainstream reverse attribution baselines (DiCE, CETD, CMKT, RCKT) on core metrics (Validity, Sparsity, Pedagogical Relevance, Robustness), with relative improvements of the best-performing RA4KT-gs variant over the strongest baseline on each core metric ranging from 2.1% to 16.6% (per-metric, per-dataset values and calculation details in Tables 2–3 and Section "Main experimental results and analysis"), maintains stable performance in long-sequence scenarios, and delivers significant knowledge mastery efficiency gains in offline intervention simulations, especially for students with low initial mastery levels. This work fills the technical gap between black-box KT prediction and actionable intervention schemes, providing a technical pathway toward interpretable engineering deployment of educational AI, with potential extensibility to high-stakes time-series scenarios including healthcare, financial risk control, and industrial predictive maintenance, subject to domain-specific validation.

title: Accelerated CO2 curing of fly ash–GGBS self-compacting geopolymer concrete: experimental, environmental and explainable machine learning assessment
abstract: The construction industry is under increasing pressure to develop sustainable cement-free materials with lower carbon emissions and enhanced durability. In this study, a high-performance self-compacting geopolymer concrete (SCGC) was developed using Fly Ash (FA) and Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag (GGBS) as binder precursors, combined with accelerated CO 2 curing to improve engineering performance and environmental sustainability. Five binder compositions with varying FA-to-GGBS ratios were prepared under ambient and carbon curing conditions, resulting in ten experimental mixtures. The fresh properties of the developed mixtures were evaluated according to EFNARC guidelines, while mechanical performance was assessed through compressive, split tensile, and flexural strength tests at 7, 28, and 56 days. Durability performance was investigated using water absorption, sorptivity, acid resistance, and sulfate resistance tests. Carbon sequestration behavior was quantified through mass gain analysis, while microstructural evolution was examined using Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS), X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR). The environmental performance of the developed SCGC mixtures was evaluated through cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) using openLCA. In addition, machine learning (ML) models including Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were developed to predict compressive strength. The results demonstrated that accelerated CO₂ curing significantly enhanced the fresh, mechanical, and durability performance of SCGC. Among all investigated mixtures, the M3-C mixture exhibited the optimum performance, achieving a compressive strength of 68.4 MPa at 56 days along with significantly reduced water absorption and sorptivity. Microstructural investigations confirmed enhanced geopolymerization, pore refinement, and carbonate formation in carbon-cured mixtures. LCA revealed that M3-C exhibited the lowest global warming potential (148.8 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 ), low embodied energy (2384 MJ/m 3 ), and the lowest carbon intensity (2.38 kg CO 2 /MPa·m 3 ) among all investigated mixtures. ML analysis demonstrated excellent predictive capability, with XGBoost showing the highest prediction accuracy (R 2 = 0.983). The integrated experimental, microstructural, environmental, and data-driven findings confirm that carbon-cured slag-modified SCGC has strong potential as a sustainable next-generation construction material for low-carbon infrastructure applications.
