title: Impact of medical law education based on the IRAC model on the medical law reasoning of internal medicine and surgery residents
abstract: Medical-legal challenges have intensified over the past decade, leading to substantial financial burdens and psychological distress for physicians. Literature reviews indicate that the medical law skills of specialists and residents, particularly their medical law reasoning abilities, are insufficient, underscoring the necessity for appropriate educational interventions. This study aimed to determine the impact of medical law education based on the IRAC (Issue, Rule, Analysis, Conclusion) model on the medical law reasoning of internal medicine and surgery residents at Zanjan University of Medical Sciences. A quasi-experimental study employing a non-randomized control group with a pretest-posttest design was conducted. The ADDIE model guided the design of the educational intervention. Residents were non-randomly assigned to an intervention group ( n = 27) receiving IRAC-based training and a control group ( n = 27) receiving no such training. Attitudes toward medical law reasoning were assessed using the Medical Law Reasoning Attitude Questionnaire (MLRAQ), while cognitive medical law reasoning was assessed using the participant-completed, scenario-based Medical Law Reasoning Skill Test (MLRST), which measures respondents’ reasoning judgments in hypothetical medico-legal scenarios. Data were analyzed using independent t-test, paired t-test, Chi-square, and Welch. No statistically significant differences were observed between the groups in baseline total attitude scores ( P = 0.213) or total medical law reasoning skill scores ( P = 0.572). Posttest results, however, revealed significant differences favoring the intervention group in total attitude scores (101.48 ± 9.32 vs. 82.63 ± 13.08; P < 0.001) and all its subscales. Similarly, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher total medical law reasoning skill scores posttest (79.00 ± 8.27 vs. 58.81 ± 7.39; P < 0.001) across all subscales. The primary between-group analysis of pretest-to-posttest change confirmed these improvements for both outcomes ( P < 0.001), and supplementary Welch’s tests on posttest scores were consistent. The IRAC-based medical law education intervention was associated with significant improvements in residents’ measured attitudes and cognitive reasoning scores. This model offers a practical framework for medical educators and curriculum planners to employ creative, integrated, model-based, and active learning strategies to enhance legal reasoning competencies. Ultimately, fostering these skills may help reduce future legal disputes, mitigate physicians’ criminal and civil liabilities, and ensure better adherence to patient rights.

title: Probabilistic representation learning of baseline transcriptomes enables prediction and pathway-level interpretation of anticancer drug responses
abstract: Baseline transcriptomes can predict anticancer drug response, but their high dimensionality complicates pathway-level interpretation. We developed a probabilistic representation learning framework using a reusable variational autoencoder (VAE) latent space to prioritize response-associated factors by aggregate importance and drug preferentiality. Across five reference drugs, leakage-free repeated cross-validation showed that gene-level Ridge regression performed best, whereas 64-dimensional latent representations retained predictive signal after compression. In a separate interpretation VAE fitted to 939 cancer cell lines, six aggregate-importance candidates were bootstrap-robust within the fixed representation and were associated with immune/inflammatory, oncogenic, cell-cycle, stress-response, and cellular-processing programs. Drug-preferential candidates lacked factor-level bootstrap robustness, although several pathway associations remained supported after lineage adjustment. Five independent VAE refits showed partial gene-program concordance but seed-sensitive axes, while a principal component analysis baseline supported stable factor selection and pathway annotation. As an exploratory application, baseline transcriptomes from 15 QAL333-tested cell lines were projected into the fixed VAE without encoder retraining. QAL333-prioritized factors were associated with inflammatory, oncogenic, cellular-processing, and microenvironment-related pathways. The two-model zebrafish xenograft comparison remained descriptive and hypothesis-generating. These findings support reusable, stability-aware latent-space analysis as a framework for pathway-level hypothesis generation from high-dimensional transcriptomic drug-response data.

title: Latent-aligned scalable interpolant transformer for controllable chest X-ray synthesis
abstract: Controllable chest X-ray (CXR) synthesis requires control over both semantic findings and their spatial relationship to thoracic anatomy. Text-conditioned generative models can specify disease labels or report-level descriptions but often provide limited control over pathology location and extent. We introduce LatAlignCXR, which represents anatomical layout, pathology location, and residual appearance within a structured latent space. Text prompts, reference radiographs, and user-defined coordinates are mapped to this representation, from which anatomical, pathology, and thoracic structural priors are decoded to condition a scalable interpolant transformer (SiT). The same representation supports text-, image-, and coordinate-conditioned synthesis. On MIMIC-CXR, LatAlignCXR achieved the highest anatomical Dice (0.6564), the lowest Fréchet distance in three of four feature spaces, and the highest pneumonia-localization consistency (Dice 0.1385, IoU 0.0741). In a blinded radiologist evaluation, LatAlignCXR received mean ratings of 4.63 for pathology consistency and 4.50 for spatial consistency, compared with 3.63 and 3.37 for Cheff, respectively. In downstream classification, synthetic augmentation increased accuracy from 69.0% to 76.0% with 1000 real images, with smaller and non-monotonic effects as real-data availability increased. These findings support structured latent conditioning for spatially controllable CXR synthesis, particularly for pathology representation and spatial consistency.

title: Plasma metabolomics reveals systemic alterations associated with cardiac surgery and identifies candidate predictors of postoperative outcomes: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is associated with systemic metabolic alterations related to stress and immune responses. We aimed to map these dynamics through perioperative metabolomics. Furthermore, we assessed whether baseline metabolites predict postoperative outcomes. Plasma was sampled pre- and post-surgery in a discovery (n = 98) and validation cohort (n = 24). Targeted metabolomics was performed with the Biocrates MxP Quant 500XL kit. Statistical analysis involved principal component analysis, linear mixed effects models, and machine learning-based approaches. The plasma metabolome exhibited marked pre- to post-surgery alterations, primarily driven by postoperative lipid reduction. Baseline metabolic profiles showed no global separation between outcome groups. Individual preoperative metabolites however demonstrated exploratory evidence of higher discriminative performance than established biomarkers (CRP, urea) and clinical risk scores for prolonged ICU stay (> 3 days) in the discovery cohort (n = 22 events). External validation showed discrimination comparable to conventional parameters, although precision was limited by only five outcome events. Our findings highlight substantial metabolic alterations following CPB and suggest baseline metabolites as candidate predictors of postoperative outcomes, supporting further evaluation as prognostic markers in larger cohorts. Trial registration: The study was registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00016493, https://drks.de/search/en/trial/DRKS00016493 ) on 15 March 2019.

title: Bi-directional ANN framework for forward and inverse design of microstrip antenna in RF applications
abstract: In this paper, a bidirectional machine learning (ML)-based framework is introduced to predict the performance parameters such as \(|S_{11}|\) , VSWR and radiation pattern in two planes (XZ and YZ), radiation efficiency, and total efficiency, as well as to estimate the design variables including the patch and feed line dimensions (L, W, L1, and W1) and the dielectric constant ( \( \varepsilon _r \) ) of a quarter-wave transformer (QWT)-microstrip patch (MSP) antenna at an operating frequency of 3 GHz. A Forward Artificial Neural Network (F-ANN) is developed to predict performance parameters based on given design variables. At the same time, an inverse artificial neural network (I-ANN) is implemented to estimate design variables from the desired performance parameter. This technique involves designing, training, and optimizing an MSP antenna in real time. The F-ANN architecture has five input features and one output, whereas the I-ANN has three input features and five outputs. Model evaluation is done using the R-squared (R 2 ) and mean squared error (MSE). The F-ANN and I-ANN achieve R 2 values of 0.99 and minimal MSE values. The estimated design variables from inverse modeling are further re-verified using retro simulation and compared with simulated and predicted results; the developed models \(|S_{11}|\) and VSWR parameters are also validated with measured performance. Both F-ANN and I-ANN predict and estimate parameters with higher accuracy. As a comparative model, the prediction of the ANN framework is compared with two other regression-based models, namely Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). All the developed models are able to predict the performance with good prediction accuracy.

title: User perceptions of serendipity-control, cognitive-level labelling, and explanation features in an LLM-based academic article recommender: a single-institution pilot study
abstract: Serendipity in recommender systems has been studied mainly as an algorithmic property rather than as an interface-design question. This pilot study examined how undergraduates perceived three interface features of ScholarMind, a prototype in which a large language model (LLM) generates article recommendations directly: accuracy and serendipity sliders, LLM-assigned Bloom’s taxonomy labels, and an explanation panel of LLM-generated weights labelled as SHAP values. Forty-one students at one institution in Pakistan completed a task requiring use of all three features, followed by a self-report battery (ResQue, SUS, UEQ-S and three unvalidated feature scales). Mean feature ratings lay on the agreement side of the midpoint (3.62–3.80 on 5-point scales), but reverse-worded items correlated negatively with their scales, indicating acquiescent responding. Exploratory correlations linked explanation-panel perceptions with perceived trust (rₛ = 0.47, 95% CI [0.18, 0.68]) and Bloom’s-label perceptions with perceived usefulness (rₛ = 0.51, 95% CI [0.23, 0.71]). Perceived usability was below benchmark (SUS = 56.6 vs. 68), and preference relative to Google Scholar was evenly split. Inspection of the source code showed that the sliders only reorder a fixed set of generated articles. The findings describe perceptions of an interface prototype, not recommender performance.

title: Multi-omic cancer subtype clustering with random-walk-refined cross-view contrastive learning
abstract: Cancer heterogeneity complicates precision oncology, and robust multi-omic subtyping remains challenging. Existing contrastive integration methods often force heterogeneous omics into a single shared latent space and treat all non-matching samples as negatives, which can suppress modality-specific structure and separate biologically similar patients. We present Subtype-DIVIDE, a self-supervised multi-view contrastive framework for integrative cancer subtyping. The model encodes each omic modality separately and performs target-conditioned cross-view alignment, using the target modality’s affinity structure to guide inter-view consistency. To reduce false negatives, Subtype-DIVIDE further refines contrastive supervision with per-omic random-walk soft-positive masks constructed from modality-specific affinity graphs. Across nine TCGA cohorts spanning copy number, DNA methylation, mRNA, and miRNA data, Subtype-DIVIDE achieved statistically significant survival separation in all datasets and the highest mean number of clinically enriched variables among the compared methods. Cox models, leave-one-cluster-out analyses, and technical covariate tests supported the clinical relevance and robustness of the inferred subtypes. Ablation studies showed that cross-view alignment is essential, while diffusion-based soft positives improved robustness. A KIRC case study identified coherent subtype programs involving metabolism, vascular and inflammatory signaling, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and epithelial transport. External validation on two independent cohorts, performed without hyperparameter retuning, supported the generalizability of the inferred subtypes. In 222 CPTAC-3 clear-cell renal carcinoma cases, the subtypes were significantly associated with pathologic stage and T category across all training repeats and recapitulated the KIRC subtype programs. In 1,980 METABRIC breast tumors, they consistently showed significant survival separation and enrichment for age, nodal status, and stage across all repeats.

title: Biologically interpretable multi-scale feature engineering with two-stage pruning for tomato leaf disease classification
abstract: Automated tomato leaf disease classification remains challenging when different diseases exhibit similar color, texture, and necrotic symptoms. To improve pathological interpretability while maintaining competitive classification performance, this study proposes a multi-scale feature engineering framework that explicitly represents disease symptoms at both global and local scales. A composite Excess Green (ExG)-Triangle segmentation strategy is first used to preserve green, chlorotic, and diseased leaf tissues, achieving a Dice coefficient of 92.45% and a Recall of 99.40% on manually annotated leaf masks. Color, multi-scale Local Binary Pattern (LBP), shape, and lesion descriptors are then integrated, with a Lesion Spatial Logic (LSL) descriptor introduced to characterize the relative allocation of necrotic tissue between the marginal and interior regions of the leaf. A two-stage pruning strategy based on permutation importance and Pearson correlation reduces the feature dimensionality from 296 to 164, corresponding to a 44.6% reduction. The pruned Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieves 96.44% accuracy on the independent PlantVillage test set, while Early Blight Recall increases from 88.50% to 92.00%. An exact McNemar test shows no statistically significant difference between the full and pruned SVM models ( \(\:p=0.644\) ), and five-fold cross-validation shows limited performance variability across training partitions. Modern pretrained CNNs achieve higher absolute accuracy on PlantVillage, whereas the proposed framework provides explicit pathological feature representation, a compact classifier, and lower memory and model-storage requirements. These findings support pathology-guided feature engineering as an interpretable approach for tomato disease classification under controlled conditions, while further validation under greenhouse and field conditions remains necessary.

title: Hybrid GWO–GA optimized LSTM–MLP framework for highly accurate palmer drought severity index prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of the Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) is essential for drought monitoring, climate-risk assessment, and the effective management of water resources. This study proposes a hybrid Long Short-Term Memory–Multilayer Perceptron (LSTM–MLP) model for PDSI prediction, integrated with a Grey Wolf Optimizer–Genetic Algorithm (GWO–GA) optimization framework. The model is evaluated using a climate dataset comprising 864 observations characterized by scenario information and multiple climatic variables, including pr , tas , tasmin , tasmax , and srad . The predictive performance of the proposed approach is assessed using the mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), median absolute error (MedAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination ( \(R^2\) ). Furthermore, its performance is compared with several deep-learning architectures, including convolutional neural network (CNN), LSTM, gated recurrent unit (GRU), bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and bidirectional GRU (BiGRU) models. The proposed LSTM–MLP model achieved an MSE of 0.0004, RMSE of 0.0201, MAE of 0.0169, MedAE of 0.0160, MAPE of 0.0018, and an \(R^2\) of 99.97%. In comparison, the CNN, LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, and BiGRU models achieved \(R^2\) values of 94.58%, 90.84%, 88.70%, 87.39%, and 86.48%, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed LSTM–MLP framework provides highly accurate PDSI predictions and consistently improves predictive performance relative to the investigated benchmark deep-learning models. The findings give a focus to the potential of the proposed hybrid modeling framework as an effective data-driven approach for PDSI prediction and drought-related climate analysis.

title: A deep learning method for ECG heartbeat classification based on Gaussian features
abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is a vital tool for diagnosing and screening cardiovascular diseases. Accurately extracting ECG signal features is key to improving the accuracy of arrhythmia classification. To address the limitations of traditional methods in terms of feature extraction precision and discrimination capability, this study proposes an ECG signal classification method based on Gaussian features. First, the R-peak is identified via the visibility graph algorithm, and its prominence is computed to locate the onset and offset of the P, Q, R, S, and T waves across the heartbeat waveform. Five Gaussian components are then fitted to the segmented signal, yielding 16 highly discriminative features for classification. Furthermore, an AMH–BiLSTM architecture is developed by integrating convolutional neural networks, bidirectional long short-term memory, and multi-head attention mechanisms, with two fully connected layers performing the final classification task. To address class imbalance in the MIT–BIH Arrhythmia Database, the SMOTE algorithm is employed to oversample minority classes. Moreover, over 10 independent random seeds, the proposed method achieves a mean classification accuracy of 97.93%, precision of 98.10%, recall of 97.92%, and F1-score of 97.99%, with a mean AUC of 99.90%. Compared to the baseline model under the same experimental setup, our proposed method has shown some improvements. In addition, we also provide reference comparisons with recent representative methods, and our method demonstrates competitive classification performance under comparable evaluation protocols.

title: Technology acceptance mediates associations between pre-service physical education teachers’ AI-TPACK and study engagement and behavioral intentions in digital teaching
abstract: Against the backdrop of artificial intelligence (AI) reshaping the educational landscape, the digital transformation of physical education has placed greater demands on preservice physical education teachers’ (PSPETs’) capacity to integrate technology. However, research remains limited on the effects of pres-ervice physical education teachers’ artificial intelligence technological pedagogical content knowledge (PSPETs AI-TPACK) on their study engagement (SE) and behavioral intentions (BI) in digital teaching, as well as on the role played by technology acceptance (TA) in these relationships.This study involved 1,144 undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled in physical education, physical education teaching, or physical education and training programmes at five higher education institutions in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province. Using adapted scales, data were collected on PSPETs AI-TPACK, TA, SE, and BI. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was then employed to examine the relationships among these variables and the mediating effects. The findings showed that PSPETs AI-TPACK significantly and positively predicted both SE and BI in digital teaching. TA played a significant partial mediating role in the relationships between PSPETs AI-TPACK and SE, and between PSPETs AI-TPACK and BI. These results indicate that PSPETs AI-TPACK can promote PSPETs’ SE and BI both directly and indirectly by enhancing their TA. This study extends the theoretical understanding of the relationships between PSPETs AI-TPACK and SE and BI in digital physical education teaching, while also providing empirical evidence for improving preservice physical education teacher education in higher education institutions. Higher education institutions should incorporate AI-based instructional design and practice into physical education teacher education curricula, implement tiered and progressive technology training, create authentic digital teaching contexts, and enhance PSPETs’ TA through resource provision and exemplary applications. These measures can, in turn, strengthen PSPETs’ SE and BI in using AI technologies to support physical education teaching.

title: GIS-MCDA-based groundwater recharge potential zonation and artificial recharge site identification in coastal Ramanathapuram, India
abstract: In this study, an effort was made to demarcate the zones of groundwater recharge potential along with the identification of preliminary candidate locations for the construction of artificial recharge structures (ARS) in the coastal region of Ramanathapuram District, Tamil Nadu State of India through an integrated approach of GIS & MCDA technique. There are eight thematic layers like rainfall, lineament density, drainage density, geomorphology, lithology, soil, slope, and land use/land cover (LULC) used in this study depending upon the influence of each factor on the recharge of groundwater. The random forest technique was adopted to prepare LULC map. The recharge potential zones generated from the analysis were categorized into very high, high, moderate, low, and very low recharge potential zones. The very high potential zone occupies 38.94% (1621.38 km 2 ) of the district, followed by high (22.23%; 925.64 km 2 ), moderate (19.12%; 796.29 km 2 ), low (11.00%; 458.14 km 2 ) and very low (8.71%; 362.55 km 2 ). From the above spatial distribution, it can be seen that rainfall, lineament density, drainage density, geomorphology and favorable lithology and soil conditions have a strong influence on the recharge potential, where the relatively favorable zones occur in central, northern, coastal and deltaic areas of the district. Preliminary candidate locations for construction of artificial recharge structures like check dams, percolation tanks, nala bunds have been determined based on groundwater potential zones, hydrogeomorphological features and drainage conditions. The aforementioned sites are screening level locations that need to be validated through field hydrogeology before their application. The findings of this study are useful for spatial planning for conservation of groundwater and artificial recharge operations in the semi-arid coastal region of Ramanathapuram District.

title: Mathematical analysis of a reaction-diffusion gambling information diffusion model
abstract: This study develops and analyses a non-linear reaction–diffusion model for information spread, motivated by gambling-related information diffusion. The model is formulated as a susceptible–exposed–excessive–skeptical (SEIZ) system, in which individuals transition between information-related states through exposure, interaction, engagement, and resistance, while spatial diffusion captures heterogeneity across the population. The mathematical analysis establishes the existence, uniqueness, positivity, and boundedness of solutions, and derive both gambling-free and endemic equilibria. Two threshold quantities, \(\mathcal {R}_0^{ext} = \beta /\varepsilon\) and \(\mathcal {R}_0 = \alpha /\sigma\) , are obtained for the non-excessive and excessive states, respectively, yielding conditions for the persistence or elimination of these states. Diffusion-driven stability further assess how spatial effects modify the dynamics of the corresponding homogeneous system. For numerical analysis, the reaction–diffusion system is discretized using a semi-implicit Euler finite-difference method and the resulting non-linear system is solved by Newton’s method. The numerical experiments support the theoretical consistency, stability, and convergence of the method. Sensitivity analysis demonstrates that variations in the parameters entering the threshold quantities directly change the predicted qualitative dynamics. Although framed around gambling-related information, the main contribution of this work is the formulation and analysis of a general non-linear reaction–diffusion model that can be adapted to a broad class of spatial information and behavioral diffusion processes.

title: A federated learning framework for anomaly detection in electric vehicle charging networks
abstract: Charging networks for electric vehicles (EVs) are also coming under attack from cyber threats such as Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks, unauthorized access, load balancing the network, and sudden charging network disruptions. The traditional centralized anomaly-detection and authentication schemes are not suitable for large-scale, geographically distributed and privacy-focused charging infrastructure, as they include SPOF, high communication overhead and limited adaptability to the changing threats. This paper proposes a federated-learning (FL) framework, which is composed of (i) a dual-layer authentication architecture, namely a Global Authentication Protocol (GAP) using TLS with a fallback Local Authentication Protocol (LAP), and (ii) a heterogeneous pipeline of anomaly detections, such as supervised models (Random Forest, Decision Trees), unsupervised models (Autoencoders, Principal Component Analysis), and regression-based normal-behavior forecasters (Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression), with BERT-based log preprocessing. To ensure the parameters of the neural-network part of the model can be meaningfully aggregated, only the Autoencoder and the BERT-based log encoder are being aggregated using Federated Averaging. To achieve this aggregation for the other models, either the tree-based model or the PCA model are replaced by the global model after each round, which is referred to as a model-replacement strategy. A combined real-world dataset (ACN (Caltech and JPL sites) and ElaadNL (snapshot) was used together with a simulated dataset of 500 K events generated using ACN-Sim. DoS, unauthorized-access, load-balancing and abrupt-charging-disruption events were synthesized using a formal threat model and attack-injection procedure. To compare the baselines, all baselines (Hybrid IDS, System used in and a protocol-compliance reference implementation of ISO 15118) were re-implemented and tested using the same data splits, preprocessing and hardware. Across five repeated runs, the proposed framework achieved a mean detection accuracy of 95.4% (95% CI: 94.6–96.2%) on ACN, 92.1% (91.2–93.0%) on ElaadNL, and 90.3% (89.2–91.4%) on the simulated set, with mean latency of 205 ms (ACN), 223 ms (ElaadNL), and 248 ms (simulated). The framework has been tested to support an average of 1,500 concurrent charging sessions and achieved a measured 28.7% decrease in communication costs from a centralized baseline. We further study the framework’s ability to resist model-poisoning attacks through a secure aggregation mechanism (coordinate-wise median, with a fallback to a trimmed-mean algorithm). We also discuss the question of compatibility of the framework with Distributed Ledger Technologies (DLTs) for auditable federated updates. There are clear specifications and open discussion regarding the limitations of dataset diversity, real-time live-network validation, and lack of differential privacy.

title: Adaptive Knowledge Fusion Ensemble (AKFE) for Flow Zone Indicator prediction and Hydraulic Flow Unit classification from well logs
abstract: Accurate hydraulic flow characterization in uncored reservoir intervals remains challenging because the Flow Zone Indicator (FZI) requires core-derived porosity and permeability, which are available only at discrete depths. This study introduces an Adaptive Knowledge Fusion Ensemble (AKFE) for continuous FZI prediction and subsequent Hydraulic Flow Unit (HFU) classification from conventional well logs. AKFE integrates well-log features, heterogeneous model predictions, model-disagreement information, and ensemble consensus through a leakage-controlled meta-learning framework. Seven base learners are combined using a CatBoost meta-regressor, and the resulting FZI predictions are classified into four interpreter-defined HFUs using a Gaussian mixture model (GMM). The framework was developed using 1,072 depth-matched core observations from two cored wells and independently evaluated on three blind wells. AKFE outperformed Simple Averaging, Weighted Averaging, and Conventional Stacking, achieving an R² of 0.991, RMSE of 0.0374, MAE of 0.0291, and MAPE of 6.7936. Compared with conventional stacking, AKFE reduced RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by approximately 26.8, 29.7, and 50.0%, respectively. Blind-well application further demonstrated that the predicted FZI profiles preserved meaningful variations in hydraulic quality and yielded consistent HFU patterns supported by cumulative-FZI and porosity–permeability analyses. The results demonstrate that integrating geological context with collective model behavior can improve the transferability of machine-learning-based hydraulic characterization to uncored reservoir intervals.
