title: Intelligent clinical decision support system for intracranial aneurysm lesion-based detection using biomedical imaging data
abstract: An intracranial aneurysm (IA) is a type of cerebrovascular condition that occurs due to focal bulging or expansion in the wall of a cerebral artery, most frequently affecting the internal carotid artery. An IA is seemingly connected with conditions such as fibrous dysplasia, adult-dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), and coarctation of aorta. A ruptured brain aneurysm can result in a severe and life-threatening subarachnoid hemorrhage if not treated early, often leading to long-lasting neurological damage and a higher chance of death. However, the traditional diagnostic technique is time-consuming, and it necessitates a trained and skilled medical practitioner. Hence, building an automated model to help physicians precisely detect IA can reduce the clinicians’ burden. Recently, deep learning has gained significant interest in the domain of medical imaging as it automatically learns patterns and accurately detects several types of diseases, such as IAs. Therefore, this article introduces a Clinical Decision Support System for Intracranial Aneurysm Lesion-Based Detection (CDSS-IALD). The main purpose of this work is to develop a robust system that can automatically detect and identify intracranial aneurysms using medical imaging data to assist clinicians with treatment decisions. Initially, the proposed CDSS-IALD model pre-processes the input biomedical images using image normalization, noise reduction, contrast improvement, and skull stripping to refine image quality and consistency for subsequent analysis. Following that, a ConvNeXt hierarchical model is employed for feature extraction, which effectively extracts local details and global context from pre-processed images. Finally, these extracted representations are then forwarded to a spiking neural network, which performs accurate aneurysm detection and classification. To ensure the enhanced performance of the CDSS-IALD system, extensive experiments were conducted on the benchmark Intracranial Aneurysm Dataset. The experimental outcomes clearly demonstrate the betterment of the proposed CDSS-IALD system over the other approaches in detecting and localizing intracranial aneurysms from biomedical imaging.

title: Fresh and mechanical properties of hemp fiber-reinforced concrete: an experimental dosage study with multi-output artificial neural network modelling of mechanical strength
abstract: The construction sector’s dependence on carbon-intensive binders and synthetic reinforcement has intensified interest in plant-based fibers as sustainable crack-control reinforcement for concrete. This study experimentally characterises the fresh and 28-day mechanical properties of hemp (Cannabis sativa bast) fiber-reinforced concrete (HFRC) and develops a multi-output Artificial Neural Network (ANN) that predicts its compressive, splitting tensile and flexural strength from fiber dosage. The physical programme comprised eleven dosage levels (0–2.0% by volume in 0.2% steps) of 5% NaOH-treated fiber (aspect ratio ≈ 235) in a fixed M30 base mix (cement 340 kg/m³, water–cement ratio 0.45, superplasticizer 7.48 kg/m³). Slump, compaction factor and Vee-Bee time were measured in triplicate, and three cubes, cylinders and prisms per mix were tested to IS 516; dosage effects were assessed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey and Dunnett comparisons. The 33 physical specimen results per property were kept distinct from 1,100 augmented rows generated from truncated-normal distributions bounded by each mix’s measured mean, standard deviation and range. A 64–32 ReLU multi-output perceptron was evaluated by leave-one-dosage-out cross-validation over ten seeds and benchmarked against polynomial, spline, ridge, tree-ensemble and single-output models. Fiber dosage significantly affected all three strengths ( p < 0.001). Compressive strength peaked at 0.6% (32.8 MPa, + 5.8%), statistically indistinguishable from 0.4 to 0.8%, while splitting tensile and flexural strength peaked at 1.2% (3.95 MPa, + 33.9%; 5.50 MPa, + 31.0%) within statistically equivalent plateaus. On unseen dosages the ANN reproduced the experimental means with RMSE of 0.36, 0.09 and 0.13 MPa, respectively, and outperformed three single-output networks, although a cubic smoothing spline was equally or more accurate. Slump fell from 95 mm to 40 mm and Vee-Bee time rose from 3 s to 20 s across the dosage range, confirming a workability–reinforcement trade-off. The results support hemp fiber dosages of about 0.6–1.2% and show that, for a single-variable dosage study, the multi-output ANN is best used as an exploratory response-curve model rather than as a substitute for physical testing.

title: Hard attention mechanism integrated with VGG16 for high-precision tomato leaf disease classification
abstract: Tomato diseases represent a major threat to agricultural productivity and global food security. Early and accurate identification of these diseases is essential for effective crop management and yield preservation. In this study, we propose a hard attention–enhanced VGG16 model for automatic tomato leaf disease identification. By integrating a hard attention mechanism into the VGG16 architecture, the proposed model is able to focus on the most informative regions of the input images, thereby improving its capability to discriminate between healthy and diseased tomato leaves. The proposed approach is evaluated using a publicly available dataset of tomato leaf images. Experimental results demonstrate that the hard attention–based VGG16 model significantly improves classification performance compared to the standard VGG16 architecture and several existing deep learning models. In particular, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 96.0%, outperforming the baseline VGG16 model, which achieves 92.3% accuracy on the same dataset. Furthermore, the integration of the attention mechanism enhances the interpretability of the model by highlighting the image regions that contribute most to the prediction process. This explainability provides valuable insights into the model’s decision-making process, making it a reliable and transparent tool for intelligent plant disease identification systems.

title: FS-VMADW: a frequency–spatial vision mamba framework for dual watermarking of medical MRI images
abstract: Secure transmission and copyright protection of medical images require watermarking methods that preserve image quality and enable reliable payload recovery. However, the currently available deep watermarking architectures either encode only a single watermark or use convolutional networks with inherently restricted receptive fields, which limits their ability to capture long-range anatomical dependencies in medical images. Moreover, spatial modeling alone does not explicitly capture the frequency characteristics that influence watermark imperceptibility and robustness. This work proposes FS-VMADW - a Frequency-Spatial Vision Mamba Dual Watermarking architecture for abdominal MRI security. The proposed encoder combines the Vision Mamba spatial branch with a four-direction selective scan of state-space models applied with linear complexity, along with a two-stage Haar Discrete Wavelet Transform frequency branch, which are fused with a gating module generating location-specific weighting of spatial and frequency feature maps. Two independent spread-spectrum carriers encode two 64-bit binary watermarks, while an adaptively generated Vision Mamba mask controls their embedding. A two-phase training curriculum mitigates the gradient conflict between imperceptibility and extraction fidelity by decoupling the two objectives across successive training phases. Experiments on the CHAOS abdominal MRI benchmark demonstrate PSNR = 42.37 dB, SSIM = 0.9557, NC = 0.9511, BER = 0.0491, and BitAcc = 0.9509 under clean conditions. Controlled backbone comparisons further show that Vision Mamba outperforms CNN and Transformer alternatives, while the addition of DWT provides further improvements in both imperceptibility and watermark recovery. These results demonstrate that long-range spatial modeling and multi-scale frequency information provide complementary benefits for dual watermarking of medical images.

title: Quad-directional frequency-aware state space modeling for low-light image enhancement
abstract: Low-Light Image Enhancement (LLIE) is a fundamental inverse problem in computational photography characterised by spatially non-uniform underexposure, amplified photon shot noise, and inter-channel colour imbalance. State-of-the-art (SOTA) Transformer based methods achieve compelling global context modelling but impose quadratic self-attention complexity, precluding efficient deployment at high resolutions. We present QDFA-SSM, a novel end-to-end framework built entirely on selective State Space Models (SSMs). Three principled architectural components constitute our design. First, a Quad-Directional Visual Mamba Encoder (QD-VME) scans 2D feature maps along four spatial orientations horizontal forward/backward and vertical forward/backward recovering isotropic long-range illumination context at strictly \(\mathscr {O}(N)\) complexity via hardware efficient parallel scanning. Second, a Frequency-Aware SSM Decoder (FA-SSMD) decomposes decoder features into low- and high-frequency spectral bands via 2D FFT, applying independent SSM chains to each band to separately optimise global luminance consistency and local texture fidelity, preventing cross-band interference. Third, a Spatially-Adaptive Illumination Modulator (SAIM) estimates pixel-wise enhancement weight maps conditioned on local Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) maps, concentrating correction capacity on severely underexposed regions without requiring additional supervision. Evaluated on the LOL-v1 benchmark, QDFA-SSM attains PSNR = 25.15 dB and SSIM = 0.863, which improves upon the strongest prior selective-SSM baselines MMamba-LLIE and LatentDark by \(+0.67\) dB and \(+0.42\) dB respectively, and upon the Retinex-guided Transformer baselines represented by Retinexformer and LLFormer. These gains are obtained with 1.340 M parameters and 32.105 GFLOPs at 41.53 FPS on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU. It may be noted that the proposed model is not the smallest or the fastest among the compared methods; rather, it is reported here as offering the most favourable balance between restoration accuracy and computational cost.

title: Bio-electrochemical swarm intelligence with quantum constrained graph learning for distributed battery optimization in urban microgrids
abstract: The integration of distributed battery storage in urban microgrids is becoming increasingly common. Yet, most existing methods for optimizing urban microgrid operation are incapable of jointly representing battery physics, device-to-device relationships, and the temporal variability of intermittent renewable generation. Conventional swarm and deterministic methods also commonly rely on random initialization, homogeneous agent behavior, or post-hoc constraint handling. Therefore, this research proposes a unifying framework that integrates five key components into a single pipeline: (1) Bio-Electrochemical Swarm Field Initialization (BESFI); (2) Adaptive Multi-Species Co-Evolutionary Swarm Routing (AMSCESR); (3) a Spatio-Temporal Energy Diffusion Graph Transformer (STED-GT); (4) Quantum-Inspired Stability-Constrained Optimization (QISCO); and (5) a Digital Twin Reinforcement Validation Engine (DT-RVE). The novelty lies in the closed coupling of physics-aware initialization, role-diverse swarm search, relational graph learning, in-loop stability filtering, and digital-twin reinforcement validation rather than in any isolated module. On the reported 25-node urban microgrid testbed, the framework achieved 95.8% dispatch accuracy, 94.6% energy efficiency, ± 3.7% voltage deviation, ± 0.019 Hz frequency deviation, 10.6% capacity fade, and 2.3 s supervisory adaptation latency. These results indicate improved load balancing, grid stability, battery-life preservation, and adaptive operation within the evaluated simulation conditions.

title: Transfer learning enables automated pituitary gland segmentation on brain MRI in 6-year-old children
abstract: Pediatric pituitary gland (PG) segmentation is challenging owing to anatomical variability and the limited availability of labeled datasets, which restricts the direct application of adult-trained deep learning models. We aimed to develop and validate a specialized transfer learning (TL) pipeline for automated PG segmentation in 6-year-old children and to test two competing predictions, persistence versus catch-up, about the association of perinatal factors with PG volume at school age. A three-dimensional U-Net model pre-trained on 153 adult T1-weighted magnetic resonance images was adapted to a pediatric cohort of 61 children, using consensus ground truth established by majority agreement among three experts. The TL strategy incorporated dynamic region-of-interest (ROI) cropping derived from consensus centroids, ± 8-voxel spatial jitter, and extensive 20-fold data augmentation to improve model robustness. On an independent test set of 15 children evaluated with label-independent ROI placement, the TL model (Dice = 0.83 ± 0.23) significantly outperformed the adult-only model (Dice = 0.72 ± 0.22; P = 0.0002) in the evaluation that included one localization failure. Mean absolute relative volume error was 17.1% and the volume intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.48. Ablating the spatial-jitter component showed that it conferred robustness to ROI placement error rather than peak accuracy: with the ROI placed at the training-set mean centroid, the jitter-free variant fell to a Dice of 0.61 ± 0.38 whereas the full model reached 0.83 ± 0.23 ( P = 0.031). After adjusting for age at scan, the associations of gestational age and birth weight with PG volume were small (partial r = 0.17 and 0.18; 90% confidence interval [CI] − 0.02 to 0.36 and − 0.01 to 0.37), and equivalence testing excluded moderate-to-large residual effects (|partial r| ≥ 0.4; P = 0.021 and P = 0.025), a pattern more compatible with catch-up by school age, although small effects remain undetermined. These findings show that pediatric adaptation improves segmentation and suggest that moderate-to-large persistent perinatal associations with PG volume are unlikely in this cohort.

title: Quality-aware cost minimization for multi-tier LLM routing in heterogeneous data centers
abstract: The rapid expansion of Large Language Model (LLM) inference workloads poses a significant challenge for cloud service providers by increasing operational costs through intensive computational demand. Traditional resource provisioning strategies typically assume homogeneous hardware and static service levels, failing to exploit the economic efficiencies available in heterogeneous data center environments. In this paper, we propose HARP (Heterogeneity-Aware Routing and Provisioning), a cost optimization framework that minimizes operational expenditure for LLM inference services. We introduce a multi-tier quality adaptation strategy that dynamically routes requests across heterogeneous GPU instance types, from legacy to state-of-the-art, under varying Quality of responses (QoR) constraints. We formalize the problem as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) that balances the trade-offs between hardware lease costs and throughput characteristics across GPU tiers. By decoupling strict hardware dependencies from service requirements, HARP allows for intelligent offloading of lower-tier requests to more cost-effective hardware without violating Service Level Objectives (SLOs). Under a throughput estimation model combining public benchmarks with theoretical memory bandwidth scaling estimates, simulations using workload traces and on-demand pricing profiles show up to \(\sim \) 23% lower modeled operational cost than a QoR-cost greedy heuristic (QCGH) routing baseline, with double-digit average savings across the evaluated demand compositions. Our analysis further reveals that these gains are largest in the intermediate QoR regime and that the optimizer systematically matches request complexity to the most cost-effective GPU generation, retaining legacy hardware for lower-quality tiers while reserving premium instances for the most demanding requests, underscoring that economic efficiency stems from heterogeneous instance mixing rather than from uniformly provisioning the highest-capacity hardware.

title: Parametric sensitivity assessment of slip flow and thermophoretic effects on a vertical stretching surface using response surface methodology
abstract: The present study was devoted to the investigation of the effect of velocity slip and energy slip on the magnetohydrodynamic boundary layer flow with special emphasis on thermophoresis under steady flow conditions. The governing partial differential equations are converted to ordinary differential equations using the similarity transformations and then solved numerically by using the bvp4c solver of the MATLAB software. The effects of velocity slip, energy slip, thermophoresis and dipole parameter on velocity and temperature characteristics are systematically investigated. A sensitivity analysis is performed to determine the most influential parameters and to optimize the heat-transfer performance which is one of the novelties of the study. The results reveal that the velocity slip parameter increases from 0.7 to 1.9, significantly impacting the velocity and temperature profiles, which result in approximately 3.3% enhancement in Nusselt number and about 19.3% decline in skin friction. The energy slip parameter also has a significant effect on the temperature distribution and heat-transfer rate, demonstrating its important role in controlling thermal transport. The combined effects of velocity slip and energy slip indicate that velocity slip mainly alters the flow characteristics, while energy slip directly influences the thermal boundary layer and heat transfer. Furthermore, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) demonstrate superior predictive accuracy compared with Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Comparison with previously published results confirms the validity of the present model. Overall, the findings demonstrate that appropriate control of velocity slip and energy slip, together with thermophoretic effects, can provide an effective approach for enhancing and controlling heat transfer in advanced thermal management systems.

title: QSAR-guided generative framework for the discovery of synthetically viable odorants
abstract: The discovery of novel odorant molecules is key for the fragrance and flavor industries, yet efficiently navigating the vast chemical space to identify structures with desirable olfactory properties remains a significant challenge. Generative artificial intelligence offers a promising approach for de novo molecular design but typically requires large sets of molecules to learn from. To address this problem, we present a framework combining a variational autoencoder (VAE) with a quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) model to generate novel odorants from limited training sets of odor molecules. The self-supervised learning capabilities of the VAE allow it to learn SMILES grammar from the ChEMBL database, while its training objective is augmented with a loss term derived from an external QSAR model to structure the latent representation according to odor probability. While the VAE demonstrates high internal consistency in learning the QSAR supervision signal, validation against an external, unseen ground truth dataset (Unique Good Scents) confirms the model generates syntactically valid structures (100% validity achieved via rejection sampling) and 93.9% unique structures. The latent space is effectively structured by odor likelihood, evidenced by a Fréchet ChemNet Distance (FCD) of \(\approx\) 6.96 between generated molecules and known odorants, compared to \(\approx\) 21.6 for the ChEMBL baseline. An ablation of the property head shows that its contribution lies in the density of retrievable structures near an odorant seed — a 4.3-fold increase in distinct novel compounds per seed — rather than in the odor-likeness of any individual compound. Bemis-Murcko analysis shows 2,499 of 6,765 ring-containing candidates, spanning 1,429 distinct core frameworks, are absent from all training sets, while a further 294 molecules, spanning 57 frameworks, independently recover odorant cores found only in an external catalog withheld from training. Generated candidates display physicochemical properties consistent with ground-truth odorants (mean MW \(\sim\) 159 Da, LogP \(\sim\) 1.67) and predicted ADMET profiles comparable to those compounds. Furthermore, quantum-mechanical calculations (GFN2-xTB) verify thermodynamic stability with energy distributions matching known volatiles, and automated retrosynthesis identifies candidate synthesis routes yields valid routesfor 100% of candidates, averaging 2.89 steps from commercially available precursors. This integrated approach provides a novel and systematic methodology for applying generative AI to explore chemical space specifically for the discovery of new candidate odorant molecules.

title: Entropy-Guided Adaptive Confidence-Weighted Complementary Deep Ensemble for osteopenia and osteoporosis classification from knee radiographs
abstract: Automated osteoporosis assessment from knee radiographs remains a challenging computer-aided diagnosis task due to subtle structural differences among normal, osteopenic, and osteoporotic bone patterns, together with the limited availability of transparent and reproducible evaluation frameworks based on publicly accessible datasets. Existing studies predominantly rely on standalone deep learning models or conventional ensemble methods that assume fixed classifier reliability and rarely incorporate predictive uncertainty into decision-level fusion. To address this limitation, this study proposes an Entropy-Guided Adaptive Confidence-Weighted Complementary Deep Ensemble (E-ACW Ensemble) for uncertainty-aware osteoporosis-related knee radiograph classification in both binary and multi-class settings. The proposed framework integrates standardized radiographic preprocessing, fold-specific data augmentation, complementary deep feature learning, and an entropy-guided adaptive fusion strategy. Predictive uncertainty is estimated using Shannon entropy to enable sample-specific confidence weighting during decision-level fusion. The framework was evaluated on publicly available knee radiograph datasets using a rigorous five-fold stratified cross-validation protocol. Comprehensive experimental evaluation, including comparative benchmarking, ablation studies, fold-wise stability analysis, statistical significance testing, and computational efficiency assessment, was conducted to validate predictive performance, robustness, and reproducibility. Among the investigated configurations, the proposed EfficientNetB0 + MobileNetV2 + E-ACW Ensemble achieved the best overall performance, reaching 99.2% accuracy and 99.1% F1-score for binary classification and 98.7% accuracy and 98.5% F1-score for multi-class classification while requiring substantially lower computational cost than the corresponding high-capacity ensemble. These findings demonstrate that entropy-guided adaptive confidence weighting provides an effective and computationally efficient decision-level fusion strategy for osteoporosis-related knee radiograph classification. The proposed E-ACW Ensemble establishes a reproducible framework that can be readily extended to future computer-aided musculoskeletal image analysis and uncertainty-aware medical imaging applications.

title: Machine learning classification of prevalent cardiovascular disease in middle-aged and older Chinese adults with circadian syndrome from CHARLS
abstract: Circadian syndrome (CircS) integrates metabolic abnormalities with sleep and psychological disturbances and is increasingly linked to cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, few studies have applied machine learning (ML) to characterize and identify prevalent CVD specifically in individuals with CircS. This cross-sectional study analyzed 4,091 middle-aged and older adults with CircS from the 2015 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). To eliminate data leakage, missing-data multiple imputation (MICE) was fitted strictly on the partitioned training set (70%, n = 2,863) and applied to the held-out testing set (30%, n = 1,228). Several ML algorithms—generalized linear model (GLM), gradient boosting machine (GBM), random forest (RF), deep learning (DL), and a stacked ensemble—were trained and hyperparameter-tuned with 5-fold cross-validation. Discrimination and calibration were rigorously evaluated using bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for AUC, Brier scores, calibration slope, calibration-in-the-large, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The unweighted prevalence of self-reported CVD in the analytic sample was 26.9% (1,101/4,091). In the independent testing set, the stacked ensemble achieved an AUC of 0.733 (95% CI: 0.703–0.764) and a Brier score of 0.176, which was comparable to RF (AUC = 0.730, 95% CI: 0.699–0.761; Brier = 0.179) and GLM (AUC = 0.728, 95% CI: 0.697–0.759; Brier = 0.176). The AUC differences between the ensemble and RF or GLM were numerically small. Quantitative calibration showed satisfactory agreement, with calibration slopes of 1.100 (95% CI: 0.938–1.286) for the ensemble and 0.960 (95% CI: 0.818–1.130) for GLM. Dyslipidemia, hypertension, kidney disease, and age were the leading variables contributing to CVD classification across models. DCA showed positive net benefit across threshold probabilities of 10%–70%. ML algorithms, including both transparent linear models and tree-based ensembles, demonstrated acceptable discriminative capacity and favorable calibration for identifying prevalent self-reported CVD among individuals with CircS. Simpler models such as RF and GLM showed comparable utility to complex ensembles, providing feasible tools for clinical risk stratification. Prospective studies are needed to assess whether these variables can identify individuals who subsequently develop CVD.

title: Mechanism-guided generative chemistry yields distinct agonist-like and antagonist-like ligand populations for the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor
abstract: Designing serotonin 5-HT2A receptor ligands with a specified functional direction is difficult because binding affinity, assay-derived mechanism labels, molecular properties and receptor conformation are only partially coupled. We developed a mechanism-guided generative chemistry workflow integrating curated ChEMBL data, scaffold-aware supervised learning, a recurrent SMILES prior, reinforcement learning, medicinal-chemistry prioritization, receptor-context docking, MM-GBSA rescoring and property-adjusted contact analysis. The dataset comprised 8,949 measurements and 6,252 compounds. A five-seed binding Ki ensemble achieved scaffold-test mean absolute error of 0.588 pChEMBL and R² of 0.607; non-generalizing functional EC50 models were excluded from the reward. Separate campaigns generated 500 valid unique agonist-like and 500 antagonist-like molecules. Antagonist-like candidates showed higher predicted affinity and mechanism-label confidence, whereas agonist-like candidates showed higher QED, greater internal diversity and lower training-set similarity. Matched frozen-prior sampling showed only modest policy-level shifts from the already HTR2A-focused prior, whereas the reward-retained candidate populations were strongly enriched for the campaign objectives. Native-ligand redocking reproduced four deposited poses with heavy-atom RMSD values of 0.357–1.082 Å. Under fully contact-neutral pose selection and the prespecified repeated-measures model, S242, L229 and L362 showed FDR-supported campaign-by-receptor-context interactions; S242 and L229 retained the directions observed with the original selector, whereas L362 emerged in the contact-neutral analysis. The study identifies distinct model-defined chemical regimes and links campaign-level property drift to receptor-contact topology; generated compounds remain computational hypotheses requiring experimental validation.

title: Development and psychometric validation of the barriers to AI integration in nursing education scale (BAI-NE): a multi-institutional study
abstract: This multi-institutional study aimed to develop and psychometrically validate the Barriers to AI Integration in Nursing Education Scale (BAI-NE). A methodological study with a mixed-methods exploratory design was conducted in two phases: scale development and content validation, followed by psychometric evaluation. The 15-item BAI-NE was developed based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and an extensive literature review. Content validity was assessed by a panel of ten experts. A convenience sample of 470 nurse educators from seven faculties of nursing participated in the study. The sample was randomly divided for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA; n = 235) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA; n = 235). EFA identified a four-factor structure explaining 42.7% of the total variance, comprising Technical and Infrastructure Barriers, Knowledge and Training Barriers, Ethical and Regulatory Barriers, and Attitudinal and Organizational Barriers. EFA factor loadings ranged from 0.566 to 0.738. CFA provided preliminary support for the proposed model, with good fit indices (χ²/df = 0.90, RMSEA = 0.00, CFI = 1.000, TLI = 1.015, SRMR = 0.043, GFI = 0.961); because χ² was lower than df and CFI and RMSEA were at their bounds, these values should be interpreted cautiously and replicated in independent samples. Standardized CFA loadings ranged from 0.54 to 0.82. Internal consistency was satisfactory, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.713 to 0.754 and McDonald’s omega values ranging from 0.715 to 0.754. Test–retest reliability over a two-week interval was excellent for all subscales (ICC = 0.85–0.92). Convergent validity was modest, with composite reliability values exceeding 0.70, while AVE values ranged from 0.426 to 0.451. Discriminant validity was supported using the Fornell-Larcker criterion and HTMT values < 0.85. Among the four subscales, Knowledge and Training Barriers received the highest mean score (M = 14.0, SD = 2.51), followed by Attitudinal and Organizational Barriers (M = 13.1, SD = 2.63), Technical and Infrastructure Barriers (M = 12.8, SD = 2.68), and Ethical and Regulatory Barriers (M = 9.1, SD = 2.10). The BAI-NE demonstrated preliminary evidence of satisfactory validity and reliability and provides a practical instrument for identifying barriers to AI integration in nursing education, informing faculty development initiatives, institutional planning, and future research. The BAI-NE is intended to be scored and interpreted at the subscale level only.

title: Causal machine learning reveals heterogeneous effects of loss versus gain framing on retirement savings
abstract: Abstract: As Western countries face rapidly aging populations, insufficient retirement savings threaten individual financial security and the sustainability of social welfare systems. Behavioral interventions such as loss–gain message framing are often proposed as scalable solutions, yet evidence on their effectiveness is mixed, largely because little is known about when and for whom they work. We analyze heterogeneity in the effects of loss–gain framing on real-life, high-stakes retirement saving decisions. In a large-scale randomized field experiment ( \(N = 22{,}919\) ) with a European retirement savings company, individuals were randomized to loss- or gain-framed reminders designed to increase participation (extensive margin) and savings amount (intensive margin). Using causal machine learning, we estimate heterogeneous treatment effects across socioeconomic characteristics and validate them in a second, independent experiment ( \(N = 18{,}288\) ). In this validation experiment, for the 25% most responsive to loss framing, conversion is estimated to rise by 9.4 percentage points relative to gain framing, whereas for the 25% most responsive to gain framing it is expected to fall by 8.4 points. For savings amount, we estimate that loss framing raises contributions for 64% of contributors (by €737 on average) but backfires for the rest (by €615 on average). Overall, a personalized targeting policy based on causal machine learning is expected to increase participation by 51% (from 4.53% to 6.86%) and average savings by 18% (from €2,062 to €2,442 per converted customer) relative to uniform loss framing.

title: Identifiability assessment and physics-informed residual machine learning for calculated Ti–Zr–Nb–Ta–X thermodynamics (X = Mo, Hf)
abstract: Calculated alloy properties can produce misleading measures of machine-learning accuracy when the prediction target is generated by the same equation used as the model prior. This study examines that dependence in 140 Ti–Zr–Nb–Ta–X records (X = Mo, Hf), reduced to 129 unique compositions. The tabulated mixing enthalpies agree with a fixed regular-solution prior to within rounding precision. With complete elemental-enrichment trajectories withheld in turn, the prior and a regularized residual learner both give an RMSE of 0.00285 kJ mol \(^{-1}\) ; the maximum learned correction on the candidate grid is \(1.18\times 10^{-6}\) kJ mol \(^{-1}\) . This agreement will be inherited from the analytical prior and will not be an independent physical validation or measurable improvement in accuracy of machine learning. In the other hand, the composition-only support vector regression changes from the RMSE of 0.0202 (shuffled validation) to 1.5687 kJ mol \(^{-1}\) (omitting a complete enrichment trajectory). The features of each pair are ranked with 12 for 15 in post hoc singular-value analysis. There are two null directions, one being the absence of the Mo–Hf interaction, and two others being sampled interaction. There are 3051 possible compositions of the grid, of which 3005 satisfy the empirical thermodynamic criteria, 126 satisfy both proposed geometric restrictions, and 36 satisfy both restrictions and the empirical thermodynamic criteria and form a resulting Pareto set. The global equal-weight compromise is Ti \(_{15}\) Zr \(_{15}\) Nb \(_{25}\) Ta \(_{15}\) Mo \(_{30}\) . The fact that the calculations were performed with fixed priors is reflected in the results of the sensitivity tests and in the 300 interior compositions separately produced, which indicate that the geometric restrictions do not guarantee the reliability of the calculations. Controlled synthetic tests distinguish a learnable smooth deviation from unpredictable point offsets. The contribution is a reproducible assessment of analytical dependence, validation design and coefficient identifiability in a deterministic dataset. Biomedical suitability is not evaluated.

title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature
abstract: Fragmentation is common in interdisciplinary fields with diverse methods and theoretical commitments. Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve. Here, we describe a local multi-LLM pipeline for ontology-constrained literature synthesis. The pipeline reads papers, extracts evidence, incorporates figure descriptions, assembles constrained prompts, and validates outputs against an expert glossary. We defined a predictive-coding glossary of thirty-six concepts grouped into three hypotheses: predictive suppression, feedforward error propagation, and ubiquity. A council of ten local language models scored 31 studies across local and global oddball contexts. This enabled pairwise study-agreement analysis, cross-model comparison, and three-dimensional hypothesis-space mapping. Agreement was stronger for local than global oddball contexts, particularly for feedforward error propagation. Hypothesis-space temperature was lower for local oddball contexts and higher for global oddball contexts, indicating greater dispersion in the latter. These results show that local multi-LLM councils can produce auditable disagreement measurements that map heterogeneous literatures into quantitative evidence spaces.

title: Integrating graph neural networks with urine metabolomics for non-invasive detection of bladder cancer: a multi-centre case–control diagnostic study
abstract: Bladder cancer remains a major global health burden, and the stage at which a tumour is found largely determines what follows for the patient. Cystoscopy and urine cytology, the current mainstays, are invasive or insensitive, which keeps the search for accurate non-invasive alternatives open. We therefore asked a narrower question than a screening trial would ask: can a graph-based model separate treatment-naive bladder cancer patients from healthy controls using urinary metabolomic profiles alone? Liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry data were acquired for 338 participants (186 patients, 152 controls) at three centres, and 847 reproducible metabolite features passed quality control. Metabolite interaction graphs encoding partial correlations and KEGG pathway co-membership were estimated on training participants only, and a graph attention network (GAT) fusion architecture was trained on the resulting patient-level graphs. Every data-dependent step—quality-control filtering, normalisation, graph estimation, hyperparameter search and selection of the operating threshold—was confined to training and validation data, so that the internal test set and the external cohort were touched once. At the prespecified threshold the model reached an AUROC of 0.946 (95% CI 0.887–0.987), with sensitivity 0.919 (0.781–0.983) and specificity 0.900 (0.735–0.979) in 67 held-out participants, and an AUROC of 0.931 (0.873–0.977) in an independent cohort of 89 participants from a fourth centre. The model ranked above all conventional baselines, although with this sample size none of the pairwise differences survived correction for multiple comparisons, and a control model trained on randomised graph topology performed almost as well. Attention weights, permutation importance, integrated gradients and feature ablation converged on tryptophan catabolism, nucleotide biosynthesis and lipid remodelling. Because cases were histologically confirmed and controls were disease-free volunteers, these results describe case–control diagnostic discrimination; they do not establish detection before clinical presentation, and prospective enrolment of asymptomatic individuals remains necessary before any screening claim can be made.

title: A hybrid framework with uncertainty-aware cooperative fusion for robust spectrum sensing in beyond 5G cognitive radio networks
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid Gated Recurrent Unit–Long Short-Term Memory–Convolutional Neural Network (GRU–LSTM–CNN) deep learning framework designed to enhance Cooperative Spectrum Sensing (CSS) in Cognitive Radio (CR) networks. The proposed architecture combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for spatial–spectral feature extraction, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units for long-term temporal modeling, and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layers for efficient short-term dependency learning. This integrated framework enables reliable detection of Primary User (PU) activity under challenging wireless environments. A reliability-aware fusion mechanism is incorporated, where each Secondary User (SU) transmits soft sensing reports containing PU-presence probability and predictive uncertainty. The key novelty is a sequential multiscale spatiotemporal representation in which CNN, LSTM, and GRU respectively learn localized spectral structure, long-term temporal dependencies, and short-term temporal variations, followed by uncertainty-aware reliability-weighted cooperative fusion. This mechanism allows the Fusion Center (FC) to assign adaptive reliability weights according to Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and confidence level. The system processes 256-QAM modulated Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) signals transformed into time–frequency representations using the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT). For comparative purposes, an Orthogonal Time Space Modulation (OTSM) waveform is additionally used as a reference signaling scheme in the BER and PSD analyses (consistently denoted OTSM in Figs. 9, 10 and 11). The model is trained using a composite loss function combining Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE), Brier Score, and sparsity loss to improve detection accuracy, probability calibration, and communication efficiency. Simulation results over AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels show that the proposed GRU–LSTM–CNN framework achieves higher Probability of Detection (Pd), lower Probability of False Alarm, improved BER performance, and reduced Power Spectral Density (PSD) compared with conventional Energy Detection (ED), Matched Filter (MF), and existing deep learning models. The proposed model achieves Pd ≈ 1 at − 4 dB SNR and maintains strong robustness under 15–25% channel estimation error, confirming its suitability for next-generation CR and IoT communication systems.

title: RELAX: Reliability enhancement by limiting adverse eXertions
abstract: Accurate and well-calibrated confidence estimates are essential for the safe use of artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical imaging workflows, where overconfident errors can directly affect diagnostic decisions and patient outcomes. Conventional training objectives such as cross-entropy often encourage uniformly high confidence across all samples, leading to substantial miscalibration, particularly on rare pathologies, heterogeneous patient populations, and inherently ambiguous cases. Recent work addresses this by modifying loss functions to improve calibration, yet these approaches typically penalize errors equally across samples, including intrinsically difficult or noisy examples, which can contribute to suboptimal calibration. To address this limitation, we introduce the Perpetual Burden Score (PBS), a measure of sample difficulty derived from prediction instability observed during training. Building on PBS, we propose RELAX , a burden-aware optimization framework that down-weights chronically unstable (hard) samples during training, thereby reducing their influence on confidence formation. Across four medical imaging datasets spanning ophthalmology, histopathology, neuroimaging, and chest radiography, RELAX demonstrates overall improvements in calibration, while maintaining comparable diagnostic accuracy. For example, across 5 different architectural configurations on the ophthalmology dataset, on average, RELAX reduces Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Maximum Calibration Error (MCE) by 2.38% and 11.72%, respectively, while the reduction in F1-score is observed at 0.86%. These findings suggest that incorporating prediction stability into the training process can improve the reliability of confidence estimates without additional inference-time cost. As an architecture-agnostic and lightweight framework, RELAX provides a practical approach for enhancing the trustworthiness of clinical AI systems.

title: Reliable image reconstruction from DNA storage through marker-guided decoding and candidate filtering
abstract: Abstract DNA has emerged as a promising medium for long-term digital data storage because of its exceptional information density and durability. However, reliable data recovery remains challenging for Oxford Nanopore sequencing, where insertion, deletion, and substitution errors can disrupt sequence synchronization and increase ambiguity during decoding. In this study, we present a proof-of-concept framework for DNA-based RGB image storage and reconstruction that integrates marker-aware codebook construction, consensus-based marker-guided decoding from a single sequence, and AI-assisted image restoration. The framework systematically evaluates how different codebook construction strategies influence downstream decoding, candidate ambiguity, and final image reconstruction. Under simulated nanopore sequencing conditions, all constrained codebooks achieved high payload recovery (> 91%), but substantial differences were observed in their ability to preserve the correct payload among decoded candidate sequences. The codebook combining sequence-space discrimination, biochemical quality control, and structural compatibility produced the highest candidate-set quality and, when coupled with Random Forest-based reliability filtering, achieved the best image reconstruction performance, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 29.82 dB, a structural similarity index of 0.9309, and 80.19% exact pixel recovery. These findings demonstrate that payload recovery alone is insufficient to evaluate DNA storage performance, as downstream candidate ambiguity directly impacts the quality of reconstructed data. The proposed framework provides an end-to-end approach to investigating the relationship among codebook design, decoding robustness, and image reconstruction, thereby supporting the development of more reliable nanopore-based DNA data storage systems.

title: Interpretable physics-guided multi-output learning for optimizing circular-path cold metal transfer wire arc additive manufacturing of ER5356 aluminium alloy
abstract: Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) has emerged as a promising technology for fabricating large-scale aluminium components; however, reliable process optimization remains challenging owing to the complex interactions among deposition parameters, thermal history, and mechanical performance. This study proposes an interpretable physics-guided machine learning framework for predictive modelling and multi-objective optimization of circular-path Cold Metal Transfer (CMT)-WAAM of ER5356 aluminium alloy. A Taguchi L27 experimental design with three centre-point replications was employed to investigate the effects of wire feed speed, travel speed, interpass temperature, and shielding gas flow rate on ultimate tensile strength, elongation, flexural strength, and hardness. Physics-guided descriptors representing deposition intensity, thermal accumulation, cooling severity, and shielding adequacy were integrated into a multi-output stacking regressor to embed manufacturing knowledge and provide a physically structured representation of the process variables. The optimized process window predicted an ultimate tensile strength of 295.20 MPa, 40.10% elongation, 397.80 MPa flexural strength, and 71.80 HV hardness. A single confirmatory experiment produced deviations below 5%, with composite desirability decreasing from 0.9989 to 0.9565. Fractographic analysis revealed ductile failure through microvoid coalescence and ligament stretching, providing additional microstructural support for the behaviour observed at the optimized condition. By integrating physics-guided feature engineering with interpretable multi-output learning, the proposed framework provides a data-efficient and data-efficient decision-support approach within the investigated WAAM process window tool for intelligent WAAM process optimization, offering a practical pathway toward AI-enabled, digitally integrated additive manufacturing.

title: Personality expression and perception in large language models and humans
abstract: Growing numbers of people frequently turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) for concerns from various areas of life. Because its content has become ubiquitous, examining user perceptions of LLM-produced text and its distinguishability from human writing is crucial. This study investigated how seven LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemma, Gemini, Phi-3, Orca-2) describe themselves when compared to humans. LLM-generated outputs and human responses were collected using psychological questionnaires (Big Five, self-esteem, narcissism) and tailored prompts to elicit short self-descriptive texts. Six LLM and ten human judges then evaluated personality traits and text origin based on these self-descriptions (140 total, half LLM-generated). Results show that current LLM outputs can convey personality-consistent cues in questionnaires and texts. The perception of such significantly differed from that of humans. Both LLM and human judges accurately inferred personality from short self-descriptions and correctly differentiated between LLM-generated and human text. Linguistic analysis and participant feedback revealed textual cues distinguishing LLM-produced from human language and offered insights into how LLM versus human judgment and decisionmaking differ.

title: Multifractal signatures reveal source-dependent differences between tectonic earthquakes and icequakes
abstract: Discriminating between local tectonic earthquakes and cryo-seismic events (icequakes) poses a significant challenge for automated seismic monitoring due to the similarity of their waveforms in the time and frequency domains. To address this, we present a robust classification framework utilizing Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (MFDFA) combined with machine learning. The framework represents each waveform by explicitly defined multifractal parameters, which quantify the nonlinear scaling behavior and structural organization of the waveform. A total of 28,022 station-event waveform records obtained from nine seismic stations in the Columbia Glacier region, Alaska, were analyzed under different Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and data-availability conditions. The analysis of the seismic-network dataset shows class-dependent differences in the multiscale organization of tectonic earthquake and icequake waveforms. Although the expression of individual descriptors varies from one station to another, the complete multifractal representation supports a robust station-specific discrimination under different recording conditions. For each station, an independent Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier was trained. The mean accuracy obtained from the nine classifiers was 94.28%, while the highest accuracy at an individual station reached 98.01%. These results demonstrate that the proposed multifractal framework provides a physically grounded and highly accurate tool for purifying seismic catalogs in complex glaciated environments.

title: A document classification benchmark dataset on cybersecurity policy domain
abstract: Document classification in the cybersecurity domain is essential for the efficient identification of emerging threats, technologies, and policy trends. However, existing datasets and language models are biased toward technical, attack-oriented texts such as CTI reports and CVE descriptions, and there is a critical lack of data for the cybersecurity policy domain. To address this gap, we introduce the first benchmark dataset for cybersecurity policy document classification, comprising 1,723 expert-verified samples categorized into three labels: Strategy (490), Legislation (415), and Guideline (818). The dataset was constructed through automated web crawling from five sources: UNIDIR, CIPedia, NIST, ENISA, and ACSC. To demonstrate the dataset’s effectiveness, we conducted classification experiments using three BERT-based models. With sliding window-based data augmentation applied, XLM-RoBERTa-base achieved the highest document accuracy of 99.99% and an F1 score of 99.36%. The dataset and code are publicly available to facilitate future research.

title: An integrated deep learning framework for EEG-based sleep disorder detection
abstract: Sleep disorders require accurate and timely detection to support effective diagnosis and intervention. However, EEG-based sleep disorder detection is challenging due to noise, signal variations, and the difficulty of extracting informative features for reliable classification. To address these limitations, this paper introduces an innovative framework called Enhanced Batch Normalization-based Parallel Convolutional Neural Network for Sleep Disorder Detection (EB-PSDD). The process begins with the acquisition of EEG signals from the CAP Sleep Database. Then the preprocessing using the Adaptive Weighted Moving Average Filtering (AWMAF) technique, which helps reduce noise and smooth the signal, ensuring its suitability for analysis. In the next phase, features are extracted using methods such as Modified Window S-Transform (MWS-T), cross-correntropy, and Common Spatial Pattern (CSP), allowing for the identification of informative characteristics within the EEG signals. For classification, a hybrid deep learning model, Hybrid LeNet-PCNN (HLNet-P), is employed. This model integrates the classic LeNet architecture with the Enhanced Batch Normalization-based Parallel Convolutional Neural Network (EBN-PCNN) to accurately analyze the extracted features and detect signs of sleep disorders. The final output indicates whether a sleep disorder is present, enabling timely detection and intervention. Experimental results show that the proposed EB-PSDD framework outperforms traditional methods, achieving a maximum accuracy of 0.949, precision of 0.799, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.971.

title: An integrated analytical framework linking green and blue infrastructure spatial patterns with human thermal stress using UTCI
abstract: Urban heat stress poses a critical challenge under climate change and rapid urbanization, prompting the adoption of Green-Blue Infrastructure (GBI) as a key mitigation strategy. Despite its potential, previous studies have reported inconsistent relationships between GBI spatial configuration and urban thermal environments due to methodological variations and urban structural diversity. To address these limitations, this study proposes an analytical framework grounded in the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI), which incorporates multiple meteorological factors and enables GBI spatial patterns to be evaluated from a human-centered thermal perspective. Using data from the Seoul metropolitan area, 1800 m was selected as a common analysis extent based on scale-dependent responses of representative landscape metrics. Sequential exploratory screening and LASSO-based variable-selection retained seven landscape metrics characterizing vegetation condition, spatial composition, configuration, and connectivity. These metrics included NDVI_mean, C_G_PLAND, C_G_SHAPE_AM and C_GB_SHAPE_AM, C_G_SPLIT, L_GB_PD, and L_GB_COHESION. Random Forest Regression-based variable-importance analysis identified C_G_PLAND as a consistently prominent metric, while C_G_SPLIT, L_GB_COHESION, and NDVI_mean also showed relatively high importance. These findings indicate that GI quantity, vegetation condition, and GBI spatial configuration are jointly associated with urban thermal conditions. Overall, the proposed framework provides a reproducible basis for context-sensitive evaluation of GBI–thermal relationships across urban settings.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and machine-learning analysis reveals shared molecular signatures linking osteoporosis and atherosclerosis
abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) and atherosclerosis (AS) frequently coexist with ageing, yet their shared molecular features remain incompletely understood. We separately analyzed femoral-bone OP and arterial AS transcriptomes using Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted differential expression. Arterial-territory adjustment, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and repeated-resampling machine learning were applied to the AS cohort, alongside functional enrichment and STRING network analyses. Intersecting OP differentially expressed genes with AS-associated WGCNA modules identified 2788 shared candidates, of which 88 also met stringent differential-expression criteria in both diseases. Functional and network analyses highlighted translation, endosomal–lysosomal biology, endocytosis, sphingolipid metabolism, myeloid-associated processes, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. C1orf174, FBXL18, and RBM4B were consistently prioritized by LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE. A fixed nine-gene candidate panel was evaluated in independent circulating-transcriptome cohorts. In GSE56815, C1orf174 met targeted panel-level correction (FDR = 0.0429), but not genome-wide correction. Exploratory clinical RT-qPCR showed nominally lower FBN1 expression in the OP + AS group, whereas PTEN and SMAD2 showed no statistically significant differences. These findings provide an integrative framework for the bone–vascular axis and prioritize candidate genes for further mechanistic investigation and independent validation.

title: Deconvoluting the influence of environmental forcings on chemical weathering rates using machine learning model
abstract: Quantifying the contributions of silicate and carbonate weathering to global carbon dioxide sequestration is crucial for understanding Earth’s climate regulation mechanisms. In this study, we introduce a framework that integrates explainable machine learning with partial dependence analysis to understand the relationships between environmental forcings and chemical weathering rates. We trained machine learning models on a geochemical dataset from the Tibetan Plateau together with climatic and environmental factors, achieving a weathering model with high predictive ability (R 2 = 0.84–0.96). Furthermore, we separated direct environmental driving effects from indirect mediating effects through systemic partial dependence plots. The results indicate that runoff is the dominant controlling factor of both riverine dissolved SiO 2 and HCO 3 ⁻ flux. Warming promotes riverine HCO 3 ⁻ flux in the river, but its effect on riverine dissolved SiO 2 flux is bidirectional-first inhibiting, then promoting. Further, our analysis reveals that the effect of precipitation on riverine dissolved SiO 2 flux is mainly mediated indirectly by runoff. Our study establishes a framework for investigating chemical weathering, highlighting the potential of machine learning to advance predictive modeling and reveal complex interactions between environmental forcings and chemical weathering.

title: Comparative analysis of real-time appearance-based mapping and cartographer algorithms using deep learning object detection
abstract: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) shares computation, memory, sensing, and middleware resources with other robotic perception tasks. This study evaluates Cartographer and RTAB-Map in ROS 2 Humble/Gazebo using a TurtleBot3 Waffle Pi, both alone and while a separate YOLOv8n object-detection node runs concurrently on the CPU. Ten runs were analyzed per configuration (40 runs total). Independent Gazebo ground truth and TF-derived SLAM trajectories were converted to planar x-y-yaw TUM trajectories, associated within 20 ms, and evaluated using translation and yaw absolute pose error (APE) and 1 m relative pose error (RPE). Baseline translation APE RMSE was 0.030965 ± 0.007947 m for Cartographer and 0.014013 ± 0.003691 m for RTAB-Map; corresponding translation RPE RMSE was 0.017614 ± 0.002281 m and 0.006209 ± 0.001787 m. With concurrent YOLOv8n, translation APE RMSE was 0.031711 ± 0.007119 m and 0.017177 ± 0.007964 m, respectively. Combined monitored process CPU reached 670.491 ± 15.741% and 624.513 ± 12.703%, while Gazebo real-time factor remained near 1.0. Because the groups were independently teleoperated, baseline-to-YOLO differences are interpreted descriptively rather than causally. The workflow integrates repeated-run localization accuracy, orientation error, resource profiling, and motion characterization under documented simulation conditions.

title: Transformer-based soft-output MIMO detection for coded systems
abstract: Deep learning (DL)–based multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detection has emerged as a promising technique for future wireless communication systems. In this paper, we propose a transformer-based DL framework for MIMO detection, specifically designed for coded MIMO systems with soft iterative decoding. To address the prohibitive computational cost associated with collecting soft-information training labels, a computationally efficient recursive label generation method is employed. The proposed framework demonstrates strong generalization capability, as it is trained at a single signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and evaluated over a wide range of SNR values. In addition, its generalization capability and scalability are validated across various antenna configurations and modulation orders. Simulation results show that the proposed method significantly improves bit error rate (BER) performance, achieving near–maximum-likelihood (ML) performance for coded MIMO systems while maintaining excellent generalization performance.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and spatially explicit drivers of eco-geological coupling coordination in a mountainous region
abstract: This study developed an integrated framework combining remote sensing assessment, coupling coordination analysis, and interpretable machine learning to investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of eco-geological coupling coordination and the spatially explicit drivers of its 2020 pattern in a mountainous region. Landsat imagery from 2000 to 2020 was used to derive the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI), while geological hazard susceptibility was inversely transformed into a Geological Environmental Stability Index (GESI). The coupling coordination degree (CCD) was evaluated under a consistent geological background, and XGBoost–GeoShapley was applied to identify the nonlinear drivers and spatial interaction effects of the 2020 CCD pattern. Mean RSEI increased from 0.54 in 2000 to 0.61 in 2020, indicating an improvement in ecological environmental quality. The CCD exhibited an overall improving trend, with higher values in peripheral mountainous areas and lower values in river valleys and areas with intensive human activity. The proportion of well- and highly coordinated areas increased from 55.6% in 2000 to a peak of 66.7% in 2015 before declining slightly to 64.3% in 2020. Mean annual temperature, population density, and actual evapotranspiration were the three most influential drivers of the 2020 CCD spatial variation. Moreover, GeoShapley revealed pronounced spatial effects and GEO–feature interactions, indicating that the magnitude and direction of driver contributions varied across spatial locations. Strong GEO–feature interaction effects were mainly concentrated in the western–southwestern region, central transition zone, and southern margin. These findings highlight the importance of spatially differentiated ecological restoration and geological hazard mitigation in mountainous eco-geological systems.

title: DrowsyFormer-Gen: classical baselines match a triple-stream transformer with diffusion augmentation for driver drowsiness detection
abstract: Driver drowsiness detectors must be judged on minority-class sensitivity, calibration and alarm behaviour, not accuracy alone. DrowsyFormer-Gen combines physiological, vehicle and behavioural transformer streams with cross-modal fusion, an adaptive classification head and class-conditional diffusion augmentation. We re-implemented and evaluated it on shared causal windows and subject-disjoint folds against five classical baselines, using DMPS (225,000 samples; 15 drivers) and SC-DD (87,430 segments; 20 participants); DMPS drivers are a subset of SC-DD participants. Baselines received nested hyperparameter optimisation; thresholds were fixed on training data. Tuned logistic regression reached 99.747 ± 0.031% accuracy, 0.953 drowsy-class recall and expected calibration error 0.0008, ahead of every neural configuration. Each proposed component failed a controlled test: removing diffusion augmentation improved every metric, and class weighting alone reached 0.989 recall; zeroing the adaptive head’s reference halved calibration error while its refresh interval was inert; and the fusion ablation, over 25 runs, ranged from 0.000 to 1.000 recall at a fixed threshold despite stable ranking. A single sample reached 0.915 recall against 0.956 for the 32-sample window. We report a negative result, conditional on the supplied records being what the source publications describe.

title: ResNet-GA: genetic algorithm-driven optimization of ResNet for automated dental caries detection in medical imaging
abstract: Dental caries is one of the most prevalent oral diseases worldwide and remains a major public health concern because delayed or inaccurate diagnosis can lead to irreversible tooth destruction, pain, infection, and more invasive treatment. Early and reliable detection from dental images is therefore essential for improving preventive care and supporting clinical decision-making. However, manual interpretation of dental radiographs is time-consuming, subjective, and prone to inter-observer variability. Although deep learning has shown strong potential for automated caries detection, its performance often depends on manually selected hyperparameters and may be affected by image variability, low contrast, artifacts, and class imbalance. To address these limitations, we propose ResNet-GA, a hybrid deep learning framework that combines deep convolutional feature learning with a genetic algorithm to automatically optimize selected convolutional configurations, particularly the number of filters and kernel sizes in three convolutional blocks. The proposed framework was evaluated on a publicly available dental caries dataset obtained from Kaggle, comprising caries and non-caries images. Images were resized, normalized, and divided into training and validation subsets, with class balancing applied to reduce bias toward the majority class. The genetic algorithm iteratively evolved candidate convolutional configurations using classification accuracy as the fitness criterion. The optimized model achieved high diagnostic performance, with a mean test accuracy of 87.89% ± 1.41% (macro precision 89.74% ± 0.95%, macro recall 80.38% ± 3.04%, macro F1-score 83.32% ± 2.58%) across five independent runs on an independent test set. These results indicate that evolutionary optimization of convolutional configurations can improve robustness and classification performance for automated dental caries detection. By reducing dependence on manual architectural tuning and improving diagnostic consistency, the proposed framework offers a promising computer-aided decision-support approach for dental image analysis.

title: Patient-anatomy-referenced multiscale modelling of median nerve conduction in carpal tunnel syndrome
abstract: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS) is a common compressive peripheral neuropathy causing focal conduction slowing and sensory dysfunction. Existing computational models are either mechanical or electrophysiological in isolation, precluding mechanistic understanding of nerve dysfunction across severity grades. We introduce a multiscale computational system built on a patient-anatomy-referenced median nerve pathway, rigidly registered and anatomically deformed against this patient’s own segmented bone and skin geometry, with the compression zone defined at 0–29.4 mm from the detected wrist point. A reduced-order conduction-velocity model, a FitzHugh–Nagumo (FHN) reaction–diffusion model and an unfitted McIntyre–Richardson–Grill (MRG) double-cable model were analysed on this pathway. The velocity and FHN models were calibrated to Kimura’s Normal and Mild data (zone velocities 57–59 and about 41 m/s) and predicted about 24 and 7 m/s for Moderate and Severe CTS. The MRG model predicted a normal velocity of 56.1 m/s without fitting and complete conduction block in Severe CTS, but under-predicted Mild and Moderate slowing (52.8 and 43.6 m/s). Convergence, sensitivity analysis and ten-run registration repeatability are reported, with registration limitations (16.0% of tube-surface points outside the skin) disclosed rather than assumed away. The framework is a research platform for peripheral neuropathy investigation, not a validated diagnostic tool.

title: Deep learning-based binary classification and probabilistic calibration of navicular bone pathology in equine radiographs
abstract: Radiographic assessment of the equine navicular bone is challenging because pathological changes may be subtle, surrounding anatomical structures can overlap, and image interpretation may vary among observers. This retrospective single-center study developed and evaluated deep learning models for the binary classification of equine navicular bone radiographs as radiographically normal or pathological. The dataset comprised 528 radiographs from 176 horses. ResNet-50 was used as the primary classifier, while Xception and VGG-16 were evaluated as comparator architectures. All data partitions were created at the horse level to prevent subject leakage. The development dataset included 140 horses and was evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, while a temporally separated internal hold-out set containing 36 horses and 108 radiographs was reserved for final testing. ResNet-50 achieved a mean AUROC of 0.893, an accuracy of 79.6%, and an F1-score of 85.5% across the cross-validation folds. On the hold-out test set, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.905, an accuracy of 82.4%, a sensitivity of 90.5%, a specificity of 71.1%, and an F1-score of 85.7%. Temperature scaling produced modest improvements in probability calibration, reducing the Brier score from 0.1582 to 0.1533 and the expected calibration error from 0.1639 to 0.1595 without altering discrimination. Qualitative Grad-CAM analysis was additionally used to illustrate image regions associated with model predictions. These findings support the feasibility of deep learning for automated classification of navicular bone radiographic appearances. However, the model does not diagnose clinical navicular syndrome, assess lesion severity, or replace veterinary interpretation. Prospective external validation using multi-center datasets is required before clinical implementation.

title: AI-integrated multi-omics fusion for precision cardiovascular diagnostics
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide, requiring accurate and early diagnostic systems for effective intervention. Traditional prediction approaches relying only on clinical data often fail to capture complex biological interactions underlying disease progression. This study proposes CardioPrecision-BioFusion, an AI-driven framework that combines clinical, genomic, transcriptomic, and simulated proteomic representations. The clinical and omics datasets were obtained from independent cohorts and were not patient matched; consequently, the framework performs cohort-level latent representation integration and does not claim patient-level multi-omics fusion. Modality-specific encoders, target-blind prototype retrieval, multi-head attention, transformer-based learning, an autoencoder, and stacking were used to model heterogeneous feature interactions, while masked attention handled structurally unavailable modalities without imputing unobserved patient-level omics measurements. On the internal held-out constructed fusion test set, the model achieved 97.96% accuracy (95% CI, 97.14–98.55%), 98.05% precision, 98.05% recall, and a 98.05% F1-score. In a source-disjoint, transcriptomics-only external evaluation using 332 samples from GSE141910, the frozen transcriptomics branch achieved 84.64% accuracy and an AUC-ROC of 91.20%. SHAP analysis identified influential clinical and molecular features. These findings support the framework as an exploratory multimodal methodology, but prospective validation in patient-matched multi-omics cohorts is required before clinical use.

title: Effective source selection of solar-grid powered electric vehicle charger circuit using machine learning algorithm
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has increased the demand for charging systems integrated with renewable energy sources for efficient operation. Solar-grid integrated systems offer a promising solution; however, photovoltaic (PV) fluctuations and varying grid conditions reduce power efficiency and increase battery stress. To address these challenges, a machine learning-based source selection method for a Quasi-Z-Source Network Converter (QZNC) used in EV charging is proposed. Different machine learning algorithms, including Fine Tree, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Weighted KNN, and Random Forest, are implemented and analyzed. Simulations are carried out in MATLAB/Simulink under different load and power conditions to evaluate system performance. Under the considered MATLAB/Simulink simulation scenarios, the Random Forest classifier achieved the best performance with a classification accuracy of 99.67% and an AUC value of 1.0 on the generated test dataset. The proposed system attains a maximum efficiency of nearly 90%, maintains voltage fluctuations below 2.5 V, and reduces charging cost by about 13% compared to conventional methods. In addition, the use of a fast-recovery diode minimizes switching noise and enhances converter performance while supporting bidirectional vehicle-to-grid (V2G) operation.

title: Explainable vision Mamba–Kolmogorov–Arnold learning for multi-temporal monitoring of vegetation stress and land degradation in drylands
abstract: Monitoring vegetation stress and land degradation in dryland environments is challenging because short-term spectral variability can obscure persistent ecological change. Complex deep-learning architectures also do not necessarily provide higher predictive performance or independently validated explanations. The study developed and evaluated an explainable Vision Mamba (VMamba)–Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) framework for multi-temporal vegetation monitoring in Badr Al-Janub, Saudi Arabia, using Landsat observations from 2015 to 2025. Multi-temporal vegetation and moisture indices were integrated with terrain variables, while a geographic partition defined training, validation, and locked independent-test subsets. On the locked independent-test set, VMamba–KAN achieved an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 78.76%, frequency-weighted Intersection over Union (FWIoU) of 71.28%, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 20.06%, and Macro-F1 of 25.11%. The CNN baseline achieved higher OA, FWIoU, mIoU, and Macro-F1 values than VMamba–KAN. Cohen's Kappa was 0.424 for VMamba–KAN and 0.404 for the CNN baseline. The Kappa difference is reported separately and is not interpreted as evidence of overall or class-balanced predictive superiority. Temporal analysis identified broad improvement in vegetation condition toward 2023 followed by partial deterioration in 2025 rather than continuous landscape-scale degradation. Integrated Gradients provided descriptive attribution patterns associated with VMamba–KAN predictions. Full-scene softmax probabilities provided descriptive predictive-confidence information and were not interpreted as calibrated uncertainty estimates. The results emphasize temporal persistence, geographic evaluation, class imbalance, predictive performance, and cautious interpretation of attribution evidence.
