title: EEG network features and APOE ε4 for amyloid classification in mild cognitive impairment
abstract: Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) may provide information complementary to apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE ε4) for identifying amyloid pathology in mild cognitive impairment. We evaluated this hypothesis in an exploratory cross-sectional study of 93 patients, including 54 with amyloid-positive positron emission tomography, using EEG functional connectivity, graph features and 11 classifiers under nested cross-validation. In the original partition, extreme gradient boosting with all domains achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.806 versus 0.682 for its APOE-only model (paired difference 0.124, 95% confidence interval 0.010–0.238). The median paired difference across 30 additional partitions was 0.088. Among non-carriers, the combined model identified 11 of 16 amyloid-positive patients, with 10 false positives among 31 amyloid-negative patients. The gain was smaller against carrier status used directly (difference 0.057, −0.043–0.157). Nesting classifier selection reduced the median AUC to 0.734, and alternative EEG epoch samples yielded AUCs of 0.571–0.773 on the original partition. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of complementary EEG and genetic information, while demonstrating dependence on the comparator, model selection and epoch sampling. Reliable EEG estimation and external validation are required before clinical use.

title: Integrated computational pipelines using machine learning and deep neural networks for modelling Drosophila cardiac aging and disease classification
abstract: High-speed optical microscopy of Drosophila hearts has become an essential approach for modelling cardiovascular disease and aging. However, manual evaluation of cardiac function is time-consuming, subjective, and prone to error, highlighting the need for reliable computational frameworks. Here, we present computational pipelines that combine segmentation-derived cardiac parameters with ensemble machine learning and raw video-based representations with deep convolutional neural networks, enabling the development of new predictive models while extending our previous framework. This integrated approach enables automated and quantitative phenotyping of cardiac function across both aging and cardiovascular disease contexts. We evaluated the performance of the pipelines across three biological problems relevant to cardiovascular systems biology: distinguishing between young (1-week-old) and aged (5-week-old) Drosophila hearts, classifying healthy hearts from those carrying the lamin C mutation ( LamC G489V ), and identifying phenotypes associated with Ogdh knockdown. Ensemble learning with Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, and XGBoost (age classification) and Random Forest ( LamC G489V and Ogdh classification) applied to segmentation-derived features achieved accuracies (mean ± standard deviation across 5-fold cross-validation) of 83.7% ± 5.2% for aging classification, 78.2% ± 8.2% for L amC G489V mutant detection, and 98.5% ± 3.1% for Ogdh knockdown identification. In parallel, video-based modelling using a custom dual-input convolutional neural network and 3D residual networks (R3D-18 and MC3-18) achieved accuracies of 89.5% ± 4.3% for age classification, 75.6% for lamin C mutant detection, and 90.8% ± 6.0% for Ogdh knockdown classification. By integrating classical feature-based machine learning with modern deep learning architectures, this work provides a scalable computational framework for modeling Drosophila cardiac aging and disease. More broadly, the study demonstrates how multimodal machine learning can enhance quantitative phenotyping, reduce human error in analysis, and accelerate the application of models in systems-level investigations of cardiovascular health and aging.

title: MGS-DETR: a multi-granularity spatial representation learning framework for joint driver fatigue and distraction detection
abstract: Driver fatigue and distracted driving are major causes of traffic accidents, yet existing vision-based detectors often suffer from imbalanced feature modeling, insufficient cross-layer fusion, and loss of fine-grained spatial details under complex in-vehicle conditions. To address these issues, we propose MGS-DETR, a multi-granularity spatial representation learning framework built upon RT-DETR for joint driver fatigue and distraction detection. In the encoding stage, we develop a Multi-scale Spatial Awareness Encoder (MSAE) to balance local fine-grained fatigue cues and global distracted-action context. In the feature-fusion stage, we design Global-guided Cross-Modulation Fusion (G-CMF) to enhance the interaction between shallow spatial details and deep semantic features under pose variation and occlusion. In the multi-scale transmission stage, we construct a Spatial-Detail Enhanced Feature Pyramid Network (SDE-FPN) to preserve fine-grained spatial details during feature transmission and improve the localization of annotated regions for fatigue-related visual signs. Experiments are conducted on the Composite Distraction and Fatigue Dataset (CDFD) and the self-collected Real-World Fatigue and Distracted Driving Dataset (RWFDD). On CDFD, MGS-DETR achieves 0.9628 precision, 0.9618 recall, 0.9708 mAP50, and 0.8159 mAP50-95, improving mAP50-95 by 5.44 percentage points over RT-DETR-r18. Under the source-video-group-disjoint RWFDD split, it obtains 0.8868 precision, 0.8946 recall, 0.8907 F1-score, 0.9123 mAP50, and 0.8501 mAP50-95. Bidirectional transfer experiments are reported separately under the stated nine-class protocol. The full model runs at 164.50 FPS with 21.90 M parameters and 64.0 GFLOPs on the desktop test platform; embedded-device throughput is measured separately on Jetson Orin NX.

title: Benchmarking latent-space reasoning abilities in large language models through forced response-language selection
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can perform reasoning computations both internally within their latent space and externally by generating explicit token sequences like chains of thought. Significant progress in enhancing reasoning abilities has been made by scaling test-time compute. However, understanding and quantifying model-internal reasoning abilities – the inferential “leaps” models make between individual token predictions – remains crucial. This study introduces a benchmark (n = 4,000 items) designed to quantify model-internal reasoning in different domains. We achieve this by having LLMs indicate the correct solution to reasoning problems not through descriptive text, but by selecting a specific language of their initial response token that is different from English, the benchmark language. This not only requires models to reason beyond their context window, but at the same time to overcome their default behavior to respond in the same language as the prompt, posing an additional cognitive strain. We evaluate a set of 18 LLMs, showing significant performance variations, with GPT-4.5 achieving the highest accuracy (74.7%), outperforming models like Grok-2 (67.2%), or Llama 3.1 405B (65.6%). Control experiments and difficulty scaling analyses suggest that while LLMs engage in internal reasoning, we cannot rule out heuristic exploitations under certain conditions, marking an area for future investigation. Our experiments demonstrate that LLMs can “think” via latent-space computations, highlighting model-internal inference processes that need further understanding, especially in view of safety-related aspects like covert planning, goal-seeking, or deception emerging without explicit token traces. Significance Statement – Large language models (LLMs) often appear to "reason" only when they show step-by-step chains of thought. We introduce a benchmark that instead measures reasoning carried out silently in a model’s latent space. Tasks require models to infer the correct answer and indicate it solely by choosing a pre-specified non-English response language—preventing them from "thinking in the context window." Across eight reasoning domains, models show wide variation, with some large dense transformer models substantially outperforming others. Control studies and difficulty scaling suggest genuine internal computation, while also revealing potential heuristic shortcuts. By isolating model-internal "reasoning leaps," our approach helps quantify hidden inferences and highlights oversight and safety risks from capabilities that leave no explicit token trace.

title: Machine learning-driven reverse prediction of concrete mix design: a comparative study of twelve algorithms
abstract: Concrete mix design is usually treated as a forward, iterative task: proportions are adjusted until the required compressive strength is met. Here, we work in the reverse direction. From a target 28-day compressive strength and curing age, the model estimates seven proportions directly: cement, blast furnace slag, fly ash, water, superplasticizer, coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate. The workflow combines machine learning with a deterministic physics-informed correction layer. Twelve algorithms from six model families (linear, instance-based, tree-based, ensemble, kernel, and deep learning) were trained on the UCI Concrete Compressive Strength dataset 1 ( n = 1,030). For a fair comparison, each model used the same multi-output regression wrapper, hyperparameters were tuned with 30-iteration RandomizedSearchCV and 5-fold internal cross-validation, robustness was assessed by 10-fold cross-validation, and pairwise differences were tested with paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. The study contributes a tuned twelve-algorithm benchmark with statistical comparisons, a per-component analysis linked to concrete-material mechanisms, and a post-processing layer that enforces 0.30 ≤ W/C ≤ 0.80, cement ≥ 200 kg/m³, supplementary cementitious replacement ≤ 50% of binder, and non-negative superplasticizer dosage. After tuning, Extra Trees gave the highest test-set R² (0.341), while Gradient Boosting gave the highest 10-fold CV R² (0.262 ± 0.041). The leading four models were not significantly different (paired t-test, p > 0.05). Per-component R² ranged from about 0.52 for superplasticizer and 0.46 for cement to below 0.16 for fine aggregate and slag. This pattern is consistent with concrete chemistry: hydration-controlled components can be partly inferred from strength, whereas aggregate proportions are set largely by grading and workability. For a 15 MPa target, the unconstrained model returned a W/C of about 1.0; the physics layer corrected it to 0.80 with only a modest test-set R² reduction (0.341 to 0.302). The full pipeline was then applied to an independent ultra-high-performance concrete dataset (863 mixtures, 17 variables). The algorithm ranking was preserved and the best inverse R² increased to 0.608, indicating that input dimensionality strongly affects inverse predictability. A conditional-variance analysis shows the tuned models operate near the upper bound of the two-input formulation: mixtures with the same strength form several distinct design families, so the prediction is best read as a screening anchor within a family of valid designs. The proposed framework should be used as a screening tool, not as a replacement for ACI 211.1 design or laboratory verification.

title: Characterization of corynacin K411, a leaderless bacteriocin from Corynebacterium jeikeium
abstract: Bacteriocins are ribosomally synthesized antimicrobial peptides that are emerging as natural preservatives and alternatives to conventional antibiotics in response to the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. Here, we provide a comprehensive experimental characterization of corynacin K411, previously reported as K411/AucA. The corynacin K411 biosynthetic gene cluster encodes a set of proteins that support a coordinated system for peptide production, secretion, and self-immunity. Corynacin K411 exhibits potent activity against various bacteria, including the foodborne pathogen Listeria monocytogenes . It demonstrates stability across acidic and alkaline pH (pH 2 to 10) and high temperatures (37 °C and 60 °C). It exerts bactericidal activity by disrupting membrane integrity, causing leakage of nucleic acids, proteins, potassium and magnesium ions. Importantly, corynacin K411 is non-hemolytic and non-cytotoxic to human keratinocytes. In addition, it inhibits L. monocytogenes biofilm formation, reduces the biomass of pre-formed biofilms, and lowers bacterial cell counts in a milk preservation model system. Structural analysis of the AlphaFold-predicted three-dimensional structure indicates a saposin-like fold, consistent with other characterized saposin-like leaderless bacteriocins.

title: Lightweight adaptive split federated learning for patient-independent ECG arrhythmia classification
abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram monitoring in the Internet of Medical Things requires arrhythmia classifiers that run on resource-constrained devices and learn across hospitals without pooling patient data. We propose FedIoMT-RPM, a split federated learning framework in which each device trains only a 28.4 KiB client-side network, 6.8 times smaller than in full-model federated learning, while a bounded adaptive weighted aggregation adjusts each client''s contribution to its smoothed validation performance. Under the patient-independent inter-patient protocol of the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, with five clients holding complete patient records and six seeds per method, its detection performance was statistically comparable to that of the best federated baselines, with an accuracy of 93.97 ± 1.72%, a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.731 ± 0.039 and a macro-F1 score of 60.07 ± 2.41%. This macro-F1 reflects limited detection of supraventricular beats, with a sensitivity of 64.8%, and near-zero detection of fusion beats, and 1,381 of the 1,781 supraventricular test beats come from a single record. Among the split methods, FedIoMT-RPM averaged 18.9% less communication than SplitFed. Zero-shot INCART and PTB-XL benchmarks gave results comparable to the federated baselines. Reconstruction attacks recovered the ECG from the transmitted activations, which need protection before clinical use; membership inference stayed near chance.

title: A novel ferro-aging-related gene signature for prognosis and targeted drug prediction in cervical cancer
abstract: Cervical cancer (CESC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in women. Recent studies have identified ferro-aging as a genuine biological pathway in primates, representing an iron-dependent metabolic process. However, cellular ageing and the decline in overall physiological function play a crucial role in tumour progression. Based on this, we have established a prognostic model related to ferro-aging and evaluated its predictive and diagnostic value in cervical cancer. We integrated data from the The Cancer Genomics Atlas (TCGA), the Gene Expression Online Resource (GEO) and single-cell RNA sequencing datasets. Following the identification of ferro-aging-related gene (FARGs) based on the literature, we constructed a prognostic model using machine learning algorithms and analysed model features via Shapley-based interpretability (SHAP) analysis. The Scissor algorithm was employed to evaluate cell populations associated with high- and low-risk groups. Studies on intercellular communication and spatial transcriptomics revealed the process of tumour microenvironment remodelling. Finally, potential therapeutic compounds were identified through AI-assisted virtual screening and molecular docking. A total of eight FAR model genes were ultimately identified: DUOX1 , E2F1 , IL1B , KEAP1 , MAP3K14 , SLAMF8 , TFRC and TNFAIP3 . This study constructed and validated a novel risk profile model comprising these eight ferro-aging-related genes; this model demonstrated moderate prognostic discriminatory power in both internal and external cohorts, with the tumour microenvironment in the high-risk group exhibiting an immunosuppressive state. Using single-cell RNA sequencing to assess cellular heterogeneity, macrophages, epithelial cells and CD8 + T cells were identified as key factors in CESC progression. Pseudotime analysis was performed to visualize the expression levels of FARGs along the pseudotime axis and explore how FARGs participate in the dynamic process of EndMT. Spatial transcriptomics was employed to map the distribution and expression of FARGs within epithelial cells in the tumour microenvironment. Intercellular communication intensity was increased in the low-risk group, with epithelial cells in this group signalling to macrophages via the APP-CD74 pathway. Drug screening indicated that BRD-A56371469 is likely to bind to DUOX1. The FARG signature is a candidate prognostic indicator for CESC, meriting further exploration in prospective cohorts. In silico screening prioritized BRD‑A56371469 as a computational binding scaffold for DUOX1, warranting subsequent experimental validation.

title: Research on stroke detection algorithm based on the improved model of YOLOv8-CBAM-ASFF
abstract: Accurate early diagnosis of stroke is critical for reducing mortality and disability. Leveraging the rapid advances in deep learning, automated stroke detection has become an active research focus. Yet, existing approaches still underperform in detecting small lesions, adapting to complex backgrounds, and operating in real time. Four YOLOv8 variants of different scales were systematically evaluated, and an optimized architecture integrating the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and the Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (Detect_ASFF) component was proposed. CBAM selectively amplifies salient features while suppressing background noise, whereas Detect_ASFF dynamically reweights multi-scale features, mitigating small-object loss and contextual degradation. Compared with the baseline, the refined model achieved a comparable overall mAP while improving lesion-level sensitivity for medium and large lesions. On a strictly patient-level held-out test set (34 patients, 474 images), the enhanced YOLOv8n reached 74.9% mean average precision at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.5, where a lesion counts as detected when the predicted box overlaps the annotated lesion by at least 50% (mAP@0.5), and 36.1% when the same measure is averaged over thresholds from 0.5 to 0.95 (mAP@0.5:0.95). It also increased the recall of medium-sized lesions (32–96 px) from 62.5% to 73.5% and of large lesions from 84.9% to 90.3%, at a modest cost of 0.2 additional false positives per image. Owing to its lightweight design, the optimized YOLOv8n is a promising candidate for real-time stroke-lesion detection; this work is presented as a proof of principle, and clinical deployment requires further validation.

title: Identification of genes related to mitochondrial DNA methylation in osteoarthritis based on transcriptomic data and clinical validation
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common chronic joint disorder, which is characterized by cartilage deterioration and joint function impairment. Recent studies suggest that mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) methylation is important for OA development. In this study, we analyzed transcriptomic data (GSE55235) to identify differentially expressed genes using ssGSEA, WGCNA, protein interaction networks, and machine learning. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analyses examined 182 biological processes. CALML4 and MXRA5 were identified as candidate key genes through bioinformatics analysis. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that CALML4 correlated with MXRA5 and Treg enrichment. MiRNA-single nucleotide polymorphism-gene network analysis revealed 6 SNPs associated with CALML4 and 58 miRNAs. Valproic acid exhibited the highest correlation with CALML4 . RT-qPCR validation confirmed a statistically significant expression difference for MXRA5 between the OA and control groups, but not for CALML4 . The discrepancy between bioinformatics predictions and clinical validation indicates that CALML4 should be considered a candidate key gene, rather than a validated key gene. At the transcriptomic level, this study suggested that mtDNA methylation-related alterations might be involved in OA and identified CALML4 and MXRA5 as candidate OA-related genes requiring further validation. Of these, differential MXRA5 expression received preliminary support from RT-qPCR in a small sample, whereas the clinical diagnostic value of both genes still requires validation in large independent cohorts.

title: Comparison of selected CNN and transformer models for choledocholithiasis classification and localization on MRCP
abstract: While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promise for automated choledocholithiasis detection on magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP), transformer-based models have recently emerged as alternatives. However, the relative performance of these approaches for stone classification and localization remains unclear, necessitating systematic comparison. This study therefore compared selected CNN and transformer architectures for MRCP-based choledocholithiasis classification and detection. In this retrospective multicenter study (2022–2025) across two tertiary-care hospitals in Iran, patients with and without common bile duct (CBD) stones were included. Patient-level MRCP scans were partitioned (70:20:10 for training, validation, and internal testing) into cropped and uncropped datasets. CNN (ResNet50, YOLOv12) and transformer-based (Vision Transformer [ViT], RF-DETR) models were evaluated, with an independent dataset from a third institution reserved for external testing. The classification cohort included 1037 patients (523 with CBD stones; mean age 53 ± 14 years), and the detection cohort included 633 patients (523 with CBD stones; mean age 57 ± 16 years). On external cropped images, ResNet50 and ViT achieved accuracies of 96.0% (95% CI 93.5, 98.5) and 97.0% (95% CI 94.0, 99.0), with AUCs of 0.999 and 0.991, respectively; neither the accuracy difference ( P = 0.80) nor the AUC difference (DeLong P = 0.16) was statistically significant. On external uncropped images, ViT yielded significantly higher accuracy than ResNet50 (93.5% [95% CI 90.0, 96.5] vs. 87.0% [95% CI 82.5, 91.5]; P = 0.04), whereas the corresponding AUCs (0.979 vs. 0.969) did not differ significantly (DeLong P = 0.39). For object detection, RF-DETR achieved higher mAP@0.5:0.95 than YOLOv12 in both the internal (0.723 [95% CI 0.703, 0.744] vs. 0.687 [95% CI 0.667, 0.709]) and external test datasets (0.668 [95% CI 0.630, 0.707] vs. 0.626 [95% CI 0.588, 0.664]), with statistically significant differences for this metric in each dataset .In conclusion, selected CNN and transformer architectures demonstrated comparable diagnostic performance for MRCP-based choledocholithiasis classification. For object detection, RF-DETR demonstrated higher localization performance than YOLOv12 on the evaluated metrics.

title: A region-aware spatial-frequency adaptive fusion framework for robust single image dehazing
authors: N. V. P. S. Rajesh Kandala
abstract: Atmospheric haze diminishes image visibility, contrast, and obscure fine details, adversely affecting visual perception and high-level vision tasks. Although prior-based dehazing methods have shown promising performance, these approaches relying solely on either the dark channel or bright channel prior estimates. These estimates, often fail to handle both non-sky and sky regions simultaneously. This paper proposes a region-aware spatial-frequency adaptive fusion framework. It integrates the complementary strengths of dark and bright channel priors transmission maps for effective scene radiance recovery. The fused image is further enhanced using Non-Subsampled Contourlet Transform (NSCT) based processing, incorporating gamma correction for low frequency components and wavelet-based denoising for high frequency components. Extensive experiments on five publicly available datasets demonstrate consistent performance based on PSNR, SSIM and other image-quality metrics. The proposed method demonstrates competitive performance with several conventional and deep learning-based dehazing approaches.

title: Sensorless closed-loop speed estimation of BLDC motor drive using physics-informed NN algorithm
abstract: Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motors are predominantly used in Electric Vehicle (EV) applications because of their higher efficiency, higher torque-to-weight ratio, lower maintenance requirements and capability to operate in a wide speed range. However, conventional sensor-based and traditional sensorless estimation methods experiences inaccurate performance under high-speed operating conditions because of parameter variations and nonlinear system dynamics. To overcome these limitations, this article implemented an improved sensorless Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)-based closed-loop speed estimation algorithm using Machine Learning (ML) based Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) algorithm specifically designed for high-speed applications. Performance of the implemented sensorless speed estimation scheme is experimentally validated and compared with conventional algorithms using the LAUNCHXL-F28379D development board. The experimental results indicates that the implemented method has a maximum steady-state error of 7 at 500 rpm and 8.95 at 1000 rpm between the actual motor speed and the reference speed. Furthermore, during higher operating speeds of 1500 rpm and 1600 rpm, the motor precisely tracks the reference speed.

title: Adaptive reinforcement learning-driven personalized training plan generation and effect evaluation for college students’ physical fitness tests
abstract: Conventional college fitness training in China relies on uniform schedules that ignore between-student variability, producing marginal gains for many and elevated risk for those pushed beyond their adaptive ceiling. We propose an adaptive reinforcement learning framework that generates and revises individualized training plans aligned with the National Student Physical Health Standard. The framework binds five layers—input ingestion, adaptive feature extraction, an improved Proximal Policy Optimization decision module, plan rendering, and dual-rate feedback—into a closed loop that ingests fitness scores, demographic descriptors, and longitudinal training logs to issue weekly prescriptions across endurance, strength, and flexibility components. Because no agent may experiment on students, we treat the historical records as an offline decision problem: a validated student-response model supplies the state transitions, and returns for prescriptions the records never contain are estimated only inside the support of the teaching policy that generated them. Three design elements distinguish the system: a slowly refreshed adaptive state representation that absorbs cohort drift; a four-component reward with deficit-driven scalarization balancing fitness gain, safety, adherence, and plan rationality; and a bounded-staleness prioritized buffer with importance-sampling correction, paired with cosine-annealed learning rates, for stable convergence under noisy educational signals. Experiments on 4128 students from four cohorts, partitioned so that no student ever spans two folds, returned a composite fitness improvement of 14.6% in held-out cross-validation. A 16-week randomized field study with 312 participants produced a 13.8% gain against 7.1% in the control arm; the prespecified intention-to-treat mixed model places the adjusted between-arm effect at 4.71 composite points (95% CI 3.92–5.50), or roughly six percentage points of relative improvement. Plan rationality reached 91.7% and adherence 87.3%, with the largest absolute gains accruing to initially failing students. Adaptive reinforcement learning therefore offers a workable—though not yet longitudinally proven—path toward precision physical education in higher education settings.

title: Assessment of influential geotechnical and seismic features for soil liquefaction using SPT- and Vs-based machine learning models
abstract: This study presents a machine learning-based framework to evaluate soil liquefaction susceptibility using two geotechnical datasets: Standard Penetration Test (SPT) and Shear Wave Velocity (V s ), integrated with strong ground motion parameters. Feature selection techniques were applied to identify the most influential predictors. For the SPT dataset, corrected blow count, maximum acceleration, and velocity pulse period were identified as key factors. For the Vs dataset, shear wave velocity, epicentral distance, maximum displacement, and the number of effective cycles were found to be critical. Three classification models; Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Neural Networks (NNs) were developed and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and AUC (Area Under Curve). Among them, RF consistently achieved the best performance, with accuracy and AUC values of 0.78 and 0.83 for the SPT dataset, and 0.75 and 0.83 for V s dataset, respectively. The results demonstrate that combining feature selection with ensemble learning enhances the reliability and predictive performance of liquefaction susceptibility assessment across varying site conditions. This study presents a unified machine learning framework integrating multidimensional strong ground motion parameters with both SPT- and Vs-based liquefaction datasets. The results demonstrate that combining advanced seismic features with ensemble learning significantly enhances the reliability of liquefaction susceptibility prediction.

title: A dual-stream Pyramid ViT–ConvFormer architecture leverages dynamic early stopping to classify diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
abstract: Molecular stratification of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) based on MYC rearrangement status (confirmed via fluorescence in situ hybridization) guides frontline therapeutic selection. Although Vision Transformers (ViTs) effectively model global tissue context, lacking localized inductive biases extends training convergence. We developed PyConv, an asymmetrical hybrid architecture engineered for the three-class histopathological classification of MYC -rearranged ( \(MYC+\) ) DLBCL, non-rearranged ( \(MYC-\) ) DLBCL, and reactive lymph node ( RLN ). PyConv combines local ConvFormer blocks with global Pyramid ViT blocks via Multi-Head Cross-Attention (MHCA) fusion. We evaluated the network on a patient-stratified cohort of 180 whole-slide images (69,480 testing patches) against 12 baseline backbones at both patch and patient levels. PyConv achieved a patch classification accuracy and macro F1-score of 0.9962 [95% CI: 0.9884–0.9991 via patient-level clustered bootstrapping] and a macro AUROC of 0.9999. Patient-level probability pooling yielded 100% classification concordance on the held-out test cohort (18/18 patients), showing no statistically significant discriminative loss compared to top-performing baselines (e.g., ConvFormer, \(p = 0.9866\) ) while integrating global stromal context. PyConv converged by epoch 20, reducing training duration by 68.7% compared to pure Pyramid ViT. PyConv provides an accurate, computationally efficient benchmarking framework for automated lymphoma classification. Although high patient concordance demonstrates internal feasibility, the model serves as an exploratory proof of concept requiring multi-center and multi-scanner validation before clinical translation.

title: MDFR-Net for enhanced feature refinement in aerial small object detection
abstract: Detecting tiny objects in aerial imagery remains challenging due to their minimal scale, diverse orientations, and complex background interference, limiting the ability of existing methods to capture discriminative features. To address these limitations, we propose MDFR-Net with the following key contributions. Firstly, the Multi-scale Hierarchical Attentional Fusion (MHAF) module leverages hierarchical convolution layers and dual-path attention to jointly extract salient features while suppressing background noise. Next, the Orientation Decoupled Feature Enhancer (ODFE) module incorporates direction-separated paths with lightweight attention to focus on orientation-specific target details. Additionally, the Hierarchical Convolution Pooling Fusion (HCPF) module employs parallel dilated convolutions and pooling operations to capture cross-scale contextual information. Finally, a high-resolution P2 detection layer preserves spatial details of tiny objects by incorporating high-resolution features into the detection head. Experiments on the VisDrone and AI-TOD datasets show that MDFR-Net improves detection performance under the evaluated settings. Multi-seed experiments on VisDrone provide evidence of the stability of these improvements, while the single-run results on AI-TOD offer preliminary evidence of cross-dataset applicability.

title: Hybrid PER–TD3–HER reinforcement learning for joint UAV trajectory, IRS phase, and resource allocation in energy-harvesting cell-free IoT networks
abstract: This paper proposes a customized hybrid deep reinforcement learning framework, termed PER–TD3–HER, for joint optimization of three-dimensional UAV trajectory design, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) phase configuration, transmit power allocation, and time-switching energy harvesting in UAV-assisted, IRS-enabled energy-harvesting cell-free IoT networks. The proposed framework integrates the Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm with Prioritized Experience Replay (PER) and Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) mechanisms to improve learning efficiency, exploration capability, and robustness in high-dimensional continuous control environments. Unlike conventional approaches that optimize network components separately, the proposed framework provides a unified learning-based solution for the coupled optimization of UAV mobility, IRS-assisted propagation control, resource allocation, and energy sustainability under dynamic network conditions and imperfect channel state information (CSI). In the proposed framework, PER enhances sample efficiency by prioritizing informative experiences associated with critical learning transitions, QoS requirements, energy constraints, and challenging channel conditions. Meanwhile, HER improves goal-oriented learning by transforming unsuccessful trajectories into valuable training experiences through goal relabeling. Furthermore, the continuous action-space formulation enables adaptive and simultaneous control of UAV trajectory, IRS phase shifts, transmit power allocation, and energy-harvesting ratios, overcoming the limitations of discrete decision-making approaches. Comprehensive simulations under realistic channel conditions and imperfect CSI demonstrate that the proposed PER–TD3–HER framework achieves improved convergence behavior, throughput–energy trade-off, and QoS satisfaction compared with TD3-based, DDPG-based, DQN-based, and SAC benchmark methods. The results verify the effectiveness, robustness, and scalability of the proposed framework for sustainable UAV-assisted IRS-enabled cell-free IoT networks and its potential applicability to future intelligent wireless communication systems.

title: AI-generated medical advice is rated favourably but GP advice is more trusted in India
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to provide health information and advice, yet its acceptance depends not only on how credible the information appears but also on whether individuals are willing to rely on it. Existing research has documented resistance to medical AI and source-labelling effects, but evidence from non-Western settings and factorial designs examining source, transparency, and clinical risk together remains comparatively limited. This study examined how individuals evaluate medical advice presented as AI-generated versus general practitioner (GP)-generated, whether source-related differences vary across transparency and clinical-risk conditions, and how these evaluations relate to stated willingness to follow the advice. We conducted a mixed-methods, partially within-subject 2 × 2 × 2 factorial experiment with 797 participants in Mumbai, India. Each participant evaluated four vignettes randomly drawn from eight conditions varying by source (AI or GP), transparency (high or low), and clinical risk (high or low), yielding 3,188 vignette observations. Following examination of the item structure, trustworthiness and a two-item uniqueness-recognition score (α = 0.944) were analysed as separate principal epistemically relevant outcomes. Perceived accuracy and binary behavioural intention were examined separately. The originally constructed three-item epistemic-value composite (α = 0.15) was retained only as an exploratory supplementary analysis. Data were analysed using linear and logistic mixed-effects models, participant-level paired comparisons, and equivalence testing using operational ± 0.20-SD bounds. Qualitative responses were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. Perceived recognition of individual uniqueness did not differ significantly between AI-generated and GP-generated advice, and equivalence was supported within the operational bounds. In contrast, GP-generated advice was rated as more trustworthy and more accurate than AI-generated advice and elicited greater stated willingness to follow. Nevertheless, willingness to follow remained high for both sources, with 86.5% of AI-generated advice responses and 97.3% of GP-generated advice responses indicating an intention to follow the advice. Transparency and clinical risk did not significantly influence the continuous evaluative outcomes. Qualitative findings indicated that AI-generated advice was valued particularly for accessibility and informational clarity, whereas GP-generated advice was more strongly associated with professional expertise, accountability, safety, and relational care. Favourable responses to AI-generated medical advice can coexist with a relative preference for advice attributed to a medical professional. Although AI- and GP-generated advice were comparable in perceived recognition of individual uniqueness within the operational equivalence bounds, GP-generated advice retained advantages in trustworthiness, perceived accuracy, and intended reliance. These findings suggest that responses to medical AI are multidimensional and support positioning AI as a complementary source of health information rather than as an interchangeable substitute for human medical expertise.

title: Intelligent manufacturing system and hybrid generative-attention framework for quality prediction of high-performance aluminum alloys
abstract: High-performance aluminum alloys are extensively used in aerospace, rail transit, and new-energy vehicles owing to their high specific strength, corrosion resistance, and formability. Meeting the stringent reliability standards in these sectors relies on the melting–casting process; however, characterized by complex multi-process coupling and small, imbalanced datasets, this process poses significant challenges for conventional modeling approaches in achieving accurate quality classification. To address these challenges, we develop a SCADA–MES integrated intelligent manufacturing data management system tailored to the full aluminum-alloy melting and casting route, providing dynamic, high-dimensional, and cross-process data support for predictive modeling. Building on this end-to-end infrastructure, we propose a deep-learning-based quality classification method that integrates Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN), Self-Attention and Inter-sample Transformer (SAINT), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). CTGAN performs data augmentation by generating synthetic samples consistent with the empirical distribution under categorical and process-condition constraints, thereby alleviating the issues of data scarcity and imbalance. SAINT employs a dual-channel attention mechanism to capture nonlinear dependencies across both features and samples, while CNN extracts stable local patterns and attenuates noise. Evaluations of the algorithm’s performance in comparison with the baseline approach indicate the proposed method achieves approximately 5% improvement in all key metrics such as accuracy, macro F1 and recall, which demonstrates outstanding accuracy and stability in multi-stage quality prediction across the entire melting-casting process and thus can provide a practical pathway for data-driven quality control of high-performance aluminum alloy.
